commentary.entry: <milestone type="x-importer" subType="x-osis2mod" n="$Rev: 3769 $ (SWORD: 1.9.0)"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Gen" sID="gen2" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/> <div sID="gen3" type="x-p"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Gen.1" sID="Gen.1"/>

<div eID="gen3" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Genesis</title> <div sID="gen4" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ge 1">Read first chapter of Genesis</reference><div eID="gen4" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5" type="x-p"/> GENESIS is the book of beginnings. It records not only the beginning of the heavens and the earth, and of plant, animal, and human life, but also of all human institutions and relationships. Typically, it speaks of the new birth, the new creation, where all was chaos and ruin. With Genesis begins also that progressive self-revelation of God which culminates in Christ. The three primary names of Deity, Elohim, Jehovah, and Adonai, and the five most important of the compound names, occur in Genesis; and that in an ordered progression which could not be changed without confusion. The problem of sin as affecting man's condition in the earth and his relation to God, and the divine solution of that problem are here in essence. Of the eight great covenants which condition human life and the divine redemption, four, the Edenic, Adamic, Noahic, and Abrahamic Covenants are in this book; and these are the fundamental covenants to which the other four, the Mosaic, Palestinian, Davidic, and New Covenants, are related chiefly as adding detail or development. Genesis enters into the very structure of the New Testament, in which it is quoted above sixty times in seventeen books. In a profound sense, therefore, the roots of all subsequent revelation are planted deep in Genesis, and whoever would truly comprehend that revelation must begin here. The inspiration of Genesis and it character as a divine revelation are authenticated by the testimony of Christ (<reference osisRef="mt 19:4-6">Matthew 19:4-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:37-39"> 24:37-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 10:4-9">Mark 10:4-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 11:49-51">Luke 11:49-51</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 17:26-29 lu 17:32"> 17:26-29,32</reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 1:5">John 1:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 7:21-23"> 7:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:44 joh 8:56"> 8:44,56</reference>).<div eID="gen5" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen6" type="x-p"/> Genesis is in five chief divisions:<div eID="gen6" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Creation (1:1-2:25)</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The fall and redemption (3:1-4,7).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Diverse Seeds, Cain and Seth, to the Flood (4:8-7:24).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Flood to Babel (8:1-11:9).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">From the call of Abram to the death of Joseph (11:10-50:26).</item> </list> <div sID="gen7" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in Genesis cover a period of 2,315 years (Ussher).<div eID="gen7" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">Elohim</hi> (sometimes <hi type="italic">El</hi> or <hi type="italic">Elah</hi>), English form “God.” the first of the three primary names of Deity, is a uni-plural noun formed from El = strength, or the strong e and <hi type="italic">Alah</hi>, to swear, to bind oneself by an oath, so implying faithfulness. This uni-plurality implied in the name is directly asserted in <reference osisRef="Gen 1:26"> Gen. 1:26</reference> (plurality), 27 unity)- see also <reference osisRef="Gen 3:22"> Gen. 3:22</reference>. Thus the Trinity is latent in Elohim. As meaning primarily the Strong One it is fitly used in the first chapter of Genesis. Used in the O. T. about 2500 times. See also <reference osisRef="Gen 2:4"> Gen. 2:4</reference>, note; <reference osisRef="Gen 2:7"> Gen. 2:7</reference>; 14. 18, note; 15. 2, note; 7. 1, note; 21. 33, note; 1 Sam. 1. 3, note.

<hi type="bold">without form and void</hi><div eID="gen8" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jer 4:23-27">Jeremiah 4:23-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 24:1">Isaiah 24:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 45:18"> 45:18</reference> clearly indicate that the earth had undergone a cataclysmic change as the result of divine judgment. The face of the earth bears everywhere the marks of such a catastrophe. There are not wanting imitations which connect it with a previous testing and fall of angels.<div eID="gen9" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10" type="x-p"/> See <reference osisRef="eze 28:12-15">Ezekiel 28:12-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 14:9-14">Isaiah 14:9-14</reference> which certainly go beyond the kings of Tyre and Babylon.

<hi type="bold">Let there be light</hi><div eID="gen10" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen11" type="x-p"/> Neither here nor in verses 14-18 is an original creative act implied. A different word is used. The sense is, made to appear; made visible. The sun and moon were created "in the beginning." The "light" of course came from the sun, but the vapour diffused the light. Later the sun appeared in an unclouded sky.

<hi type="bold">day</hi><div eID="gen11" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen12" type="x-p"/> The word "day" is used in Scripture in three ways:<div eID="gen12" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) that part of the solar day of twenty-four hours which is light <reference osisRef="ge 1:5 ge 1:14">Genesis 1:5,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 9:4">John 9:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 11:9"> 11:9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) such a day, set apart for some distinctive purpose, as, "day of atonement" (<reference osisRef="le 23:27">Leviticus 23:27</reference>); "day of judgment" <reference osisRef="mt 10:15">Matthew 10:15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) a period of time, long or short, during which certain revealed purposes of God are to be accomplished, as "day of the Lord."</item> </list> <div sID="gen13" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">evening</hi> <div eID="gen13" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14" type="x-p"/> The use of "evening" and "morning" may be held to limit "day" to the solar day; but the frequent parabolic use of natural phenomena may warrant the conclusion that each creative "day" was a period of time marked off by a beginning and ending.
<hi type="bold">firmament</hi> Lit. expanse (i.e. of waters beneath, of vapour above).
<hi type="bold">firmament</hi> i.e. the expanse above, the "heaven" of the clouds. <reference osisRef="ge 7:11">Genesis 7:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 8:2"> 8:2</reference>.

<hi type="bold">bring forth grass</hi><div eID="gen14" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15" type="x-p"/> It is by no means necessary to suppose that the life-germ of seeds perished in the catastrophic judgment which overthrew the primitive order. With the restoration of dry land and light the earth would "bring forth" as described. It was "animal" life which perished, the traces of which remain as fossils. Relegate fossils to the primitive creation, and no conflict of science with the Genesis cosmogony remains. Typist's Note: THE GAP THEORY]]
<div eID="gen15" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="psa 136:5-9">Psa 136:5-9</reference>

<hi type="bold">greater light</hi><div eID="gen16" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen17" type="x-p"/> The "greater light" is a type of Christ, the "Sun of righteousness" <reference osisRef="mal 4:2">Malachi 4:2</reference>. He will take this character at His second advent. Morally the world is now in the state between ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:3-16">Genesis 1:3-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 6:12">Ephesians 6:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 26:18">Acts 26:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>. The sun is not seen, but there is light. Christ is that light <reference osisRef="joh 1:4 joh 1:5 joh 1:9">John 1:4,5,9</reference> but "shineth in darkness," comprehended only by faith. As "Son of righteousness" He will dispel all darkness. Dispensationally the Church is in place as the "lesser light," the moon, reflecting the light of the unseen sun. The stars <reference osisRef="ge 1:16">Genesis 1:16</reference> are individual believers who are "lights" ; <reference osisRef="php 2:15 php 2:16">Philippians 2:15,16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:5">John 1:5</reference>.<div eID="gen17" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen18" type="x-p"/> A type is a divinely purposed illustration of some truth. It may be:<div eID="gen18" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) a person <reference osisRef="ro 5:14">Romans 5:14</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) an event <reference osisRef="1co 10:11">1 Corinthians 10:11</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) a thing <reference osisRef="heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:20</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) an institution <reference osisRef="heb 9:11">Hebrews 9:11</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) a ceremonial <reference osisRef="1co 5:7">1 Corinthians 5:7</reference></item> </list> <div sID="gen19" type="x-p"/> Types occur most frequently in the Pentateuch, but are found, more sparingly, elsewhere. The antitype, or fulfilment of the type, is found, usually, in the New Testament.<div eID="gen19" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">made</hi> The word does not imply a creative act; vs. <reference osisRef="ge 1:14-18">Genesis 1:14-18</reference> are declarative of function merely.

<hi type="bold">heaven</hi><div eID="gen20" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21" type="x-p"/> i.e. the "heaven" of the stars; e.g. <reference osisRef="ge 15:5">Genesis 15:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:43">Luke 23:43</reference>.

<hi type="bold">every living creature</hi><div eID="gen21" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22" type="x-p"/> The second clause, "every living creature," as distinguished from fishes merely, is taken up again in verse 24, showing that in the second creative act all animal life is included.

<hi type="bold">living creature</hi><div eID="gen22" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23" type="x-p"/> "Creature," Heb. nephesh, trans. soul in <reference osisRef="ge 2:7">Genesis 2:7</reference> and usually. In itself nephesh, or soul, implies self-conscious life, as distinguished from plants, which have unconscious life. In the sense of self-conscious life animals also have "soul." See verses ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:26 ge 1:27">Genesis 1:26,27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 2:7 ge 2:21-23"> 2:7,21-23</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">make man in our image</hi><div eID="gen23" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24" type="x-p"/> Man. <reference osisRef="ge 1:26 ge 1:27">Genesis 1:26,27,</reference> gives the general, <reference osisRef="ge 2:7 ge 2:21-23">Genesis 2:7,21-23</reference> the particular account of the creation of man. The revealed facts are:<div eID="gen24" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Man was created not evolved. This is</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) expressly declared, and the declaration is confirmed by Christ <reference osisRef="mt 19:14">Matthew 19:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 10:6">Mark 10:6,</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(b) "an enormous gulf, a divergence practically infinite" (Huxley) between the lowest man and the highest beast, confirms it;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(c) the highest beast has no trace of God-consciousness--the religious nature;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(d) science and discovery have done nothing to bridge that "gulf."</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) That man was made in the "image and likeness" of God. This image is found chiefly in man's tri-unity, and in his moral nature. Man is "spirit and soul and body" <reference osisRef="1th 5:23">1 Thessalonians 5:23</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen25" type="x-p"/> "Spirit" is that part of man which "knows" <reference osisRef="1co 2:11">1 Corinthians 2:11</reference> and which allies him to the spiritual creation and gives him God-consciousness. "Soul" in itself implies self-consciousness life, as distinguished from plants, which have unconscious life. In that sense animals also have "soul" <reference osisRef="ge 1:24">Genesis 1:24</reference>. But the "soul" of man has a vaster content than "soul" as applied to beast life. It is the seat of emotions, desires, affections <reference osisRef="ps 42:1-6">Psalms 42:1-6</reference>. The "heart" is, in Scripture usage, nearly synonymous with "soul." Because the natural man is, characteristically, the soulual or physical man, "soul" is often used as synonymous with the individual, e.g. <reference osisRef="ge 12:5">Genesis 12:5</reference>. The body, separable from spirit and soul, and susceptible to death, is nevertheless an integral part of man, as the resurrection shows ; <reference osisRef="joh 5:28 joh 5:29">John 5:28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:47-50">1 Corinthians 15:47-50</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:11-13">Revelation 20:11-13</reference>. It is the seat of the senses (the means by which the spirit and soul have world-consciousness) and of the fallen Adamic nature. <reference osisRef="ro 7:23 ro 7:24">Romans 7:23,24</reference>.<div eID="gen25" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen26" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">us</hi> <reference osisRef="ge 11:7">Genesis 11:7</reference>

<hi type="bold">DISPENSATION</hi><div eID="gen26" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27" type="x-p"/> A dispensation is a period of time during which man is tested in respect of obedience to some specific revelation of the will of God. Seven such dispensations are distinguished in Scripture. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi>, note 5.<div eID="gen27" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">And God blessed them</hi> <div eID="gen28" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29" type="x-p"/> The First Dispensation: Innocency. Man was created in innocency, placed in a perfect environment, subjected to an absolutely simple test, and warned of the consequence of disobedience. The woman fell through pride; the man deliberately. <reference osisRef="1ti 2:14">1 Timothy 2:14</reference> God restored His sinning creatures, but the dispensation of innocency ended in the judgment of the Expulsion <reference osisRef="ge 3:24">Genesis 3:24</reference> See, for the other dispensations;<div eID="gen29" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30" type="x-p"/> Conscience <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen30" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen31" type="x-p"/> Human Government <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen31" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen32" type="x-p"/> Promise <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen32" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen33" type="x-p"/> Law <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen33" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34" type="x-p"/> Grace <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen34" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen35" type="x-p"/> Kingdom <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen35" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen36" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Be fruitful</hi> <div eID="gen36" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen37" type="x-p"/> The Edenic Covenant, the first of the eight great covenants of Scripture which condition life and salvation, and about which all Scripture crystallizes, has seven elements. The man and woman in Eden were responsible:<div eID="gen37" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) To replenish the earth with a new order--man;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) to subdue the earth to human uses;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) to have dominion over the animal creation;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) to eat herbs and fruits;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) to till and keep the garden;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) to abstain from eating of the tree of knowledge of good and evil;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the penalty--death. See, for the other seven covenants:</item> </list> <div sID="gen38" type="x-p"/> ADAMIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:14">Genesis 3:14</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen38" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen39" type="x-p"/> NOAHIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen39" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen40" type="x-p"/> ABRAHAMIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen40" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen41" type="x-p"/> MOSAIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:25">Exodus 19:25</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen41" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen42" type="x-p"/> PALESTINIAN <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen42" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen43" type="x-p"/> DAVIDIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen43" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen44" type="x-p"/> NEW <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi> <chapter eID="Gen.1"/><div eID="gen44" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen45" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Gen.2" sID="Gen.2"/>

<hi type="bold">sanctified</hi> <div eID="gen45" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen46" type="x-p"/> In the O.T. the same Hebrew word (qodesh) is translated sanctify, consecrate, dedicate, and holy. It means, set apart for the service of God. See refs. following "Sanctify," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 2:3">Genesis 2:3</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Lord</hi><div eID="gen46" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen47" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Lord God</hi> <div eID="gen47" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen48" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Lord</hi> <div eID="gen48" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen49" type="x-p"/> LORD (Heb. Jehovah)<div eID="gen49" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The primary meaning of the name LORD (Jehovah) is the "self-existent One." Literally (as in <reference osisRef="ex 3:14">Exodus 3:14</reference>), "He that is who He is, therefore the eternal I AM:"</item> </list> <div sID="gen50" type="x-p"/> But Havah, from which Jehovah, or Yahwe, is formed, signifies also "to become," that is, to become known, thus pointing to a continuous and increasing self-revelation. Combining these meanings of Havah, we arrive at the meaning of the name Jehovah. He is "the self- existent One who reveals Himself." The name is, in itself, an advance upon the name "God" (El, Elah, Elohim), which suggests certain attributes of Deity, as strength, etc., rather than His essential being.<div eID="gen50" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) It is significant that the first appearance of the name Jehovah in Scripture follows the creation of man. It was God (Elohim) who said, "Let us make man in our image" (<reference osisRef="ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>); but when man, as in the second chapter of Genesis, is to fill the scene and become dominant over creation, it is the Lord God (Jehovah Elohim) who acts. This clearly indicates a special relation of Deity, in His Jehovah character, to man, and all Scripture emphasizes this.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Jehovah is distinctly the redemption name of Deity. When sin entered and redemption became necessary, it was Jehovah Elohim who sought the sinning ones <reference osisRef="ge 3:9-13">Genesis 3:9-13</reference> and clothed them with "coats of skins" <reference osisRef="ge 3:21">Genesis 3:21</reference> a beautiful type of righteousness provided by the Lord God through sacrifice <reference osisRef="ro 3:21 ro 3:22">Romans 3:21,22</reference>. The first distinct revelation of Himself by His name Jehovah was in connection with the redemption of the covenant people out of Egypt <reference osisRef="ex 3:13-17">Exodus 3:13-17</reference>. As Redeemer, emphasis is laid upon those attributes of Jehovah which the sin and salvation of man bring into exercise. These are:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) His holiness <reference osisRef="le 11:44 le 11:45">Leviticus 11:44,45</reference>; <reference osisRef="le 19:1-2 le 20:26"> 19:1,2 20:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="hab 1:12 hab 1:13">Habakkuk 1:12,13</reference> (b) His hatred and judgment of sin ; <reference osisRef="de 32:35-42">Deuteronomy 32:35-42</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 6:5-7">Genesis 6:5-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 11:4-6">Psalms 11:4-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 66:18"> 66:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 34:6 ex 34:7">Exodus 34:6,7</reference> (c) His love for and redemption of sinners, but always righteously ; <reference osisRef="ge 3:21">Genesis 3:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 8:20 ge 8:21"> 8:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 12:12 ex 12:13">Exodus 12:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="le 16:2 le 16:3">Leviticus 16:2,3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 53:5 isa 53:6 isa 53:10">Isaiah 53:5,6,10</reference> Salvation by Jehovah apart from sacrifice is unknown to Scripture.</item> </list> <div sID="gen51" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen51" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) In his redemptive relation to man, Jehovah has seven compound names which reveal Him as meeting every need of man from his lost state to the end. These compound names are:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) Jehovah-jireh, "the Lord will provide" <reference osisRef="ge 22:13 ge 22:14">Genesis 22:13,14</reference> i.e., will provide a sacrifice; (b) Jehovah-rapha, "the Lord that healeth" <reference osisRef="ex 15:26">Exodus 15:26</reference>. That this refers to physical healing the context shows, but the deeper healing of soul malady is implied. (c) Jehovah-nissi, "the Lord our banner" <reference osisRef="ex 17:8-15">Exodus 17:8-15</reference>. The name is interpreted by the context. The enemy was Amalek, a type of the flesh, and the conflict that day stands for the conflict of <reference osisRef="ga 5:17">Galatians 5:17</reference> the war of the Spirit against the flesh. Victory was wholly due to divine help. (d) Jehovah-Shalom, "the Lord our peace," or "the Lord send peace" <reference osisRef="jud 6:24">Judges 6:24</reference>. Almost the whole ministry of Jehovah finds expression and illustration in that chapter. Jehovah hates and judges sin <reference osisRef="ge 2:1-5">Genesis 2:1-5</reference>. Jehovah loves and saves sinners <reference osisRef="ge 2:7-18">Genesis 2:7-18</reference> but only through sacrifice <reference osisRef="ge 2:19-21">Genesis 2:19-21</reference> see also ; <reference osisRef="ro 5:1">Romans 5:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:14">Ephesians 2:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:20">Colossians 1:20</reference>. (e) Jehovah-ra-ah, "the Lord my shepherd" (Psa 23.). In Ps. 22 Jehovah makes peace by the blood of the cross; in Ps 23. Jehovah is shepherding His own who are in the world. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 10:7">John 10:7</reference>")</hi> (f) Jehovah-tsidkenu, "the Lord our righteousness" <reference osisRef="jer 23:6">Jeremiah 23:6</reference>. This name of Jehovah occurs in a prophecy concerning the future restoration and conversion of Israel. Then Israel will hail him as Jehovah-tsidkenu--"the Lord our righteousness." (g) Jehovah-shammah, "the Lord is present" <reference osisRef="eze 48:35">Ezekiel 48:35</reference>. This name signifies Jehovah's abiding presence with His people ; <reference osisRef="ex 33:14 ex 33:15">Exodus 33:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 16:27 1ch 16:33">1 Chronicles 16:27,33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 16:11">Psalms 16:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 97:5"> 97:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 28:20">Matthew 28:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 13:5">Hebrews 13:5</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Lord (Jehovah) is also the distinctive name of Deity as in covenant with Israel <reference osisRef="ex 19:3">Exodus 19:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 20:1 ex 20:2"> 20:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 31:31-34">Jeremiah 31:31-34</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Lord God (Heb. Jehovah Elohim) is the first of the compound names of Deity. Lord God is used distinctly:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) of the relation of Deity to man (a) as Creator <reference osisRef="ge 2:7-15">Genesis 2:7-15</reference> (b) as morally in authority over man <reference osisRef="ge 2:16 ge 2:17">Genesis 2:16,17</reference> (c) as creating and governing the earthly relationships of man ; <reference osisRef="ge 2:18-24">Genesis 2:18-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 3:16-19 ge 3:22-24"> 3:16-19,22-24</reference> and (d) as redeeming man <reference osisRef="ge 3:8-15 ge 3:21">Genesis 3:8-15,21</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of the relation of Deity to Israel <reference osisRef="ge 24:7">Genesis 24:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 28:13"> 28:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:15 ex 3:18">Exodus 3:15,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 4:5"> 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 5:1"> 5:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 7:6"> 7:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 1:11 de 1:21">Deuteronomy 1:11,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 4:1"> 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 6:3"> 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 12:1"> 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 7:13 jos 7:19 jos 7:20">Joshua 7:13,19,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 10:40 jos 10:42"> 10:40,42</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 2:12">Judges 2:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 2:30">1 Samuel 2:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 1:48">1 Kings 1:48</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 9:6">2 Kings 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 10:31">2 Kings 10:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 22:19">1 Chronicles 22:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ch 1:9">2 Chronicles 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ezr 1:3">Ezra 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 21:17">Isaiah 21:17</reference> See other names of Deity,</item> </list> <div sID="gen52" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:1">Genesis 1:1</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 15:2">Genesis 15:2</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 17:1">Genesis 17:1</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 21:33">Genesis 21:33</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1sa 1:3">1 Samuel 1:3</reference>"<div eID="gen52" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen53" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Lord God</hi> Deity (names of God) <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mal 3:18">Malachi 3:18</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">Hiddekel</hi> Hiddekel = ancient name of the Tigris.

<hi type="bold">Eve</hi><div eID="gen53" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen54" type="x-p"/> Eve, type of the Church as bride of Christ <reference osisRef="joh 3:28 joh 3:29">John 3:28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 11:2">2 Corinthians 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-32">Ephesians 5:25-32</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:7 re 19:8">Revelation 19:7,8</reference><div eID="gen54" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen55" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Woman</hi> "Isha," "because she was taken out of man" (Ish) <reference osisRef="ho 2:16">Hosea 2:16</reference>

Cf. <reference osisRef="Mt 19.51">Mt. 19.5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor 6:16">1 Corinthians 6:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph 5:31">Ephesians 5:31</reference>; <div eID="gen55" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1"/><div sID="gen56" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.2"/>
<div eID="gen56" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen57" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Gen.3" sID="Gen.3"/>

<hi type="bold">The serpent</hi> <div eID="gen57" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen58" type="x-p"/> The serpent, in his Edenic form, is not to be thought of as a writhing reptile. That is the effect of the curse <reference osisRef="ge 3:14">Genesis 3:14</reference>. The creature which lent itself to Satan may well have been the most beautiful as was the most "subtle" of creatures less than man. Traces of that beauty remain despite the curse. Every movement of a serpent is graceful, and many species are beautifully coloured. In the serpent, Satan first appeared as "an angel of light" <reference osisRef="2co 11:14">2 Corinthians 11:14</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Satan</hi> vs. 1,2,4,13,14; <reference osisRef="1chr 21:1">1 Chr 21:1</reference>;<div eID="gen58" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen59" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">Temptation vs</hi> 1-6,12,13; <reference osisRef="ge 22:1">Gen. 22:1</reference> (<reference osisRef="ge 2:1">Gen. 2.1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas 1:2">Jas. 1.2</reference>.)

<hi type="bold">And the Lord God said</hi><div eID="gen59" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60" type="x-p"/> The Adamic Covenant conditions the life of fallen man--conditions which must remain till, in the kingdom age, "the creation also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the sons of God" <reference osisRef="ro 8:21">Romans 8:21</reference>. The elements of the Adamic Covenant are:<div eID="gen60" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The serpent, Satan's tool, is cursed (<reference osisRef="ge 3:14">Genesis 3:14</reference>), and becomes God's illustration in nature of the effects of sin--from the most beautiful and subtle of creatures to a loathsome reptile! The deepest mystery of the atonement is intimated here. Christ, "made sin for us," in bearing our judgment, is typified by the brazen serpent ; <reference osisRef="nu 21:5-9">Numbers 21:5-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:14">John 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 5:21">2 Corinthians 5:21</reference>. Brass speaks of judgment--in the brazen altar, of God's judgment, and in the laver, of self-judgment.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The first promise of a Redeemer (<reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>). Here begins the "Highway of the Seed," Abel, Seth, Noah <reference osisRef="ge 6:8-10">Genesis 6:8-10,</reference> Shem <reference osisRef="ge 9:26 ge 9:27">Genesis 9:26,27,</reference> Abraham <reference osisRef="ge 12:1-4">Genesis 12:1-4,</reference> Isaac <reference osisRef="ge 17:19-21">Genesis 17:19-21</reference> Jacob <reference osisRef="ge 28:10-14">Genesis 28:10-14,</reference> Judah <reference osisRef="ge 49:10">Genesis 49:10,</reference> David <reference osisRef="2sa 7:5-17">2 Samuel 7:5-17</reference> Immanuel-Christ ; <reference osisRef="isa 7:9-14">Isaiah 7:9-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 1:1 mt 1:20-23">Matthew 1:1,20-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:8">1 John 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:31">John 12:31</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The changed state of the woman (<reference osisRef="ge 3:16">Genesis 3:16</reference>). In three particulars:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) Multiplied conception; (b) motherhood linked with sorrow; (c) the headship of the man (cf) <reference osisRef="ge 1:26 ge 1:27">Genesis 1:26,27</reference> The entrance of sin, which is disorder, makes necessary a headship, and it is vested in man ; <reference osisRef="1ti 2:11-14">1 Timothy 2:11-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:22-25">Ephesians 5:22-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:7-9">1 Corinthians 11:7-9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The earth cursed (<reference osisRef="ge 3:17">Genesis 3:17</reference>) for man's sake. It is better for fallen man to battle with a reluctant earth than to live without toil.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The inevitable sorrow of life (<reference osisRef="ge 3:17">Genesis 3:17</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The light occupation of Eden <reference osisRef="ge 2:15">Genesis 2:15</reference> changed to burdensome labour <reference osisRef="ge 3:18 ge 3:19">Genesis 3:18,19</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) Physical death <reference osisRef="ge 3:19">Genesis 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 5:12-21">Romans 5:12-21,</reference> See "Death (spiritual)" <reference osisRef="ge 2:17">Genesis 2:17</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 2:5">Ephesians 2:5</reference>")</hi>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen61" type="x-p"/> See for the other covenants:<div eID="gen61" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen62" type="x-p"/> EDENIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen62" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen63" type="x-p"/> NOAHIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen63" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen64" type="x-p"/> ABRAHAMIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen64" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen65" type="x-p"/> MOSAIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:25">Exodus 19:25</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen65" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen66" type="x-p"/> PALESTINIAN <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen66" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen67" type="x-p"/> DAVIDIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen67" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen68" type="x-p"/> NEW <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">thou shalt bruise his heel</hi><div eID="gen68" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen69" type="x-p"/> The chain of references which begins here includes the promises and prophecies concerning Christ which were fulfilled in His birth and works at His first advent. See, for line of unfulfilled promises and prophecies: "Christ (second advent)" <reference osisRef="de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 1:11">Acts 1:11</reference>")</hi> "Kingdom" ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference> "Kingdom (N.T.)" ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31">Luke 1:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:28">1 Corinthians 15:28</reference> "Day of the Lord" ; <reference osisRef="isa 2:10">Isaiah 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11">Revelation 19:11</reference>

<hi type="bold">return</hi> Death (physical).<div eID="gen69" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen70" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ge 5:5">Genesis 5:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 3:19"> 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:27">Hebrews 9:27</reference>
<hi type="bold">Eve</hi><div eID="gen70" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen71" type="x-p"/> i.e. living, or life-giver.

<hi type="bold">coats of skins</hi><div eID="gen71" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen72" type="x-p"/> Coats of skins: Type of "Christ, made unto us righteousness"-- a divinely provided garment that the first sinners might be made fit for God's presence. See Righteousness, garment <reference osisRef="ge 3:21">Genesis 3:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:8">Revelation 19:8</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Therefore the Lord God</hi><div eID="gen72" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen73" type="x-p"/> The Second Dispensation: Conscience. By disobedience man came to a personal and experimental knowledge of good and evil--of good as obedience, of evil as disobedience to the known will of God. Through that knowledge conscience awoke. Expelled from Eden and placed under the second, or ADAMIC COVENANT, man was responsible to do all known good, to abstain from all known evil, and to approach God through sacrifice. The result of this second testing of man is stated in <reference osisRef="ge 6:5">Genesis 6:5</reference> and the dispensation ended in the judgment of the Flood. Apparently "the east of the garden" <reference osisRef="ge 3:24">Genesis 3:24</reference> where were the cherubims and the flame, remained the place of worship through this second dispensation. See for the other six dispensations:<div eID="gen73" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen74" type="x-p"/> INNOCENCE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen74" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen75" type="x-p"/> HUMAN GOVERNMENT <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen75" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen76" type="x-p"/> PROMISE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen76" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen77" type="x-p"/> LAW <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen77" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen78" type="x-p"/> GRACE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen78" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen79" type="x-p"/> KINGDOM <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Cherubims</hi><div eID="gen79" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen80" type="x-p"/> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 1:5">Ezekiel 1:5</reference>")</hi> <chapter eID="Gen.3"/><div eID="gen80" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen81" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Gen.4" sID="Gen.4"/>

<hi type="bold">Cain</hi> <div eID="gen81" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen82" type="x-p"/> Cain ("acquisition") is a type of the mere man of the earth. His religion was destitute of any adequate sense of sin, or need of atonement. This religious type is described in 2Pe 2. Seven things are said of him:<div eID="gen82" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) he worships in self-will</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) is angry with God</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) refuses to bring a sin offering</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) murders his brother</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) lies to God</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) becomes a vagabond</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) is, nevertheless, the object of the divine solicitude.

<hi type="bold">Abel</hi></item> </list> <div sID="gen83" type="x-p"/> Abel ("exhalation," or, "that which ascends") is a type of the spiritual man. His sacrifice, in which atoning blood was shed <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference> was therefore at once his confession of sin and the expression of his faith in the interposition of a substitute <reference osisRef="heb 11:4">Hebrews 11:4</reference> <div eID="gen83" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1"/><div sID="gen84" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1"/> <hi type="bold">Abel</hi> <div eID="gen84" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen85" type="x-p"/> Abel ("exhalation," or, "that which ascends") is a type of the spiritual man. His sacrifice, in which atoning blood was shed <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference> was therefore at once his confession of sin and the expression of his faith in the interposition of a substitute <reference osisRef="heb 11:4">Hebrews 11:4</reference>.<div eID="gen85" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen86" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">flock</hi> <div eID="gen86" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen87" type="x-p"/> Type of Christ, the Lamb of God, the most constant type of the suffering Messiah--"the Lamb of God that taketh away the sin of the world" <reference osisRef="joh 1:29">John 1:29</reference>.<div eID="gen87" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen88" type="x-p"/> A lamb fitly symbolizes the unresisting innocency and harmlessness of the Lord Jesus <reference osisRef="isa 53:7">Isaiah 53:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:9">Luke 23:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:53 mt 26:54">Matthew 26:53,54</reference>. This type is brought into prominence by contrast with Cain's bloodless offering of the fruit of his own works, and proclaims, in the very infancy of the race, the primal truth that "without shedding of blood is no remission" ; <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 11:4"> 11:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">sin</hi><div eID="gen88" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen89" type="x-p"/> Or, sin-offering. In Hebrew the same word is used for "sin," and "sin- offering," thus emphasizing in a remarkable way the complete identification of the believer's sin with his sin offering (cf) <reference osisRef="joh 3:14">John 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 5:21">2 Corinthians 5:21</reference>.<div eID="gen89" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen90" type="x-p"/> Here both meanings are brought together. "Sin lieth at the door," but so also "a sin-offering croucheth at the tent door." It is "where sin abounded" that "grace did much more abound" <reference osisRef="ro 5:20">Romans 5:20</reference>.<div eID="gen90" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen91" type="x-p"/> Abel's offering implies a previous instruction (cf) <reference osisRef="ge 3:21">Genesis 3:21</reference> for it was "by faith" <reference osisRef="heb 11:4">Hebrews 11:4</reference> and faith is taking God at His word; so that Cain's unbloody offering was a refusal of the divine way. But Jehovah made a last appeal to Cain <reference osisRef="ge 4:7">Genesis 4:7</reference> even yet to bring the required offering.
<hi type="bold">mark</hi><div eID="gen91" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen92" type="x-p"/> i.e. for Cain's protection. The law of <reference osisRef="ge 9:6">Genesis 9:6</reference> was not yet enacted.
<hi type="bold">Nod</hi><div eID="gen92" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen93" type="x-p"/> Lit. wandering.

<hi type="bold">builded a city</hi><div eID="gen93" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen94" type="x-p"/> The first civilization, that which perished in the judgment of the Flood, was Cainitic in origin, character, and destiny. Every element of material civilization is mentioned in verses <reference osisRef="ge 4:16-22">Genesis 4:16-22,</reference> city and pastoral life, and the development of arts and manufactures. Enoch, after whom the first city was named, means "teacher." The el termination of the names of Enoch's son and grandson shows that for a time the knowledge of Elohim was preserved, but this soon disappears <reference osisRef="ro 1:21-23">Romans 1:21-23</reference>. Adah means "pleasure," or "adornment"; Zillah, to "hide"; Lamech, "conqueror," or "wild man." (Cf) <reference osisRef="ro 1:21-25">Romans 1:21-25</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 6:4">Genesis 6:4</reference>")</hi>. The Cainitic civilization may have been as splendid as that of Greece or Rome, but the divine judgment is according to the moral state, not the material. <reference osisRef="ge 6:5-7">Genesis 6:5-7</reference>.

<hi type="bold">to my wounding</hi><div eID="gen94" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen95" type="x-p"/> Or, who wounded me. Cain had slain an unoffending man and yet was protected by Jehovah; how much more Lamech, who had slain in self-defence.
<hi type="bold">Seth</hi><div eID="gen95" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen96" type="x-p"/> i.e. Sheth = appointed.

<hi type="bold">Enos</hi> i.e. mortal.<div eID="gen96" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen97" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">call upon the name</hi> Or, call themselves by the name of Jehovah. Contra. <reference osisRef="ge 12:8">Genesis 12:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 26:25"> 26:25</reference>. <div eID="gen97" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2"/><div sID="gen98" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.4"/>
<div eID="gen98" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen99" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Gen.5" sID="Gen.5"/>

<hi type="bold">Adam</hi> <div eID="gen99" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen100" type="x-p"/> Adam, as the natural head of the race <reference osisRef="lu 3:38">Luke 3:38</reference> is a contrasting type of Christ, the Head of the new creation. See ; <reference osisRef="ro 5:14">Romans 5:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:21-22 1co 15:45-47">1 Corinthians 15:21,22,45-47</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Enoch</hi><div eID="gen100" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen101" type="x-p"/> Enoch, "translated that he should not see death" <reference osisRef="heb 11:5">Hebrews 11:5</reference> before the judgment of the Flood, is a type of those saints who are to be translated before the apocalyptic judgments <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>. Noah, left on the earth, but preserved through the judgment of the Flood, is a type of the Jewish people, who will be kept through the apocalyptic judgments ; <reference osisRef="jer 30:5-9">Jeremiah 30:5-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 12:13-16">Revelation 12:13-16</reference> and brought as an earthly people to the new heaven and new earth ; <reference osisRef="isa 65:17-19">Isaiah 65:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 66:20-22"> 66:20-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 21:1">Revelation 21:1</reference>. <chapter eID="Gen.5"/><div eID="gen101" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen102" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="Gen.6" sID="Gen.6"/>

<hi type="bold">sons of God</hi> <div eID="gen102" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen103" type="x-p"/> Some hold that these "sons of God" were the "angels which kept not their first estate" <reference osisRef="jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>. It is asserted that the title is in the O.T. exclusively used of angels. But this is an error <reference osisRef="isa 43:6">Isaiah 43:6</reference>. Angels are spoken of in a sexless way. No female angels are mentioned in Scripture, and we are expressly told that marriage is unknown among angels. <reference osisRef="mt 22:30">Matthew 22:30</reference>.<div eID="gen103" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen104" type="x-p"/> The uniform Hebrew and Christian interpretation has been that verse <reference osisRef="ge 6:2">Genesis 6:2</reference> marks the breaking down of the separation between the godly line of Seth and the godless line of Cain, and so the failure of the testimony to Jehovah committed to the line of Seth <reference osisRef="ge 4:26">Genesis 4:26</reference>. For apostasy there is no remedy but judgment ; <reference osisRef="isa 1:2-7 isa 1:24-25">Isaiah 1:2-7,24,25</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 6:4-8">Hebrews 6:4-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:26-31"> 10:26-31</reference>. Noah, "a preacher of righteousness," is given 120 years, but he won no convert, and the judgment predicted by his great- grandfather fell ; <reference osisRef="jude 1:14 jude 1:15">Jude 1:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 7:11">Genesis 7:11</reference>.

<hi type="bold">imagination</hi><div eID="gen104" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen105" type="x-p"/> Or, the whole imagination. The Hebrew word signifies not only the imagination but also the purposes and desires.

<hi type="bold">walked</hi><div eID="gen106" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen107" type="x-p"/> Noah and Enoch are the two antediluvians of whom it is said that they "walked with God" <reference osisRef="ge 5:24">Genesis 5:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 6:9"> 6:9</reference>. Enoch, "translated that he should not see death" <reference osisRef="heb 11:5">Hebrews 11:5</reference> becomes a type of the saints who will be "caught up" before the great tribulation ; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:10">Revelation 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 12:1">Daniel 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:21">Matthew 24:21</reference>. Noah, preserved through the Flood, is a type of the Israelitish people who will be preserved through the tribulation <reference osisRef="jer 30:5-9">Jeremiah 30:5-9</reference>. <hi type="bold">ark</hi><div eID="gen107" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen108" type="x-p"/> "Ark": type of Christ as the refuge of His people from judgment <reference osisRef="heb 11:7">Hebrews 11:7</reference>. In strictness of application this speaks of the preservation through the "great tribulation" <reference osisRef="mt 24:21 mt 24:22">Matthew 24:21,22</reference> of the remnant of Israel who will turn to the Lord after the Church (typified by Enoch, who was translated to heaven before the judgment of the Flood) has been caught up to meet the Lord ; <reference osisRef="ge 5:22-24">Genesis 5:22-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:15-17">1 Thessalonians 4:15-17</reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 11:5">Hebrews 11:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 2:10 isa 2:11">Isaiah 2:10,11</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 26:20 isa 26:21"> 26:20,21</reference>. But the type also has a present reference to the position of the believer "in Christ" (Ep 1.), etc. It should be noted that the word translated "pitch" in <reference osisRef="ge 6:14">Genesis 6:14</reference> is the same word translated "atonement" in <reference osisRef="le 17:11">Leviticus 17:11</reference> etc. It is atonement that keeps out the waters of judgment and makes the believer's position "in Christ" safe and blessed.

<hi type="bold">the Lord said in heart</hi><div eID="gen122" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen123" type="x-p"/> The Third Dispensation: Human Government. Under Conscience, as in Innocency, man utterly failed, and the judgment of the Flood marks the end of the second dispensation and the beginning of the third. The declaration of the Noahic Covenant subjects humanity to a new test. Its distinctive feature is the institution, for the first time, of human government--the government of man by man. The highest function of government is the judicial taking of life. All other governmental powers are implied in that. It follows that the third dispensation is distinctively that of human government. Man is responsible to govern the world for God. That responsibility rested upon the whole race, Jew and Gentile, until the failure of Israel under the Palestinian Covenant (Deu 28.-<reference osisRef="ge 30:1-10"> 30:1-10</reference>) brought the judgment of the Captivities, when "the times of the Gentiles" (See) ; <reference osisRef="lu 21:24">Luke 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference> began, and the government of the world passed exclusively into Gentile hands ; <reference osisRef="da 2:36-45">Daniel 2:36-45</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 21:24">Luke 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>. That both Israel and the Gentiles have governed for self, not God, is sadly apparent. The judgment of the confusion of tongues ended the racial testing; that of the captivities the Jewish; while the Gentile testing will end in the smiting of the Image (Da 2.) and the judgment of the nations <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference>.<div eID="gen123" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen124" type="x-p"/> See, for the other six dispensations:<div eID="gen124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen125" type="x-p"/> INNOCENCE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen125" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen126" type="x-p"/> CONSCIENCE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen127" type="x-p"/> PROMISE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen128" type="x-p"/> LAW <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen128" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen129" type="x-p"/> GRACE <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen130" type="x-p"/> KINGDOM <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen130" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2"/><div sID="gen131" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.8"/>

<hi type="bold">generations of Shem</hi><div eID="gen154" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen155" type="x-p"/> Genesis 11. and 12. mark an important turning point in the divine dealing. Heretofore the history has been that of the whole Adamic race. There has been neither Jew nor Gentile; all have been one in "the first man Adam." Henceforth, in the Scripture record, humanity must be thought of as a vast stream from which God, in the call of Abram and the creation of the nation of Israel, has but drawn off a slender rill, through which He may at last purify the great river itself. Israel was called to be a witness to the unity of God in the midst of universal idolatry <reference osisRef="de 6:4">Deuteronomy 6:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 43:10-12">Isaiah 43:10-12</reference> to illustrate the blessedness of serving the true God <reference osisRef="de 33:26-29">Deuteronomy 33:26-29</reference> to receive and preserve the divine revelations ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:1 ro 3:2">Romans 3:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 4:5-8">Deuteronomy 4:5-8</reference> and to produce the messiah ; <reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 21:12"> 21:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 28:10 ge 28:14"> 28:10,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 49:10"> 49:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:16 2sa 7:17">2 Samuel 7:16,17</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 4:3 isa 4:4">Isaiah 4:3,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 1:1">Matthew 1:1</reference>.<div eID="gen155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen156" type="x-p"/> The reader of scripture should hold firmly in mind:<div eID="gen156" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) that from Gen 12. to <reference osisRef="mt 12:45">Matthew 12:45</reference> the Scriptures have primarily in view Israel, the little rill, not the great Gentile river; though again and again the universality of the ultimate divine intent breaks into view (e.g. ; <reference osisRef="ge 12:3">Genesis 12:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 2:2 isa 2:4">Isaiah 2:2,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 5:26"> 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 9:1 isa 9:2"> 9:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-12 isa 42:1-6"> 11:10-12 42:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 49:6 isa 49:12"> 49:6,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 52:15">Isaiah 52:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 54:3"> 54:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 55:5"> 55:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 60:3 isa 60:5 isa 60:11-16"> 60:3,5,11-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 61:6 isa 61:9"> 61:6,9</reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 62:2"> 62:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 66:12 isa 66:18 isa 66:19"> 66:12,18,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 16:19">Jeremiah 16:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="joe 3:9 joe 3:10">Joel 3:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 1:11">Malachi 1:11</reference> Ro 9. 10. 11. <reference osisRef="ga 3:8-14">Galatians 3:8-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) that the human race, henceforth called Gentile in distinction from Israel, goes on under the Adamic and Noahic covenants; and that for the race (outside Israel) the dispensations of Conscience and of Human government continue. The moral history of the great Gentile world is told in <reference osisRef="ro 1:21-32">Romans 1:21-32</reference> and its moral accountability in <reference osisRef="ro 2:1-16">Romans 2:1-16</reference>. Conscience never acquits: it either "accuses" or "excuses." Where the law is known to the Gentiles it is to them, as to Israel, "a ministration of death," a "curse" ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:19 ro 3:20">Romans 3:19,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 7:9 ro 7:10"> 7:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 3:7">2 Corinthians 3:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:10">Galatians 3:10</reference>. A wholly new responsibility arises when either Jew or Gentile knows the Gospel ; <reference osisRef="joh 3:18 joh 3:19 joh 3:36">John 3:18,19,36</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:22-24"> 15:22-24</reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 16:9"> 16:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:9-12">1 John 5:9-12</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">Now the Lord</hi> <div eID="gen159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen160" type="x-p"/> The Fourth Dispensation: Promise. For Abraham, and his descendants it is evident that the Abrahamic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi> made a great change. They became distinctively the heirs of promise. That covenant is wholly gracious and unconditional. The descendants of Abraham had but to abide in their own land to inherit every blessing. In Egypt they lost their blessings, but not their covenant. The Dispensation of Promise ended when Israel rashly accepted the law <reference osisRef="ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>. Grace had prepared a deliverer (Moses), provided a sacrifice for the guilty, and by divine power brought them out of bondage <reference osisRef="ex 19:4">Exodus 19:4</reference> but at Sinai they exchanged grace for law. The Dispensation of Promise extends from <reference osisRef="ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference> to <reference osisRef="ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8,</reference> and was exclusively Israelitish. The dispensation must be distinguished from the covenant. The former is a mode of testing; the latter is everlasting because unconditional. The law did not abrogate the Abrahamic Covenant <reference osisRef="ga 3:15-18">Galatians 3:15-18</reference> but was an intermediate disciplinary dealing "till the Seed should come to whom the promise was made" ; <reference osisRef="ga 3:19-29">Galatians 3:19-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-7"> 4:1-7</reference>. Only the dispensation, as a testing of Israel, ended at the giving of the law.<div eID="gen160" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen161" type="x-p"/> See, for the other six dispensations: <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen162" type="x-p"/> INNOCENCE (<reference osisRef="ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>) CONSCIENCE (<reference osisRef="ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>) HUMAN GOVERNMENT (<reference osisRef="ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>) LAW (<reference osisRef="ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>) GRACE (<reference osisRef="joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>) KINGDOM (<reference osisRef="eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>)

<hi type="bold">Melchizedek</hi><div eID="gen171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen172" type="x-p"/> 1 Melchizedek, type of Christ the King-Priest. The type strictly applies to the priestly work of Christ in resurrection, since Melchizedek presents only the memorials of sacrifice, bread and wine. "After the order of Melchizedek" <reference osisRef="heb 6:20">Hebrews 6:20</reference> refers to the royal authority and unending duration of Christ's high priesthood <reference osisRef="heb 7:23 heb 7:24">Hebrews 7:23,24</reference>. The Aaronic priesthood was often interrupted by death. Christ is a priest after the order of Melchizedek, as King of righteousness, King of peace ; <reference osisRef="isa 11:4-9">Isaiah 11:4-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:2">Hebrews 7:2</reference> and in the endlessness of his priesthood; but the Aaronic priesthood typifies His priestly work.<div eID="gen172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen173" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">most high God</hi> <div eID="gen173" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen174" type="x-p"/> 2 "Most high," or "most high God" (Heb. El Elyon). "Elyon means simply "highest."<div eID="gen174" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The first revelation of this name (<reference osisRef="ge 14:8">Genesis 14:8</reference>) indicates its distinctive meanings. Abram, returning from his victory over the confederated kings <reference osisRef="ge 14:1-17">Genesis 14:1-17</reference> is met by Melchizedek, King of Salem... the "priest of the most high God" (El Elyon), who blesses Abram in the name of El Elyon, "possessor of heaven and earth." This revelation produced a remarkable impression upon the patriarch. Not only did he at once give Melchizedek "tithes of all" the spoil of the battle, but when the King of Sodom offered other of that spoil to Abram, his answer was; "I have lift up mine hand unto the Lord Jehovah, the most high God El-Elyon, the possessor of heaven and earth, that I will not take from a thread even to a shoelatchet," etc. <reference osisRef="ge 14:18-23">Genesis 14:18-23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) The Lord (Jehovah) is know to a Gentile king (Melchizedek) by the name "most high god" El Elyon);</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) a Gentile is the priest of El Elyon and</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(c) His distinctive character as most high God is "possessor of heaven and earth."</item> </list> <div sID="gen175" type="x-p"/> Appropriately to this Gentile knowledge of God by His name "Most High," we read that "the Most High divided to the nations i.e. Gentiles] their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam," etc. <reference osisRef="de 32:8">Deuteronomy 32:8</reference>. "Lord" (Heb. Adon, Adonai)<div eID="gen183" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The primary meaning of Adon, Adonai, is Master, and it is applied in the Old Testament Scriptures both to Deity and to man. The latter instances are distinguished in the English version by the omission of the capital. As applied to man, the word is used of two relationships; master and husband <reference osisRef="ge 24:9 ge 24:10 ge 24:12">Genesis 24:9,10,12</reference> "master" may illustrate the former; <reference osisRef="ge 18:12">Genesis 18:12</reference> "lord," the latter). Both these relationships exist between Christ and the believer <reference osisRef="joh 13:13">John 13:13</reference> "master"; <reference osisRef="2co 11:2 2co 11:3">2 Corinthians 11:2,3</reference> "husband").</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Two principles inhere in the relation of master and servant:</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) the Master's right to implicit obedience <reference osisRef="joh 13:13">John 13:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 23:10">Matthew 23:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 6:46">Luke 6:46</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) the servant's right to direction in service <reference osisRef="isa 6:8-11">Isaiah 6:8-11</reference></item> </list> <div sID="gen184" type="x-p"/> Clear distinction in the use of the divine names is illustrated in <reference osisRef="ex 4:10-12">Exodus 4:10-12</reference>. But now power is in question, and it not the Lord (Adonai) but Jehovah (Lord) who answers (referring to creation power)--"and Jehovah said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth?.. Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth." The same distinction in <reference osisRef="jos 7:8-11">Joshua 7:8-11</reference>. Fulfilled in two ways:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) temporally <reference osisRef="ge 13:14 ge 13:15 ge 13:17">Genesis 13:14,15,17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 15:18"> 15:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 24:34 ge 24:35"> 24:34,35</reference> (b) spiritually ; <reference osisRef="ge 15:6">Genesis 15:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:56">John 8:56</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) "And make thy name great." Abraham's is one of the universal names.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) "And thou shalt be a blessing" <reference osisRef="ga 3:13 ga 3:14">Galatians 3:13,14</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) "I will bless them that bless thee." In fulfilment closely related to the next clause.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) "And curse him that curseth thee." Wonderfully fulfilled in the history of the dispersion. It has invariably fared ill with the people who have persecuted the Jew--well with those who have protected him. The future will still more remarkably prove this principle <reference osisRef="de 30:7">Deuteronomy 30:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 14:1">Isaiah 14:1,</reference>; <reference osisRef="joe 3:1-8">Joel 3:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 5:7-9">Micah 5:7-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="hag 2:22">Haggai 2:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 14:1-3">Zechariah 14:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:40 mt 25:45">Matthew 25:40,45</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) "In thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed." This is the great evangelic promise fulfilled in Abraham's Seed, Christ <reference osisRef="ga 3:16">Galatians 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:56-58">John 8:56-58</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen194" type="x-p"/> It brings into greater definiteness the promise of the Adamic Covenant concerning the Seed of the woman <reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference><div eID="gen194" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen195" type="x-p"/> NOTE.--The gift of the land is modified by prophecies of three dispossessions and restorations <reference osisRef="ge 15:13 ge 15:14 ge 15:16">Genesis 15:13,14,16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 25:11 jer 25:12">Jeremiah 25:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 28:62-65">Deuteronomy 28:62-65</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 30:1-3"> 30:1-3</reference>. Two dispossessions and restorations have been accomplished. Israel is now in the third dispersion, from which she will be restored at the return of the Lord as King under the Davidic Covenant ; <reference osisRef="de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 23:5-8">Jeremiah 23:5-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 37:21-25">Ezekiel 37:21-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:30-33">Luke 1:30-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference><div eID="gen195" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen196" type="x-p"/> See, for the other seven covenants:<div eID="gen196" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen197" type="x-p"/> EDENIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi> ADAMIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>" NOAHIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>" MOSAIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ex 19:25">Exodus 19:25</reference>" PALESTINIAN See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>" DAVIDIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>" NEW See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>" <chapter eID="Gen.15"/><div eID="gen197" type="x-p"/>
