<hi type="bold">Almighty God</hi> <div eID="gen203" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen204" type="x-p"/> "Almighty God" (Heb. El Shaddai)<div eID="gen204" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The etymological signification of Almighty God (El Shaddai) is both interesting and touching. God (El) signifies the "Strong One" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:1">Genesis 1:1</reference>")</hi>. The qualifying word Shaddai is formed from the Hebrew word "shad," the breast, invariably used in Scripture for a woman's breast; e.g. <reference osisRef="ge 49:25">Genesis 49:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="job 3:12">Job 3:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 22:9">Psalms 22:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="so 1:13">Song 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="so 4:5"> 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="so 7:3 so 7:7 so 7:8">Song 7:3,7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="so 8:1 so 8:8 so 8:10"> 8:1,8,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 28:9">Isaiah 28:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 16:7">Ezekiel 16:7</reference>. Shaddai therefore means primarily "the breasted." God is "Shaddai," because He is the Nourisher, the Strength-giver, and so, in a secondary sense, the Satisfier, who pours himself into believing lives. As a fretful, unsatisfied babe is not only strengthened and nourished from the mother's breast, but also is quieted, rested, satisfied, so El Shaddai is that name of God which sets Him forth as the Strength-giver and Satisfier of His people. It is on every account to be regretted that "Shaddai" was translated "Almighty." The primary name El or Elohim sufficiently signifies almightiness. "All-sufficient" would far better express both the Hebrew meaning and the characteristic use of the name in Scripture.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Almighty God (El Shaddai) not only enriches, but makes fruitful. This is nowhere better illustrated than in the first occurrence of the name <reference osisRef="ge 17:1-8">Genesis 17:1-8</reference>. To a man ninety-nine years of age, and "as good as dead" <reference osisRef="heb 11:12">Hebrews 11:12</reference>. He said: "I am the Almighty God El Shaddai... I will... multiply thee exceedingly." To the same purport is the use of the name in <reference osisRef="ge 28:3 ge 28:4">Genesis 28:3,4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) As Giver of fruitfulness, Almighty God (El Shaddai) chastens His people. For the moral connection of chastening with fruit bearing, see <reference osisRef="joh 15:2">John 15:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:10">Hebrews 12:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ru 1:20">Ruth 1:20</reference>. Hence, Almighty is the characteristic name of God in Job, occurring thirty-one times in that book. The hand of El Shaddai falls upon Job, the best man of his time, not in judgment, but in purifying unto greater fruitfulness <reference osisRef="job 5:17-25">Job 5:17-25</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen205" type="x-p"/> See, for other names of Deity:<div eID="gen205" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen206" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:1">Genesis 1:1</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 2:4">Genesis 2:4</reference>" <reference osisRef="ge 2:7">Genesis 2:7</reference> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 15:2">Genesis 15:2</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 21:33">Genesis 21:33</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1sa 1:3">1 Samuel 1:3</reference>"

<hi type="bold">Abram</hi> Or, high father.<div eID="gen206" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen207" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Abraham</hi> Or, father of many nations. <div eID="gen207" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3"/><div sID="gen208" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.17"/>
<div eID="gen208" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen209" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="18" osisID="Gen.18" sID="Gen.18"/>

<hi type="bold">tent</hi> <div eID="gen209" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen210" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 19:1">Genesis 19:1</reference>. For significance of Abraham's tent, <reference osisRef="heb 11:9 heb 11:10">Hebrews 11:9,10</reference>.

<hi type="bold">near</hi><div eID="gen210" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen211" type="x-p"/> Communion vs. <reference osisRef="ge 18:23">Genesis 18:23,</reference> and intercession go together. <div eID="gen211" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3"/><div sID="gen212" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.18"/>
<div eID="gen212" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen213" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="19" osisID="Gen.19" sID="Gen.19"/>

<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen213" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen214" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Lot sat</hi> Cf. <reference osisRef="da 2:49">Daniel 2:49</reference>.<div eID="gen214" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen215" type="x-p"/> Lot the compromiser with Daniel the inflexible. Lot was a great man <reference osisRef="de 21:19 de 21:20">Deuteronomy 21:19,20</reference> in a place devoted to judgment. Cf. <reference osisRef="ac 17:31">Acts 17:31</reference>.
<hi type="bold">And they said</hi><div eID="gen215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen216" type="x-p"/> The world's contempt for a worldly believer.

<hi type="bold">Lot</hi><div eID="gen216" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen217" type="x-p"/> Lot had utterly lost his testimony. In gaining influence <reference osisRef="ge 19:1">Genesis 19:1</reference> he had lost power, even in his own family.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen217" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen218" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">when God</hi><div eID="gen218" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen219" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 19:36">Genesis 19:36</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Come</hi><div eID="gen219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen220" type="x-p"/> Lot "pitched toward Sodom" <reference osisRef="ge 13:12">Genesis 13:12</reference> for worldly advantage; then became a great man in Sodom <reference osisRef="ge 19:1">Genesis 19:1</reference> at the cost of his daughter's accepting the morals of Sodom.

<hi type="bold">Thus were</hi><div eID="gen220" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen221" type="x-p"/> Abraham and Lot are contrasted characters. Of the same stock <reference osisRef="ge 11:31">Genesis 11:31</reference> subjected to the same environment, and both justified men ; <reference osisRef="ge 15:6">Genesis 15:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:7 2pe 2:8">2 Peter 2:7,8</reference> the contrast in character and career is shown to be the result of their respective choices at the crisis of their lives. Lot "chose him all the plain of Jordan" for present advantage; Abraham "looked for a city which hath foundations" ; <reference osisRef="heb 11:10">Hebrews 11:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 13:18">Genesis 13:18</reference> "came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre (fatness), which is in Hebron" (communion). The men remain types of the worldly and spiritual believer. <chapter eID="Gen.19"/><div eID="gen221" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen222" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="20" osisID="Gen.20" sID="Gen.20"/>

<hi type="bold">fear</hi> <div eID="gen222" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen223" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.20"/><div eID="gen223" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen224" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="21" osisID="Gen.21" sID="Gen.21"/>

<hi type="bold">Sarah</hi> <div eID="gen224" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen225" type="x-p"/> Sarah, type of grace, "the freewoman," and of the "Jerusalem which is above." See <reference osisRef="ge 17:15-19">Genesis 17:15-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:22-31">Galatians 4:22-31</reference><div eID="gen225" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen226" type="x-p"/> 2 Isaac is typical in fourfold way:<div eID="gen226" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) of the Church as composed of the spiritual children of Abraham <reference osisRef="ga 4:28">Galatians 4:28</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of Christ as the Son "obedient unto death" <reference osisRef="ge 22:1-10">Genesis 22:1-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:5-8">Philippians 2:5-8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) of Christ as the Bridegroom of a called-out bride see Gen 24; also, "Church," <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) of the new nature of the believer as "born after the Spirit" <reference osisRef="ga 4:29">Galatians 4:29</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3"/><div sID="gen227" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3"/> <hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen227" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen228" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">everlasting God</hi><div eID="gen228" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The Hebrew "Olam" is used in Scripture:</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) of secret or hidden things (e.g. <reference osisRef="le 5:2">Leviticus 5:2</reference> "hidden"; <reference osisRef="2ki 4:27">2 Kings 4:27,</reference> "hid"; <reference osisRef="ps 10:1">Psalms 10:1,</reference> "hidest");</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) an indefinite time or age <reference osisRef="le 25:32">Leviticus 25:32,</reference> "at any time"; <reference osisRef="jos 24:2">Joshua 24:2</reference> "in old time"). Hence the word is used to express the eternal duration of the being of God, <reference osisRef="ps 90:2">Psalms 90:2</reference>. "From everlasting to everlasting"), and is the Hebrew synonym of the Greek "aion," age or dispensation. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>")</hi>, note (4).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The ideas therefore of things kept secret and of indefinite duration combine in this word. Both ideas inhere in the doctrine of the dispensations or ages. They are among the "mysteries" of God <reference osisRef="eph 1:9 eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:2-6"> 3:2-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>. The "everlasting" God (El Olam) is therefore that name of Deity in virtue of which He is the God whose wisdom has divided all time and eternity into the mystery of successive ages or dispensations. It is not merely that He is everlasting, but that He is God over everlasting things. See, for other names of Deity:</item> </list> <div sID="gen229" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:1">Genesis 1:1</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 2:4">Genesis 2:4</reference>" <reference osisRef="ge 2:7">Genesis 2:7</reference> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 15:2">Genesis 15:2</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 17:1">Genesis 17:1</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1sa 1:3">1 Samuel 1:3</reference>" <div eID="gen229" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4"/><div sID="gen230" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.21"/>
<div eID="gen230" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen231" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="22" osisID="Gen.22" sID="Gen.22"/>

<hi type="bold">And it came to pass</hi> <div eID="gen231" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen232" type="x-p"/> The spiritual experience of Abraham was marked by four great crises, each of which involved a surrender of something naturally most dear. These were:<div eID="gen232" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Country and kindred <reference osisRef="ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 10:34-39">Matthew 10:34-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 6:14-18">2 Corinthians 6:14-18</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) His nephew, Lot; especially dear to Abraham by nature, as a possible heir and as a fellow believer <reference osisRef="2pe 2:7 2pe 2:8">2 Peter 2:7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 13:1-18">Genesis 13:1-18</reference>. The completeness of Abraham's separation from one who, though a believer, was a "vessel unto dishonour," is shown by ; <reference osisRef="ge 15:1-3">Genesis 15:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 2:20 2ti 2:21">2 Timothy 2:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:36-40">Acts 15:36-40</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) His own plan about Ishmael <reference osisRef="ge 17:17 ge 17:18">Genesis 17:17,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 13:1-14">1 Chronicles 13:1-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 15:1 1ch 15:2"> 15:1,2</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Isaac, "thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest" <reference osisRef="ge 22:1-19">Genesis 22:1-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 11:17 heb 11:18">Hebrews 11:17,18</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4"/><div sID="gen233" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4"/> <hi type="bold">laid</hi> <div eID="gen233" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen234" type="x-p"/> The typical lessons here are:<div eID="gen234" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Isaac, type of Christ "obedient unto death" <reference osisRef="php 2:5-8">Philippians 2:5-8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Abraham, type of the Father, who "spared not His own son, but delivered Him up for us all" <reference osisRef="joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:32">Romans 8:32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the ram, type of substitution--Christ offered as a burnt-offering in our stead, <reference osisRef="heb 10:5-10">Hebrews 10:5-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) cf. resurrection <reference osisRef="heb 11:17-19">Hebrews 11:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:21-23">James 2:21-23</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5"/><div sID="gen235" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5"/> <hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen235" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen236" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">fearest</hi><div eID="gen236" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen237" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen237" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen238" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.22"/><div eID="gen238" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen239" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="23" osisID="Gen.23" sID="Gen.23"/>

<hi type="bold">buryingplace</hi> <div eID="gen239" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen240" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 33:19">Genesis 33:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 50:13"> 50:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 24:32">Joshua 24:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 7:15 ac 7:16">Acts 7:15,16</reference>. A discrepancy in these statements has been fancied. It disappears entirely before the natural supposition that in the interval of about eighty years between the purchase by Abraham of the family sepulchre <reference osisRef="ge 23:4-20">Genesis 23:4-20</reference> and Jacob's purchase <reference osisRef="ge 33:19">Genesis 33:19,</reference> the descendants of Hamor (or "Emmor," <reference osisRef="ac 7:15 ac 7:16">Acts 7:15,16</reference> had resumed possession of the field in which the burial cave was situated. Instead of asserting an ancient title by inheritance, Jacob repurchased the field. Heth was the common ancestor.

<hi type="bold">And Abraham</hi><div eID="gen240" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen241" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 23:4">Genesis 23:4</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen241" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6"/><div sID="gen242" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.23"/>
<div eID="gen242" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen243" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="24" osisID="Gen.24" sID="Gen.24"/>

<hi type="bold">And Abraham</hi> <div eID="gen243" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen244" type="x-p"/> The entire chapter is highly typical:<div eID="gen244" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Abraham, type of a certain king who would make a marriage for his son <reference osisRef="mt 22:2">Matthew 22:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:44">John 6:44</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the unnamed servant, type of the Holy Spirit, who does not "speak of himself," but takes of the things of the Bridegroom with which to win the bride <reference osisRef="joh 16:13 joh 16:14">John 16:13,14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the servant, type of the Spirit as enriching the bride with the Bridegroom's gifts <reference osisRef="ga 5:22">Galatians 5:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 12:7-11">1 Corinthians 12:7-11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the servant, type of the Spirit as bringing the bride to the meeting with the Bridegroom <reference osisRef="ac 13:4">Acts 13:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 16:6 ac 16:7"> 16:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:11">Romans 8:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-16">1 Thessalonians 4:14-16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Rebekah, type of the Church, the ecclesia, the "called out" virgin bride of Christ <reference osisRef="ge 24:16">Genesis 24:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 11:2">2 Corinthians 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-32">Ephesians 5:25-32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Isaac, type of the Bridegroom, "whom not having seen," the bride loves through the testimony of the unnamed Servant <reference osisRef="1pe 1:8">1 Peter 1:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) Isaac, type of the Bridegroom who goes out to meet and receive His bride <reference osisRef="ge 24:63">Genesis 24:63</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-16">1 Thessalonians 4:14-16</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6"/><div sID="gen245" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6"/> <hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen246" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">thereby</hi><div eID="gen246" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen247" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jud 6:17 jud 6:37">Judges 6:17,37</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 20:9">2 Kings 20:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="pr 16:33">Proverbs 16:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:26">Acts 1:26</reference>. Cf: <reference osisRef="mt 12:39">Matthew 12:39</reference>. Signs are given to faith, not to doubt.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen247" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen248" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Lahairoi</hi><div eID="gen248" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen249" type="x-p"/> i.e. "the well of him that liveth and seeth me." <reference osisRef="ge 16:14">Genesis 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 25:11"> 25:11</reference>.

<hi type="bold">servant</hi> This is the model servant:<div eID="gen249" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) he does not run unsent, <reference osisRef="ge 24:2-9">Genesis 24:2-9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) goes where he is sent, <reference osisRef="ge 24:4 ge 24:10">Genesis 24:4,10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) does nothing else;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) is prayerful and thankful, <reference osisRef="ge 24:12-14 ge 24:26-27">Genesis 24:12-14,26,27</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) is wise to win, vs. <reference osisRef="ge 24:17 ge 24:18 ge 24:21">Genesis 24:17,18,21</reference>. (Cf) <reference osisRef="joh 4:7">John 4:7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) speaks not of himself, but of his master's riches and Isaac's heirship, <reference osisRef="ge 24:22 ge 24:34-36">Genesis 24:22,34-36</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) presents the true issue, and requires clear decision, <reference osisRef="ge 24:49">Genesis 24:49</reference>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen250" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.24"/>
<div eID="gen250" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen251" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="25" osisID="Gen.25" sID="Gen.25"/>

<hi type="bold">Keturah</hi> <div eID="gen251" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen252" type="x-p"/> As Sarah stands for "the mother of us all," i.e. of those who, by grace, are one with the true Son of promise, of whom Isaac was the type <reference osisRef="joh 3:6-8">John 3:6-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:26 ga 4:28 ga 4:29">Galatians 4:26,28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:11-13">Hebrews 2:11-13</reference> and joint heirs of His wealth ; <reference osisRef="heb 1:2">Hebrews 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:16 ro 8:17">Romans 8:16,17,</reference> so Keturah (wedded after the full blessing of Isaac) and her children by Abraham may well stand for the fertility of Israel the natural seed, Jehovah's wife <reference osisRef="ho 2:1-23">Hosea 2:1-23</reference> after the future national restoration under the Palestinian covenant.<div eID="gen252" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen253" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Esau</hi><div eID="gen253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen254" type="x-p"/> Esau stands for the mere man of the earth. <reference osisRef="heb 12:16 heb 12:17">Hebrews 12:16,17</reference>. In many respects a nobler man, naturally, than Jacob, he was destitute of faith, and despised the birthright because it was a spiritual thing, of value only as there was faith to apprehend it.

<hi type="bold">birthright</hi><div eID="gen254" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen255" type="x-p"/> The "birthright" had three elements:<div eID="gen255" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Until the establishment of the Aaronic priesthood the head of the family exercised priestly rights.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The Abrahamic family held the Edenic promise of the Satan-Bruiser <reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>. --Abel, Seth, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, Esau.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Esau, as the firstborn, was in the direct line of the Abrahamic promise of the Earth-Blesser <reference osisRef="ge 12:3">Genesis 12:3</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen256" type="x-p"/> For all that was revealed, in Esau might have fulfilled those two great Messianic promises. This birthright Esau sold for a momentary fleshly gratification. Jacob's conception of the birthright at that time was, doubtless, carnal and inadequate, but his desire for it evidenced true faith. <div eID="gen256" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen257" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.25"/>
<div eID="gen257" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen258" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="26" osisID="Gen.26" sID="Gen.26"/>
<hi type="bold">famine</hi> <div eID="gen258" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen259" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:10">Genesis 12:10</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Go not down</hi><div eID="gen259" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen260" type="x-p"/> Cf. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 46:3">Genesis 46:3</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">name of the well</hi><div eID="gen260" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen261" type="x-p"/> The wells of Genesis have significant names, and are associated with significant events:<div eID="gen261" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Beer-lahai-roi, the well of him that liveth and seeth me <reference osisRef="ge 16:14">Genesis 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 24:62"> 24:62</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 25:11"> 25:11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Beer-sheba, the well of the oath or covenant <reference osisRef="ge 21:15-33">Genesis 21:15-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 22:19">Genesis 22:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 26:23-25"> 26:23-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 46:1-5"> 46:1-5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Esek, contention <reference osisRef="ge 26:20">Genesis 26:20</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Sitnah, hatred <reference osisRef="ge 26:21">Genesis 26:21</reference>. Esek and Sitnah were Isaac's own attempts at well-digging. Afterward, he dwelt by the old wells of his father.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Rehoboth, enlargement <reference osisRef="ge 26:22">Genesis 26:22</reference>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen262" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.26"/>
<div eID="gen262" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen263" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="27" osisID="Gen.27" sID="Gen.27"/>

<hi type="bold">cursed</hi> <div eID="gen263" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen264" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="ge 12:3">Genesis 12:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 15:18"> 15:18,</reference> See note 3,(5), <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">and Esau</hi><div eID="gen264" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen265" type="x-p"/> Esau wept because of a lost advantage, but "found no way to change his mind, though he sought it carefully with tears" <reference osisRef="heb 12:17">Hebrews 12:17</reference> so far may regret or remorse be from true repentance:

<hi type="bold">life</hi> <reference osisRef="ge 26:34 ge 26:35">Genesis 26:34,35</reference>.<div eID="gen265" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen266" type="x-p"/> Heth was ancestor of the Hittites. <div eID="gen266" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen267" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.27"/>
<div eID="gen267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen268" type="x-p"/><chapter n="28" osisID="Gen.28" sID="Gen.28"/>
<hi type="bold">life</hi> <reference osisRef="ge 26:34 ge 26:35">Genesis 26:34,35</reference>.<div eID="gen268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen269" type="x-p"/> Heth was ancestor of the Hittites.
<hi type="bold">Mahalath</hi><div eID="gen269" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen270" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ge 36:3">Genesis 36:3</reference> is called Bashemath:

<hi type="bold">And Jacob went out</hi><div eID="gen270" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen271" type="x-p"/> Bethel becomes, because of Jacob's vision there, one of the significant places of Scripture. To the Christian it stands for a realization, however imperfect, of the heavenly and spiritual contents of faith, answering to Paul's prayer in <reference osisRef="eph 1:17-23">Ephesians 1:17-23</reference>. Dispensationally, the scene speaks of Israel the nation, cast out of the Land of Promise because of evil-doing there, but holding the promise of restoration and blessing ; <reference osisRef="ge 28:15">Genesis 28:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 30:1-10">Deuteronomy 30:1-10</reference>. To "an Israelite indeed" Christ speaks of Jacob's vision as to be fulfilled in the Son of man (cf) ; <reference osisRef="ge 28:12">Genesis 28:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:47-51">John 1:47-51</reference>.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen272" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Bethel</hi><div eID="gen272" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen273" type="x-p"/> i.e. the house of God. Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 35:7">Genesis 35:7</reference>. <div eID="gen273" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen274" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.28"/>
<div eID="gen274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen275" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="29" osisID="Gen.29" sID="Gen.29"/>

<hi type="bold">and came into the land</hi> <div eID="gen275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen276" type="x-p"/> Jacob at Haran becomes a sterling illustration, if not type, of the nation descended from him in its present long dispersion. Like Israel, he was:<div eID="gen276" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Out of the place of blessing <reference osisRef="ge 26:3">Genesis 26:3</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) without an altar <reference osisRef="ho 3:4 ho 3:5">Hosea 3:4,5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) gained an evil name <reference osisRef="ge 31:1">Genesis 31:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 2:17-24">Romans 2:17-24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) but was under the covenant care of Jehovah <reference osisRef="ge 28:13 ge 28:14">Genesis 28:13,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:1 ro 11:25-30">Romans 11:1,25-30</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) and was ultimately brought back <reference osisRef="ge 31:3">Genesis 31:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 35:1-4"> 35:1-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 37:21-23">Ezekiel 37:21-23</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen277" type="x-p"/> The personal lesson is obvious: while Jacob is not forsaken, he is permitted to reap the shame and sorrow of his self-chosen way. <chapter eID="Gen.29"/><div eID="gen277" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen278" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="31" osisID="Gen.31" sID="Gen.31"/>

<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen279" type="x-p"/> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Jegarsahadutha</hi><div eID="gen279" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen280" type="x-p"/> Chald, the heap of witness. <div eID="gen280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen281" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.31"/>
<div eID="gen281" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen282" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="32" osisID="Gen.32" sID="Gen.32"/>
<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen282" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen283" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Mahanaim</hi><div eID="gen283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen284" type="x-p"/> i.e. two hosts, or bands -- the visible band, Jacob and his servants; the invisible band, God's angels. Cf. <reference osisRef="2ki 6:13-17">2 Kings 6:13-17</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Edom</hi><div eID="gen284" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen285" type="x-p"/> i.e. Esau's country. <reference osisRef="ge 25:30">Genesis 25:30</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 36:1">Genesis 36:1</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">and there wrestled</hi><div eID="gen285" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen286" type="x-p"/> Jacob's crisis. Cf. <reference osisRef="jos 5:13-15">Joshua 5:13-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="job 42:5 job 42:6">Job 42:5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 6:1-8">Isaiah 6:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 1:4-9">Jeremiah 1:4-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 1:28">Ezekiel 1:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 2:1-7"> 2:1-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 10:1-12">Daniel 10:1-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:1-6">Acts 9:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:13-18">Revelation 1:13-18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">shall be no more called Jacob</hi><div eID="gen286" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen287" type="x-p"/> Both names are applied to the nation descended from Jacob. When used characteristically "Jacob" is the name for the natural posterity of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; "Israel" for the spiritual part of the nation. See <reference osisRef="isa 9:8">Isaiah 9:8</reference>. The "word" was sent to all the people, "Jacob," but it "lighted upon Israel," i.e. was comprehended by the spiritual part of the people. See "Israel" <reference osisRef="ge 12:2 ge 12:3">Genesis 12:2,3</reference>.<div eID="gen287" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen288" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:26">Romans 11:26</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.32"/><div eID="gen288" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen289" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="33" osisID="Gen.33" sID="Gen.33"/>

<hi type="bold">My lord</hi> <div eID="gen289" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen290" type="x-p"/> Not all at once does "Jacob" cease to dominate the walk of "Israel." Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 35:1-10">Genesis 35:1-10</reference> where the walk becomes according to the new name.
<hi type="bold">Shechem's</hi><div eID="gen290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen291" type="x-p"/> Called "Sychem," <reference osisRef="ac 7:16">Acts 7:16</reference>.

<hi type="bold">El-elohe-Israel</hi><div eID="gen291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen292" type="x-p"/> i.e. God, the God of Israel. Jacob's act of faith, appropriating his new name, but also claiming Elohim in this new sense as the God through whom alone he could walk according to his new name. See <reference osisRef="ge 14:18-23">Genesis 14:18-23</reference>.<div eID="gen292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen293" type="x-p"/> See note 2 of <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>")</hi> for a similar appropriation by Abraham. <div eID="gen293" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen294" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.33"/>
<div eID="gen294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen295" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="34" osisID="Gen.34" sID="Gen.34"/>

<hi type="bold">El-elohe-Israel</hi> <div eID="gen295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen296" type="x-p"/> i.e. God, the God of Israel. Jacob's act of faith, appropriating his new name, but also claiming Elohim in this new sense as the God through whom alone he could walk according to his new name. See <reference osisRef="ge 14:18-23">Genesis 14:18-23</reference>.<div eID="gen296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen297" type="x-p"/> See note 2 of <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>")</hi> for a similar appropriation by Abraham. <chapter eID="Gen.34"/><div eID="gen297" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen298" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="35" osisID="Gen.35" sID="Gen.35"/>

<hi type="bold">El-beth-el</hi> <div eID="gen298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen299" type="x-p"/> i.e. the God of Bethel. Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 28:19">Genesis 28:19</reference>. There it was the place as the scene of the ladder vision which impressed jacob. He called the place "Bethel," i.e. the house of God. Now it is the God of the place, rather than the place, and he calls it El-Bethel, i.e. "the God of the house of God." Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 33:20">Genesis 33:20</reference>.

<hi type="bold">drink offering</hi><div eID="gen299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen300" type="x-p"/> The first mention of the drink-offering. It is not mentioned among the Levitical offerings of Lev 1.-7., though included in the instructions for sacrifice in the land <reference osisRef="nu 15:5-7">Numbers 15:5-7</reference>. It was always "poured out," never drunk, and may be considered a type of Christ in the sense of ; <reference osisRef="ps 22:14">Psalms 22:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 53:12">Isaiah 53:12</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Benjamin</hi><div eID="gen300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen301" type="x-p"/> i.e. son of my right hand. Benjamin, "son of sorrow" to his mother, but "son of my right hand" to his father, becomes thus a double type of Christ. As Ben-oni He was the suffering One because of whom a sword pierced His mother's heart <reference osisRef="lu 2:35">Luke 2:35</reference> as Benjamin, head of the warrior tribe <reference osisRef="ge 49:27">Genesis 49:27</reference> firmly joined to Judah the kingly tribe ; <reference osisRef="ge 49:8-12">Genesis 49:8-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 12:21">1 Kings 12:21</reference> he becomes a type of the victorious One. It is noteworthy that Benjamin was especially honoured among the Gentiles <reference osisRef="ge 45:22">Genesis 45:22</reference>.<div eID="gen301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen302" type="x-p"/> So manifold are the distinctions of Christ that many personal types of Him are needed. Joseph is not complete, Benjamin standing only for Christ the sorrowful One <reference osisRef="isa 53:3 isa 53:4">Isaiah 53:3,4</reference> yet have power on earth. (Cf) <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 43:34">Genesis 43:34</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen302" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7"/><div sID="gen303" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.35"/>
<div eID="gen303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen304" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="36" osisID="Gen.36" sID="Gen.36"/>

<hi type="bold">Edom</hi> <div eID="gen304" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen305" type="x-p"/> Edom (called also "Seir,") <reference osisRef="ge 32:3">Genesis 32:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 36:8"> 36:8</reference> is the name of the country lying south of the ancient kingdom of Judah, and extending from the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Akaba. It includes the ruins of Petra, and is bounded on the north by Moab. Peopled by descendants of Esau <reference osisRef="ge 36:1-9">Genesis 36:1-9</reference>. Edom has a remarkable prominence in the prophetic word as (together with Moab) the scene of the final destruction of Gentile world-power in the day of the Lord. See "Armageddon" ; <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:21">Revelation 19:21</reference> and "Times of the Gentiles" ; <reference osisRef="lu 21:24">Luke 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>. Cf. ; <reference osisRef="ps 137:7">Psalms 137:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ob 1:8-16">Obadiah 1:8-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 34:1-8">Isaiah 34:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-6"> 63:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 49:14-22">Jeremiah 49:14-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 25:12-14">Ezekiel 25:12-14</reference>.
<hi type="bold">Amalek</hi><div eID="gen305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen306" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 17:8">Exodus 17:8</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Horite</hi><div eID="gen306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen307" type="x-p"/> Lit. Rock dweller.

<hi type="bold">kings that reigned in the land of Edom</hi><div eID="gen307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen308" type="x-p"/> It is characteristic of Scripture that the kings of Edom should be enumerated before the kings of Israel. The principle is stated in <reference osisRef="1co 15:46">1 Corinthians 15:46</reference>. First things are "natural," man's best, and always fail; second things are "spiritual," God's things, and succeed. Adam--Christ; Cain--Abel; Cain's posterity--Seth's posterity; Saul--David; Israel--the true Church, etc. <chapter eID="Gen.36"/><div eID="gen308" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen309" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="37" osisID="Gen.37" sID="Gen.37"/>

<hi type="bold">Joseph</hi> <div eID="gen309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen310" type="x-p"/> While it is nowhere asserted that Joseph was a type of Christ, the analogies are too numerous to be accidental. They are:<div eID="gen310" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) both were especial objects of a father's love <reference osisRef="ge 37:3">Genesis 37:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 3:17">Matthew 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:35">John 3:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:20"> 5:20</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) both were hated by their brethren <reference osisRef="ge 37:4">Genesis 37:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:25">John 15:25</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the superior claims of both were rejected by their brethren <reference osisRef="ge 37:8">Genesis 37:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:37-39">Matthew 21:37-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:24 joh 15:25">John 15:24,25</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the brethren of both conspired against them to slay them <reference osisRef="ge 37:18">Genesis 37:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:3 mt 26:4">Matthew 26:3,4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Joseph was, in intent and figure, slain by his brethren, as was Christ <reference osisRef="ge 37:24">Genesis 37:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 27:35-37">Matthew 27:35-37</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) each became a blessing among the Gentiles, and gained a Gentile bride <reference osisRef="ge 41:1-45">Genesis 41:1-45</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14">Acts 15:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-32">Ephesians 5:25-32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) as Joseph reconciled his brethren to himself, and afterward exalted them, so will it be with Christ and His Jewish brethren <reference osisRef="ge 45:1-15">Genesis 45:1-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 30:1-10">Deuteronomy 30:1-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 2:14-18">Hosea 2:14-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:1 ro 11:15 ro 11:25 ro 11:26">Romans 11:1,15,25,26</reference>. </item> </list>

"Sheol," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5">Habakkuk 2:5</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.37"/><div eID="gen312" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen313" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="41" osisID="Gen.41" sID="Gen.41"/>

<hi type="bold">Zaphnath-paaneah</hi> <div eID="gen313" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen314" type="x-p"/> Asenath, the Gentile bride espoused by Joseph the rejected one <reference osisRef="joh 19:15">John 19:15</reference> type of the Church, called out from the Gentiles to be the bride of Christ during the time of His rejection by His brethren, Israel. ; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14">Acts 15:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:31 eph 5:32">Ephesians 5:31,32</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 37:2">Genesis 37:2</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen315" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Zaphnath-paaneah</hi> Coptic, revealer of secret things. <chapter eID="Gen.41"/><div eID="gen315" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen316" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="42" osisID="Gen.42" sID="Gen.42"/>

<hi type="bold">famine</hi> <div eID="gen316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen317" type="x-p"/> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:10">Genesis 12:10</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">fear</hi><div eID="gen317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen318" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grave</hi><div eID="gen318" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen319" type="x-p"/> Heb. "Sheol," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5">Habakkuk 2:5</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen319" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8"/><div sID="gen320" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.42"/>
<div eID="gen320" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen321" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="43" osisID="Gen.43" sID="Gen.43"/>
<hi type="bold">famine</hi> <div eID="gen321" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen322" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:10">Genesis 12:10</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">But Benjamin's mess</hi><div eID="gen322" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen323" type="x-p"/> Cf. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 35:18">Genesis 35:18</reference>")</hi>. It is important to observe that Benjamin now becomes prominent. Joseph is peculiarly the type of Christ in His first advent, rejection, death, resurrection, and present exaltation among the Gentiles, but unrecognized of Israel. As the greater Benjamin, "Son of sorrow," but also "Son of my right hand," He is to be revealed in power in the Kingdom <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>". It is then, and not till then, that Israel is to be restored and converted. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>". Typically <reference osisRef="ge 45:1 ge 45:2">Genesis 45:1,2</reference> anticipates the revelation prophetically described, ; <reference osisRef="eze 20:33-36">Ezekiel 20:33-36</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 2:14-23">Hosea 2:14-23</reference> at which time the Benjamin type of Christ will be fulfilled. <div eID="gen323" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8"/><div sID="gen324" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.43"/>
<div eID="gen324" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen325" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="44" osisID="Gen.44" sID="Gen.44"/>

<hi type="bold">But Benjamin's mess</hi> <div eID="gen325" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen326" type="x-p"/> Cf. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 35:18">Genesis 35:18</reference>")</hi>. It is important to observe that Benjamin now becomes prominent. Joseph is peculiarly the type of Christ in His first advent, rejection, death, resurrection, and present exaltation among the Gentiles, but unrecognized of Israel. As the greater Benjamin, "Son of sorrow," but also "Son of my right hand," He is to be revealed in power in the Kingdom <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>". It is then, and not till then, that Israel is to be restored and converted. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>". Typically <reference osisRef="ge 45:1 ge 45:2">Genesis 45:1,2</reference> anticipates the revelation prophetically described, ; <reference osisRef="eze 20:33-36">Ezekiel 20:33-36</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 2:14-23">Hosea 2:14-23</reference> at which time the Benjamin type of Christ will be fulfilled.
<hi type="bold">grave</hi> Heb. Sheol, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5">Habakkuk 2:5</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.44"/><div eID="gen326" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen327" type="x-p"/><chapter n="45" osisID="Gen.45" sID="Gen.45"/>

<hi type="bold">preserve</hi> Heb. to make you a remnant. <reference osisRef="isa 1:9">Isaiah 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.45"/><div eID="gen327" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen328" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="46" osisID="Gen.46" sID="Gen.46"/>

<hi type="bold">I am God</hi> <div eID="gen328" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen329" type="x-p"/> It is important to distinguish between the directive and the permissive will of God. In the first sense the place for the covenant family was Canaan <reference osisRef="ge 26:1-5">Genesis 26:1-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 46:3">Genesis 46:3</reference> is a touching instance of the permissive will of God. Jacob's family, broken, and in part already in Egypt, the tenderness of Jehovah would not forbid the aged patriarch to follow. God will take up His people and, so far as possible, bless them, even when they are out of His best. In Israel's choice of a king <reference osisRef="1sa 8:7-9">1 Samuel 8:7-9</reference> in the turning back from Kadesh <reference osisRef="de 1:19-22">Deuteronomy 1:19-22</reference> in the sending of the spies; in the case of Balaam--illustrations of this principle are seen. It is needless to say that God's permissive will never extends to things morally wrong. The highest blessing is ever found in obedience to His directive will.

<hi type="bold">All the souls</hi><div eID="gen329" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen330" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="ge 46:27">Genesis 46:27</reference>. A discrepancy has been imagined. The "souls" that came with Jacob" were 66. The "souls of the house of Jacob" <reference osisRef="ge 46:27">Genesis 46:27</reference> i.e. the entire Jacobean family) were 70, viz. the 66 which came with Jacob, Joseph and his two sons, already in Egypt=69; Jacob himself=70. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 7:14">Acts 7:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.46"/><div eID="gen330" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen331" type="x-p"/><chapter n="47" osisID="Gen.47" sID="Gen.47"/>
<hi type="bold">whole age</hi> Or, days of the years of his life. <chapter eID="Gen.47"/><div eID="gen331" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen332" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="48" osisID="Gen.48" sID="Gen.48"/>

<hi type="bold">Angel</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen332" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen333" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">redeemed</hi> Heb. goel, Redemp. (Kinsman type). <reference osisRef="isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.48"/><div eID="gen333" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen334" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="49" osisID="Gen.49" sID="Gen.49"/>

<hi type="bold">blessed them</hi> <div eID="gen334" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen335" type="x-p"/> Jacob's life, ending in serenity and blessing, testifies to the power of God to transform character. His spiritual progress has six notable phases:<div eID="gen335" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the first exercise of faith, as shown in the purchase of the birthright <reference osisRef="ge 25:28-34">Genesis 25:28-34</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 27:10-22"> 27:10-22</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the vision at bethel <reference osisRef="ge 28:10-19">Genesis 28:10-19</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) walking in the flesh <reference osisRef="ge 29:1-ge 31:55">Genesis 29:1-31:55</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the transforming experience <reference osisRef="ge 32:24-31">Genesis 32:24-31</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the return to Bethel: idols put away <reference osisRef="ge 35:1-7">Genesis 35:1-7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the walk of faith <reference osisRef="ge 37:1-ge 49:33">Genesis 37:1-49:33</reference>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8"/><div sID="gen336" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gen.49"/>
<div eID="gen336" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen337" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="50" osisID="Gen.50" sID="Gen.50"/>

<hi type="bold">buried</hi> <div eID="gen337" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen338" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 23:4">Genesis 23:4</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gen.50"/><div eID="gen338" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2" osisID="Gen" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Exod" sID="gen339" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Exod.1" sID="Exod.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Exodus</title> <div sID="gen340" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ex 1">Read first chapter of Exodus</reference><div eID="gen340" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen341" type="x-p"/> EXODUS, "going out," records the redemption out of Egyptian bondage of the descendants of Abraham, and sets forth, in type, all redemption. It is therefore peculiarly the book of redemption. But as all redemption is unto a relationship with God of which worship, fellowship, and service are expressions, so Exodus, in the giving of the law and the provisions of sacrifice and priesthood, becomes not only the book of redemption, but also, in type, of the conditions upon which all relationships with God exist.<div eID="gen341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen342" type="x-p"/> Broadly, the book teaches that redemption is essential to any relationship with a holy God; and that even a redeemed people cannot have fellowship with Him unless constantly cleaned of defilement.<div eID="gen342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen343" type="x-p"/> In EXODUS, God, hitherto connected with the Israelitish people only through His covenant with Abraham, brings them to himself nationally through redemption, puts them under the Mosaic Covenant, and dwells among them in the cloud of glory. Galatians explains the relation of the law to the Abrahamic Covenant. In the Commandments God taught Israel His just demands. Experience under the Commandments convicted Israel of sin; and the provision of priesthood and sacrifice (filled with precious types of Christ) gave a guilty people a way of forgiveness, cleansing, restoration to fellowship, and worship.<div eID="gen343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen344" type="x-p"/> Exodus falls into three chief divisions:<div eID="gen344" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Israel in Egypt (1-15.)</item> <item type="x-indent-1">From the Red Sea to Sinai (16-18.)</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Israel at Sinai (19:40.)</item> </list> <div sID="gen345" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in Exodus cover a period of 216 years (Ussher). <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8"/><hi type="bold">feared</hi><div eID="gen345" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen346" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Exod.1"/><div eID="gen346" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen347" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Exod.2" sID="Exod.2"/>

<hi type="bold">son</hi> <div eID="gen347" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen348" type="x-p"/> Moses, type of Christ the Deliverer <reference osisRef="isa 61:1">Isaiah 61:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 4:18">Luke 4:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 1:10">2 Corinthians 1:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 1:10">1 Thessalonians 1:10</reference>.<div eID="gen348" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) A divinely chosen deliverer <reference osisRef="ex 3:7-10">Exodus 3:7-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 7:25">Acts 7:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Rejected by Israel he turns to the Gentiles <reference osisRef="ex 2:11-15">Exodus 2:11-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 7:25">Acts 7:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 18:5 ac 18:6"> 18:5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 28:17-28"> 28:17-28</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) During his rejection he gains a Gentile bride <reference osisRef="ex 2:16-21">Exodus 2:16-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 12:14-21">Matthew 12:14-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 11:2">2 Corinthians 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:30-32">Ephesians 5:30-32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Afterward he again appears as Israel's deliverer, and is accepted <reference osisRef="ex 4:29-31">Exodus 4:29-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:14-26">Romans 11:14-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Officially, Moses typifies Christ as Prophet <reference osisRef="ac 3:22 ac 3:23">Acts 3:22,23</reference>. Advocate ; <reference osisRef="ex 32:31-35">Exodus 32:31-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:1 1jo 2:2">1 John 2:1,2,</reference> Intercessor ; <reference osisRef="ex 17:1-6">Exodus 17:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:25">Hebrews 7:25</reference> and Leader, or King ; <reference osisRef="de 33:4 de 33:5">Deuteronomy 33:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 55:4">Isaiah 55:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:10">Hebrews 2:10</reference> while, in relation to the house of God, he is in contrast with Christ. Moses was faithful as a servant over another's house; Christ as a Son over His own house <reference osisRef="heb 3:5 heb 3:6">Hebrews 3:5,6</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9"/><div sID="gen349" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9"/> <hi type="bold">Reuel</hi> <div eID="gen349" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen350" type="x-p"/> Called Raguel. <reference osisRef="nu 10:29">Numbers 10:29</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.2"/><div eID="gen350" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen351" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Exod.3" sID="Exod.3"/>
<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen352" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">borrow</hi> The use of little things. Cf. <reference osisRef="jud 3:31">Judges 3:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 17:12-16">1 Kings 17:12-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:9">John 6:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:25-31">1 Corinthians 1:25-31</reference> <div eID="gen352" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10"/><div sID="gen353" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.3"/>
<div eID="gen353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen354" type="x-p"/><chapter n="4" osisID="Exod.4" sID="Exod.4"/>

<hi type="bold">borrow</hi> The use of little things. Cf. <reference osisRef="jud 3:31">Judges 3:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 17:12-16">1 Kings 17:12-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:9">John 6:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:25-31">1 Corinthians 1:25-31</reference>

<hi type="bold">rod</hi> Sign of the rod = power <reference osisRef="ps 110:2">Psalms 110:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 2:9"> 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 2:27">Revelation 2:27</reference>. It was Moses' shepherd's crook, the tool of his calling. Cast down, it became a serpent; taken up in faith, it became "the rod of God" ; <reference osisRef="ex 4:20">Exodus 4:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 7:12"> 7:12</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 7:12">Exodus 7:12</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Put now thine hand</hi><div eID="gen354" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen355" type="x-p"/> The sign of leprosy. The heart ("bosom") stands for what we are, the hand for what we do. What we are, that ultimately we do. It is a sign of <reference osisRef="lu 6:43-45">Luke 6:43-45</reference>. The two signs, rod and hand, speak of preparation for service:<div eID="gen355" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) consecration--our capacity taken up for God;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the hand that holds the rod of God's power must be a cleansed hand swayed by a new heart. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10"/><div sID="gen356" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10"/> <hi type="bold">Aaron the Levite</hi> <div eID="gen356" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen357" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="ex 28:1">Exodus 28:1</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 28:1">Exodus 28:1</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen357" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11"/><div sID="gen358" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11"/> <hi type="bold">harden his heart</hi> <div eID="gen358" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen359" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="ex 8:15 ex 8:32">Exodus 8:15,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 9:34"> 9:34</reference>. In the face of the righteous demand of Jehovah and of the tremendous attestations by miracle that He was indeed God, and that Moses and Aaron were His representatives, Pharaoh "hardened his heart." Instrumentally God hardened Pharaoh's heart by forcing him to an issue against which he hardened his own heart in refusal. Light rejected, rightful obedience refused, inevitably hardens conscience and heart. <reference osisRef="ro 9:17-24">Romans 9:17-24</reference>.

<hi type="bold">kill him</hi><div eID="gen359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen360" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="ge 17:14">Genesis 17:14</reference> The context (<reference osisRef="ge 4:25">Genesis 4:25</reference>) interprets v. 25. Moses was forgetful of the very foundation sign of Israel's covenant relation to Jehovah. On the eve of delivering Israel he was thus reminded that without circumcision an Israelite was cut off from the covenant. <reference osisRef="jos 5:3-9">Joshua 5:3-9</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.4"/><div eID="gen360" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen361" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Exod.5" sID="Exod.5"/>

<hi type="bold">Let my people</hi> <div eID="gen361" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen362" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 4:22 ex 4:23">Exodus 4:22,23</reference>. Possibly Moses and Aaron shrank from delivering the message concerning the firstborn.

<hi type="bold">three days</hi> Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 12:38-40">Matthew 12:38-40</reference>. By death and resurrection will God have his people separated from Egypt -- the world. ; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1-11">Romans 6:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:14-15">Galatians 6:14-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 13:12 heb 13:13">Hebrews 13:12,13</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.5"/><div eID="gen362" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen363" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="Exod.6" sID="Exod.6"/>

<hi type="bold">redeem</hi> <div eID="gen363" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen364" type="x-p"/> Heb. "goel," Redemp. (Kinsman type). See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi> <chapter eID="Exod.6"/><div eID="gen364" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen365" type="x-p"/><chapter n="7" osisID="Exod.7" sID="Exod.7"/>

<hi type="bold">when</hi> A prophetic sign also. The nations shall know Jehovah when He restores and blesses Israel in the kingdom. <reference osisRef="isa 2:1-3">Isaiah 2:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-isa 1214:1"> 11:10-1214:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 60:4 isa 60:5"> 60:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 37:28">Ezekiel 37:28</reference>.

<hi type="bold">like</hi> CF. <reference osisRef="2ti 3:8">2 Timothy 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 8:18">Exodus 8:18</reference><div eID="gen365" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen366" type="x-p"/> Neither Satan nor his tools can create life: <reference osisRef="re 13:15">Revelation 13:15</reference> will be a "lying wonder": <reference osisRef="2th 2:9">2 Thessalonians 2:9</reference>

<hi type="bold">Aaron's rod</hi><div eID="gen366" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(Cf) <reference osisRef="ex 4:2">Exodus 4:2</reference> As Moses' rod was the rod of power, the rod of the King <reference osisRef="de 33:4 de 33:5">Deuteronomy 33:4,5</reference> so Aaron's was the rod of life, the rod of the Priest. As here the serpents, symbols of Satan, who had the power of death ; <reference osisRef="re 12:9">Revelation 12:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:14">Hebrews 2:14</reference> are swallowed up, so in resurrection death will be "swallowed up in victory" ; <reference osisRef="1co 15:54">1 Corinthians 15:54</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 17:8">Numbers 17:8</reference>. </item> </list> <chapter eID="Exod.7"/>
<div sID="gen367" type="x-p"/><chapter n="8" osisID="Exod.8" sID="Exod.8"/>

<hi type="bold">division</hi> Heb. peduth, trans. "reemption."<div eID="gen367" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen368" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ps 111:9">Psalms 111:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 130:7"> 130:7</reference>. It is, in type, <reference osisRef="ga 6:14">Galatians 6:14</reference>.

<hi type="bold">in the land</hi><div eID="gen368" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen369" type="x-p"/> The compromises proposed by Pharaoh are those urged upon Christians today. The first says in effect: "Be a Christian if you will, but not a 'narrow' one-- stay in Egypt." Invariably it ends in world-conformity, world-pleasing, and seeking the world's money for God <reference osisRef="ps 50:9-17">Psalms 50:9-17</reference> (Cf) ; <reference osisRef="2co 6:14-18">2 Corinthians 6:14-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 1:4">Galatians 1:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">very far</hi> The second compromise is a modification merely of the first. "Do not be too unwordly." Cf. <reference osisRef="1sa 15:3 1sa 15:9 1sa 15:13-15 1sa 15:19-23">1 Samuel 15:3,9,13-15,19-23</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.8"/><div eID="gen369" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen370" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="10" osisID="Exod.10" sID="Exod.10"/>

<hi type="bold">ye that are</hi> <div eID="gen370" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen371" type="x-p"/> The third compromise proposed by Pharaoh is, perhaps, as applied to believers, the sublest and most successful of them all. The most godly parents desire worldly prosperity and position for their children. <reference osisRef="mt 20:20 mt 20:21">Matthew 20:20,21</reference>.

<hi type="bold">said, Go ye</hi><div eID="gen371" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen372" type="x-p"/> i.e. "Leave your property in the world." Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 16:25-27">Matthew 16:25-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:18-25">Luke 18:18-25</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.10"/><div eID="gen372" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen373" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="12" osisID="Exod.12" sID="Exod.12"/>
<hi type="bold">first month</hi> <div eID="gen373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen374" type="x-p"/> i.e. April.

<hi type="bold">passover</hi><div eID="gen374" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen375" type="x-p"/> The Passover, type of Christ our Redeemer <reference osisRef="ex 12:1-28">Exodus 12:1-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:29">John 1:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 5:6 1co 5:7">1 Corinthians 5:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:18 1pe 1:19">1 Peter 1:18,19</reference>.<div eID="gen375" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The lamb must be without blemish, and to test this it was kept up for four days <reference osisRef="ex 12:5 ex 12:6">Exodus 12:5,6</reference>. So our Lord's public life, under hostile scrutiny, was the testing which proved his holiness ; <reference osisRef="lu 11:53 lu 11:54">Luke 11:53,54</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:46">John 8:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:38"> 18:38</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The Lamb thus tested must be slain <reference osisRef="ex 12:6">Exodus 12:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:24">John 12:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The blood must be applied <reference osisRef="ex 12:7">Exodus 12:7</reference> This answers to appropriation by personal faith, and refutes universalism <reference osisRef="joh 3:36">John 3:36</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The blood thus applied of itself, without anything, constituted a perfect protection from judgment <reference osisRef="ex 12:13">Exodus 12:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 1:7">1 John 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:10 heb 10:14">Hebrews 10:10,14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The feast typified Christ as the bread of life, answering to the memorial supper. <reference osisRef="mt 26:26-28">Matthew 26:26-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:23-26">1 Corinthians 11:23-26</reference>. To observe the feast was a duty and privilege, but not a condition of safety. As a matter of fact, the bread was not eaten by the Israelites on the night in which, nevertheless, they were preserved from the judgment upon the firstborn. <reference osisRef="ex 12:34-39">Exodus 12:34-39</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12"/><div sID="gen376" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12"/> <hi type="bold">mixed</hi> <div eID="gen376" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen377" type="x-p"/> This mixed multitude, standing for unconverted church-members, was a source of weakness and division, then as now <reference osisRef="nu 11:4-6">Numbers 11:4-6</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Nu 11:4">Numbers 11:4</reference>")</hi>. There had been a manifestation of divine power, and men were drawn to it without change of heart. CF. <reference osisRef="lu 14:25-27">Luke 14:25-27</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.12"/><div eID="gen377" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen378" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="13" osisID="Exod.13" sID="Exod.13"/>
<hi type="bold">Abib</hi> <div eID="gen378" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen379" type="x-p"/> First month, i.e. April.
<hi type="bold">firstling</hi><div eID="gen379" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen380" type="x-p"/> The redemption of firstlings made a memorial sign to Israel of their own redemption.

<hi type="bold">Thus the Lord saved Israel</hi><div eID="gen383" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen384" type="x-p"/> Redemption: (Exodus type) Summary. Exodus is the book of redemption and teaches:<div eID="gen384" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) redemption is wholly of God <reference osisRef="ex 3:7 ex 3:8">Exodus 3:7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) redemption is through a person. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 2:2">Exodus 2:2</reference>")</hi>. <reference osisRef="joh 3:16 joh 3:17">John 3:16,17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) redemption is by blood <reference osisRef="ex 12:13 ex 12:23 ex 12:27">Exodus 12:13,23,27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:18">1 Peter 1:18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) redemption is by power <reference osisRef="ex 6:6">Exodus 6:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 13:14"> 13:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:2">Romans 8:2</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen385" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>".<div eID="gen385" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen386" type="x-p"/> The blood of Christ redeems the believer from the guilt and penalty of sin. <reference osisRef="1pe 1:18">1 Peter 1:18</reference> as the power of the Spirit delivers from the dominion of sin. ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:2">Romans 8:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:2">Ephesians 2:2</reference>.

<hi type="bold">feared</hi><div eID="gen386" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen387" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen387" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13"/><div sID="gen388" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.14"/>
