<hi type="bold">redeemed</hi><div eID="gen390" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen391" type="x-p"/> Heb. "gaal," Redemp. (Kinsman type). <reference osisRef="isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">when he had cast into the waters</hi><div eID="gen391" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen392" type="x-p"/> These bitter waters were in the very path of the Lord's leading, and stand for the trials of God's people, which are educatory and not punitive. The "tree" is the cross <reference osisRef="ga 3:13">Galatians 3:13</reference> which became sweet to Christ as the expression of the Father's will <reference osisRef="joh 18:11">John 18:11</reference>. When our Marahs are so taken we cast the "tree" into the waters. <reference osisRef="ro 5:3 ro 5:4">Romans 5:3,4</reference>. <div eID="gen392" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13"/><div sID="gen393" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.15"/>
<div eID="gen393" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen394" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="16" osisID="Exod.16" sID="Exod.16"/>
<hi type="bold">second month</hi> <div eID="gen394" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen395" type="x-p"/> i.e. May.
<hi type="bold">manna</hi><div eID="gen395" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen396" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 16:35">Exodus 16:35</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">according</hi><div eID="gen396" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen397" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 6:33">John 6:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:41 joh 6:42 joh 6:52"> 6:41,42,52</reference>. Christ gives himself unreservedly, but we have no more of Him than faith appropriates, ; <reference osisRef="ex 16:18 ex 16:2">Exodus 16:18,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 1:1">Joshua 1:1</reference>. <reference osisRef="ex 16:2">Exodus 16:2</reference> is our title. <reference osisRef="ex 16:3">Exodus 16:3</reference> is the law of possession:

<hi type="bold">left</hi><div eID="gen397" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen398" type="x-p"/> As we are not nourished by the memory of food, so neither can spirituality be sustained on past appropriations of Christ.

<hi type="bold">manna</hi><div eID="gen398" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen399" type="x-p"/> Manna, type of Christ as the "bread of life," come down from heaven to die "for the life of the world." <reference osisRef="joh 6:35 joh 6:48-51">John 6:35,48-51</reference>. A "small" thing <reference osisRef="ex 16:14">Exodus 16:14</reference> having but the taste of "fresh oil." <reference osisRef="nu 11:8">Numbers 11:8</reference> or "wafers with honey" <reference osisRef="ex 16:31">Exodus 16:31,</reference> it typifies Christ in humiliation as presented in Matthew, Mark, and Luke; "having no form nor comeliness;... no beauty that we should desire him" <reference osisRef="isa 53:2">Isaiah 53:2</reference>. But as such He must be received by faith if we would be saved <reference osisRef="joh 6:53-58">John 6:53-58</reference>. To meditate upon Christ as He went about among men, doing not His own will but the will of the Father <reference osisRef="joh 6:38-40">John 6:38-40</reference> is to feed on the manna. This is, of necessity, the spiritual food of young believers, and answers to "milk" <reference osisRef="1co 3:1 1co 3:2">1 Corinthians 3:1,2</reference>.<div eID="gen399" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen400" type="x-p"/> But Christ in glory, and the believer's present and eternal association with Him there, answers to "the old corn of the land" <reference osisRef="jos 5:11">Joshua 5:11</reference> the "meat" of <reference osisRef="heb 5:13 heb 5:14">Hebrews 5:13,14</reference> or Christ as presented in the Epistles of Paul. (Cf) <reference osisRef="2co 5:16">2 Corinthians 5:16</reference>. <chapter eID="Exod.16"/><div eID="gen400" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen401" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="17" osisID="Exod.17" sID="Exod.17"/>

<hi type="bold">rock</hi> <div eID="gen401" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen402" type="x-p"/> The rock, type of life through the Spirit by grace:<div eID="gen402" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Christ the Rock <reference osisRef="1co 10:4">1 Corinthians 10:4</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The people utterly unworthy <reference osisRef="ex 17:2">Exodus 17:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:1-6">Ephesians 2:1-6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Characteristics of life through grace: </item> </list> <chapter eID="Exod.17"/>
<chapter n="18" osisID="Exod.18" sID="Exod.18"/> <div sID="gen403" type="x-p"/>
<hi type="bold">Eliezer</hi> <div eID="gen403" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen404" type="x-p"/> i.e. God is help.

<hi type="bold">Hearken now unto my voice</hi><div eID="gen404" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen405" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="nu 11:14-17">Numbers 11:14-17</reference>. Jehovah entirely ignored this worldly-wise organization, substituting His own order.

<hi type="bold">fear</hi><div eID="gen405" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen406" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen406" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13"/><div sID="gen407" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.18"/>
<div eID="gen407" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen408" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="19" osisID="Exod.19" sID="Exod.19"/>

<hi type="bold">In the third month</hi> <div eID="gen408" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen409" type="x-p"/> At Sinai Israel learned the lessons:<div eID="gen409" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) of the holiness of Jehovah through the Commandments;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of their own sinfulness and weakness through failure;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) and of the goodness of Jehovah through the provision of priesthood and sacrifice. The Christian learns through the experience of <reference osisRef="ro 7:7-24">Romans 7:7-24</reference> what Israel learned at Sinai. This division of Exodus should be read in light of ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:19-27">Romans 3:19-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 7:7-24"> 7:7-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-3">Galatians 4:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:6-25">Galatians 3:6-25</reference> explains the relation of the law to the Abrahamic Covenant:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the law cannot disannul that covenant;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) it was "added" to convict of sin;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) it was a child-leader unto Christ;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) it was but preparatory discipline "till the Seed should come."</item> </list> <div sID="gen410" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">third month</hi> i.e. June.

<hi type="bold">Thus shalt thou say</hi><div eID="gen410" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen411" type="x-p"/> It is exceedingly important to observe:<div eID="gen411" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) that Jehovah reminded the people that hitherto they had been the objects of His free grace;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) that the law is not proposed as a means of life, but as a means by which Israel might become "a peculiar treasure" and a "kingdom of priests";</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) that the law was not imposed until it had been proposed and voluntarily accepted. The principle is stated in <reference osisRef="ga 5:1-4">Galatians 5:1-4</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen412" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301181<div eID="gen412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen413" type="x-p"/> Additional Factors to Consider See Topic 301321 <div eID="gen413" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13"/><div sID="gen414" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13"/> <hi type="bold">if ye will obey</hi> <div eID="gen414" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen415" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:6">Revelation 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 5:10"> 5:10</reference>. What, under law, was condition, is under grace, freely given to every believer. The "if" of <reference osisRef="ex 19:5">Exodus 19:5</reference> is the essence of law as a method of divine dealing, and the fundamental reason why "the law made nothing perfect" ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:3">Romans 8:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:18 heb 7:19">Hebrews 7:18,19</reference>.<div eID="gen415" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen416" type="x-p"/> The Abrahamic: <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi> and<div eID="gen416" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen417" type="x-p"/> New <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen418" type="x-p"/> covenants minister salvation and assurance because they impose but one condition, faith.

<hi type="bold">we will do</hi><div eID="gen418" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen419" type="x-p"/> The Fifth Dispensation: Law. This dispensation extends from Sinai to Calvary--from Exodus to the Cross. The history of Israel in the wilderness and in the land is one long record of the violation of the law. The testing of the nation by law ended in the judgment of the Captivities, but the dispensation itself ended at the Cross.<div eID="gen419" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Man's state at the beginning <reference osisRef="ex 19:1-4">Exodus 19:1-4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) His responsibility <reference osisRef="ex 19:5 ex 19:6">Exodus 19:5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:5">Romans 10:5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) His failure <reference osisRef="2ki 17:7-17 2ki 17:19">2 Kings 17:7-17,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:22 ac 2:23">Acts 2:22,23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The judgment <reference osisRef="2ki 17:1-6 2ki 17:20">2 Kings 17:1-6,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 25:1-11"> 25:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference></item> </list> <div sID="gen420" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301180<div eID="gen420" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen421" type="x-p"/> See, for the other six dispensations: INNOCENCE (<reference osisRef="ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>); CONSCIENCE (<reference osisRef="ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>); HUMAN GOVERNMENT (<reference osisRef="ge 8:20">Genesis 8:20</reference>); PROMISE (<reference osisRef="ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>); GRACE (<reference osisRef="joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>); KINGDOM (<reference osisRef="eph 1:10">Eph 1:10</reference>)<div eID="gen421" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen422" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>". See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>". See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>". See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>". See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>". <div eID="gen422" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14"/><div sID="gen423" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14"/> <hi type="bold">So Moses</hi> <div eID="gen423" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen424" type="x-p"/> The Mosaic Covenant,<div eID="gen424" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) given to Israel</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) in three divisions, each essential to the others, and together forming the Mosaic Covenant, viz.: the Commandments, expressing the righteous will of God <reference osisRef="ex 20:1-26">Exodus 20:1-26</reference> the "judgments," governing the social life of Israel ; <reference osisRef="ex 21:1">Exodus 21:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 24:11"> 24:11</reference> and the "ordinances," governing the religious life of Israel ; <reference osisRef="ex 24:12">Exodus 24:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 31:18"> 31:18</reference>. These three elements form "the law," as that phrase is generically used in the New Testament (e.g.) <reference osisRef="mt 5:17 mt 5:18">Matthew 5:17,18</reference>. The Commandments and the ordinances formed one religious system. The Commandments were a "ministry of condemnation" and of "death" <reference osisRef="2co 3:7-9">2 Corinthians 3:7-9</reference> the ordinances gave, in the high priest, a representative of the people with Jehovah; and in the sacrifices a "cover" (see "Atonement," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 16:6">Leviticus 16:6</reference>")</hi> for their sins in anticipation of the Cross ; <reference osisRef="heb 5:1-3">Hebrews 5:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:6-9"> 9:6-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:25 ro 3:26">Romans 3:25,26</reference>. The Christian is not under the conditional Mosaic Covenant of works, the law, but under the unconditional New Covenant of grace. ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:21-27">Romans 3:21-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:14 ro 6:15"> 6:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:16">Galatians 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:10-14 ga 3:16-18 ga 3:24-26">Galatians 3:10-14,16-18,24-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:21-31"> 4:21-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:11-17">Hebrews 10:11-17</reference>. See NEW COVENANT.</item> </list> <div sID="gen425" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen425" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen426" type="x-p"/> See,for the other seven covenants:<div eID="gen426" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen427" type="x-p"/> EDENIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi> ; ADAMIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>"; NOAHIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>"; ABRAHAMIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>"; PALESTINIAN See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>"; DAVIDIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>"; NEW See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Heb 8:8</reference>". <div eID="gen427" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15"/><div sID="gen428" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.19"/>
<div eID="gen428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen429" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="20" osisID="Exod.20" sID="Exod.20"/>

<hi type="bold">So Moses</hi> <div eID="gen429" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen430" type="x-p"/> The Mosaic Covenant,<div eID="gen430" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) given to Israel</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) in three divisions, each essential to the others, and together forming the Mosaic Covenant, viz.: the Commandments, expressing the righteous will of God <reference osisRef="ex 20:1-26">Exodus 20:1-26</reference> the "judgments," governing the social life of Israel ; <reference osisRef="ex 21:1">Exodus 21:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 24:11"> 24:11</reference> and the "ordinances," governing the religious life of Israel ; <reference osisRef="ex 24:12">Exodus 24:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 31:18"> 31:18</reference>. These three elements form "the law," as that phrase is generically used in the New Testament (e.g.) <reference osisRef="mt 5:17 mt 5:18">Matthew 5:17,18</reference>. The Commandments and the ordinances formed one religious system. The Commandments were a "ministry of condemnation" and of "death" <reference osisRef="2co 3:7-9">2 Corinthians 3:7-9</reference> the ordinances gave, in the high priest, a representative of the people with Jehovah; and in the sacrifices a "cover" (see "Atonement," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 16:6">Leviticus 16:6</reference>")</hi> for their sins in anticipation of the Cross ; <reference osisRef="heb 5:1-3">Hebrews 5:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:6-9"> 9:6-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:25 ro 3:26">Romans 3:25,26</reference>. The Christian is not under the conditional Mosaic Covenant of works, the law, but under the unconditional New Covenant of grace. ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:21-27">Romans 3:21-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:14 ro 6:15"> 6:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:16">Galatians 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:10-14 ga 3:16-18 ga 3:24-26">Galatians 3:10-14,16-18,24-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:21-31"> 4:21-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:11-17">Hebrews 10:11-17</reference>. See NEW COVENANT.</item> </list> <div sID="gen431" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen431" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen432" type="x-p"/> See,for the other seven covenants:<div eID="gen432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen433" type="x-p"/> EDENIC <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi> ; ADAMIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>"; NOAHIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>"; ABRAHAMIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>"; PALESTINIAN See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>"; DAVIDIC See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>"; NEW See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Heb 8:8</reference>".

<hi type="bold">shalt not make</hi><div eID="gen433" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen434" type="x-p"/> There is a threefold giving of the law. First, orally, in <reference osisRef="ex 20:1-17">Exodus 20:1-17</reference>. This was pure law, with no provision of priesthood and sacrifice for failure, and was accompanied by the "judgments" ; <reference osisRef="ex 21:1-ex 23:13">Exodus 21:1-23:13</reference>; relating to the relations of Hebrew with Hebrew; to which were added <reference osisRef="ex 23:14-19">Exodus 23:14-19</reference> directions for keeping three annual feasts, and <reference osisRef="ex 23:20-33">Exodus 23:20-33</reference> instructions for the conquest of Canaan. These words Moses communicated to the people. <reference osisRef="ex 24:3-8">Exodus 24:3-8</reference>. Immediately, in the persons of their elders, they were admitted to the fellowship of God. <reference osisRef="ex 24:9-11">Exodus 24:9-11</reference>.<div eID="gen434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen435" type="x-p"/> Second, Moses was then called up to receive the tables of stone. <reference osisRef="ex 24:12-18">Exodus 24:12-18</reference>. The story then divides. Moses, in the mount, receives the gracious instructions concerning the tabernacle, priesthood, and sacrifice (Ex 25.-31.) Meantime (Ex 32.), the people, led by Aaron, break the first commandment. Moses, returning, breaks the tables "written with the finger of God." ; <reference osisRef="ex 31:18">Exodus 31:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 32:16-19"> 32:16-19</reference>.<div eID="gen435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen436" type="x-p"/> Third, the second tables were made by Moses, and the law again written by the hand of Jehovah <reference osisRef="ex 34:1 ex 34:28 ex 34:29">Exodus 34:1,28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 10:4">Deuteronomy 10:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">afar off</hi><div eID="gen436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen437" type="x-p"/> For contrast between law and grace, cf. <reference osisRef="eph 2:13">Ephesians 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:10">Luke 1:10</reference> with <reference osisRef="heb 10:19-22">Hebrews 10:19-22</reference>.

<hi type="bold">fear</hi><div eID="gen437" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen438" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Exod.20"/><div eID="gen438" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen439" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="21" osisID="Exod.21" sID="Exod.21"/>

<hi type="bold">Eye for eye</hi> <div eID="gen439" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen440" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="le 24:20">Leviticus 24:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 19:21">Deuteronomy 19:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 5:38-44">Matthew 5:38-44</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:19-21">1 Peter 2:19-21</reference>. The provision in Exodus is law, and righteous; the N.T. passages, grace, and merciful. <chapter eID="Exod.21"/><div eID="gen440" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen441" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="23" osisID="Exod.23" sID="Exod.23"/>

<hi type="bold">Three times</hi> <div eID="gen441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen442" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="le 23:4-44">Leviticus 23:4-44</reference>. Exodus for the wilderness; Leviticus for the land.
<hi type="bold">Abib</hi><div eID="gen442" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen443" type="x-p"/> First month, i.e. April.

<hi type="bold">Angel</hi><div eID="gen443" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen444" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Exod.23"/><div eID="gen444" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen445" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="24" osisID="Exod.24" sID="Exod.24"/>

<hi type="bold">builded</hi> <div eID="gen445" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen446" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 33:7-11">Exodus 33:7-11</reference>. This arrangement for worship was temporarily called the "tabernacle."

<hi type="bold">eat and drink</hi><div eID="gen446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen447" type="x-p"/> Symbol of communion. Cf. <reference osisRef="lu 22:15-18">Luke 22:15-18</reference>. A blood-sprinkled people, see <reference osisRef="heb 9:19-22">Hebrews 9:19-22</reference> who had not yet broken the law could thus commune with God. Never again was this repeated. Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 24:9-11">Exodus 24:9-11</reference> with <reference osisRef="le 16:2">Leviticus 16:2</reference> and <reference osisRef="heb 9:6-8">Hebrews 9:6-8</reference> But cf., under grace, ; <reference osisRef="eph 2:13">Ephesians 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:19 heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:19,20</reference>. <div eID="gen447" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15"/><div sID="gen448" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.24"/>
<div eID="gen448" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen449" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="25" osisID="Exod.25" sID="Exod.25"/>

<hi type="bold">the Lord spoke unto Moses</hi> <div eID="gen449" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen450" type="x-p"/> The general authority for the types of Exodus is found:<div eID="gen450" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) as to the persons and events, in <reference osisRef="1co 10:1-11">1 Corinthians 10:1-11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) as to the tabernacle, in <reference osisRef="heb 9:1-24">Hebrews 9:1-24</reference>. Having the assurance that in the tabernacle everything is typical, the details must of necessity be received as such. Two warnings are necessary:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Nothing may be dogmatically asserted to be a type without explicit New Testament authority; and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) all types not so authenticated must be recognized as having the authority of analogy, or spiritual congruity, merely. The typical meanings of the materials and colours of the tabernacle are believed to be as follows: Gold, Deity in manifestation--divine glory; silver, redemption <reference osisRef="ex 30:12-16">Exodus 30:12-16</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 38:27">Exodus 38:27</reference>")</hi> , brass, symbol of judgment, as in the brazen altar and in the serpent of brass <reference osisRef="nu 21:6-9">Numbers 21:6-9</reference> blue, heavenly in nature or origin; purple, royalty; scarlet, sacrifice. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15"/><div sID="gen451" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15"/> <hi type="bold">willingly</hi> <div eID="gen451" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen452" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Co 8:1">2 Corinthians 8:1</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">shittim wood</hi><div eID="gen452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen453" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">tabernacle pattern</hi><div eID="gen453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen454" type="x-p"/> The tabernacle, speaking comprehensively, is explained in the N.T. as typical in three ways:<div eID="gen454" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) of the Church as a habitation of God through the Spirit <reference osisRef="ex 25:8">Exodus 25:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:19-22">Ephesians 2:19-22</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of the believer <reference osisRef="2co 6:16">2 Corinthians 6:16</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) as a figure of things in the heavens <reference osisRef="heb 9:23 heb 9:24">Hebrews 9:23,24</reference>. In detail, all speaks of Christ:</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(1) The ark, in its materials, acacia-wood <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:15">Exodus 26:15</reference>")</hi> and gold, is a type of the humanity and deity of Christ.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(2) In its contents, a type of Christ, as:</item> <item type="x-indent-3">(a) having God's law in His heart <reference osisRef="ex 25:16">Exodus 25:16</reference>. (b) the wilderness food (or portion) of His people <reference osisRef="ex 16:33">Exodus 16:33</reference> (c) Himself the resurrection, of which Aaron;s rod is the symbol <reference osisRef="nu 17:10">Numbers 17:10</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen455" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen455" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-2">(3) In its use the ark, especially the mercy-seat, was a type of God's throne. That it was, to the sinning Israelite, a throne of grace and not of judgment was due to the mercy-seat formed of gold and sprinkled with the blood of atonement, which vindicated the law, and divine holiness guarded by the cherubim <reference osisRef="ge 3:24">Genesis 3:24</reference></item> </list> <div sID="gen456" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 1:5">Ezekiel 1:5</reference>")</hi> See PROPITIATION, See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>" <div eID="gen456" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv16"/><div sID="gen457" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv16"/> <hi type="bold">make an ark</hi> <div eID="gen457" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen458" type="x-p"/> All begins with the ark, which, in the completed tabernacle, was placed in the holy of holies, because, in revelation, God begins from Himself, working outward toward man; as, in approach, the worshipper begins from himself, moving toward God in the holy of holies. The same order is followed in the Levitical offerings (Le 1.-5.). In approach man begins at the brazen altar, type of the Cross, where, in the fire of judgment, atonement is made.<div eID="gen458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen459" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make an ark</hi> The most inclusive type of Christ, Gold = Deity; wood = humanity. History:<div eID="gen459" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen460" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="nu 3:31">Numbers 3:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 10:33"> 10:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 3:3-15">Joshua 3:3-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 6:11"> 6:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 20:27">Judges 20:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 3:3">1 Samuel 3:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 4:1-11"> 4:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 5:1-10"> 5:1-10</reference> ; <reference osisRef="1sa 6:1-21"> 6:1-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 7:1 1sa 7:2">1 Samuel 7:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 6:2-17">2 Samuel 6:2-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:2"> 7:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 15:24-29"> 15:24-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 8:1-21">1 Kings 8:1-21</reference> not carried to Babylon, ; <reference osisRef="2ki 24:13">2 Kings 24:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ch 35:3">2 Chronicles 35:3,</reference> not mentioned in Ezra or Neh. Where is it? <reference osisRef="re 11:19">Revelation 11:19</reference><div eID="gen460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen461" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shittim wood</hi> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">mercy</hi><div eID="gen461" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen462" type="x-p"/> See "Propitiation." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">shittim wood</hi><div eID="gen462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen463" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.
<hi type="bold">shittim wood</hi><div eID="gen463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen464" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">shewbread</hi><div eID="gen464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen465" type="x-p"/> Showbread, type of Christ, the Bread of God, nourisher of the Christian's life as a believer-priest <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:6">Revelation 1:6</reference>. In <reference osisRef="joh 6:33-58">John 6:33-58</reference> our Lord has more in mind the manna, that food which "came down"; but all typical meanings of "bread" are there gathered into His words. The manna is the life-giving Christ; the showbread, the life-sustaining Christ. The showbread typifies Christ as the "corn of wheat" <reference osisRef="joh 12:24">John 12:24</reference> ground in the mill of suffering <reference osisRef="joh 12:27">John 12:27</reference> and brought into the fire of judgment <reference osisRef="joh 12:31-33">John 12:31-33</reference>. We, as priests, by faith feed upon Him as having undergone that in our stead and for our sakes. It is meditation upon Christ, as in <reference osisRef="heb 12:2 heb 12:3">Hebrews 12:2,3</reference>.

<hi type="bold">candlestick</hi><div eID="gen465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen466" type="x-p"/> Candlestick, type of Christ our Light, shining in the fullness of the power of the sevenfold Spirit <reference osisRef="isa 11:2">Isaiah 11:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:9">Hebrews 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:4">Revelation 1:4</reference>. Natural light was excluded from the tabernacle. (Cf) <reference osisRef="1co 2:14 1co 2:15">1 Corinthians 2:14,15</reference>.<div eID="gen466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen467" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:16">Genesis 1:16</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="joh 1:4">John 1:4</reference>. <div eID="gen467" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17"/><div sID="gen468" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.25"/>
<div eID="gen468" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen469" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="26" osisID="Exod.26" sID="Exod.26"/>

<hi type="bold">cherubims</hi> <div eID="gen469" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen470" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fine twined linen</hi> Fine linen typifies personal righteousness <reference osisRef="re 19:8">Revelation 19:8</reference>. The fine linen here typifies the sinless life of Christ.<div eID="gen470" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen471" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">blue</hi> Blue. Christ's heavenly origin; purple, His royalty as David's son; scarlet, His sacrifice.<div eID="gen471" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen472" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cherubims</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 1:5">Ezekiel 1:5</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">goats' hair</hi> CF. <reference osisRef="le 16:5 le 16:7-10">Leviticus 16:5,7-10</reference>. The reference seems to be to the result of the ordinance of the two goats as "covering" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 16:5">Leviticus 16:5</reference>")</hi> thus speaking of Christ in atonement See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:21">Genesis 3:21</reference>". This thought is intensified in the colour of the rams' skins, <reference osisRef="ex 26:14">Exodus 26:14</reference>.

<hi type="bold">boards</hi><div eID="gen472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen473" type="x-p"/> The typical meaning of the boards is clear as to Christ. Acacia wood, a desert growth, is a fitting symbol of Christ in His humanity as "a root out of dry ground" <reference osisRef="isa 53:2">Isaiah 53:2</reference>. The covering, gold, typifies Deity in manifestation, speaks of His divine glory. As applied to the individual believer the meaning of the boards is less clear. The connection may be found in ; <reference osisRef="joh 17:21 joh 17:22 joh 17:23">John 17:21,22,23</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:4 eph 1:6">Ephesians 1:4,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 4:13">1 John 4:13</reference>. Only as seen "in Him" could the boards be taken as representing the believer. So viewed the type is beautiful. In the world, and yet separated from it by the silver of redemption ; <reference osisRef="ga 1:4">Galatians 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 30:11-16">Exodus 30:11-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 38:25-27"> 38:25-27</reference> as the boards of the tabernacle were separated from the earth by the sockets of silver, and united by the "middle bar" <reference osisRef="ex 26:28">Exodus 26:28</reference> representing both the one life <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference> and one Spirit <reference osisRef="eph 4:3">Ephesians 4:3</reference> "all the building, fitly framed together, groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord." <reference osisRef="eph 2:21">Ephesians 2:21</reference>.

<hi type="bold">sockets of silver</hi><div eID="gen473" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen474" type="x-p"/> Silver symbolizes redemption. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 25:1">Exodus 25:1</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen475" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 38:27">Exodus 38:27</reference>")</hi>. All the tabernacle rests upon silver except the hangings of the gate, the way of access. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ex 27:17">Exodus 27:17</reference>".
<hi type="bold">shittim</hi><div eID="gen475" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen476" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">vail</hi><div eID="gen476" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen477" type="x-p"/> The inner veil, type of Christ's human body <reference osisRef="mt 26:26">Matthew 26:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 27:50"> 27:50</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:20</reference>. This veil, barring entrance into the holiest, was the most expressive symbol of the truth that "by the deeds of the law shall no flesh be justified" ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:20">Romans 3:20,</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:8">Hebrews 9:8</reference>. Rent by an unseen hand when Christ Died <reference osisRef="mt 27:51">Matthew 27:51</reference> thus giving instant access to God to all who come by faith in Him, it was the end of all legality; the way to God was open. It is deeply significant that the priests must have patched together again the veil that God had rent, for the temple services went on yet for nearly forty years. That patched veil is Galatianism--the attempt to put saint or sinner back under the law. (Cf) <reference osisRef="ga 1:6-9">Galatians 1:6-9</reference> Anything but "the grace of Christ" is "another gospel," and under anathema.
<hi type="bold">shittim</hi><div eID="gen477" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen478" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">shittim</hi> i.e. acacia.<div eID="gen478" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen479" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">brass</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 27:17">Exodus 27:17</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen479" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17"/><div sID="gen480" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.26"/>
<div eID="gen480" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen481" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="27" osisID="Exod.27" sID="Exod.27"/>

<hi type="bold">altar</hi> <div eID="gen481" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen482" type="x-p"/> Brazen altar, type of the Cross upon which Christ, our whole burnt-offering offered Himself without spot to God <reference osisRef="heb 9:14">Hebrews 9:14</reference>.<div eID="gen482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen483" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">height</hi> (Cf) <reference osisRef="ex 25:10">Exodus 25:10</reference>. The altar of burnt offering is double the height of the mercy-seat. The atonement more than saves us-- it glorifies God <reference osisRef="joh 17:14">John 17:14</reference>.<div eID="gen483" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen484" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shittim</hi> i.e. acacia.<div eID="gen484" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen485" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wood</hi> The wood (Christ's humanity), completely inclosed in brass, must have become completely charred by sacrificial fires. Cf. <reference osisRef="heb 10:5-7">Hebrews 10:5-7</reference>.

<hi type="bold">brass</hi><div eID="gen485" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen486" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="nu 21:9">Numbers 21:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:14">John 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:31-33"> 12:31-33</reference> thus fixing the symbolic meaning of brass as divine manifestation in judgment.
<hi type="bold">shittim</hi><div eID="gen486" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen487" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">fine twined linen</hi><div eID="gen487" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen488" type="x-p"/> The fine linen commonly typifies personal righteousness <reference osisRef="ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference> ref. (d), and in the hangings of the court stands for that measure of righteousness which God demands of any who would, in his own righteousness, approach. Christ, figuratively speaking, put up the hangings of the court in <reference osisRef="lu 10:25-28">Luke 10:25-28</reference>. The only way of approach was the "gate" ; <reference osisRef="ex 27:16">Exodus 27:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 10:9">John 10:9</reference>. The hangings of the court bar out equally the self-righteous man and the open sinner, for the height was above seven feet. <reference osisRef="ex 27:18">Exodus 27:18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">gate</hi><div eID="gen488" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen489" type="x-p"/> In the hangings of the court (<reference osisRef="ex 27:9">Exodus 27:9</reference>), representing that practical righteousness which God demands in the law, and which, therefore, bars out all men ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:19 ro 3:20">Romans 3:19,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:3-5"> 10:3-5</reference>. No colours are inwrought. But the "gate" is Christ <reference osisRef="joh 10:9">John 10:9</reference> and so the colours reappear as in the veil <reference osisRef="ex 26:31">Exodus 26:31</reference>.

<hi type="bold">pillars</hi><div eID="gen489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen490" type="x-p"/> The fillets and hooks upholding the linen hangings are of silver <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 38:27">Exodus 38:27</reference>")</hi> for it is in virtue of His redemptive work that Christ is our way of access, and not by virtue of His righteous life (symbolized by the fine linen); but the pillars of the court rest upon brass sockets, not silver as in the case of the boards See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ex 26:19">Exodus 26:19</reference>" and brass symbolizes divine righteousness in judgment See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:nu 21:9">Numbers 21:9</reference>". Redemption not only displays God's mercy, but vindicates His righteousness in showing that mercy. <reference osisRef="ro 3:21-26">Romans 3:21-26</reference>.
<hi type="bold">brass</hi><div eID="gen490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen491" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Nu 21:9">Numbers 21:9</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">oil</hi><div eID="gen491" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen492" type="x-p"/> Oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit (Cf) <reference osisRef="joh 3:34">John 3:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:9">Hebrews 1:9</reference>. In Christ the oil- fed Light ever burns, the Light of the world <reference osisRef="joh 8:12">John 8:12</reference>. But here we have not the world, but the sanctuary. It is a question, not of testimony in and to the world, but of our communion and worship as believer-priests in the holiest <reference osisRef="heb 10:19 heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:19,20</reference>. In the Tabernacle there were two compartments, two lights: the holy place with the candlestick <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 25:31">Exodus 25:31</reference>")</hi> the holy of holies with the shekinah, or manifested glory of God. These two places are now one ; <reference osisRef="mt 27:50 mt 27:51">Matthew 27:50,51</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:6-8">Hebrews 9:6-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:19-21"> 10:19-21</reference> but it is important to see that there are still two lights: Christ, the Light of life <reference osisRef="joh 8:12">John 8:12</reference> through the Spirit giving light upon the holy things of God, the showbread and altar of incense; and also the shekinah, now on the face of Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="2co 4:6">2 Corinthians 4:6</reference>. Into this twofold light we, as believer- priests, are brought <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>. We "walk in the light," not merely which He gives, but in which He lives <reference osisRef="1jo 1:7">1 John 1:7</reference>. But what of the command to "bring pure oil" <reference osisRef="ex 27:20">Exodus 27:20</reference>. Because our access, apprehension, communion, and transformation are by the Spirit ; <reference osisRef="eph 2:18">Ephesians 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 2:14 1co 2:15">1 Corinthians 2:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 13:14">2 Corinthians 13:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:1">Philippians 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 3:18">2 Corinthians 3:18</reference>. Our title to His presence is the blood <reference osisRef="eph 2:13">Ephesians 2:13</reference> but only as filled with the Spirit <reference osisRef="eph 5:18">Ephesians 5:18</reference> do we really walk in the light. <div eID="gen492" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17"/><div sID="gen493" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.27"/>
<div eID="gen493" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen494" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="28" osisID="Exod.28" sID="Exod.28"/>

<hi type="bold">Aaron</hi> <div eID="gen494" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen495" type="x-p"/> Type of Christ, our High Priest. Christ is a priest after the order of Melchizedek, but He executes his priestly office after the pattern of Aaron. Heb. 7. gives the order; Heb. 9., the pattern.<div eID="gen495" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen496" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">holy garments</hi><div eID="gen496" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen497" type="x-p"/> Heb. qodesh= "set apart" for God. Trans. "holy," v.2; "consecrate," v.3. Often trans. "sanctify." See summary, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:3">Zechariah 8:3</reference>")</hi>. This is always the fundamental idea of a holy, consecrated, separated, or sanctified person or thing--something set apart for God. Infinite confusion would have been spared the reader if qodesh had been uniformly trans. "set apart."

<hi type="bold">consecrate</hi><div eID="gen497" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen498" type="x-p"/> Heb. qodesh= "set apart" for God. Trans. "holy," v.2; "consecrate," v.3. Often trans. "sanctify." See summary, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:3">Zechariah 8:3</reference>")</hi>. This is always the fundamental idea of a holy, consecrated, separated, or sanctified person or thing--something set apart for God. Infinite confusion would have been spared the reader if qodesh had been uniformly trans. "set apart."
<hi type="bold">garments</hi><div eID="gen498" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen499" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 29:5">Exodus 29:5</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">take gold</hi> Gold, Deity in manifestation; blue, heavenly; purple, royalty; scarlet, sacrifice; fine linen, personal righteousness, see margin ref., <reference osisRef="ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>.<div eID="gen499" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen500" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">ephod</hi> Gold, Deity in manifestation; blue, heavenly; purple, royalty; scarlet, sacrifice; fine linen, personal righteousness, see margin ref., <reference osisRef="ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>.<div eID="gen500" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen501" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">shoulders</hi><div eID="gen501" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen502" type="x-p"/> The place of strenghth. <reference osisRef="isa 9:6">Isaiah 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 15:4 lu 15:5">Luke 15:4,5</reference>.

<hi type="bold">gold</hi> Gold, Deity in manifestation; blue, heavenly; purple, royalty; scarlet, sacrifice; fine linen, personal righteousness, see margin ref., <reference osisRef="ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>.<div eID="gen502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen503" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:1">Exodus 26:1</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">heart</hi><div eID="gen503" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen504" type="x-p"/> The place of affection. Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 28:12">Exodus 28:12</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Urim and Thummim</hi><div eID="gen504" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen505" type="x-p"/> Urim and Thummim, meaning "lights and perfections." Some make these to be simply a collective name for the stones of the breastplate, so that the total effect of the twelve stones is to manifest the "lights and perfections" of Him who is the antitype of the Aaronic high priest. Per contra, <reference osisRef="le 8:8">Leviticus 8:8</reference>. This would seem to be conclusive that "the Urim and Thummim" are additional to the stones of the breastplate. In use the Urim and Thummim were connected, in some way not clearly expressed, with the ascertainment of the divine will in particular cases ; <reference osisRef="nu 27:21">Numbers 27:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 33:8">Deuteronomy 33:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 28:6">1 Samuel 28:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ezr 2:63">Ezra 2:63</reference>.
<hi type="bold">robe</hi><div eID="gen505" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen506" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 29:5">Exodus 29:5</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">bear</hi><div eID="gen506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen507" type="x-p"/> i.e. be responsible for every neglect or offence respecting "the holy things," etc. <div eID="gen507" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17"/><div sID="gen508" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.28"/>
<div eID="gen508" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen509" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="29" osisID="Exod.29" sID="Exod.29"/>

<hi type="bold">do unto them to hallow them</hi> <div eID="gen509" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen510" type="x-p"/> The priest type of consecration. (Cf. the temple type, <reference osisRef="1ki 8:1-11">1 Kings 8:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ch 5:4 2ch 5:14">2 Chronicles 5:4,14</reference>. The order in ; <reference osisRef="le 8:1-le 9:24">Leviticus 8:1-9:24</reference>; differs from the order here. In Leviticus the filling the hands precedes the sprinkling.<div eID="gen510" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen511" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bullock, rams</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 1:3">Leviticus 1:3</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">cakes</hi><div eID="gen511" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen512" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 25:30">Exodus 25:30</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:le 2:1">Leviticus 2:1</reference>".

Aaron shares in the washing (i.e., symbol of regeneration), <reference osisRef="tit 3:5">Titus 3:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:5 joh 3:6">John 3:5,6</reference><div eID="gen512" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) as needing it, be in this in contrast with Christ <reference osisRef="heb 7:26-28">Hebrews 7:26-28</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) to typify Christ's action, who received the baptism of John, not as needing it, but as thus identifying Himself with sinners, and as fulfilling the Aaronic type. As in Aaron's case, His anointing followed the washing <reference osisRef="ex 29:4 ex 29:7">Exodus 29:4,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 3:14-16">Matthew 3:14-16</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen513" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wash</hi> Distinguish the washing from the use of the laver.<div eID="gen513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen514" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ex 30:18-21">Exodus 30:18-21</reference> This washing typifies regeneration<div eID="gen514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen515" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="tit 3:5">Titus 3:5</reference> the laver, daily cleansing<div eID="gen515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen516" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1jo 1:9">1 John 1:9</reference> See both <reference osisRef="joh 13:10">John 13:10</reference>. <div eID="gen516" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17"/><div sID="gen517" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv17"/> <hi type="bold">garments</hi> <div eID="gen517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen518" type="x-p"/> The priest's garments were put on in reverse order of the instructions for making them:<div eID="gen518" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The "coat" <reference osisRef="ex 28:39">Exodus 28:39</reference> the oriental long garment worn next to the person, made of fine linen. <reference osisRef="ex 27:9">Exodus 27:9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The "robe of the ephod" <reference osisRef="ex 28:31-35">Exodus 28:31-35</reference> a long seamless garment of blue linen with an opening for the head, worn over the "coat." Pomegranates, symbol of fruitfulness, were embroidered on the skirt of the robe in blue, purple, and scarlet, alternated with golden bells, symbol of testimony, which gave a sound as the high priest went in and out of the sanctuary. The robe was secured by a golden girdle.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The ephod <reference osisRef="ex 28:5-12">Exodus 28:5-12</reference> was next put on. A short garment made of linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet, it consisted of two pieces, front and back, united by two shoulder-pieces and by a band about the bottom. Two onyx stones, set in gold and fastened upon the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, were engraved with the names of the twelve tribes: "and Aaron shall bear their names before Jehovah upon his two shoulders (the place of strength) for a memorial." Cf. ; <reference osisRef="isa 9:6">Isaiah 9:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 15:4 lu 15:5">Luke 15:4,5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The breastplate was a square pouch <reference osisRef="ex 28:16">Exodus 28:16</reference> of linen to contain the Urim and Thummim. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 28:30">Exodus 28:30</reference>")</hi>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen519" type="x-p"/> To the linen pouch was attached the oblong gold setting containing four rows of precious stones, on each stone a tribal name. The breastplate with the jewel work was attached at the upper corners to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod by golden chains. Golden rings were sewn on ephod and breastplate, and the latter was further secured to the ephod by laces of blue through the rings. Altogether, it was called "the breastplate of judgment" because worn by the high priest when judging the causes of the people. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 28:30">Exodus 28:30</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen519" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) A mitre (or "turban") of fine line was made <reference osisRef="ex 28:37">Exodus 28:37</reference> to cover the head, bearing upon the front a gold plate engraved, "Holiness to the Lord" <reference osisRef="ex 29:36">Exodus 29:36</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) To these were added linen breeches, "from the loins even to the thighs" <reference osisRef="ex 28:42">Exodus 28:42</reference>. The "coat" and linen breeches were made for the priests, also, and were the ordinary garments of high priest and priests as distinguished from the other garments, which were "for glory and beauty." </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv18"/><div sID="gen520" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv18"/> <hi type="bold">gird</hi> <div eID="gen520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen521" type="x-p"/> Symbol of service. <reference osisRef="lu 12:37">Luke 12:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 17:8"> 17:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 13:4">John 13:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:13">Revelation 1:13</reference>.

<hi type="bold">put their hands</hi><div eID="gen521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen522" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 1:4">Leviticus 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">atonement</hi> <div eID="gen522" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen523" type="x-p"/> Heb. kaphar, "to cover." The English word "atonement" (at-one-ment) is not a translation of the Heb. kaphar, but a translator's interpretation. According to Scripture the legal sacrifice "covered" the offerer's sin and secured the divine forgiveness; according to the translators it made God and the sinner at- one. But the O.T. sacrifices did not at-one the sinner and God. "It is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins." <reference osisRef="heb 10:4">Hebrews 10:4</reference>. The Israelite's offering implied confession of sin and of its due desert, death; and God "covered" (passed over," <reference osisRef="ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference> his sin, in anticipation of Christ's sacrifice, which did, finally, "put away" the sins "done aforetime in the forbearance of God." ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:15">Hebrews 9:15</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>")</hi>. The word "atonement" does not occur in the N.T.; <reference osisRef="ro 5:11">Romans 5:11</reference> meaning reconciliation, and so rendered in the R.V.<div eID="gen523" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen524" type="x-p"/> See "Sacrifice," <reference osisRef="ge 4:4">Genesis 4:4,</reference> and refs. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 4:4">Genesis 4:4</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen524" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen525" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Le 16:5">Leviticus 16:5</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">atonement</hi> <div eID="gen525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen526" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 29:33">Exodus 29:33</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen526" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19"/><div sID="gen527" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.29"/>
<div eID="gen527" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen528" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="30" osisID="Exod.30" sID="Exod.30"/>

<hi type="bold">incense</hi> <div eID="gen528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen529" type="x-p"/> Altar of incense, type of Christ our intercessor <reference osisRef="joh 17:1-26">John 17:1-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:25">Hebrews 7:25</reference> through whom our own prayers and praises ascend to God ; <reference osisRef="heb 13:15">Hebrews 13:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 8:3 re 8:4">Revelation 8:3,4</reference> and of the believer-priest's sacrifice of praise and worship <reference osisRef="heb 13:15">Hebrews 13:15</reference>.
<hi type="bold">shittim</hi><div eID="gen529" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen530" type="x-p"/> i.e. acacia.

<hi type="bold">strange</hi><div eID="gen530" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen531" type="x-p"/> (Cf.) <reference osisRef="le 10:1-3">Leviticus 10:1-3,</reference> two prohibitions are given concerning worship:<div eID="gen531" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) No "strange" incense is to be offered. This speaks of simulated or purely formal worship.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) No "strange" fire was permitted. This refers to the excitation of "religious" feelings by merely sensuous means, and to the substitution for devotion to Christ of any other devotion, as to religious causes, or sects. (Cf) <reference osisRef="1co 1:11-13">1 Corinthians 1:11-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 2:8 col 2:16-19">Colossians 2:8,16-19</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 30:38">Exodus 30:38</reference>")</hi>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv19"/><div sID="gen532" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv19"/> <hi type="bold">atonement</hi> <div eID="gen532" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen533" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 29:33">Exodus 29:33</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">This they shall give</hi><div eID="gen533" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen534" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 38:25-27">Exodus 38:25-27</reference>. Silver thus becomes a type of redemption. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:19">Exodus 26:19</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">laver</hi><div eID="gen534" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen535" type="x-p"/> Laver, type of Christ cleansing us from defilement, and from "every spot or wrinkle or any such thing" <reference osisRef="joh 13:2-10">John 13:2-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-27">Ephesians 5:25-27</reference>. It is significant that the priests could not enter the holy place after serving at the brazen altar till hands and feet were cleansed.
<hi type="bold">oil</hi><div eID="gen535" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen536" type="x-p"/> Anointing oil, type of the Holy Spirit for service <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>.

<hi type="bold">frankincense</hi><div eID="gen536" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen537" type="x-p"/> Frankincense is not to be confounded with incense (to which it was to be added), as it is often used apart from incense. We are told what composed the incense--never in Scripture what the frankincense was. All speaks of Christ--the sweet spices of those perfections which we may apprehend, the frankincense of that which God saw in Jesus ineffable.

<hi type="bold">smell</hi><div eID="gen537" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen538" type="x-p"/> What is condemned here is making worship a mere pleasure to the natural man, whether sensuous, as in beautiful music to please the ear, or eloquence, merely to give delight to the natural mind. (Cf) <reference osisRef="joh 4:23 joh 4:24">John 4:23,24</reference>. <div eID="gen538" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv20"/><div sID="gen539" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Exod.30"/>

<hi type="bold">let me alone</hi><div eID="gen545" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen546" type="x-p"/> This whole scene affords a striking contrast between law and grace. (Cf) Moses' intercession with Christ's <reference osisRef="joh 17:1-26">John 17:1-26</reference> Israel was a nation, under probation <reference osisRef="ex 19:5 ex 19:6">Exodus 19:5,6</reference> believers under grace are a family, awaiting glory ; <reference osisRef="joh 20:17">John 20:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 5:1 ro 5:2">Romans 5:1,2</reference>. For them there is "an advocate with the Father, whose propitiatory sacrifice never loses efficacy <reference osisRef="1jo 2:1 1jo 2:2">1 John 2:1,2</reference>. Moses pleads a covenant <reference osisRef="ex 32:13">Exodus 32:13</reference>. Christ points to a sacrifice <reference osisRef="joh 17:4">John 17:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">silver</hi><div eID="gen574" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen575" type="x-p"/> Silver thus receives its symbolic meaning--redemption. The sockets were made of the redemption money of the children of Israel. Cf. <reference osisRef="ex 26:19">Exodus 26:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 30:13-16"> 30:13-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 3:44-51">Numbers 3:44-51</reference>.<div eID="gen575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen576" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sockets</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:19">Exodus 26:19</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Exod.38"/><div eID="gen576" type="x-p"/>
