<hi type="bold">servant</hi> <div eID="gen2267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2268" type="x-p"/> There is a twofold account of the Coming Servant:<div eID="gen2268" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) he is represented as weak, despised, rejected, slain:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) and also as a mighty conqueror, taking vengeance on the nations and restoring Israel (e.g. <reference osisRef="isa 40:10">Isaiah 40:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-4"> 63:1-4</reference>). The former class of passages relate to the first advent, and are fulfilled; the latter to the second advent, and are unfulfilled. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv52"/><div sID="gen2269" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv52"/> <hi type="bold">for a light of the Gentiles</hi> <div eID="gen2269" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2270" type="x-p"/> The prophets connect the Gentiles with Christ in a threefold way"<div eID="gen2270" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) as the Light He brings salvation to the Gentiles <reference osisRef="lu 2:32">Luke 2:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:47 ac 13:48">Acts 13:47,48</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) as the "Root of Jesse" He is to reign over the Gentiles in His kingdom. <reference osisRef="isa 11:10">Isaiah 11:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 15:12">Romans 15:12</reference>. He saves the Gentiles, which is the distinctive feature of this present age. ; <reference osisRef="ro 11:17-24">Romans 11:17-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:11 eph 2:12">Ephesians 2:11,12</reference> He reigns over the Gentiles in the kingdom-age, to follow this. See "Kingdom (O.T.)," ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Believing Gentiles in the present age, together with believing Jews, constitute "the church which is His body." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 3:6">Ephesians 3:6</reference>")</hi> </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv53"/><div sID="gen2271" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv53"/> <hi type="bold">former things</hi> <div eID="gen2271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2272" type="x-p"/> i.e. Isaiah's prediction of Sennacherib's invasion and its results, Isa. 10 and 37. See also, <reference osisRef="isa 41:21-23">Isaiah 41:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 43:8-isa 1244:7"> 43:8-1244:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 48:3 isa 48:5 isa 48:16"> 48:3,5,16</reference>. This appeal of the prophet to the fulfilment of his former predictions strongly confirms the unity of the book. <div eID="gen2272" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv54"/><div sID="gen2273" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Isa.42"/>

<hi type="bold">Cyrus</hi><div eID="gen2280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2281" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="1ki 13:2">1 Kings 13:2</reference> where Josiah was mentioned by name three hundred years before his birth. <div eID="gen2281" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv54"/><div sID="gen2282" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Isa.44"/>

<hi type="bold">anointed</hi> <div eID="gen2283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2284" type="x-p"/> The only instance where the word is applied to a Gentile. Nebuchadnezzar is called the "servant" of Jehovah <reference osisRef="jer 25:9">Jeremiah 25:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 27:6"> 27:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 43:10"> 43:10</reference> This, with the designation "My shepherd" <reference osisRef="isa 44:28">Isaiah 44:28</reference> also a Messianic title, marks Cyrus as that startling exception, a Gentile type of Christ. The points are:<div eID="gen2284" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) both are irresistible conquerors of Israel's enemies. <reference osisRef="isa 45:1">Isaiah 45:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:19-21">Revelation 19:19-21</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) both are restorers of the holy city <reference osisRef="isa 44:28">Isaiah 44:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 14:1-11">Zechariah 14:1-11</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) through both is the name of the one true God glorified <reference osisRef="isa 45:6">Isaiah 45:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:28">1 Corinthians 15:28</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv54"/><div sID="gen2285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv54"/> <hi type="bold">create evil</hi> <div eID="gen2285" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2286" type="x-p"/> Heb. <hi type="bold">so marred</hi><div eID="gen2309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2310" type="x-p"/> The literal rendering is terrible: "So marred from the form of man was His aspect that His appearance was not that of a son of man"--i.e. not human--the effect of the brutalities described in <reference osisRef="mt 26:67 mt 26:68">Matthew 26:67,68</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 27:27-30"> 27:27-30</reference>. <div eID="gen2310" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv55"/><div sID="gen2311" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Isa.52"/>

<hi type="bold">Redeemer</hi><div eID="gen2320" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2321" type="x-p"/> Redemption: Kinsman type, summary. The goel, or Kinsman-Redeemer, is a beautiful type of Christ.<div eID="gen2321" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The kinsman redemption was of persons, and an inheritance <reference osisRef="le 25:48">Leviticus 25:48</reference>; <reference osisRef="le 25:25"> 25:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:5">Galatians 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:7 eph 1:11 eph 1:14">Ephesians 1:7,11,14</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The Redeemer must be a kinsman <reference osisRef="le 25:48 le 25:49">Leviticus 25:48,49</reference>; <reference osisRef="ru 3:12 ru 3:13">Ruth 3:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:4">Galatians 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:14 heb 2:15">Hebrews 2:14,15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The Redeemer must be able to redeem <reference osisRef="ru 4:4-6">Ruth 4:4-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 50:34">Jeremiah 50:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 10:11 joh 10:18">John 10:11,18</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Redemption is effected by the goel paying the just demand in full <reference osisRef="le 25:27">Leviticus 25:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:18 1pe 1:19">1 Peter 1:18,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:13">Galatians 3:13</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 14:30">Exodus 14:30</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>"</item> </list> <div sID="gen2322" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">come to Zion</hi> <div eID="gen2322" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2323" type="x-p"/> The time when the "Redeemer shall come to Zion" is fixed, relatively, by <reference osisRef="ro 11:23-29">Romans 11:23-29</reference> as following the completion of the Gentile Church. That is also the order of the great dispensational passage, <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>.<div eID="gen2323" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2324" type="x-p"/> In both, the return of the Lord to Zion follows the outcalling of the Church. <chapter eID="Isa.59"/><div eID="gen2324" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">redeemer</hi> <div eID="gen2326" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2327" type="x-p"/> Heb. goel, Redemp. (Kinsman type). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi> <chapter eID="Isa.60"/><div eID="gen2327" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2328" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="61" osisID="Isa.61" sID="Isa.61"/>

<hi type="bold">acceptable year of the Lord</hi> <div eID="gen2328" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2329" type="x-p"/> Observe that Jesus suspended the reading of this passage in the synagogue at Nazareth <reference osisRef="lu 4:16-21">Luke 4:16-21</reference> at the comma in the middle of <reference osisRef="isa 61:2">Isaiah 61:2</reference>. The first advent, therefore, opened the day of grace, "the acceptable year of Jehovah," but does not fulfil the day of vengeance. That will be taken up when Messiah returns <reference osisRef="2th 1:7-10">2 Thessalonians 1:7-10</reference> Cf. ; <reference osisRef="isa 34:8">Isaiah 34:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 35:4-10"> 35:4-10</reference>. The last verse, taken with the 4th, gives the historic connection: the vengeance precedes the regathering of Israel, and synchronizes with the day of the Lord. ; <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-6">Isaiah 63:1-6</reference>. <chapter eID="Isa.61"/><div eID="gen2329" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">our Father</hi><div eID="gen2337" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2338" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="isa 1:2">Isaiah 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 64:8"> 64:8</reference>. Israel, collectively, the national Israel, recognizes God as the national Father (cf) <reference osisRef="ex 4:22 ex 4:23">Exodus 4:22,23,</reference> Doubtless the believing Israelite was born anew (cf) ; <reference osisRef="joh 3:3 joh 3:5">John 3:3,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 13:28">Luke 13:28</reference> but the O.T. Scriptures show no trace of the consciousness of personal sonship. The explanation is given in <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-7">Galatians 4:1-7</reference>.<div eID="gen2338" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2339" type="x-p"/> The Israelite, though a child, "differed nothing from a servant." The Spirit, as the "Spirit of His Son," could not be given to impart the consciousness of sonship until redemption had been accomplished. <reference osisRef="ga 4:4-6">Galatians 4:4-6</reference> See "Adoption" ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:15">Romans 8:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:5">Ephesians 1:5</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:5">Ephesians 1:5</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen2339" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2340" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">redeemer</hi> Heb. "goel," Redemp. (Kinsman type). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">fear</hi><div eID="gen2340" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2341" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Isa.63"/><div eID="gen2341" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">our father</hi> <div eID="gen2342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2343" type="x-p"/> Here the reference is to relationship through creation, rather than through faith, as in <reference osisRef="ac 17:28 ac 17:29">Acts 17:28,29</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 17:29">Acts 17:29</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Isa.64"/><div eID="gen2343" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2344" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="65" osisID="Isa.65" sID="Isa.65"/>

<hi type="bold">behold</hi> <div eID="gen2344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2345" type="x-p"/> Verse 17 looks beyond the kingdom-age to the new heavens and the new earth (see refs. at "create"), but verses 18-25 describe the kingdom-age itself. Longevity is restored, but death, the "last enemy" <reference osisRef="1co 15:26">1 Corinthians 15:26</reference> is not destroyed till after Satan's rebellion at the end of the thousand years. <reference osisRef="re 20:7-14">Revelation 20:7-14</reference>. <chapter eID="Isa.65"/><div eID="gen2345" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2346" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="66" osisID="Isa.66" sID="Isa.66"/>

Marg<div eID="gen2347" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2348" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">render his anger</hi> (Day of Jehovah)<div eID="gen2348" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2349" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 4:1-6"> 4:1-6</reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-13"> 11:10-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 13:9-16"> 13:9-16</reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 24:21-23"> 24:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 26:20 isa 26:21"> 26:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-6">Isaiah 63:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 66:15-24"> 66:15-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference> <chapter eID="Isa.66"/><div eID="gen2349" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2111" osisID="Isa" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Jer" sID="gen2350" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Jer.1" sID="Jer.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv55"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Jeremiah</title> <div sID="gen2351" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jer 1">Read first chapter of Jeremiah</reference><div eID="gen2351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2352" type="x-p"/> Jeremiah began his ministry in the 13th year of Josiah, about 60 years after Isaiah's death. Zephaniah and Habakkuk were contemporaries of his earlier ministry. Daniel of his later. After the death of Josiah, the kingdom of Judah hastened to its end in the Babylonian captivity. Jeremiah remained in the land ministering to the poor Remnant (<reference osisRef="2ki 24:14">2 Kings 24:14</reference>) until they went into Egypt, whither he followed them, and where he died, early in the 70 year's captivity. Jeremiah, prophesying before and during the exile of Judah, connects the pre-exile prophets with Ezekiel and Daniel, prophets of the exile.<div eID="gen2352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2353" type="x-p"/> Jeremiah's vision includes: the Babylonian captivity; the return after 70 years; the world- wide dispersion; the final regathering; the kingdom-age; the day of judgment on the Gentile powers, and the Remnant.<div eID="gen2353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2354" type="x-p"/> Jeremiah is in six chief divisions:<div eID="gen2354" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">From the prophet's call to his message to the first captives. 1:1-29:32.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Prophecies and events not chronological, 30:1-36:2.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">From the accession to the captivity of Zedekiah, 37:1-39,18.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Jeremiah's prophecies in the land after the final captivity of Judah, 40:1-42:22.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The prophet in Egypt, 43:1-44:30.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Miscellaneous prophecies45:1-52:34.</item> </list> <div sID="gen2355" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in Jeremiah cover a period of 41 years (Ussher). <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv55"/><hi type="bold">fifth month</hi><div eID="gen2355" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2356" type="x-p"/> i.e. August.

<hi type="bold">rod</hi><div eID="gen2356" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2357" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Nu 17:8">Numbers 17:8</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen2357" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv56"/><div sID="gen2358" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.1"/>
<div eID="gen2358" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2359" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Jer.2" sID="Jer.2"/>

<hi type="bold">word of the Lord</hi> <div eID="gen2359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2360" type="x-p"/> The general character of the first message from Jehovah to Judah by Jeremiah is threefold:<div eID="gen2360" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) He reminds Israel of the days of blessing and deliverance, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 2:1-7">Jeremiah 2:1-7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He reproaches them with forsaking Him, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 2:13">Jeremiah 2:13</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) He accuses them of choosing other, and impotent, gods, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 2:10-12 jer 2:26-28">Jeremiah 2:10-12,26-28</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen2361" type="x-p"/> All these messages are to be thought of as inspired sermons, spoken to the people and subsequently written. Cf. <reference osisRef="jer 36:1-32">Jeremiah 36:1-32</reference>. <chapter eID="Jer.2"/><div eID="gen2361" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2362" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Jer.3" sID="Jer.3"/>

<hi type="bold">The Lord said</hi> <div eID="gen2362" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2363" type="x-p"/> The general character of the second message to Judah is:<div eID="gen2363" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) of reproach that the example of Jehovah's chastening of the northern kingdom <reference osisRef="2ki 17:1-18">2 Kings 17:1-18</reference> had produced no effect upon Judah, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 3:6-10">Jeremiah 3:6-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of warning of a like chastisement impending over Judah, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 3:15-17">Jeremiah 3:15-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) of touching appeals to return to Jehovah, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 3:12-14">Jeremiah 3:12-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) of promises of final national restoration and blessing, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 3:16-18">Jeremiah 3:16-18</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen2364" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Israel</hi> <div eID="gen2364" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2365" type="x-p"/> "Israel" and "Ephraim": names by which the northern kingdom (the ten tribes) is usually called in the prophets. When by "Israel" the whole nation is meant, it will appear from the context. <chapter eID="Jer.3"/><div eID="gen2365" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2366" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Jer.4" sID="Jer.4"/>

<hi type="bold">without form and void</hi> <div eID="gen2366" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2367" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 1:2">Genesis 1:2</reference>. "Without form and void" describes the condition of the earth as the result of judgment ; <reference osisRef="jer 4:24-26">Jeremiah 4:24-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 24:1">Isaiah 24:1</reference> which overthrew the primal order of <reference osisRef="ge 1:1">Genesis 1:1</reference>. SCOFIELD'S "GAP" THEORY!<div eID="gen2367" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2368" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 401495 (Gap Theory) For Another Point of View: See Topic 8756 <div eID="gen2368" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">trustedst</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">fear</hi> <div eID="gen2370" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2371" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen2371" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2372" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.5"/>
<div eID="gen2372" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2373" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="7" osisID="Jer.7" sID="Jer.7"/>

<hi type="bold">The word that came</hi> <div eID="gen2373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2374" type="x-p"/> The general character of the message in the temple gate is, like the first and second messages, one of rebuke, warning, and exhortation, but this message is addressed more to such in Judah as still maintaining outwardly the worship of Jehovah; it is a message to religious Judah, e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 7:2 jer 7:9 jer 7:10">Jeremiah 7:2,9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 9:10 jer 9:11"> 9:10,11</reference>.
<hi type="bold">trust</hi><div eID="gen2374" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2375" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">nor commanded</hi><div eID="gen2375" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2376" type="x-p"/> Cf. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 20:4">Exodus 20:4</reference>")</hi> , note 2, the threefold giving of the law. The command concerning burnt-offerings and sacrifices was not given to the people till they had broken the decalogue, the law of obedience.

<hi type="bold">carcases</hi> See <reference osisRef="jer 19:11">Jeremiah 19:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 23:10">2 Kings 23:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 6:5">Ezekiel 6:5</reference>. Fulfilled in part in all the destructions of Jerusalem, but with a final look toward <reference osisRef="re 19:17-21">Revelation 19:17-21</reference>. <chapter eID="Jer.7"/><div eID="gen2376" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2377" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="8" osisID="Jer.8" sID="Jer.8"/>

<hi type="bold">repented</hi> <div eID="gen2377" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2378" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:14">Zechariah 8:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.8"/><div eID="gen2378" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2379" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="9" osisID="Jer.9" sID="Jer.9"/>

<hi type="bold">trust</hi> <div eID="gen2379" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2380" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.9"/><div eID="gen2380" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2381" type="x-p"/><chapter n="10" osisID="Jer.10" sID="Jer.10"/>

<hi type="bold">fear</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 19:9">Psalms 19:9</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen2381" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2382" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.10"/>
<div eID="gen2382" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2383" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="11" osisID="Jer.11" sID="Jer.11"/>

<hi type="bold">The word</hi> <div eID="gen2383" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2384" type="x-p"/> This, like the other messages, is made up of rebuke, exhortation, and warning, but in this instance these are based upon the violation of the Palestinian Covenant <reference osisRef="de 28:1-de 30:9">Deuteronomy 28:1-30:9</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi>. The Assyrian and Babylonian captivities of Israel and of Judah were the execution of the warning, <reference osisRef="de 28:63-68">Deuteronomy 28:63-68</reference>.

<hi type="bold">holy flesh</hi><div eID="gen2384" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2385" type="x-p"/> See <reference osisRef="hag 2:12">Haggai 2:12</reference> i.e. to what purpose the "holy flesh" of sacrifices? Its efficacy is "passed from thee" who rejoicest in evil. Cf. <reference osisRef="isa 1:13-15">Isaiah 1:13-15</reference>. <chapter eID="Jer.11"/><div eID="gen2385" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2386" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="12" osisID="Jer.12" sID="Jer.12"/>

<hi type="bold">swelling of Jordan</hi> <div eID="gen2386" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2387" type="x-p"/> i.e. under such a test as in <reference osisRef="jer 49:19">Jeremiah 49:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 50:44"> 50:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="jos 3:15">Joshua 3:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 12:15">1 Chronicles 12:15</reference> <chapter eID="Jer.12"/><div eID="gen2387" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2388" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="13" osisID="Jer.13" sID="Jer.13"/>

<hi type="bold">trusted</hi> <div eID="gen2388" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2389" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen2389" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2390" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.13"/>
<div eID="gen2390" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2391" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="14" osisID="Jer.14" sID="Jer.14"/>

<hi type="bold">dearth</hi> <div eID="gen2391" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2392" type="x-p"/> The significance of a drought at this time was very great. It was one of the signs predicted in the Palestinian Covenant <reference osisRef="de 28:23 de 28:24">Deuteronomy 28:23,24</reference> and already fulfilled in part in the reign of Ahab. <reference osisRef="1ki 17:1">1 Kings 17:1,</reference> etc. As that sign had been followed, even though after a long interval, by the Assyrian captivity of the northern kingdom, it should have been received by Judah as a most solemn warning. <chapter eID="Jer.14"/><div eID="gen2392" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2393" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="15" osisID="Jer.15" sID="Jer.15"/>

<hi type="bold">repenting</hi> <div eID="gen2393" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2394" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:14">Zechariah 8:14</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">the Lord said</hi> <div eID="gen2394" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2395" type="x-p"/> The Remnant, of whom Jeremiah was the representative, are carefully distinguished from the unbelieving mass of the people. The coming captivity, which they must share, for they too have sinned <reference osisRef="jer 15:13">Jeremiah 15:13</reference> though Jehovah's judgment upon the nation, will be but a purifying chastisement to them, and they receive a special promise <reference osisRef="jer 15:11">Jeremiah 15:11</reference>. Verses <reference osisRef="jer 15:15-18">Jeremiah 15:15-18</reference> give the answer of the Remnant to verses <reference osisRef="jer 15:11-14">Jeremiah 15:11-14</reference>. Two things characterize the believing Remnant always-loyal to the word of God, and separation from those who mock at that word <reference osisRef="jer 15:16 jer 15:17">Jeremiah 15:16,17</reference> Cf. <reference osisRef="re 3:8-10">Revelation 3:8-10</reference>.

<hi type="bold">thee</hi> Marg<div eID="gen2395" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2396" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">redeem</hi> <div eID="gen2396" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2397" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thee</hi> Remnant.<div eID="gen2397" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2398" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jer 15:11-21">Jeremiah 15:11-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 23:3-8">Jeremiah 23:3-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 31:7 jer 31:14"> 31:7,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 1:9">Isaiah 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 6:8">Ezekiel 6:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 8:11-14"> 8:11-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 9:4"> 9:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 11:16-21">Ezekiel 11:16-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="joe 2:32">Joel 2:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="am 5:15">Amos 5:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 2:12">Micah 2:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 4:1"> 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 5:3"> 5:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 7:18"> 7:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="zep 2:7">Zephaniah 2:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="zep 3:13"> 3:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="hag 1:14">Haggai 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 8:6">Zechariah 8:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 3:16-18">Malachi 3:16-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen2398" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2399" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">redeem</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ex 14:30">Exodus 14:30</reference>". <chapter eID="Jer.15"/><div eID="gen2399" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2400" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="16" osisID="Jer.16" sID="Jer.16"/>

<hi type="bold">saying</hi> <div eID="gen2400" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2401" type="x-p"/> The sign of the unmarried prophet is interpreted by the context. The whole social life of Judah was about to be disrupted and cease from the land. But note the promises of verses <reference osisRef="jer 16:14-16">Jeremiah 16:14-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 17:7 jer 17:8"> 17:7,8</reference>.

<hi type="bold">The Lord</hi><div eID="gen2401" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2402" type="x-p"/> Or, JEHOVAH. <reference osisRef="ps 83:18">Psalms 83:18</reference>. <div eID="gen2402" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2403" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.16"/>

<hi type="bold">trusteth</hi><div eID="gen2405" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2406" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ps 2:12">Psalms 2:12</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen2406" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2407" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.17"/>
<div eID="gen2407" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2408" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="18" osisID="Jer.18" sID="Jer.18"/>

<hi type="bold">The word</hi> <div eID="gen2408" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2409" type="x-p"/> Israel (the whole nation) a vessel marred in the Potter's hand, is the key to this prophetic strain. But Jehovah will make "it again another vessel" <reference osisRef="jer 18:4">Jeremiah 18:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">repent</hi><div eID="gen2409" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2410" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:14">Zechariah 8:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.18"/><div eID="gen2410" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">repented</hi><div eID="gen2412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2413" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:14">Zechariah 8:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.20"/><div eID="gen2413" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2414" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="22" osisID="Jer.22" sID="Jer.22"/>

<hi type="bold">Coniah</hi> <div eID="gen2414" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2415" type="x-p"/> Contracted from Jeconiah, <reference osisRef="1ch 3:16">1 Chronicles 3:16</reference>. <div eID="gen2415" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv57"/><div sID="gen2416" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Jer.22"/>
<div eID="gen2416" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2417" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="23" osisID="Jer.23" sID="Jer.23"/>

<hi type="bold">restoration</hi> <div eID="gen2417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2418" type="x-p"/> This final restoration is shown to be accomplished after a period of unexampled tribulation <reference osisRef="jer 30:3-10">Jeremiah 30:3-10</reference> and in connection with the manifestation of David's righteous Branch <reference osisRef="jer 23:5">Jeremiah 23:5</reference> who is also Jehovah-tsidkenu <reference osisRef="jer 23:6">Jeremiah 23:6</reference>. The restoration here foretold is not to be confounded with the return of a feeble remnant of Judah under Ezra, Nehemiah, and Zerubbabel at the end of the 70 years <reference osisRef="jer 29:10">Jeremiah 29:10</reference>. At His first advent Christ, David's righteous Branch <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference> did not "execute justice and judgment in the earth," but was crowned with thorns and crucified. Neither was Israel the nation restored, nor did the Jewish people say, "The Lord our righteousness." Cf. <reference osisRef="ro 10:3">Romans 10:3</reference>. The prophecy is yet to be fulfilled. <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>.
<hi type="bold">remnant</hi><div eID="gen2418" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2419" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jer 15:21">Jeremiah 15:21</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Branch</hi><div eID="gen2419" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2420" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 4:2">Isaiah 4:2</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.23"/><div eID="gen2420" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2421" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="25" osisID="Jer.25" sID="Jer.25"/>

<hi type="bold">seventy years</hi> <div eID="gen2421" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2422" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="le 26:33-35">Leviticus 26:33-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ch 36:21">2 Chronicles 36:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:2">Daniel 9:2</reference> The 70 years may be reckoned to begin with the first deportation of Judah to Babylon. <reference osisRef="2ki 24:10-15">2 Kings 24:10-15</reference>. B.C. 604 according to the Assyrian Eponym Canon, or B.C. 606 according to Ussher; or from the final deportation ; <reference osisRef="2ki 25:1-30">2 Kings 25:1-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ch 36:17-20">2 Chronicles 36:17-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 39:8-10">Jeremiah 39:8-10</reference>. B.C. 586 (Assyr. Ep. Canon), or B.C. 588 (Ussher). In the first case the 70 years extend to the decree of Cyrus for the return <reference osisRef="ezr 1:1-3">Ezra 1:1-3</reference> B.C. (Assyr. Ep. Canon), or B.C. 536 (Ussher). In the second case the 70 years terminate B.C. 516 (Assyr.Ep. Canon) with the completion of the temple. The latter is more probable reckoning in the light of <reference osisRef="da 9:25">Daniel 9:25</reference>.
<hi type="bold">Uz</hi><div eID="gen2422" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2423" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Job 1:1">Job 1:1</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Sheshach</hi><div eID="gen2423" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2424" type="x-p"/> A name for Babylon. <reference osisRef="jer 51:41">Jeremiah 51:41</reference>.

<hi type="bold">all the inhabitants</hi><div eID="gen2424" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2425" type="x-p"/> The scope of this great prophecy cannot be limited to the invasion of Nebuchadnezzar. If Jehovah does not spare His own city, should the Gentile nations imagine that there is no judgment for them? The prophecy leaps to the very end of this age. (See "Day of the Lord," <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference> "Armageddon," ; <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21"> 19:11-21</reference>.<div eID="gen2425" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2426" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will call</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 2:12">Isaiah 2:12</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Jer.25"/><div eID="gen2426" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">The word</hi> <div eID="gen2441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2442" type="x-p"/> The writings of Jeremiah in chapters 30 to 36, cannot with certainty be arranged in consecutive order. Certain dates are mentioned (e.g. <reference osisRef="jer 32:1">Jeremiah 32:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 33:1"> 33:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 34:1 jer 34:8"> 34:1,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 35:1"> 35:1</reference> but retrospectively. The narrative, so far as Jeremiah gives a narrative, is resumed at <reference osisRef="jer 37:1">Jeremiah 37:1</reference>. These chapters constitute a kind of summary of prophecy concerning Israel as a nation, looking on especially to the last days, the day of the Lord, and the kingdom-age to follow. If the marginal references are carefully followed the order will become clear. But these prophecies are interspersed with much historical matter concerning Jeremiah and his time.

<hi type="bold">Write</hi><div eID="gen2442" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2443" type="x-p"/> Three "writings" by Jeremiah are to be distinguished:<div eID="gen2443" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) This is impersonal--a general prophecy, and probably the earliest. <reference osisRef="jer 30:1-jer 31:40">Jeremiah 30:1-31:40</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The prophecy destroyed by Jehoiakim. <reference osisRef="jer 1:1-jer 36:23">Jeremiah 1:1-36:23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The destroyed writing re-written doubtless the writing preserved to us. <reference osisRef="jer 36:27">Jeremiah 36:27</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">And it came to pass</hi> <div eID="gen2464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2465" type="x-p"/> Five phases of Jeremiah's prison experiences are recorded:<div eID="gen2465" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) He is arrested in the gate and committed to a dungeon on the false charge of treason <reference osisRef="jer 37:11-15">Jeremiah 37:11-15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) he is released from the dungeon, but restrained to the court of the prison;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) he is imprisoned in the miry dungeon and kept in prison court <reference osisRef="jer 38:1-6">Jeremiah 38:1-6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) he is again released from the dungeon and kept in the prison court <reference osisRef="jer 38:13-28">Jeremiah 38:13-28</reference> until the capture of the city;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) carried in chains from the city by Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard, he is finally released at Ramah. <reference osisRef="jer 40:1-4">Jeremiah 40:1-4</reference>. </item> </list> <chapter eID="Jer.37"/>

<chapter n="1" osisID="Lam.1" sID="Lam.1"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv59"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Lamentations</title> <div sID="gen2505" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="la 1">Read first chapter of Lamentations</reference><div eID="gen2505" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2506" type="x-p"/> The touching significance of this book lies in the fact that it is the disclosure of the love and sorrow of Jehovah for the very people who He is chastening--a sorrow wrought by the Spirit in the heart of Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="jer 13:17">Jeremiah 13:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 23:36 mt 23:38">Matthew 23:36,38</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 9:1-5">Romans 9:1-5</reference>).<div eID="gen2506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2507" type="x-p"/> The chapters indicate the analysis, viz., five lamentations.<div eID="gen2507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2508" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Lam.1"/>
<div eID="gen2508" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2509" type="x-p"/><chapter n="3" osisID="Lam.3" sID="Lam.3"/>

The literary form of Lamentations is necessarily obscured in the translation. It is an acrostic dirge, the line arranged in couplets or triplet, each of which begins with a letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In the third Lament, which consists of sixty-six stanzas instead of twenty-two, each line of each triplet begins with the same letter, so that the entire sixty six verses are required to give the twenty-two letters of the alphabet. Thus verses 1-3 or our version form but three lines of the original, each line beginning with A, etc.

<hi type="bold">redeemed</hi><div eID="gen2509" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2510" type="x-p"/> Heb. "goel," Redemp. (Kinsman type). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Lam.3"/><div eID="gen2510" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen2504" osisID="Lam" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Ezek" sID="gen2511" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Ezek.1" sID="Ezek.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv59"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Ezekiel</title> <div sID="gen2512" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="eze 1">Read first chapter of Ezekiel</reference><div eID="gen2512" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2513" type="x-p"/> Ezekiel was carried away to Babylon between the first and final deportation of Judah (<reference osisRef="2ki 24:11-16">2 Kings 24:11-16</reference>). Like Daniel and the Apostle John, he prophesied out of the land, and his prophecy, like theirs, follows the method of symbol and vision. Unlike the pre-exilic prophets, whose ministry was primarily to either Judah or the ten-tribe kingdom, Ezekiel is the voice of Jehovah to "the whole house of Israel."<div eID="gen2513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2514" type="x-p"/> Speaking broadly, the purpose of his ministry is to keep before the generation born in exile the national sins which had brought Israel so low (e.g. <reference osisRef="eze 14:23">Ezekiel 14:23</reference>); to sustain the faith of the exiles by predictions of national restoration, of the execution of justice upon their oppressors, and of national glory under the Davidic monarchy.<div eID="gen2514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2515" type="x-p"/> Ezekiel is in seven great prophetic strains indicated by the expression, "The hand of the Lord was upon me." (<reference osisRef="eze 1:3">Ezekiel 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 3:14 eze 3:22"> 3:14,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 8:1"> 8:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 33:22"> 33:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 37:1"> 37:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 40:1">Ezekiel 40:1</reference>).<div eID="gen2515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2516" type="x-p"/> The minor divisions are indicated in the text.<div eID="gen2516" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2517" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in Ezekiel cover a period of 21 years (Ussher). <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv59"/><hi type="bold">living creatures</hi><div eID="gen2517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2518" type="x-p"/> The "living creatures" are identical with the Cherubim. The subject is somewhat obscure, but from the position of the Cherubim at the gate of Eden, upon the cover of the ark of the covenant, and in Rev. 4., it is clearly gathered that they have to do with vindication of the holiness of God as against the presumptuous pride of sinful man who, despite his sin, would "put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life" <reference osisRef="ge 3:22-24">Genesis 3:22-24</reference>. Upon the ark of the covenant, of one substance with the mercy-seat, they saw the sprinkled blood which, in type, spake of the perfect maintenance of the divine righteousness by the sacrifice of Christ <reference osisRef="ex 25:17-20">Exodus 25:17-20</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>". See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:26">Romans 3:26</reference>". The living creatures (or Cherubim) appear to be actual beings of the angelic order. Cf. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:isa 6:2">Isaiah 6:2</reference>". The Cherubim or living creatures are not identical with the Seraphim. <reference osisRef="isa 6:2-7">Isaiah 6:2-7</reference>. They appear to have to do with the holiness of God as outraged by sin; the Seraphim with uncleanness in the people of God. The passage in Ezekiel is highly figurative, but the effect was the revelation to the prophet of the Shekinah glory of the Lord. Such revelations are connected invariably with new blessing and service. Cf. ; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2-10">Exodus 3:2-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 6:1-10">Isaiah 6:1-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 10:5-14">Daniel 10:5-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:12-19">Revelation 1:12-19</reference>. <div eID="gen2518" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv60"/><div sID="gen2519" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.1"/>
<div eID="gen2519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2520" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Ezek.2" sID="Ezek.2"/>

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <div eID="gen2520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2521" type="x-p"/> "Son of man," used by our Lord of Himself seventy-nine times, is used by Jehovah ninety one times when addressing Ezekiel.<div eID="gen2521" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) In the case of our Lord the meaning is clear: it is His racial name as the representative Man in the sense of <reference osisRef="1co 15:45-47">1 Corinthians 15:45-47</reference>. The same thought, implying transcendence of mere Judaism, is involved in the phrase when applied to Ezekiel. Israel had forgotten her mission. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 11:10">Genesis 11:10</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="eze 5:5-8">Ezekiel 5:5-8</reference>. Now, in her captivity, Jehovah will not forsake His people, but He will remind them that they are but a small part of the race for whom He also cares. Hence the emphasis upon the word "man." The Cherubim "had the likeness of a man" <reference osisRef="eze 1:5">Ezekiel 1:5</reference> and when the prophet beheld the throne of God, he saw "the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it" <reference osisRef="eze 1:26">Ezekiel 1:26</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>" <reference osisRef="re 1:12 re 1:13">Revelation 1:12,13</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) As used of Ezekiel, the expression indicates, not what the prophet is in himself, but what he is to God; a son of man</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) chosen,</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(b) endued with the Spirit, and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(c) sent of God.</item> </list> <div sID="gen2522" type="x-p"/> All this is true also of Christ who was, furthermore, the representative man--the head of regenerate humanity. <chapter eID="Ezek.2"/><div eID="gen2522" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2523" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Ezek.3" sID="Ezek.3"/>

<hi type="bold">eat it</hi> <div eID="gen2523" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2524" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="eze 2:10">Ezekiel 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 10:9">Revelation 10:9</reference>. Whatever its message, the word of God is sweet to faith because it is the word of God. <div eID="gen2524" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv60"/><div sID="gen2525" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.3"/>
<div eID="gen2525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2526" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Ezek.4" sID="Ezek.4"/>

<hi type="bold">take</hi> <div eID="gen2526" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2527" type="x-p"/> The symbolic actions during the prophet's dumbness were testimonies to the past wickedness and chastisement of the house of Israel (the whole nation), and prophetic of a coming siege. They therefore intermediate between the siege of <reference osisRef="2ki 24:10-16">2 Kings 24:10-16</reference> at which time Ezekiel was carried to Babylon, and the siege of <reference osisRef="2ki 25:1-11">2 Kings 25:1-11</reference> eleven years later. <chapter eID="Ezek.4"/><div eID="gen2527" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2528" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="Ezek.6" sID="Ezek.6"/>

<hi type="bold">remnant</hi> <div eID="gen2528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2529" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jer 15:21">Jeremiah 15:21</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen2529" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv60"/><div sID="gen2530" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.6"/>

<hi type="bold">sixth month</hi> <div eID="gen2531" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2532" type="x-p"/> i.e. September.

<hi type="bold">visions</hi><div eID="gen2532" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2533" type="x-p"/> Visions, that is, of former profanations of the temple, and of the wickedness because of which Israel was then in Babylon, show the prophet that he might justify to the new generation born in Assyria and Babylonia during the captivity, the righteousness of God in the present national chastening. The visions are retrospective; Israel had done these things, hence the captivities. This strain continues to <reference osisRef="eze 33:20">Ezekiel 33:20</reference>. It is the divine view of the national sinfulness and apostasy, revealed to Ezekiel in a series of visions so vivid that though the prophet was by the river Chebar, ; <reference osisRef="eze 1:1 eze 1:3">Ezekiel 1:1,3</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 3:23"> 3:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 10:15 eze 10:20 eze 10:22"> 10:15,20,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 43:3"> 43:3</reference> It was as if he were transported back to Jerusalem, and to the time when these things were occurring. These visions of the sinfulness of Israel are interspersed with promises of restoration and blessing which are yet to be fulfilled. See "Israel" ; <reference osisRef="ge 12:2 ge 12:3">Genesis 12:2,3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:26">Romans 11:26</reference>. Also "Kingdom, (O.T.)" ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen2533" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2534" type="x-p"/> The combined purport of the four visions of profanation in chapter 8., is idolatry set up in the entire temple, even in the holy of holies <reference osisRef="eze 8:10 eze 8:11">Ezekiel 8:10,11</reference> women given over to phallic cults <reference osisRef="eze 8:14">Ezekiel 8:14</reference> and nature-worship <reference osisRef="ex 8:16">Exodus 8:16</reference>.
<hi type="bold">Tammuz</hi><div eID="gen2534" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2535" type="x-p"/> i.e. the Greek Adonis. <chapter eID="Ezek.8"/><div eID="gen2535" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2536" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="9" osisID="Ezek.9" sID="Ezek.9"/>

<hi type="bold">was gone</hi> <div eID="gen2536" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2537" type="x-p"/> It is noteworthy that to Ezekiel the priest was given the vision of the glory of the Lord<div eID="gen2537" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) departing from the Cherubim to the threshold of the temple <reference osisRef="eze 9:3">Ezekiel 9:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 10:4"> 10:4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) from the threshold <reference osisRef="eze 10:18">Ezekiel 10:18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) from temple and city to the mountain on the East of Jerusalem (Olivet, <reference osisRef="eze 11:23">Ezekiel 11:23</reference>) and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) returning to the millennial temple to abide. <reference osisRef="eze 43:2-5">Ezekiel 43:2-5</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">for in</hi><div eID="gen2543" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2544" type="x-p"/> It must constantly be remembered that though the prophet was in Babylonia he prophesies as if in the land, and during the eleven years' interval between the first and final deportation. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 8:3">Ezekiel 8:3</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Ezek.12"/><div eID="gen2544" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2545" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="14" osisID="Ezek.14" sID="Ezek.14"/>

Cf. <reference osisRef="jer 15:1">Jeremiah 15:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 14:16">Ezekiel 14:16,</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 14:18 eze 14:20">Ezekiel 14:18,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 7:16">Jeremiah 7:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 11:14"> 11:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 14:11"> 14:11</reference>. <chapter eID="Ezek.14"/><div eID="gen2546" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">rod</hi><div eID="gen2551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2552" type="x-p"/> The passage is a prophecy of the future judgment upon Israel, regathered from all nations (see "Israel," <reference osisRef="isa 1:24-26">Isaiah 1:24-26</reference> refs. into the old wilderness wanderings. <reference osisRef="eze 20:35">Ezekiel 20:35</reference>. The issue of this judgment determines who of Israel in that day shall enter the land for kingdom blessing. ; <reference osisRef="ps 50:1-7">Psalms 50:1-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 20:33-44">Ezekiel 20:33-44</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 3:2-5">Malachi 3:2-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 4:1 mal 4:2"> 4:1,2</reference> see other judgments,<div eID="gen2552" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2553" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 12:31">John 12:31</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1co 11:31">1 Corinthians 11:31</reference>"<div eID="gen2553" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2554" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Co 5:10">2 Corinthians 5:10</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 25:32">Matthew 25:32</reference>"<div eID="gen2554" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2555" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 20:12">Revelation 20:12</reference>" <div eID="gen2555" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv61"/><div sID="gen2556" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.20"/>

<hi type="bold">repent</hi><div eID="gen2558" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2559" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 8:14">Zechariah 8:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Ezek.24"/><div eID="gen2559" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">Thus</hi> <div eID="gen2560" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2561" type="x-p"/> The prophecies upon Gentile powers, extending to <reference osisRef="eze 32:32">Ezekiel 32:32</reference> have doubtless had partial fulfilments of which history and the present condition of those cities and countries bear witness, but the mention of the day of Jehovah <reference osisRef="eze 30:3">Ezekiel 30:3</reference> makes it evident that a fulfilment in the final sense is still future. See "Day of Jehovah" <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 19:19">Revelation 19:19</reference>")</hi>. Also "Armageddon" <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 19:17">Revelation 19:17</reference>". Those countries are once more to be the battle ground of the nations.

<hi type="bold">Edom</hi><div eID="gen2561" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2562" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="eze 25:12-14">Ezekiel 25:12-14,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 36:1">Genesis 36:1</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Ezek.25"/><div eID="gen2562" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2563" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="28" osisID="Ezek.28" sID="Ezek.28"/>

<hi type="bold">Thou</hi> <div eID="gen2563" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2564" type="x-p"/> Here (<reference osisRef="eze 28:12-15">Ezekiel 28:12-15</reference>), as in <reference osisRef="isa 14:12">Isaiah 14:12</reference> the language goes beyond the king of Tyre to Satan, inspirer and unseen ruler of all such pomp and pride as that of Tyre. Instances of thus indirectly addressing Satan are: ; <reference osisRef="ge 3:14 ge 3:15">Genesis 3:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 16:23">Matthew 16:23</reference>. The unfallen state of Satan is here described; his fall in <reference osisRef="isa 14:12-14">Isaiah 14:12-14</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>")</hi>. But there is more. The vision is not of Satan in his own person, but of Satan fulfilling himself in and through an earthly king who arrogates to himself divine honours, so that the prince of Tyrus foreshadows the Beast. ; <reference osisRef="da 7:8">Daniel 7:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:20">Revelation 19:20</reference>. <div eID="gen2564" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv61"/><div sID="gen2565" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.28"/>

2 Chapter 36<div eID="gen2585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2586" type="x-p"/> A beautiful order is discernible in this and the succeeding prophecies:<div eID="gen2586" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Restoration of the land <reference osisRef="eze 36:1-15">Ezekiel 36:1-15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) of the people <reference osisRef="eze 36:16-eze 37:28">Ezekiel 36:16-37:28</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) judgment on Israel's enemies. <reference osisRef="eze 38:1-eze 39:24">Ezekiel 38:1-39:24</reference>. Afterward follows that which concerns the worship of Jehovah that He may dwell amongst His people. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv61"/><div sID="gen2587" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Ezek.36"/>
<div eID="gen2587" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2588" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="37" osisID="Ezek.37" sID="Ezek.37"/>

<hi type="bold">bones</hi> <div eID="gen2588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2589" type="x-p"/> Having announced <reference osisRef="eze 36:24-38">Ezekiel 36:24-38</reference> the restoration of the nation, Jehovah now gives in vision and symbol the method of its accomplishment. <reference osisRef="eze 37:11">Ezekiel 37:11</reference> gives the clue. The "bones" are the whole house of Israel who shall then be living. The "graves" are the nations where they dwell. The order of procedure is:<div eID="gen2589" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the bringing of the people out <reference osisRef="eze 37:12-14 eze 37:19-27">Ezekiel 37:12-14,19-27</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the bringing of them in (<reference osisRef="eze 37:12">Ezekiel 37:12</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) their conversion (<reference osisRef="eze 37:13">Ezekiel 37:13</reference>)</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the filling with the Spirit (<reference osisRef="eze 37:14">Ezekiel 37:14</reference>).</item> </list> <div sID="gen2590" type="x-p"/> The symbol follows. The two sticks are Judah and the ten tribes; united, they are one nation (<reference osisRef="eze 37:19-21">Ezekiel 37:19-21</reference>). Then follows (<reference osisRef="eze 37:21-27">Ezekiel 37:21-27</reference>) the plain declaration as to Jehovah's purpose, and <reference osisRef="eze 37:28">Ezekiel 37:28</reference> implies that then Jehovah will become known to the Gentiles in a marked way. This is also the order of <reference osisRef="ac 15:16 ac 15:17">Acts 15:16,17</reference> and the two passages strongly indicate the time of full Gentile conversion. See also <reference osisRef="isa 11:10">Isaiah 11:10</reference>. <chapter eID="Ezek.37"/><div eID="gen2590" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen2591" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="38" osisID="Ezek.38" sID="Ezek.38"/>

<hi type="bold">Gog</hi> <div eID="gen2591" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2592" type="x-p"/> That the primary reference is to the northern (European) powers, headed up by Russia, all agree. The whole passage should be read in connection with <reference osisRef="zec 12:1-4">Zechariah 12:1-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 14:1-9"> 14:1-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:14-30">Matthew 24:14-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 14:14-20">Revelation 14:14-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:17-21"> 19:17-21,</reference> "gog" is the prince, "Magog," his land. The reference to Meshech and Tubal (Moscow and Tobolsk) is a clear mark of identification. Russia and the northern powers have been the latest persecutors of dispersed Israel, and it is congruous both with divine justice and with the covenants (e.g. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>" that destruction should fall at the climax of the last mad attempt to exterminate the remnant of Israel in Jerusalem. The whole prophecy belongs to the yet future "day of Jehovah" ; <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference> and to the battle of Armageddon <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 19:19">Revelation 19:19</reference>" but includes also the final revolt of the nations at the close of the kingdom-age. <reference osisRef="re 20:7-9">Revelation 20:7-9</reference>.
