<div canonical="true" osisID="Matt" sID="gen3087" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>

<chapter n="1" osisID="Matt.1" sID="Matt.1"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Matthew</title> <div sID="gen3088" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 1">Read first chapter of Matthew</reference><div eID="gen3088" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3089" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The writer of the first Gospel, as all agree, was Matthew, called also Levi, a Jew of Galilee who had taken service as a tax-gatherer under the Roman oppressor. He was, therefore, one of the hated and ill-reputed publicans.<div eID="gen3089" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3090" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of Matthew has been much discussed, but no convincing reason has been given for the discrediting the traditional date of A.D. 37.<div eID="gen3090" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3091" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The scope and purpose of the book are indicated in the first verse. Matthew is the "book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham" (<reference osisRef="mt 1:1">Matthew 1:1</reference>). This connects him at once with two of the most important of the Old Testament Covenants: the Davidic Covenant of kingship, and the Abrahamic Covenant of promise. ; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-16">2 Samuel 7:8-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>.<div eID="gen3091" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3092" type="x-p"/> Of Jesus Christ in that twofold character, then, Matthew writes. Following the order indicated in the first verse, he writes first of the King, the son of David; then of the Son of Abraham, obedient unto death, according to the Isaac type <reference osisRef="ge 22:1-18">Genesis 22:1-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 11:17-19">Hebrews 11:17-19</reference>.<div eID="gen3092" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3093" type="x-p"/> But the prominent character of Christ in Matthew is that of the covenanted King, David's "righteous Branch" <reference osisRef="jer 23:5">Jeremiah 23:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 33:15"> 33:15</reference>. Matthew records His genealogy; His birth in Bethlehem the city of David, according to <reference osisRef="mic 5:2">Micah 5:2,</reference> the ministry of His forerunner according to Malachi <reference osisRef="mal 3:1">Malachi 3:1</reference>. His rejection by Israel; and His predictions of His second coming in power and great glory.<div eID="gen3093" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3094" type="x-p"/> Only then (Matthew 26-28) does Matthew turn to the earlier covenant, and record the sacrificial death of the son of Abraham.<div eID="gen3094" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3095" type="x-p"/> This determines the purpose and structure of Matthew. It is peculiarly the Gospel for Israel; and, as flowing from the death of Christ, a Gospel for the whole world.<div eID="gen3095" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3096" type="x-p"/> Matthew falls into three principal divisions:<div eID="gen3096" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The manifestation to Israel and rejection of Jesus Christ the Son of David, born King of the Jews, 1:1-25:46. The subdivisions of this part are:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The official genealogy and birth of the King, 1:1-25;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The infancy and obscurity of the King, 2:1-23;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The kingdom "at hand," 3:1-12:50 (the order of events of this subdivision is indicated in the text);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The mysteries of the kingdom, 13:1-52;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The ministry of the rejected King, 13:53-23:39;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The promise of the King to return in power and great glory, 24:1-25:46.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The sacrifice and resurrection of Jesus Christ, the Son of Abraham, 26:1-28:8.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The risen Lord in ministry to His own, 28:9-20.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3097" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in Matthew cover a period of 38 years (Ussher). <chapter eID="Matt.1"/><div eID="gen3097" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3098" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="1" osisID="Matt.1" sID="Matt.1"/>
<hi type="bold">Josias</hi> <div eID="gen3098" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3099" type="x-p"/> Josiah, <reference osisRef="1ki 13:2">1 Kings 13:2</reference>

1 Six Marys 2 of whom was born 3 Christ<div eID="gen3099" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3100" type="x-p"/> 1 Six Marys<div eID="gen3100" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3101" type="x-p"/> 1 Six Marys are to be distinguished in the N.T.:<div eID="gen3101" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the mother of Jesus; always clearly identified by the context.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Mary Magdalene, a woman of Magdala, " out of whom went seven demons" <reference osisRef="lu 8:2">Luke 8:2</reference> She is never mentioned apart from the identifying word "Magdalene."</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The mother of James (called "the less," <reference osisRef="mr 15:40">Mark 15:40</reference>) and Joses, the apostles. A comparison of ; <reference osisRef="joh 19:25">John 19:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 27:56">Matthew 27:56</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:40">Mark 15:40</reference> establishes the inference that this Mary, the mother of James the less, and of Joses was the wife of Alphaeus (called also Cleophas), <reference osisRef="joh 19:25">John 19:25</reference> and a sister of Mary the mother of Jesus. Except in ; <reference osisRef="mt 27:61">Matthew 27:61</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 28:1"> 28:1</reference> where she is called "the other Mary (i.e. "other" than her sister, Mary the Virgin); and <reference osisRef="joh 19:25">John 19:25</reference> where she is called "of Cleophas," she is mentioned only in connection with one or both of her sons.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Mary of Bethany, sister of Martha and Lazarus, mentioned by name only in <reference osisRef="lu 10:39-42">Luke 10:39-42</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 11:1-2 joh 11:19-20 joh 11:28 joh 11:31-32 joh 11:45">John 11:1,2,19,20,28,31,32,45</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:3"> 12:3</reference> but referred to in ; <reference osisRef="mt 26:7">Matthew 26:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:3-9">Mark 14:3-9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The mother of John Mark and sister of Barnabas <reference osisRef="ac 12:12">Acts 12:12</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) A helper of Paul in Rome <reference osisRef="ro 16:6">Romans 16:6</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3102" type="x-p"/> 2 of whom was born<div eID="gen3102" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3103" type="x-p"/> 2 The changed expression here is important. It is no longer, "who begat," but, "Mary, of whom was born Jesus." Jesus was not begotten of natural generation.<div eID="gen3103" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3104" type="x-p"/> 3 Christ<div eID="gen3104" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3105" type="x-p"/> 3 Christ (Christos=anointed), the Greek form of the Hebrew "Messiah" <reference osisRef="da 9:25 da 9:26">Daniel 9:25,26</reference> is the official name of our Lord, as Jesus is his human name ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31">Luke 1:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 2:21"> 2:21</reference>. The name, or title, "Christ" connects Him with the entire O.T. foreview <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi> of a coming prophet <reference osisRef="de 18:15-19">Deuteronomy 18:15-19,</reference> Priest <reference osisRef="ps 110:4">Psalms 110:4</reference> and king <reference osisRef="2sa 7:7-10">2 Samuel 7:7-10</reference>. As these were typically anointed with oil ; <reference osisRef="1ki 19:16">1 Kings 19:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 29:7">Exodus 29:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 16:13">1 Samuel 16:13</reference> so Jesus was anointed with the Holy Spirit ; <reference osisRef="mt 3:16">Matthew 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 1:10 mr 1:11">Mark 1:10,11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 3:21 lu 3:22">Luke 3:21,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:32 joh 1:33">John 1:32,33</reference> thus becoming officially "the Christ."

<hi type="bold">save</hi> See note, <reference osisRef="ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3105" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3106" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sins</hi> See note, <reference osisRef="ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">of the Lord</hi><div eID="gen3106" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3107" type="x-p"/> See <reference osisRef="isa 7:14">Isaiah 7:14</reference> Lit. by the Lord through the prophet.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen3107" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3108" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">JESUS</hi> <div eID="gen3108" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3109" type="x-p"/> The Greek form of the Hebrew Jehoshua meaning saviour. <div eID="gen3109" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><div sID="gen3110" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.1"/>
<div eID="gen3110" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3111" type="x-p"/><chapter n="2" osisID="Matt.2" sID="Matt.2"/>

4 Herod the king<div eID="gen3111" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3112" type="x-p"/> Called Herod the Great, son of Antipater, an Idumean <reference osisRef="ge 36:1">Genesis 36:1</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 36:1">Genesis 36:1</reference>")</hi> and Cypros, an Arabian woman. Antipater was appointed procurator of Judea by Julius Caesar, B.C. 47. At the age of fifteen Herod was appointed to the government of Galilee. B.C. 40 the Roman senate made him king of Judea. An able, strong, and cruel man, he increased greatly the splendour of Jerusalem, erecting the temple which was the centre of Jewish worship in the time of our Lord.

<hi type="bold">King</hi><div eID="gen3112" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3113" type="x-p"/> "The King" is one of the divine titles <reference osisRef="ps 10:16">Psalms 10:16</reference> and so used in the worship of the Church <reference osisRef="1ti 1:17">1 Timothy 1:17</reference> but Christ is never called "King of the Church." He is "King of the Jews" <reference osisRef="mt 2:2">Matthew 2:2</reference> and Lord and "Head of the Church" <reference osisRef="eph 1:22 eph 1:23">Ephesians 1:22,23</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>" ; <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>

<hi type="bold">Scribes</hi><div eID="gen3113" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3114" type="x-p"/> (Greek - "<w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w>" = "writer") Heb. "spherim," "to write," "set in order," "count." The scribes were so called because it was their office to make copies of the Scriptures; to classify and teach the precepts of oral law <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:7">Matthew 3:7</reference>")</hi> and to keep careful count of every letter in the O.T. writings. Such an office was necessary in a religion of law and precept, and was an O.T. function <reference osisRef="2sa 8:17">2 Samuel 8:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 20:25"> 20:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ki 4:3">1 Kings 4:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 8:8">Jeremiah 8:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 36:10 jer 36:12 jer 36:26"> 36:10,12,26</reference>. To this legitimate work the scribes added a record of rabbinical decisions on questions of ritual (Halachoth); the new code resulting from those decisions (Mishna); the Hebrew sacred legends (Gemara, forming with the Mishna the Talmud); commentaries on the O.T. (Midrashim); reasonings upon these (Hagada); and finally, mystical interpretations which found in Scripture meanings other than the grammatical, lexical, and obvious ones (the Kabbala); not unlike the allegorical method of Origen, or the modern Protestant "spiritualizing" interpretation. In our Lord's time, to receive this mass of writing superposed upon the Scriptures was to be orthodox; to return to the Scriptures themselves was heterodoxy--our Lord's most serious offence.

<hi type="bold">Out of Egypt</hi><div eID="gen3114" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3115" type="x-p"/> The words quoted are in <reference osisRef="ho 11:1">Hosea 11:1</reference> and the passage illustrates the truth that prophetic utterances often have a latent and deeper meaning than at first appears. Israel, nationally, was a "<reference osisRef="so 1:1">Song 1:1</reference>" <reference osisRef="ex 4:22">Exodus 4:22</reference> but Christ was the greater "<reference osisRef="so 1:1">Song 1:1</reference>" ; <reference osisRef="ro 9:4 ro 9:5">Romans 9:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 41:8">Isaiah 41:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 42:1-4"> 42:1-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 52:13 isa 52:14"> 52:13,14</reference> where the servant-nation and the Servant-Son are both in view.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen3115" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3116" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Archelaus</hi> <div eID="gen3116" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3117" type="x-p"/> Son of Herod the Great, <reference osisRef="mt 2:1">Matthew 2:1</reference> and Malthace, a Samaritan woman. Deposed A.D. 6.

<hi type="bold">He shall be called</hi><div eID="gen3117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3118" type="x-p"/> Probably referring to <reference osisRef="isa 11:1">Isaiah 11:1</reference> where Christ is spoken of as "a netzer (or, 'rod') out of the stem of Jesse." <div eID="gen3118" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><div sID="gen3119" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.2"/>
<div eID="gen3119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3120" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Matt.3" sID="Matt.3"/>

<hi type="bold">He shall be called</hi> <div eID="gen3120" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3121" type="x-p"/> Probably referring to <reference osisRef="isa 11:1">Isaiah 11:1</reference> where Christ is spoken of as "a netzer (or, 'rod') out of the stem of Jesse."

<div eID="gen3121" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The phrase, kingdom of heaven (lit. of the heavens), is peculiar to Matthew and signifies the Messianic earth rule of Jesus Christ, the Son of David. It is called the kingdom of the heavens because it is the rule of the heavens over the earth <reference osisRef="mt 6:10">Matthew 6:10</reference> The phrase is derived from Daniel, where it is defined ; <reference osisRef="da 2:34-36 da 2:44">Daniel 2:34-36,44</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 7:23-27">Daniel 7:23-27</reference> as the kingdom which the God of heaven will set up after the destruction by "the stone cut out without hands," of the Gentile world-system. It is the kingdom covenanted to David's seed <reference osisRef="2sa 7:7-10">2 Samuel 7:7-10</reference> described in the prophets; <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi> and confirmed to Jesus the Christ, the Son of Mary, through the angel Gabriel <reference osisRef="lu 1:32 lu 1:33">Luke 1:32,33</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The kingdom of heaven has three aspects in Matthew:</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) "at hand" from the beginning of the ministry of John the Baptist <reference osisRef="mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference> to the virtual rejection of the King, and the announcement of the new brotherhood <reference osisRef="mt 12:46-50">Matthew 12:46-50</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) in seven "mysteries of the kingdom of heaven," to be fulfilled during the present age <reference osisRef="mt 13:1-52">Matthew 13:1-52</reference> to which are to be added the parables of the kingdom of heaven which were spoken after those of Mt. 13., and which have to do with the sphere of Christian profession during this age;</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(c) the prophetic aspect--the kingdom to be set up after the return of the King in glory. <reference osisRef="mt 24:29-mt 25:46">Matthew 24:29-25:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 19:12-19">Luke 19:12-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference> See "Kingdom (N.T.)" ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:33">Luke 1:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:28">1 Corinthians 15:28</reference> Cf. "Kingdom of God," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>")</hi>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3122" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saying</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 17:30">Acts 17:30</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen3122" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3123" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Pharisees</hi><div eID="gen3123" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3124" type="x-p"/> So called from a Heb. word meaning "separate." After the ministry of the post-exilic prophets ceased, godly men called "Chasidim" (saints) arose who sought to keep alive reverence for the law amongst the descendants of the Jews who returned from the Babylonian captivity. This movement degenerated into the Pharisaism of our Lord's day-- a letter-strictness which overlaid the law with traditional interpretations held to have been communicated by Jehovah to Moses as oral explanations of equal authority with the law itself. (cf. <reference osisRef="mt 15:2 mt 15:3">Matthew 15:2,3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 7:8-13">Mark 7:8-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 1:14">Galatians 1:14</reference>).<div eID="gen3124" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3125" type="x-p"/> The Pharisees were strictly a sect. A member was "chaber" (i.e. "knit together,") <reference osisRef="jud 20:11">Judges 20:11</reference> and took an obligation to remain true to the principles of Pharisaism. They were correct, moral, zealous, and self-denying, but self-righteous <reference osisRef="lu 18:9">Luke 18:9</reference> and destitute of the sense of sin and need <reference osisRef="lu 7:39">Luke 7:39</reference>. They were the foremost prosecutors of Jesus Christ and the objects of His unsparing denunciation (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="mt 23:13-29">Matthew 23:13-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 11:42 lu 11:43">Luke 11:42,43</reference><div eID="gen3125" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3126" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Sadducees</hi> <div eID="gen3126" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3127" type="x-p"/> Not strictly a sect, but rather those amongst the Jews who denied the existence of angels or other spirits, and all miracles, especially the resurrection. They were the religious rationalists of the time <reference osisRef="mr 12:18-23">Mark 12:18-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:15-17">Acts 5:15-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 23:8"> 23:8</reference> and strongly entrenched in the Sanhedrin and priesthood ; <reference osisRef="ac 4:1">Acts 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:17"> 5:17</reference>. They are identified with no affirmative doctrine, but were mere deniers of the supernatural.

<hi type="bold">Suffer it to be so</hi><div eID="gen3127" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3128" type="x-p"/> Why one who needed no repentance should insist upon receiving a rite which signified confession (<reference osisRef="mt 3:6">Matthew 3:6</reference>) and repentance (<reference osisRef="mt 3:11">Matthew 3:11</reference>) is nowhere directly explained. It may be suggested:<div eID="gen3128" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) That Jesus was now to receive His anointing with the Holy Spirit (<reference osisRef="mt 3:16">Matthew 3:16</reference>) unto His threefold office of Prophet, Priest, and King. In the Levitical order <reference osisRef="ex 29:4-7">Exodus 29:4-7</reference> the high priest was first washed, then anointed. While Christ's priestly work did not begin till He "offered Himself without spot to God" <reference osisRef="heb 9:14">Hebrews 9:14</reference> and His full manifestation as the King- Priest after the order of Melchizedek awaits the kingdom <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>")</hi> yet He was then anointed, once for all.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) But John's baptism was the voice of God to Israel, and the believing remnant responded (<reference osisRef="mt 3:5">Matthew 3:5</reference>). It was an act of righteousness on the part of Him who had become, as to the flesh, an Israelite, to take His place with this believing remnant.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3129" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Jesus</hi><div eID="gen3129" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3130" type="x-p"/> For the first time the Trinity, foreshadowed in many ways in the O.T., is fully manifested. The Spirit descends upon the Son, and at the same moment the Father's voice is heard from heaven. <div eID="gen3130" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><div sID="gen3131" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.3"/>
<div eID="gen3131" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3132" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Matt.4" sID="Matt.4"/>

<hi type="bold">Then was Jesus</hi> <div eID="gen3132" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3133" type="x-p"/> The temptation of Christ, the "last Adam" <reference osisRef="1co 15:45">1 Corinthians 15:45</reference> is best understood when contrasted with that of the "first man Adam." Adam was tempted in his place of lord of creation, a lordship with but one reservation, the knowledge of good and evil ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 2:16 ge 2:17"> 2:16,17</reference>. Through the woman he was tempted to add that also to his dominion. Falling, he lost all. But Christ had taken the place of a lowly Servant, acting only from and in obedience to the Father. ; <reference osisRef="php 2:5-8">Philippians 2:5-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:19">John 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:57"> 6:57</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:28 joh 8:54"> 8:28,54</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 41:8">Isaiah 41:8</reference>")</hi> that He might redeem a fallen race and a creation under the curse ; <reference osisRef="ge 3:17-19">Genesis 3:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:19-23">Romans 8:19-23</reference>. Satan's one object in the threefold temptation was to induce Christ to act from Himself, in independency of His Father. The first two temptations were a challenge to Christ from the god of this world to prove Himself indeed the Son of God (<reference osisRef="mt 4:3 mt 4:6">Matthew 4:3,6</reference>). The third was the offer of the usurping prince of this world to divest himself of that which rightfully belonged to Christ as Son of man and Son of David, on the condition that He accept the sceptre on Satan's world-principles (cf. <reference osisRef="joh 18:36">John 18:36</reference>). See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>". Christ defeated Satan by a means open to His humblest follower, the intelligent use of the word of God (<reference osisRef="mt 4:4 mt 4:7">Matthew 4:4,7</reference>). In his second temptation Satan also used Scripture, but a promise available only to one in the path of obedience. The scene give emphasis to the vital importance of "rightly dividing the word of truth" <reference osisRef="2ti 2:15">2 Timothy 2:15</reference>.

<hi type="bold">holy city</hi><div eID="gen3133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3134" type="x-p"/> In the N.T. one Greek word, hagios, in its various forms, is rendered, "holy," "holiness," "sanctify," "sanctified," "sanctification." Like the heb. qodesh, it signifies "set apart for God." The important references follow <reference osisRef="mt 4:5">Matthew 4:5,</reference> marg.<div eID="gen3134" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3135" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:5">Matthew 4:5</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">angels</hi> <div eID="gen3135" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3136" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen3136" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3137" type="x-p"/> The Greek word kosmos means "order," "arrangement," and so, with the Greeks, "beauty"; for order and arrangement in the sense of system are at the bottom of the Greek conception of beauty.<div eID="gen3137" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3138" type="x-p"/> When used in the N.T. of humanity, the "world" of men, it is organized humanity-- humanity in families, tribes, nations--which is meant. The word for chaotic, unorganized humanity--the mere mass of man is thalassa, the "sea" of men (e.g.) <reference osisRef="re 13:1">Revelation 13:1</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi>. For "world" (kosmos) in the bad ethical sense, "world system" <reference osisRef="joh 7:7">John 7:7</reference>.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">at hand</hi><div eID="gen3138" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3139" type="x-p"/> "At hand" is never a positive affirmation that the person or thing said to be "at hand" will immediately appear, but only that no known or predicted event must intervene. When Christ appeared to the Jewish people, the next thing in the order of revelation as it then stood, should have been the setting up of the Davidic kingdom. In the knowledge of God, not yet disclosed, lay the rejection of the kingdom (and King), the long period of the mystery-form of the kingdom, the world-wide preaching of the cross, and the out-calling of the Church. But this was as yet locked up in the secret counsels of God. <reference osisRef="mt 13:11 mt 13:17">Matthew 13:11,17</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:3-10">Ephesians 3:3-10</reference>.<div eID="gen3139" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3140" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> See note 2, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:2">Matthew 5:2</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3140" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3141" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">is at hand</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>. For Another Point of View: See Topic 301207 <div eID="gen3141" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv93"/><div sID="gen3142" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv93"/> <hi type="bold">two brethren</hi> <div eID="gen3142" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3143" type="x-p"/> Peter and John were already disciples, <reference osisRef="joh 1:35-42">John 1:35-42</reference>. This is a call to service.

<hi type="bold">James</hi><div eID="gen3143" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3144" type="x-p"/> Two persons are called by this name in the N.T.<div eID="gen3144" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) James the son of Zebedee, an apostle <reference osisRef="mt 10:2">Matthew 10:2</reference> and the brother of the apostle John, apart from whom he is never mentioned, and with whom, together with Peter, he was admitted to the especial intimacy of our Lord. ; <reference osisRef="mt 17:1">Matthew 17:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 5:37">Mark 5:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 9:2"> 9:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:33"> 14:33</reference> He was martyred by Herod. <reference osisRef="ac 12:2">Acts 12:2</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) A son of Alphaeus (or Cleopas) and Mary the sister of Mary the mother of Jesus. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 1:16">Matthew 1:16</reference>")</hi> and brother of Joses. <reference osisRef="mr 15:40">Mark 15:40</reference>. He was, therefore, a cousin of the Lord Jesus. He is called James "the less" <reference osisRef="mr 15:40">Mark 15:40</reference> lit. little, i.e. of shorter stature than James the son of Zebedee). He was an apostle. <reference osisRef="mt 10:3">Matthew 10:3</reference> It has been conjectured that "Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus" <reference osisRef="mt 10:3">Matthew 10:3</reference> was identical with the Juda of <reference osisRef="lu 6:16">Luke 6:16</reference> who is there called "of i.e. 'son' or 'brother' as is has been variously translated] James." A Juda is mentioned with a James and Joses and Simon in <reference osisRef="mr 6:3">Mark 6:3</reference> as "brother" of our Lord (See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 13:55">Matthew 13:55,</reference> marg.). <reference osisRef="mt 13:55">Matthew 13:55</reference>. The Gospels mention no other James who could be called the brother of the Lord Jesus, but James the less was certainly the son of Alphaeus and Mary the sister of our Lord's mother. The conclusion seems, therefore most probable that ; <reference osisRef="mt 10:3">Matthew 10:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 13:55"> 13:55</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 3:18">Mark 3:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 6:3"> 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 6:15">Luke 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:13">Acts 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:17"> 12:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:13">Mark 15:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 21:18"> 21:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 1:19">Galatians 1:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:9 ga 2:12">Galatians 2:9,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 1:1">James 1:1</reference> refer to James the less, son of Alphaeus and Mary, and cousin, or, according to Jewish usage, "brother" of the Lord Jesus. He was the author of the Epistle of James. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv94"/><div sID="gen3145" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv94"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen3145" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3146" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">possessed</hi><div eID="gen3146" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3147" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G1139">δαιμονίζομαι</w> ," demonized; <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Matt.4"/><div eID="gen3147" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3148" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Matt.5" sID="Matt.5"/>

<hi type="bold">And he opened his mouth</hi> <div eID="gen3148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3149" type="x-p"/> Having announced the kingdom of heaven as "at hand," the King, in Mat 5.-7., declares the principles of the kingdom. The Sermon on the Mount has a twofold application:<div eID="gen3149" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) literally to the kingdom. In this sense it gives the divine constitution for the righteous government of the earth. Whenever the kingdom of heaven is established on earth it will be according to that constitution, which may be regarded as an explanation of the word "righteousness" as used by the prophets in describing the kingdom (e.g.) <reference osisRef="isa 11:4 isa 11:5">Isaiah 11:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 32:1"> 32:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:24">Daniel 9:24</reference> In this sense the Sermon on the Mount is pure law, and transfers the offence from the overt act to the motive. <reference osisRef="mt 5:21 mt 5:22 mt 5:27 mt 5:28">Matthew 5:21,22,27,28</reference>. Here lies the deeper reason why the Jews rejected the kingdom. They had reduced "righteousness" to mere ceremonialism, and the Old Testament idea of the kingdom to a mere affair of outward splendour and power. They were never rebuked for expecting a visible and powerful kingdom, but the words of the prophets should have prepared them to expect also that only the poor in spirit and the meek could share in it (e.g.) <reference osisRef="isa 11:4">Isaiah 11:4</reference>. The seventy-second Psalm, which was universally received by them as a description of the kingdom, was full of this. For these reasons, the Sermon on the Mount in its primary application gives neither the privilege nor the duty of the Church. These are found in the Epistles. Under the law of the kingdom, for example, no one may hope for forgiveness who has not first forgiven. <reference osisRef="mt 6:12 mt 6:14 mt 6:15">Matthew 6:12,14,15</reference>. Under grace the Christian is exhorted to forgive because he is already forgiven. <reference osisRef="eph 4:30-32">Ephesians 4:30-32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) But there is a beautiful moral application to the Christian. It always remains true that the poor in spirit, rather than the proud, are blessed, and those who mourn because of their sins, and who are meek in the consciousness of them, will hunger and thirst after righteousness, and hungering, will be filled. The merciful are "blessed," the pure in heart do "see God." These principles fundamentally reappear in the teaching of the Epistles.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3150" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saying</hi> The beatific character, unattainable by effort, is wrought in the believer by the Spirit, <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23">Galatians 5:22,23</reference>. For Another Point of View: See Topic 301232 <div eID="gen3150" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv95"/><div sID="gen3151" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv95"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen3151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3152" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen3152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3153" type="x-p"/> "kosmos" = "mankind." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">I am not come to destroy</hi><div eID="gen3153" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3154" type="x-p"/> Christ's relation to the law of Moses may be thus summarized:<div eID="gen3154" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) He was made under the law <reference osisRef="ga 4:4">Galatians 4:4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He lived in perfect obedience to the law <reference osisRef="joh 8:46">John 8:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 17:5">Matthew 17:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:21-23">1 Peter 2:21-23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) he was a minister of the law to the Jews, clearing it from rabbinical sophistries, enforcing it in all its pitiless severity upon those who professed to obey it (e.g.) <reference osisRef="lu 10:25-37">Luke 10:25-37</reference> but confirming the promises made to the fathers under the Mosaic Covenant <reference osisRef="ro 15:8">Romans 15:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) He fulfilled the types of the law by His holy life and sacrificial death <reference osisRef="heb 9:11-26">Hebrews 9:11-26</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) He bore, vicariously, the curse of the law that the Abrahamic Covenant might avail all who believe <reference osisRef="ga 3:13 ga 3:14">Galatians 3:13,14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) He brought out by His redemption all who believe from the place of servants under the law into the place of sons <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-7">Galatians 4:1-7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) He mediated by His blood the New Covenant of assurance and grace in which all believers stand <reference osisRef="ro 5:2">Romans 5:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 8:6-13">Hebrews 8:6-13</reference> so establishing the "law of Christ" <reference osisRef="ga 6:2">Galatians 6:2</reference> with its precepts of higher exaltation made possible by the indwelling Spirit. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv96"/><div sID="gen3155" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv96"/> <hi type="bold">righteousness</hi> <div eID="gen3155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3156" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 5:6 mt 5:10 mt 5:20">Matthew 5:6,10,20</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">hell fire</hi><div eID="gen3156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3157" type="x-p"/> Gr. "Geenna" = Gehenna, the place in the valley of Hinnom where, anciently, human sacrifices were offered. <reference osisRef="2ch 33:6">2 Chronicles 33:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 7:31">Jeremiah 7:31</reference> The word occurs, ; <reference osisRef="mt 5:22 mt 5:29 mt 5:30">Matthew 5:22,29,30</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 10:28"> 10:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 18:9"> 18:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 23:15 mt 23:33"> 23:15,33</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 9:43 mr 9:45 mr 9:47">Mark 9:43,45,47</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 12:5">Luke 12:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 3:6">James 3:6</reference>. In every instance except the last the word comes from the lips of Jesus Christ in most solemn warning of the consequences of sin. He describes it as the place where "their" worm never dies and of fire never to be quenched. The expression is identical in meaning with "lake of fire". ; <reference osisRef="re 19:20">Revelation 19:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10 re 20:14 re 20:15"> 20:10,14,15</reference>.<div eID="gen3157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3158" type="x-p"/> See "Death, the second" (<reference osisRef="joh 8:24">John 8:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 21:8">Revelation 21:8</reference>); also <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 21:8">Revelation 21:8</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:lu 16:23">Luke 16:23</reference>".

<hi type="bold">paid</hi><div eID="gen3158" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3159" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="isa 40:2">Isaiah 40:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ru 1:21 ru 1:22">Ruth 1:21,22</reference>

<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><div eID="gen3159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3160" type="x-p"/> The word implies full development, growth into maturity of godliness, not sinless perfection. <reference osisRef="eph 4:12 eph 4:13">Ephesians 4:12,13</reference>. In this passage the Father's kindness, not His sinlessness, is the point in question. <reference osisRef="lu 6:35 lu 6:36">Luke 6:35,36</reference> <div eID="gen3160" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv97"/><div sID="gen3161" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.5"/>
<div eID="gen3161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3162" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="Matt.6" sID="Matt.6"/>

<hi type="bold">alms</hi> <div eID="gen3162" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3163" type="x-p"/> Or, righteous acts. The word refers to religious externalities. These may be seen of men, but that must not be the motive.
<hi type="bold">reward</hi><div eID="gen3163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3164" type="x-p"/> i.e. the reward they have sought.
<hi type="bold">reward</hi><div eID="gen3164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3165" type="x-p"/> i.e. the praise of men.

<hi type="bold">kingdom come</hi><div eID="gen3165" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3166" type="x-p"/> vs. <reference osisRef="mt 11:27-30">Matthew 11:27-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">we forgive our debtors</hi><div eID="gen3166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3167" type="x-p"/> This is legal ground. Cf. <reference osisRef="eph 4:32">Ephesians 4:32</reference> which is grace. Under law forgiveness is conditioned upon a like spirit in us; under grace we are forgiven for Christ's sake, and exhorted to forgive because we have been forgiven. ; <reference osisRef="mt 18:32">Matthew 18:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:28"> 26:28</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 26:28">Matthew 26:28</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3167" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3168" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301235<div eID="gen3168" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3169" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">debts</hi> sin<div eID="gen3169" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3170" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">reward</hi><div eID="gen3170" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3171" type="x-p"/> i.e. the praise of men.
<hi type="bold">take no thought</hi><div eID="gen3171" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3172" type="x-p"/> Or, have no anxiety. <reference osisRef="mt 6:34">Matthew 6:34</reference>.

<hi type="bold">kingdom of God</hi><div eID="gen3172" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3173" type="x-p"/> The kingdom of God is to be distinguished from the kingdom of heaven <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi> , in five respects:<div eID="gen3173" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The kingdom of God is universal, including all moral intelligences willingly subject to the will of God, whether angels, the Church, or saints of past or future dispensations <reference osisRef="lu 13:28 lu 13:29">Luke 13:28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:22 heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:22,23</reference> while the kingdom of heaven is Messianic, mediatorial, and Davidic, and has for its object the establishment of the kingdom of God in the earth <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="1co 15:24 1co 15:25">1 Corinthians 15:24,25</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The kingdom of God is entered only by the new birth <reference osisRef="joh 3:3 joh 3:5-7">John 3:3,5-7</reference> the kingdom of heaven, during this age, is the sphere of a profession which may be real or false. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:3">Matthew 13:3</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="mt 25:1 mt 25:11 mt 25:12">Matthew 25:1,11,12</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Since the kingdom of heaven is the earthly sphere of the universal kingdom of God, the two have almost all things in common. For this reason many parables and other teachings are spoken of the kingdom of heaven in Matthew, and of the kingdom of God in Mark and Luke. It is the omissions which are significant. The parables of the wheat and tares, and of the net <reference osisRef="mt 13:24-30 mt 13:36-43 mt 13:47-50">Matthew 13:24-30,36-43,47-50</reference> are not spoken of the kingdom of God. In that kingdom there are neither tares nor bad fish. But the parable of the leaven <reference osisRef="mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference> is spoken of the kingdom of God also, for, alas, even the true doctrines of the kingdom are leavened with the errors of which the Pharisees, Sadducees, and the Herodians were the representatives. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The kingdom of God "comes not with outward show" <reference osisRef="lu 17:20">Luke 17:20</reference> but is chiefly that which is inward and spiritual <reference osisRef="ro 14:17">Romans 14:17</reference> while the kingdom of heaven is organic, and is to be manifested in glory on the earth. (See "Kingdom (O.T.)," <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8,</reference> note; (N.T.), ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24,</reference> note; <reference osisRef="mt 17:2">Matthew 17:2,</reference> note.) <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi> , <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 17:2">Matthew 17:2</reference>"</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The kingdom of heaven merges into the kingdom of God when Christ, having put all enemies under his feet, "shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father" <reference osisRef="1co 15:24-28">1 Corinthians 15:24-28</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi> </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv97"/><div sID="gen3174" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.6"/>
<div eID="gen3174" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3175" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="7" osisID="Matt.7" sID="Matt.7"/>
<hi type="bold">judge not</hi> <div eID="gen3175" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3176" type="x-p"/> In the sense of condemnation.
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3176" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3177" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Devils</hi><div eID="gen3177" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3178" type="x-p"/> Devils, lit demons. To the reality and personality of demons the N.T. scriptures bear abundant testimony. As to their origin nothing is clearly revealed, but they are not to be confounded with the angels mentioned in <reference osisRef="2pe 2:4">2 Peter 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>.<div eID="gen3178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3179" type="x-p"/> Summary: Demons are spirits <reference osisRef="mt 12:43 mt 12:45">Matthew 12:43,45</reference> are Satan's emissaries ; <reference osisRef="mt 12:26 mt 12:27">Matthew 12:26,27</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:41"> 25:41</reference> and so numerous as to make Satan's power practically ubiquitous. <reference osisRef="mr 5:9">Mark 5:9</reference>. They are capable of entering and controlling both men and beasts <reference osisRef="mr 5:8 mr 5:11-13">Mark 5:8,11-13</reference> and earnestly seek embodiment, without which, apparently, they are powerless for evil. ; <reference osisRef="mt 12:43 mt 12:44">Matthew 12:43,44</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 5:10-12">Mark 5:10-12</reference>. Demon influence and demon possession are discriminated in the N. T. Instances of the latter are ; <reference osisRef="mt 4:24">Matthew 4:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 8:16 mt 8:28 mt 8:33">Matthew 8:16,28,33</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 9:32"> 9:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 12:22"> 12:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 1:32">Mark 1:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 5:15 mr 5:16 mr 5:18"> 5:15,16,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 8:35">Luke 8:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 8:7">Acts 8:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 16:16"> 16:16</reference>. They are unclean, sullen, violent, and malicious ; <reference osisRef="mt 8:28">Matthew 8:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 9:23"> 9:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 10:1"> 10:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 12:43">Matthew 12:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 1:23">Mark 1:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 5:3-5"> 5:3-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 9:17 mr 9:20"> 9:17,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 6:18">Luke 6:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 9:39"> 9:39</reference>. They know Jesus Christ as Most High God, and recognize His supreme authority ; <reference osisRef="mt 8:31 mt 8:32">Matthew 8:31,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 1:24">Mark 1:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 19:15">Acts 19:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:19">James 2:19</reference>. They know their eternal fate to be one of torment ; <reference osisRef="mt 8:29">Matthew 8:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 8:31">Luke 8:31</reference>. They inflict physical maladies ; <reference osisRef="mt 12:22">Matthew 12:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 17:15-18"> 17:15-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 13:16">Luke 13:16</reference> but mental disease is to be distinguished from the disorder of mind due to demonical control. Demon influence may manifest itself in religion asceticism and formalism <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1-3">1 Timothy 4:1-3</reference> degenerating into uncleanness <reference osisRef="2pe 2:10-12">2 Peter 2:10-12</reference>. The sign of demon influence in religion is departing from the faith, i.e. the body of revealed truth in the Scriptures. <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1">1 Timothy 4:1</reference>. The demons maintain especially a conflict with believers who would be spiritual. ; <reference osisRef="eph 6:12">Ephesians 6:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1-3">1 Timothy 4:1-3</reference>. All unbelievers are open to demon possession <reference osisRef="eph 2:2">Ephesians 2:2</reference>. The believer's resources, prayer and bodily control <reference osisRef="mt 17:21">Matthew 17:21</reference> "the whole armour of God" <reference osisRef="eph 6:13-18">Ephesians 6:13-18</reference>. Exorcism in the name of Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="ac 16:18">Acts 16:18</reference> was practised for demon possession. One of the awful features of the apocalyptic judgments in which this age will end is an irruption of demons out the abyss. <reference osisRef="re 9:1-11">Revelation 9:1-11</reference>.

<hi type="bold">work iniquity</hi><div eID="gen3179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3180" type="x-p"/> sin, lawlessness. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Matt.7"/><div eID="gen3180" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3181" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="8" osisID="Matt.8" sID="Matt.8"/>

<hi type="bold">behold, there came a leper</hi> <div eID="gen3181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3182" type="x-p"/> The King, having in Chapters 5.-7. declared the principles of the kingdom, makes proof, in Chapters 8., 9., of His power to banish from the earth the consequences of sin, and to control the elements of nature.<div eID="gen3182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3183" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Lord</hi> <div eID="gen3183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3184" type="x-p"/> Gr. Kurios. The first occurrence of the word is applied to Jesus with His evident sanction. In itself the word means "master," and is so used of mere human relationships in, e.g. <reference osisRef="mt 6:24">Matthew 6:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 15:27"> 15:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 13:35">Mark 13:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 6:9">Ephesians 6:9</reference> Both uses, divine and human, are brought together in <reference osisRef="col 4:1">Colossians 4:1</reference>. It is the (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G111">ἀθέμιτος</w> Heb). "Adonai." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:2">Genesis 15:2</reference>")</hi> , and is so used by Jesus Christ in <reference osisRef="mt 22:43-35">Matthew 22:43-35</reference>. In the N.T. the distinctive uses of Kurios (Lord) are:<div eID="gen3184" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) As the N.T. translation of the Heb. Jehovah (Lord), e.g. <reference osisRef="mt 1:20 mt 1:22">Matthew 1:20,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 2:15"> 2:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 3:3"> 3:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 4:7 mt 4:10"> 4:7,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 11:25"> 11:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:9"> 21:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 12:29 mr 12:30">Mark 12:29,30</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:68">Luke 1:68</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 2:9"> 2:9</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Jesus Himself so uses Kurios, e.g. <reference osisRef="mt 4:7 mt 4:10">Matthew 4:7,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 11:25"> 11:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 12:11">Mark 12:11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) But the great use of Kurios is as the divine title of Jesus, the Christ. In this sense it occurs in the N.T. 663 times. That the intent is to identify Jesus Christ with the O.T. Deity is evident from <reference osisRef="mt 3:3">Matthew 3:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 12:8"> 12:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:9"> 21:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 118:26">Psalms 118:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 22:43-45">Matthew 22:43-45</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:43">Luke 1:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:58">John 8:58</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 14:8-10"> 14:8-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:28">John 20:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:5">Acts 9:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:33"> 13:33</reference>. (Psa.2.). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 20:28">John 20:28</reference>")</hi>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">possessed</hi><div eID="gen3187" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3188" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G1139">δαιμονίζομαι</w> - "demonized"). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen3188" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3189" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 2:1">Ezekiel 2:1</reference>")</hi>. Our Lord thus designates Himself about eighty times. It is His racial name as the representative Man, in the sense of <reference osisRef="1co 15:45-47">1 Corinthians 15:45-47</reference> as Son of David is distinctly his Jewish name, and Son of God His divine name. Our Lord constantly uses this term as implying that his mission (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="mt 11:19">Matthew 11:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 19:10">Luke 19:10</reference>. His death and resurrection (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="mt 12:40">Matthew 12:40</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 20:18"> 20:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:2"> 26:2</reference> and His second coming (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:37-44">Matthew 24:37-44</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 12:40">Luke 12:40</reference> transcended in scope and result all merely Jewish imitations. When Nathanael confesses him as "King of Israel," our Lord's answer is, "Thou shalt see greater things... the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man." When His messengers are cast out by the Jews, His thought leaps forward to the time when the Son of man shall come, not then to Israel only but to the race ; <reference osisRef="mt 10:5 mt 10:6">Matthew 10:5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 8:23"> 8:23</reference>. It is in this name, also, that universal judgment is committed to Him <reference osisRef="joh 5:22 joh 5:27">John 5:22,27</reference>. It is also a name indicating that in Him is fulfilled the O.T. foreview of blessing through a coming man. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>" ; <reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 12:3"> 12:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 8:4">Psalms 8:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 80:17"> 80:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 7:14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 9:6 isa 9:7"> 9:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 32:2"> 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 13:7">Zechariah 13:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 32:2">Isaiah 32:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 13:7">Zechariah 13:7</reference>.

<hi type="bold">apostles</hi> <div eID="gen3201" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3202" type="x-p"/> The word apostle, = "one sent forth," is used of our Lord <reference osisRef="heb 3:1">Hebrews 3:1</reference>. Elsewhere it is used for the twelve who were called to that office by our Lord during His earth ministry; of Paul, called to the apostleship by the risen and ascended Lord, and of Barnabas <reference osisRef="ac 14:14">Acts 14:14</reference> specially designated by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="ac 13:2">Acts 13:2</reference>. Of Matthias, chosen by lot by the eleven to take the place of Judas Iscariot, <reference osisRef="ac 1:16-26">Acts 1:16-26</reference> it is said: "And he was numbered with the eleven." <reference osisRef="ac 1:26">Acts 1:26</reference>.<div eID="gen3202" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3203" type="x-p"/> The "signs" of an apostle were<div eID="gen3203" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) They were chosen directly by the Lord Himself, or, as in the case of Barnabas, by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="mt 10:1 mt 10:2">Matthew 10:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 3:13 mr 3:14">Mark 3:13,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 6:13">Luke 6:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:6 ac 9:15">Acts 9:6,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:2"> 13:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 22:10 ac 22:14 ac 22:15"> 22:10,14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 1:1">Romans 1:1</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) They were endued with sign gifts, miraculous powers which were the divine credentials of their office <reference osisRef="mt 10:1">Matthew 10:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:15 ac 5:16">Acts 5:15,16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 16:16-18"> 16:16-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 28:8 mt 28:9">Matthew 28:8,9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Their relation to the kingdom was that of heralds, announcing to Israel only <reference osisRef="mt 10:5 mt 10:6">Matthew 10:5,6</reference> the kingdom as at hand. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:17">Matthew 4:17</reference>")</hi> and manifesting kingdom powers <reference osisRef="mt 10:7 mt 10:8">Matthew 10:7,8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) To one of them, Peter, the keys of the kingdom of heaven, viewed as the sphere of Christian profession, as in Mat 13, were given <reference osisRef="mt 16:19">Matthew 16:19</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Their future relation to the king will be that of judges over the twelve tribes <reference osisRef="mt 19:28">Matthew 19:28</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Consequent upon the rejection of the kingdom, and the revelation of the mystery hid in God <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:1-12">Ephesians 3:1-12</reference> the Church, the apostolic office was invested with a new enduement, the baptism with the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="ac 2:1-4">Acts 2:1-4</reference> a new power, that of imparting the Spirit to Jewish-Christian believers; a new relation, that of foundation stones of the new temple <reference osisRef="eph 2:20-22">Ephesians 2:20-22</reference> and a new function, that of preaching the glad tidings of salvation through a crucified and risen Lord to Jew and gentile alike.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) The indispensable qualification of an apostle was that he should have been an eye- witness of the resurrection <reference osisRef="ac 1:22">Acts 1:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 9:1">1 Corinthians 9:1</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3204" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">James son of Zebedee</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:21">Matthew 4:21</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Gentiles</hi><div eID="gen3204" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3205" type="x-p"/> The kingdom was promised to the Jews. Gentiles could be blessed only through Christ crucified and risen. Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 12:20-24">John 12:20-24</reference>.

<hi type="bold">lost sheep</hi><div eID="gen3205" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3206" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w>)." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>")</hi>. Also, <reference osisRef="mt 15:24 mt 15:26">Matthew 15:24,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:46">Acts 13:46</reference>.

<hi type="bold">devils</hi><div eID="gen3206" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3207" type="x-p"/> demons. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Provide neither gold</hi><div eID="gen3207" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3208" type="x-p"/> (Cf) <reference osisRef="mr 6:8 mr 6:9">Mark 6:8,9</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 9:3">Luke 9:3</reference>. The central thought here, urgency, must be kept in mind. The emphasis is upon "provide." Time is not to be taken to search for additional staves or shoes. The disciples were to go in their ordinary sandals, with such staff as they might have, or with none. Cf. Paul, <reference osisRef="ro 1:15">Romans 1:15</reference>.

<hi type="bold">send</hi><div eID="gen3208" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3209" type="x-p"/> The scope of <reference osisRef="mt 10:16-23">Matthew 10:16-23</reference> reaches beyond the personal ministry of the twelve, covering in a general sense the sphere of service during the present age. <reference osisRef="mt 10:23">Matthew 10:23</reference> has in view the preaching of the remnant. <reference osisRef="isa 1:9">Isaiah 1:9</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>")</hi> in the tribulation <reference osisRef="ps 2:5">Psalms 2:5</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 7:14">Revelation 7:14</reference>". and immediately preceding the return of Christ in glory ; <reference osisRef="de 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:9-11">Acts 1:9-11</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ac 1:11">Acts 1:11</reference>". The remnant then will not have gone over the cities of Israel till the Lord comes.
<hi type="bold">for it shall be given</hi><div eID="gen3209" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3210" type="x-p"/> An instruction to martyrs, not to preachers.
<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen3210" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3211" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Beelzebub</hi><div eID="gen3211" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3212" type="x-p"/> Beelzebul, title of a heathen deity.
<hi type="bold">hell</hi><div eID="gen3212" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3213" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:22">Matthew 5:22</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">peace</hi><div eID="gen3213" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3214" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 14:27">John 14:27</reference>. Peace is spoken of in Scripture in three ways:<div eID="gen3214" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) "Peace with God" <reference osisRef="ro 5:1">Romans 5:1</reference> this is the work of Christ into which the individual enters by faith ; <reference osisRef="eph 2:14-17">Ephesians 2:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 5:1">Romans 5:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) "The peace of God" <reference osisRef="php 4:7">Philippians 4:7</reference> inward peace, the state of soul of that believer who, having entered into peace with God through faith in Christ, has also committed to God through prayer and supplication with thanksgiving all his anxieties ; <reference osisRef="lu 7:50">Luke 7:50</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 4:6">Philippians 4:6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Peace "on earth" <reference osisRef="lu 2:14">Luke 2:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 72:7">Psalms 72:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 85:10"> 85:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 9:6 isa 9:7">Isaiah 9:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 11:1-12"> 11:1-12</reference> the universal prevalency of peace in the earth under the kingdom. <reference osisRef="mt 10:34">Matthew 10:34</reference> was Christ's warning that the truth which He was proclaiming would not bring in the kingdom age of peace, but conflict rather. <reference osisRef="joh 14:27">John 14:27</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">blessed</hi> <div eID="gen3217" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3218" type="x-p"/> In prison, the King rejected, John's faith wavers; the Lord exhorts and encourages His servant. Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 15:20">John 15:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 42:3">Isaiah 42:3</reference>.

<hi type="bold">greater</hi><div eID="gen3218" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3219" type="x-p"/> Positionally greater, not morally. John the Baptist was as great morally, as any man "born of woman," but as to the kingdom he but announced it at hand. The kingdom did not then come, but was rejected, and John was martyred, and the King presently crucified. The least in the kingdom when it is set up in glory (see "Kingdom (N.T.)") <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference> will be in the fullness of power and glory. It is not heaven which is in question, but Messiah's kingdom. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>".<div eID="gen3219" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3220" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">suffereth violence</hi> <div eID="gen3220" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3221" type="x-p"/> It has been much disputed whether the "violence" here is external, as against the kingdom in the persons of John the Baptist and Jesus; or that, considering the opposition of the scribes and Pharisees, only the violently resolute would press into it. Both things are true. The King and His herald suffered violence, and this is the primary and greater meaning, but also, some were resolutely becoming disciples. CF <reference osisRef="lu 16:16">Luke 16:16</reference>.

<hi type="bold">this is Elias</hi><div eID="gen3221" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3222" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 17:10">Matthew 17:10</reference>")</hi>. Also, <reference osisRef="mt 17:12">Matthew 17:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 4:5">Malachi 4:5</reference>

<hi type="bold">Then</hi><div eID="gen3224" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3225" type="x-p"/> The kingdom of heaven announced as "at hand" by John the Baptist, by the King Himself, and by the twelve, and attested by mighty works, has been morally rejected. The places chosen for the testing of the nation, Chorazin, Bethsaida, etc. having rejected both John and Jesus, the rejected King now speaks of judgment. The final official rejection is later. <reference osisRef="mt 27:31-37">Matthew 27:31-37</reference>.<div eID="gen3225" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3226" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301190<div eID="gen3226" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3227" type="x-p"/> For Additional Factors See Topic 301199 <div eID="gen3227" type="x-p"/>
