<hi type="bold">All things</hi><div eID="gen3229" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3230" type="x-p"/> Kingdom, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 12:3">Matthew 12:3</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Come</hi><div eID="gen3230" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3231" type="x-p"/> The new message of Jesus. The rejected King now turns from the rejecting nation and offers, not the kingdom, but rest and service to such in the nation as are conscious of the need. It is a pivotal point in the ministry of Jesus. <div eID="gen3231" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv100"/><div sID="gen3232" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.11"/>
<div eID="gen3232" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3233" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="12" osisID="Matt.12" sID="Matt.12"/>

<hi type="bold">sabbath</hi> <div eID="gen3233" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The sabbath ("cessation") appears in Scripture as the day of God's rest in the finished work of creation. <reference osisRef="ge 2:2 ge 2:3">Genesis 2:2,3</reference>. For 2500 years of human life absolutely no mention is made of it. Then the sabbath was revealed ; <reference osisRef="ex 16:23">Exodus 16:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="ne 9:13 ne 9:14">Nehemiah 9:13,14,</reference> made a part of the law <reference osisRef="ex 20:8-11">Exodus 20:8-11</reference> and invested with the character of a "sign" between Jehovah and Israel, and a perpetual reminder to Israel of their separation to God <reference osisRef="ex 31:13-17">Exodus 31:13-17</reference>. It was observed by complete rest <reference osisRef="ex 35:2 ex 35:3">Exodus 35:2,3</reference> and by Jehovah's express order a man was put to death for gathering sticks on the sabbath day. <reference osisRef="nu 15:32-36">Numbers 15:32-36</reference>. Apart from maintaining the continued burnt-offering <reference osisRef="nu 28:9">Numbers 28:9,</reference> and its connection with the annual feasts ; <reference osisRef="ex 12:16">Exodus 12:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="le 23:3 le 23:8">Leviticus 23:3,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 28:25">Numbers 28:25</reference> the seventh day sabbath was never made a day of sacrifice, worship, or any manner of religious service. It was simply and only a day of complete rest for man and beast, a humane provision for man's needs. In Christ's words, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." <reference osisRef="mr 2:27">Mark 2:27</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Our Lord found the observance of the day encrusted with rabbinical evasions <reference osisRef="mt 12:2">Matthew 12:2</reference> and restrictions, wholly unknown to the law, so that He was Himself held to be a sabbath breaker by the religious authorities of the time. The sabbath will be again observed during the kingdom age <reference osisRef="isa 66:23">Isaiah 66:23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The Christian first day perpetuates in the dispensation of grace the principle that one-seventh of the time is especially sacred, but in all other respects is in contrast with the sabbath. One is the seventh day, the other the first. The sabbath commemorates God's creation rest, the first day Christ's resurrection. On the seventh day God rested, on the first day Christ was ceaselessly active. The sabbath commemorates a finished creation, the first day a finished redemption. The sabbath was a day of legal obligation, the first day one of voluntary worship and service. The sabbath is mentioned in the Acts only in connection with the Jews, and in the rest of the N.T. but twice. <reference osisRef="col 2:16">Colossians 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 4:4">Hebrews 4:4</reference>. In these passages the seventh day sabbath is explained to be to the Christian not a day to be observed, but a type of the present rest into which he enters when "he also ceases from his own works" and trusts Christ. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv100"/><div sID="gen3234" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv100"/> <hi type="bold">what David did</hi> <div eID="gen3234" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3235" type="x-p"/> Jesus' action <reference osisRef="mt 12:1-7">Matthew 12:1-7</reference> is highly significant. "What David did" refers to the time of his rejection and persecution by Saul. <reference osisRef="1sa 21:6">1 Samuel 21:6</reference>. Jesus here is not so much the rejected Saviour as the rejected King; hence the reference to David.
<hi type="bold">shewbread</hi><div eID="gen3235" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3236" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 25:30">Exodus 25:30</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Gentiles</hi><div eID="gen3236" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3237" type="x-p"/> This too is most significant. The rejected King of Israel will turn to the Gentiles (cf.) <reference osisRef="mt 10:5 mt 10:6">Matthew 10:5,6</reference>. In fulfilment this awaited the official rejection, crucifixion, and resurrection of Christ, and the final rejection of the risen Christ. ; <reference osisRef="lu 24:46 lu 24:47">Luke 24:46,47</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:15">Acts 9:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:46"> 13:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 28:25-28">Acts 28:25-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:11">Romans 11:11</reference>.

<hi type="bold">possessed</hi><div eID="gen3237" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3238" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G1139">δαιμονίζομαι</w>," demonized). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">devils</hi><div eID="gen3238" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3239" type="x-p"/> demons. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">sin</hi> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3239" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3240" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">blasphemy</hi> Ascribing to Satan the work of the Holy Spirit. Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 12:24 mt 12:32 mt 12:40">Matthew 12:24,32,40</reference>.

<hi type="bold">generation</hi><div eID="gen3240" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3241" type="x-p"/> Progeny. <reference osisRef="mt 3:7">Matthew 3:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 23:33"> 23:33</reference>.

<hi type="bold">The men of Nineveh</hi><div eID="gen3241" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3242" type="x-p"/> Again the rejected King announces judgment (cf) <reference osisRef="mt 11:20-24">Matthew 11:20-24</reference> Israel, in the midst of the Pharisaic revival of outward religious strictness, was like a man out of whom a demon had "gone," i.e, of his own volition. He would come back and find an empty house, etc. The personal application is to a mere self-cleansed moralist.<div eID="gen3242" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3243" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Nineveh</hi> vs. <reference osisRef="jon 3:5-9">Jonah 3:5-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 11:32">Luke 11:32</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Na 1:1">Nahum 1:1</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">generation</hi><div eID="gen3243" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3244" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 24:34">Matthew 24:34</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">While</hi><div eID="gen3244" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3245" type="x-p"/> Rejected by Israel, His "kinsmen according to the flesh" (cf) <reference osisRef="ro 9:3">Romans 9:3</reference> our Lord intimates the formation of the new family of faith which, overstepping mere racial claims, receives "whosoever" will be His disciple. ; <reference osisRef="mt 12:49 mt 12:50">Matthew 12:49,50</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:28 joh 6:29">John 6:28,29</reference>.<div eID="gen3245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3246" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301191<div eID="gen3246" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3247" type="x-p"/> Additional Factors to Consider: See Topic 301372 <chapter eID="Matt.12"/><div eID="gen3247" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3248" type="x-p"/><chapter n="13" osisID="Matt.13" sID="Matt.13"/>

The seven parables of Mat 13., called by our Lord, "mysteries of the kingdom of heaven" (<reference osisRef="mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>), taken together, describe the result of the presence of the Gospel in the world during the present age, that is, the time of seed sowing which began with our Lord's personal ministry, and ends with the "harvest" <reference osisRef="mt 13:40-43">Matthew 13:40-43</reference>. Briefly, the result is mingled tares and wheat, good fish and bad, in the sphere of Christian profession. It is Christendom.<div eID="gen3248" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3249" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">sower</hi> <div eID="gen3249" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3250" type="x-p"/> The figure marks a new beginning. To labour in God's vineyard Israel, <reference osisRef="isa 5:1-7">Isaiah 5:1-7</reference> is one thing, to go forth sowing the seed of the word in a field which is the world, quite another (cf) <reference osisRef="mt 10:5">Matthew 10:5</reference>. One fourth of the seed takes permanent root, but the result is "wheat" ; <reference osisRef="mt 13:25">Matthew 13:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:23">1 Peter 1:23</reference> or "children of the kingdom" <reference osisRef="mt 13:38">Matthew 13:38</reference>. This parable <reference osisRef="mt 13:3-9 mt 13:18-23">Matthew 13:3-9,18-23</reference> is treated throughout as foundational to the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. It is interpreted by our Lord Himself.

<hi type="bold">mysteries</hi><div eID="gen3250" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3251" type="x-p"/> A "mystery" in Scripture is a previously hidden truth, now divinely revealed; but in which a supernatural element still remains despite the revelation. The greater mysteries are:<div eID="gen3251" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The mysteries of the kingdom of heaven <reference osisRef="mt 13:3-50">Matthew 13:3-50</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the mystery of Israel's blindness during this age <reference osisRef="ro 11:25">Romans 11:25</reference> (with context);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the mystery of the translation of living saints at the end of this age <reference osisRef="1co 15:51 1co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:51,52</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the mystery of N.T. church as one body composed of Jew and Gentile <reference osisRef="eph 3:1-11">Ephesians 3:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 16:25">Romans 16:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 6:19">Ephesians 6:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 4:3">Colossians 4:3</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the mystery of the church as the bride of Christ <reference osisRef="eph 5:28-32">Ephesians 5:28-32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the mystery of the inliving Christ <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:26 col 1:27">Colossians 1:26,27</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the "mystery of God even Christ," i.e. Christ as the incarnate fullness of the Godhead embodied, in whom all the divine wisdom for man subsists <reference osisRef="col 2:2 col 2:9">Colossians 2:2,9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 2:7">1 Corinthians 2:7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(8) the mystery of the processes by which godlikeness is restored to man <reference osisRef="1ti 3:16">1 Timothy 3:16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(9) the mystery of iniquity <reference osisRef="2th 2:7">2 Thessalonians 2:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(10) the mystery of the seven stars <reference osisRef="re 1:20">Revelation 1:20</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(11) the mystery of Babylon <reference osisRef="re 17:5 re 17:7">Revelation 17:5,7</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3252" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">prophets</hi><div eID="gen3252" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3253" type="x-p"/> The O.T. prophets saw in blended vision the rejection and crucifixion of the King (see "Christ, sacrifice,) <reference osisRef="ge 4:4">Genesis 4:4,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 10:18">Hebrews 10:18</reference>")</hi> and also His glory as David's Son. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>", but "what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glory that should follow," was not revealed to them--only that the vision was not for themselves. <reference osisRef="1pe 1:10-12">1 Peter 1:10-12</reference>. That revelation Christ makes in these parables. A period of time is to intervene between His sufferings and His glory. That interval is occupied with the "mysteries of the kingdom of heaven" here described.<div eID="gen3253" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3254" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteous</hi> Righteousness. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">parable</hi><div eID="gen3254" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3255" type="x-p"/> This parable <reference osisRef="mt 13:24-30">Matthew 13:24-30</reference> is also interpreted by our Lord <reference osisRef="mt 13:36-43">Matthew 13:36-43</reference>. Here the "good seed" is not the "word," as in the first parable <reference osisRef="mt 13:19 mt 13:23">Matthew 13:19,23</reference> but rather that which the word has produced. <reference osisRef="1pe 1:23">1 Peter 1:23,</reference> viz.: the children of the kingdom. These are, providentially <reference osisRef="mt 13:37">Matthew 13:37</reference> "sown," i.e. scattered, here and there in the "field" of the "world" <reference osisRef="mt 13:38">Matthew 13:38</reference>. The "world" here is both geographical and ethnic--the earth-world, and also the world of men. The wheat of God at once becomes the scene of Satan's activity. Where children of the kingdom are gathered, there "among the wheat" <reference osisRef="mt 13:25 mt 13:38 mt 13:39">Matthew 13:25,38,39</reference>. Satan "sows" "children of the wicked one," who profess to be children of the kingdom, and in outward ways are so like the true children that only the angels may, in the end, be trusted to separate them <reference osisRef="mt 13:28-30 mt 13:40-43">Matthew 13:28-30,40-43</reference>. So great is Satan's power of deception that the tares often really suppose themselves to be children of the kingdom <reference osisRef="mt 7:21-23">Matthew 7:21-23</reference>. Many other parables and exhortations have this mingled condition in view (e.g.)<div eID="gen3255" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3256" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 22:11-14">Matthew 22:11-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:1-30"> 25:1-13,14-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:10-14">Luke 18:10-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 6:4-9">Hebrews 6:4-9</reference><div eID="gen3256" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3257" type="x-p"/> Indeed, it characterizes Matthew from Chapter 13 to the end. The parable of the wheat and tares is not a description of the world, but of that which professes to be the kingdom. Mere unbelievers are never the children of the devil, but only religious unbelievers are so called (cf) <reference osisRef="mt 13:38">Matthew 13:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:38-44">John 8:38-44</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 23:15">Matthew 23:15</reference>.<div eID="gen3257" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3258" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">The kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Gather</hi><div eID="gen3258" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3259" type="x-p"/> The gathering of the tares into bundles for burning does not imply immediate judgment. At the end of this age (<reference osisRef="mt 13:40">Matthew 13:40</reference>) the tares are set apart for burning, but first the wheat is gathered into the barn. ; <reference osisRef="joh 14:3">John 14:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.

<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3259" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3260" type="x-p"/> 2 Another parable<div eID="gen3260" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3261" type="x-p"/> The parable of the Mustard Seed prefigures the rapid but unsubstantial growth of the mystery form of the kingdom from an insignificant beginning <reference osisRef="ac 1:15">Acts 1:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:41"> 2:41</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:26">1 Corinthians 1:26</reference> to a great place in the earth. The figure of the fowls finding shelter in the branches is drawn from <reference osisRef="da 4:20-22">Daniel 4:20-22</reference>. How insecure was such a refuge the context in Daniel shows.<div eID="gen3261" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3262" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Another parable</hi><div eID="gen3262" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3263" type="x-p"/> That interpretation of the parable of the Leaven (<reference osisRef="mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference>) which makes (with variation as to details) the leaven to be the Gospel, introduced into the world ("three measures of meal") by the church, and working subtly until the world is converted ("till the whole was leavened") is open to fatal objection:<div eID="gen3263" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) it does violence to the unvarying symbolical meaning of leaven, and especially to the meaning fixed by our Lord Himself. <reference osisRef="mt 16:6-12">Matthew 16:6-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 8:15">Mark 8:15</reference> See "Leaven," <reference osisRef="ge 19:3">Genesis 19:3</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The implication of a converted world in this age ("till the whole was leavened"), is explicitly contradicted by our Lord's interpretation of the parables of the Wheat and Tares, and of the Net. Our Lord presents a picture of a partly converted kingdom in an unconverted world; of good fish and bad in the very kingdom-net itself.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The method of the extension of the kingdom is given in the first parable. It is by sowing seed, not by mingling leaven. The symbols have, in Scripture, a meaning fixed by inspired usage. Leaven is the principle of corruption working subtly; is invariably used in a bad sense (see "Leaven," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 19:3">Genesis 19:3</reference>")</hi> ), and is defined by our Lord as evil doctrine. <reference osisRef="mt 16:11 mt 16:12">Matthew 16:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 8:15">Mark 8:15</reference>. Meal, on the contrary, was used in one of the sweet- savour offerings <reference osisRef="le 2:1-3">Leviticus 2:1-3</reference>. and was food for the priests <reference osisRef="le 6:15-17">Leviticus 6:15-17</reference>. A woman, in the bad ethical sense, always symbolizes something out of place, religiously, See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:zec 5:6">Zechariah 5:6</reference>". In Thyatira it was a woman teaching (cf). ; <reference osisRef="re 2:20">Revelation 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 17:1-6"> 17:1-6</reference>. Interpreting the parable by these familiar symbols, it constitutes a warning that the true doctrine, given for nourishment of the children of the kingdom ; <reference osisRef="mt 4:4">Matthew 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 4:6">1 Timothy 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:2">1 Peter 2:2</reference> would be mingled with corrupt and corrupting false doctrine, and that officially, by the apostate church itself ; <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1-3">1 Timothy 4:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 2:17 2ti 2:18">2 Timothy 2:17,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3 2ti 4:4"> 4:3,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:1-3">2 Peter 2:1-3</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3264" type="x-p"/> 4 Leaven<div eID="gen3264" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3265" type="x-p"/> Summary:<div eID="gen3265" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Leaven, as a symbolic or typical substance, is always mentioned in the O.T. in an evil sense <reference osisRef="ge 19:3">Genesis 19:3,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 19:3">Genesis 19:3</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The use of the word in the N.T. explains its symbolic meaning. It is "malice and wickedness," as contrasted with "sincerity and truth" <reference osisRef="1co 5:6-8">1 Corinthians 5:6-8,</reference> it is evil doctrine <reference osisRef="mt 16:12">Matthew 16:12</reference> in its three-fold form of Pharisasism, Sadduceeism, Herodianism ; <reference osisRef="mt 16:6">Matthew 16:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 8:15">Mark 8:15</reference>. The leaven of the Pharisees was externalism in religion. <reference osisRef="mt 23:14 mt 23:16 mt 23:23-28">Matthew 23:14,16,23-28,</reference> of the Sadducees, scepticism as to the supernatural and as to the Scriptures <reference osisRef="mt 22:23 mt 22:29">Matthew 22:23,29,</reference> of the Herodians, worldliness--a Herod party amongst the Jews ; <reference osisRef="mt 22:16-21">Matthew 22:16-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 3:6">Mark 3:6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The use of the word in <reference osisRef="mt 13:33">Matthew 13:33</reference> is congruous with its universal meaning. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv101"/><div sID="gen3266" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv101"/><hi type="bold">world</hi> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3266" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3267" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">devil</hi><div eID="gen3267" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3268" type="x-p"/> Satan. Br. diabolos, accuser. See note, <reference osisRef="mt 16:23">Matthew 16:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 3:1">Genesis 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3268" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3269" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angels</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3269" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3270" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angels</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3270" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3271" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3271" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3272" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">them which do</hi> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Then</hi><div eID="gen3272" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3273" type="x-p"/> The kingdom does not become the kingdom of the "Father" until Christ, having "put all enemies under his feet," including the last enemy, death, has "delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father" <reference osisRef="1co 15:24-28">1 Corinthians 15:24-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:2">Revelation 20:2</reference>. There is triumph over death at the first resurrection <reference osisRef="1co 15:54 1co 15:55">1 Corinthians 15:54,55</reference> but death, "the last enemy," is not destroyed till the end of the millennium. <reference osisRef="re 20:14">Revelation 20:14</reference>.<div eID="gen3273" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3274" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteous</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi> , Also, <reference osisRef="col 3:4">Colossians 3:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2th 1:5-10">2 Thessalonians 1:5-10</reference>

<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3274" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3275" type="x-p"/> 2 hid<div eID="gen3275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3276" type="x-p"/> The interpretation of the parable of the treasure, which makes the buyer of the field to be a sinner who is seeking Christ, has no warrant in the parable itself. The field is defined (v. 38) to be the world. The seeking sinner does not buy, but forsakes, the world to win Christ. Furthermore, the sinner has nothing to sell, nor is Christ for sale, nor is He hidden in a field, nor, having found Christ, does the sinner hide Him again (cf) <reference osisRef="mr 7:24">Mark 7:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 4:20">Acts 4:20</reference>. At every point the interpretation breaks down.<div eID="gen3276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3277" type="x-p"/> Our Lord is the buyer at the awful cost of His blood <reference osisRef="1pe 1:18">1 Peter 1:18,</reference> and Israel, especially Ephraim <reference osisRef="jer 31:5-12 jer 31:18-20">Jeremiah 31:5-12,18-20,</reference> the lost tribes hidden in "the field," the world (v. 38), is the treasure ; <reference osisRef="ex 19:5">Exodus 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 135:4">Psalms 135:4</reference>. Again, as in the separation of tares and wheat, the angels are used ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:31">Matthew 24:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 16:16">Jeremiah 16:16</reference>. The divine Merchantman buys the field (world) for the sake of the treasure (v. 44) <reference osisRef="ro 11:28">Romans 11:28,</reference> beloved for the fathers' sakes, and yet to be restored and saved. The note of joy (v. 44) is also that of the prophets in view of Israel's restoration. ; <reference osisRef="de 30:9">Deuteronomy 30:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 49:13">Isaiah 49:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 52:1-3"> 52:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 62:4-7"> 62:4-7</reference> <reference osisRef="isa 65:18 isa 65:19"> 65:18,19</reference>.<div eID="gen3277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3278" type="x-p"/> (See "Israel,") <reference osisRef="ge 11:10">Genesis 11:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:26">Romans 11:26</reference>.<div eID="gen3278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3279" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">pearls</hi> <div eID="gen3279" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3280" type="x-p"/> The true Church, "one body" formed by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference>. As Israel is the hid treasure, so the Church is the pearl of great cost. Covering the same period of time as the mysteries of the kingdom, is the mystery of the Church ; <reference osisRef="ro 16:25 ro 16:26">Romans 16:25,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:3-10">Ephesians 3:3-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:32">Ephesians 5:32</reference>. Of the true Church a pearl is a perfect symbol:<div eID="gen3280" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) A pearl is one, a perfect symbol of unity <reference osisRef="1co 10:17">1 Corinthians 10:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13"> 12:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:4-6">Ephesians 4:4-6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) a pearl is formed by the accretion, and that not mechanically, but vitally, through a living one, as Christ adds to the Church <reference osisRef="ac 2:41 ac 2:47">Acts 2:41,47</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:14"> 5:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 11:24"> 11:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:21">Ephesians 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 2:19">Colossians 2:19</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Christ, having given Himself for the pearl, is now preparing it for presentation to Himself <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-27">Ephesians 5:25-27</reference>. The kingdom is not the Church, but the true children of the kingdom during the fulfilment of these mysteries, baptized by one Spirit into one body <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference> compose the true Church, the pearl.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3281" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">the kingdom of heaven</hi><div eID="gen3281" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3282" type="x-p"/> The parable of the Net ( (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G1139">δαιμονίζομαι</w> -net) presents another view from that of the wheat and tares of the mysteries of the kingdom as the sphere of profession, but with this difference: there Satan was the active agent; here the admixture is more the result of the tendency of a movement to gather to itself that which is not really of it). The kingdom of heaven is like a net which, cast into the sea of humanity, gathers of every kind, good and bad, and these remain together in the net (v. 49) and not merely in the sea, until the end of the age. It is not even a converted net, much less a converted sea. Infinite violence has been done to sound exegesis by the notion that the world is to be converted in this age. Against that notion stands our Lord's own interpretation of the parables of the Sower, the Wheat and Tares, and the Net.<div eID="gen3282" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3283" type="x-p"/> Such, then, is the mystery form of the kingdom. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>". It is the sphere of Christian profession during this age. It is a mingled body of true and false, wheat and tares, good and bad. It is defiled by formalism, doubt, and worldliness. But within it Christ sees the true children of the true kingdom who, at the end, are to "shine forth as the sun." In the great field, the world, He sees the redeemed of all ages, but especially His hidden Israel, yet to be restored and blessed, Also, in this form of the kingdom, so unlike that which is to be, He sees the Church, His body and bride, and for joy He sells all that He has <reference osisRef="2co 8:9">2 Corinthians 8:9</reference> and buys the field, the treasure, and the pearl.<div eID="gen3283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3284" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">heaven</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">end of the</hi> consummation of the age. <reference osisRef="mt 24:3">Matthew 24:3</reference>.

<hi type="bold">James</hi><div eID="gen3284" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3285" type="x-p"/> Son of Alphaeus. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:21">Matthew 4:21</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen3285" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv102"/><div sID="gen3286" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.13"/>

<hi type="bold">Herod</hi> <div eID="gen3287" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3288" type="x-p"/> Called Antipas; son of Herod the Great, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 2:1">Matthew 2:1</reference>")</hi> and Malthace, a Samaritan woman; brother of Archelaus, see margin, See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 2:22">Matthew 2:22</reference>" a daughter of King Aretas; Herodias, wife of his half-brother, Philip. <chapter eID="Matt.14"/><div eID="gen3288" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3289" type="x-p"/><chapter n="15" osisID="Matt.15" sID="Matt.15"/>

<hi type="bold">gift</hi> i.e. dedicated to God.<div eID="gen3289" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3290" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 5:23 mt 5:24">Matthew 5:23,24</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 7:11">Mark 7:11</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mr 7:11">Mark 7:11</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">departed</hi><div eID="gen3290" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3291" type="x-p"/> the Syrophenician woman<div eID="gen3291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3292" type="x-p"/> For the first time the rejected Son of David ministers to a Gentile. It is a precursive fulfilment of <reference osisRef="mt 12:18">Matthew 12:18</reference> Addressed by a Gentile as Son of David, He makes no reply, for a Gentile has no claim upon Him in that character. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 2:2">Matthew 2:2</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="eph 2:12">Ephesians 2:12</reference>. Addressing him as "Lord," she obtained an immediate answer. <reference osisRef="ro 10:12 ro 10:13">Romans 10:12,13</reference>

<hi type="bold">lost sheep</hi> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301191 (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w>). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">great is thy faith</hi><div eID="gen3292" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3293" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="lu 7:7-9">Luke 7:7-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 6:6">Mark 6:6</reference> Faith honours God, knowing that he is faithful. cf. <reference osisRef="1jo 5:10">1 John 5:10</reference>. <chapter eID="Matt.15"/><div eID="gen3293" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3294" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="16" osisID="Matt.16" sID="Matt.16"/>

<hi type="bold">baskets</hi> <div eID="gen3294" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3295" type="x-p"/> A different Greek word from that translated "baskets" in <reference osisRef="mt 16:10">Matthew 16:10</reference>.

<hi type="bold">baskets</hi><div eID="gen3295" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3296" type="x-p"/> A different Greek word from that translated "baskets" in <reference osisRef="mt 16:9">Matthew 16:9</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen3296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3297" type="x-p"/> Also, <reference osisRef="mt 16:27 mt 16:28">Matthew 16:27,28,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">Barjona</hi><div eID="gen3297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3298" type="x-p"/> Son of Jonas.

<hi type="bold">Peter</hi><div eID="gen3298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3299" type="x-p"/> There is the Greek a play upon the words, "thou art Peter petros-- literally 'a little rock', and upon this rock Petra I will build my church." He does not promise to build His church upon Peter, but upon Himself, as Peter is careful to tell us (<reference osisRef="1pe 2:4-9">1 Peter 2:4-9</reference>)<div eID="gen3299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3300" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">church</hi> <div eID="gen3300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3301" type="x-p"/> 2 (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w> (ek=="out of," kaleo =="to call"), an assembly of called out ones). The word is used of any assembly; the word itself implies no more, as, e.g., the town-meeting at Ephesus <reference osisRef="ac 19:39">Acts 19:39</reference> and Israel, called out of Egypt and assembled in the wilderness <reference osisRef="ac 7:38">Acts 7:38</reference>. Israel was a true "church," but not in any sense the N.T. church--the only point of similarity being that both were "called out" and by the same God. All else is contrast.<div eID="gen3301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3302" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 7:38">Acts 7:38</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>"<div eID="gen3302" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3303" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hell</hi> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Lu 16:23">Luke 16:23</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">keys of the kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3303" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3304" type="x-p"/> Not the keys of the church, but of the kingdom of heaven in the sense of Mat 13., i.e. the sphere of Christian profession. A key is a badge of power or authority (cf) <reference osisRef="isa 22:22">Isaiah 22:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:7">Revelation 3:7</reference>. The apostolic history explains and limits this trust, for it was Peter who opened the door of Christian opportunity to Israel on the day of Pentecost <reference osisRef="ac 2:38-42">Acts 2:38-42</reference> and to Gentiles in the house of Cornelius. <reference osisRef="ac 10:34-46">Acts 10:34-46</reference>. There was no assumption by Peter of any other authority <reference osisRef="ac 15:7-11">Acts 15:7-11</reference>. In the council James, not Peter, seems to have presided ; <reference osisRef="ac 15:19">Acts 15:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:11-15">Galatians 2:11-15</reference>. Peter claimed no more for himself than to be an apostle by gift <reference osisRef="1pe 1:1">1 Peter 1:1</reference> and an elder by office <reference osisRef="1pe 5:1">1 Peter 5:1</reference>.<div eID="gen3304" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3305" type="x-p"/> The power of binding and loosing was shared <reference osisRef="mt 18:18">Matthew 18:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:23">John 20:23</reference> by the other disciples. That it did not involve the determination of the eternal destiny of souls is clear from <reference osisRef="re 1:18">Revelation 1:18</reference>. The keys of death and the place of departed spirits are held by Christ alone.<div eID="gen3305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3306" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">charged</hi> <div eID="gen3306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3307" type="x-p"/> The disciples had been proclaiming Jesus as the Christ, i.e. the covenanted King of a kingdom promised to the Jews, and "at hand." The church, on the contrary, must be built upon testimony to Him as crucified, risen from the dead, ascended, and made "Head over all things to the church." <reference osisRef="eph 1:20-23">Ephesians 1:20-23</reference>. The former testimony was ended, the new testimony was not yet ready, because the blood of the new covenant had not yet been shed, but our Lord begins to speak of His death and resurrection <reference osisRef="mt 16:21">Matthew 16:21</reference>. It is a turning- point of immense significance:<div eID="gen3307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3308" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Jesus</hi> Omit "Jesus."<div eID="gen3308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3309" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301192<div eID="gen3309" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3310" type="x-p"/> Additional Factors to Consider See Topic 301207 <div eID="gen3310" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv102"/><div sID="gen3311" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv102"/> <hi type="bold">world</hi> <div eID="gen3311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3312" type="x-p"/> kosmos = world-system. <reference osisRef="joh 7:7">John 7:7</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi>.

3<div eID="gen3316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3317" type="x-p"/> was transfigured<div eID="gen3317" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3318" type="x-p"/> The transfiguration scene contains, in miniature, all the elements of the future kingdom in manifestation:<div eID="gen3318" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the Lord, not in humiliation, but in glory (v. 2).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Moses, glorified, representative of the redeemed who have passed through death into the kingdom. <reference osisRef="mt 13:43">Matthew 13:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 9:30 lu 9:31">Luke 9:30,31</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Elijah, glorified, representative of the redeemed who have entered the kingdom by translation. <reference osisRef="1co 15:50-53">1 Corinthians 15:50-53</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Peter, James, and John, not glorified, representatives (for the moment) of Israel in the flesh in the future kingdom <reference osisRef="eze 37:21-27">Ezekiel 37:21-27</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The multitude at the foot of the mountain <reference osisRef="mt 17:2">Matthew 17:2,</reference> representative of the nations who are to be brought into the kingdom after it is established over Israel <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-12">Isaiah 11:10-12,</reference> etc. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv103"/><div sID="gen3319" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv103"/><hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> Also <reference osisRef="mt 17:12 mt 17:22">Matthew 17:12,22,</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come</hi><div eID="gen3319" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3320" type="x-p"/> Cf <reference osisRef="mt 11:14">Matthew 11:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 9:11 mr 9:12 mr 9:13">Mark 9:11,12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:17">Luke 1:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 3:1">Malachi 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mal 4:5 mal 4:6"> 4:5,6</reference> All the passages must be construed together.<div eID="gen3320" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Christ confirms the specific and still unfulfilled prophecy of <reference osisRef="mal 4:5 mal 4:6">Malachi 4:5,6</reference>: "Elias shall truly first come and restore all things." Here, as in Malachi, the prediction fulfilled in John the Baptist, and that yet to be fulfilled in Elijah, are kept distinct.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) But John the Baptist had come already, and with a ministry so completely in the spirit and power of Elijah's future ministry <reference osisRef="lu 1:17">Luke 1:17</reference> that in an adumbrative and typical sense it could be said: "Elias is come already." Cf ; <reference osisRef="mt 10:40">Matthew 10:40</reference>; <reference osisRef="phm 1:12 phm 1:17">Philemon 1:12,17</reference> where the same thought of identification, while yet preserving personal distinction, occurs. <reference osisRef="joh 1:27">John 1:27</reference>. </item> </list>
