<hi type="bold">Have ye not read</hi> <div eID="gen3338" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3339" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="ge 1:27">Genesis 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 2:23 ge 2:24"> 2:23,24</reference>. The passage is significant as Jesus' confirmation of the Genesis narrative of creation.
<hi type="bold">Moses</hi><div eID="gen3339" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3340" type="x-p"/> Thus confirming the Mosaic authorship of Deut.
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3340" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3341" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen3341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3342" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">kept from my youth</hi> <div eID="gen3342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3343" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="php 3:6 php 3:7">Philippians 3:6,7</reference> contra vs. <reference osisRef="php 3:7-9">Philippians 3:7-9</reference>
<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><div eID="gen3343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3344" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen3344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3345" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">saved</hi> <div eID="gen3345" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3346" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi> Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 13:3-9">Matthew 13:3-9</reference>

<hi type="bold">regeneration</hi><div eID="gen3346" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3347" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w> = "re-creation," "making new)." The word occurs once again in <reference osisRef="tit 3:5">Titus 3:5</reference>. There it refers to the new birth or a believing person; here to the re-creation of the social order, and renewal of the earth ; <reference osisRef="isa 11:6-9">Isaiah 11:6-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:19-23">Romans 8:19-23</reference> when the kingdom shall come. (See "Kingdom (O.T.),"<div eID="gen3347" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3348" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>"<div eID="gen3348" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3349" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">judging</hi> <div eID="gen3349" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3350" type="x-p"/> Disclosing how the promise <reference osisRef="isa 1:26">Isaiah 1:26</reference> will be fulfilled when the kingdom is set up. The kingdom will be administered over Israel through the apostles, according to the ancient theocratic judgeship. <reference osisRef="jud 2:18">Judges 2:18</reference>. <div eID="gen3350" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv105"/><div sID="gen3351" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.19"/>
<div eID="gen3351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3352" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="20" osisID="Matt.20" sID="Matt.20"/>

<hi type="bold">vineyard</hi> <div eID="gen3352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3353" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="isa 5:7">Isaiah 5:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:28-33">Matthew 21:28-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:1-5">John 15:1-5</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 28:19">Matthew 28:19</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">received</hi><div eID="gen3353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3354" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 3:14">1 Corinthians 3:14</reference>")</hi>. Also, <reference osisRef="1co 9:24">1 Corinthians 9:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:7 2ti 4:8">2 Timothy 4:7,8</reference>.
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3354" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3355" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">cup</hi><div eID="gen3355" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3356" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="mt 26:39">Matthew 26:39</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 27:46"> 27:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:41 lu 22:42">Luke 22:41,42</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:11">John 18:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 53:4-6">Isaiah 53:4-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 5:21">2 Corinthians 5:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:13">Galatians 3:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:24">1 Peter 2:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 3:18"> 3:18</reference>

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi> Also, <reference osisRef="php 2:7">Philippians 2:7</reference><div eID="gen3356" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3357" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ransom</hi> See, <reference osisRef="isa 53:10 isa 53:11">Isaiah 53:10,11</reference>.<div eID="gen3357" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3358" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 20:22">Matthew 20:22</reference> "cup," margin ref: <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 20:22">Matthew 20:22</reference>")</hi> ; <reference osisRef="ex 14:30">Exodus 14:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference><div eID="gen3358" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3359" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 14:30">Exodus 14:30</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:isa 59:20">Isaiah 59:20</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>"

<hi type="bold">two blind men</hi><div eID="gen3359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3360" type="x-p"/> A discrepancy has been imagined between this account and those in <reference osisRef="mr 10:46">Mark 10:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:35">Luke 18:35</reference>. Matthew and Mark obviously refer to a work of healing as Jesus departed from Jericho. Bartimaeus, the active one of the two, the one who cried, "Jesus, thou Son of David," is specifically mentioned by Mark. Of the other one of the "two," we know nothing. The healing described by <reference osisRef="lu 18:35">Luke 18:35</reference> occurred before Jesus entered Jericho. As to the form of appeal, "Son of David" (cf) ; <reference osisRef="mt 9:27">Matthew 9:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 15:22"> 15:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:9"> 21:9</reference>. Jesus must have been so addressed constantly. The narratives therefore supplement, but in no way contradict each other. <div eID="gen3360" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv105"/><div sID="gen3361" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.20"/>
<div eID="gen3361" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3362" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="21" osisID="Matt.21" sID="Matt.21"/>

<hi type="bold">nigh unto Jerusalem</hi> <div eID="gen3362" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3363" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mt 21:1-9">Matthew 21:1-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 9:9">Zechariah 9:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 14:4-9"> 14:4-9</reference>. The two advents are in striking contrast.

<hi type="bold">fulfilled</hi><div eID="gen3363" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3364" type="x-p"/> The king's final and official offer of Himself according to <reference osisRef="zec 9:9">Zechariah 9:9</reference>. Acclaimed by an unthinking multitude whose real belief is expressed in <reference osisRef="mt 21:11">Matthew 21:11,</reference> but with no welcome from the official representatives of the nation, He was soon to hear the multitude shout: "Crucify him."

<hi type="bold">cast</hi><div eID="gen3364" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3365" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="lu 19:45">Luke 19:45</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 11:15-18">Mark 11:15-18</reference>. Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 2:13-25">John 2:13-25</reference> which introduced, as this cleansing closed, the offer of Christ to Israel as King.

<hi type="bold">Bethany</hi><div eID="gen3365" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3366" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="joh 11:1 joh 11:2">John 11:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 10:39-42">Luke 10:39-42</reference>. Cf. ; <reference osisRef="mr 11:1-11">Mark 11:1-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 19:29-35">Luke 19:29-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:1-8">John 12:1-8</reference>. With no other place is the human Christ so tenderly associated, while it also was the place of manifestation of His divine power. <reference osisRef="joh 11:43 joh 11:44">John 11:43,44</reference>.

<hi type="bold">fig tree</hi><div eID="gen3366" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3367" type="x-p"/> Lit. a solitary fig tree. <reference osisRef="lu 13:6-9">Luke 13:6-9</reference>. The withered fig tree is a parabolic miracle concerning Israel. <reference osisRef="lu 13:6-9">Luke 13:6-9</reference>. Cf., <reference osisRef="mt 24:32 mt 24:33">Matthew 24:32,33,</reference> a prophecy that Israel shall again bud.

<hi type="bold">vineyard</hi><div eID="gen3367" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3368" type="x-p"/> See "vineyard," margin ref., <reference osisRef="mt 20:1">Matthew 20:1</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 20:1">Matthew 20:1</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">repented</hi><div eID="gen3368" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3369" type="x-p"/> Cf., <reference osisRef="lu 15:20">Luke 15:20,</reference> the other perfect illustration of repentance. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 17:30">Acts 17:30</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen3369" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3370" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Lord's</hi><div eID="gen3370" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3371" type="x-p"/> Jehovah. <reference osisRef="ps 118:23">Psalms 118:23</reference>.

<hi type="bold">kingdom of God</hi><div eID="gen3371" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3372" type="x-p"/> Note that Matthew here as in <reference osisRef="mt 21:31">Matthew 21:31</reference> uses the larger word, kingdom of God: (Cf) <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3372" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3373" type="x-p"/> The kingdom of heaven; <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>" will yet be set up. Meantime the kingdom of God and his righteousness is taken from Israel nationally and given to the Gentiles. <reference osisRef="ro 9:30-33">Romans 9:30-33</reference>.<div eID="gen3373" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3374" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">you</hi> <div eID="gen3374" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3375" type="x-p"/> i.e. national Israel, the barren vine. Mt 21: 33-41 <reference osisRef="isa 5:1-7">Isaiah 5:1-7</reference>.

<hi type="bold">stone shall be broken</hi><div eID="gen3375" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3376" type="x-p"/> Christ as the "Stone" is revealed in a threefold way:<div eID="gen3376" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) To Israel Christ, coming not as a splendid monarch but in the form of a servant, is a stumbling stone and rock of offence. <reference osisRef="isa 8:14 isa 8:15">Isaiah 8:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 9:32 ro 9:33">Romans 9:32,33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:23">1 Corinthians 1:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:8">1 Peter 2:8</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) to the church, Christ is the foundation stone and the head of the corner <reference osisRef="1co 3:11">1 Corinthians 3:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:20-22">Ephesians 2:20-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:4 1pe 2:5">1 Peter 2:4,5</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) to the Gentile world-powers (see "Gentiles," <reference osisRef="lu 21:24">Luke 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 16:19">Revelation 16:19</reference> He is to be the smiting-stone of destruction <reference osisRef="da 2:34">Daniel 2:34</reference>. Israel stumbled over Christ; the church is built upon Christ; Gentile world- dominion will be broken by Christ.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3377" type="x-p"/> See "Armageddon" <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:19"> 19:19</reference>.<div eID="gen3377" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3378" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">And whosoever</hi> <div eID="gen3378" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3379" type="x-p"/> Or, Whosoever falls on this stone shall be crushed together i.e. the Jews <reference osisRef="isa 8:14">Isaiah 8:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 9:32 ro 9:33">Romans 9:32,33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:23">1 Corinthians 1:23</reference>] but on whomsoever it may fall, he will be scattered as dust ( (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G622">ἀπόλλυμι</w>," i).e. the Gentile nations, <reference osisRef="da 2:34 da 2:35 da 2:45">Daniel 2:34,35,45</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Da 2:35">Daniel 2:35</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Matt.21"/><div eID="gen3379" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3380" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="22" osisID="Matt.22" sID="Matt.22"/>
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen3380" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3381" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">burned</hi> <div eID="gen3381" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3382" type="x-p"/> Fulfilled as to Jerusalem A.D. 70. <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference>.

<hi type="bold">go ye</hi><div eID="gen3382" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3383" type="x-p"/> The world-wide call. <reference osisRef="mt 28:16-20">Matthew 28:16-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 22:17">Revelation 22:17</reference>

<hi type="bold">Then went</hi><div eID="gen3383" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3384" type="x-p"/> In the different classes, vs. <reference osisRef="mt 23:15-40">Matthew 23:15-40</reference>. Jesus meets representatives of all Israel, Pharisees, Sadducees.<div eID="gen3384" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3385" type="x-p"/> Herodians. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:7">Matthew 3:7</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3385" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3386" type="x-p"/> For them, silenced but unrepentant, no message is left but "woe." <reference osisRef="mt 23:1-39">Matthew 23:1-39</reference>.

<hi type="bold">ye do err</hi><div eID="gen3386" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3387" type="x-p"/> Or, ye deceive yourselves, etc. Jesus' answer gives the three incapacities of the rationalist: self-deception, <reference osisRef="ro 1:21 ro 1:22">Romans 1:21,22,</reference> ignorance of the spiritual content of Scripture, <reference osisRef="ac 13:27">Acts 13:27,</reference> disbelief in the intervention of divine power, <reference osisRef="2pe 3:5-9">2 Peter 3:5-9</reference>.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen3387" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3388" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">lawyer</hi><div eID="gen3388" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3389" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G3544">νομικός</w>," "of the law"; occurs also <reference osisRef="lu 7:30">Luke 7:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 10:25"> 10:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 11:45 lu 11:46 lu 11:52"> 11:45,46,52</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 14:3">Luke 14:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 3:13">Titus 3:13</reference>. Except in the last instance, "lawyer" is another name for "scribe."<div eID="gen3389" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3390" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 2:4">Matthew 2:4</reference>")</hi>. In <reference osisRef="tit 3:13">Titus 3:13</reference> the term has the modern meaning.

<hi type="bold">asked them</hi><div eID="gen3390" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3391" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 21:24">Matthew 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:7">John 19:7</reference> Jesus' question is not personal but doctrinal: "Whose son is the Messiah?" Cf. ; <reference osisRef="ac 2:25-36">Acts 2:25-36</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 1:3 ro 1:4">Romans 1:3,4</reference>. <chapter eID="Matt.22"/><div eID="gen3391" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen3392" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="23" osisID="Matt.23" sID="Matt.23"/>

<hi type="bold">sit in</hi> <div eID="gen3392" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3393" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ezr 7:6 ezr 7:25 ezr 7:26">Ezra 7:6,25,26</reference>. Jesus' disciples were to honour the law, but not the hypocritical teachers of it.

<hi type="bold">phylacteries</hi><div eID="gen3393" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3394" type="x-p"/> Passages of Scripture enclosed in a small case, bound upon arm or forehead, <reference osisRef="de 6:8">Deuteronomy 6:8</reference>.
<hi type="bold">Woe</hi><div eID="gen3394" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3395" type="x-p"/> The best MSS. omit verse 14.

<hi type="bold">hell</hi><div eID="gen3395" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3396" type="x-p"/> Gehenna. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:22">Matthew 5:22</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">debtor</hi><div eID="gen3396" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3397" type="x-p"/> Or, bound; also <reference osisRef="mt 23:18">Matthew 23:18</reference>. "guilty:"

<hi type="bold">iniquity</hi><div eID="gen3397" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3398" type="x-p"/> Lit. Lawlessness. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">send unto you</hi><div eID="gen3398" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3399" type="x-p"/> The Jews' treatment of the apostles is proved, <reference osisRef="mt 23:31-33">Matthew 23:31-33</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Abel</hi><div eID="gen3399" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3400" type="x-p"/> Jesus' confirmation of <reference osisRef="ge 4:8-10">Genesis 4:8-10</reference>. Cf. <reference osisRef="heb 12:24">Hebrews 12:24</reference>.

<hi type="bold">come upon</hi><div eID="gen3400" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3401" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="re 18:21-24">Revelation 18:21-24</reference>. It is the way also of history; judgment falls upon one generation for the sins of centuries. The pediction was fulfilled in the destruction of Jerusalem, A.D. 70.

<hi type="bold">till</hi><div eID="gen3401" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3402" type="x-p"/> The three "untils" of Israel's blessing:<div eID="gen3402" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Israel must say, "blessed is He" <reference osisRef="mt 23:39">Matthew 23:39</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:3 ro 10:4">Romans 10:3,4</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Gentile world-power must run its course. <reference osisRef="lu 21:24">Luke 21:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 2:34 da 2:35">Daniel 2:34,35</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The elect number of Gentiles must be brought in. Then "the Deliverer shall come out of Zion." etc. <reference osisRef="ro 11:25-27">Romans 11:25-27</reference>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv105"/><div sID="gen3403" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.23"/>
<div eID="gen3403" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3404" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="24" osisID="Matt.24" sID="Matt.24"/>

<hi type="bold">departed</hi> <div eID="gen3404" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3405" type="x-p"/> Jesus leaves that which He abandons to judgment. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mr 8:23">Mark 8:23</reference>")</hi> in light of <reference osisRef="mt 11:21 mt 11:22">Matthew 11:21,22</reference> Cf., <reference osisRef="re 18:4">Revelation 18:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Tell us</hi><div eID="gen3405" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3406" type="x-p"/> The beginning of the Olivet Discourse<div eID="gen3406" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3407" type="x-p"/> Mat 24 with <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference> answers the threefold question. The order is as follows: "when shall these things be?"--i.e. destruction of the temple and city. Answer: <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference>.<div eID="gen3407" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3408" type="x-p"/> Second and third questions: "And what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the age?" Answer: <reference osisRef="mt 24:4-33">Matthew 24:4-33</reference>.<div eID="gen3408" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3409" type="x-p"/> Verses 4 to 14 have a double interpretation: They give<div eID="gen3409" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the character of the age--wars, international conflicts, famines, pestilences, persecutions, and false Christs (cf) <reference osisRef="da 9:26">Daniel 9:26</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3410" type="x-p"/> This is not the description of a converted world.<div eID="gen3410" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) But the same answer (<reference osisRef="mt 24:4-14">Matthew 24:4-14</reference>) applies in a specific way to the end of the age, viz. Daniel's seventieth week. <reference osisRef="da 9:24-27">Daniel 9:24-27</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Da 9:24">Daniel 9:24</reference>")</hi>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3411" type="x-p"/> All that has characterized the age gathers into awful intensity at the end. Verse 14 has specific reference to the proclamation of the good news that the kingdom is again "at hand" by the Jewish remnant <reference osisRef="isa 1:9">Isaiah 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 14:6 re 14:7">Revelation 14:6,7</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3411" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3412" type="x-p"/> Verse 15 gives the sign of the abomination, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Da 9:27">Daniel 9:27</reference>")</hi> , the "man of sin," or "Beast" <reference osisRef="2th 2:3-8">2 Thessalonians 2:3-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:27">Daniel 9:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 12:11"> 12:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 13:4-7">Revelation 13:4-7</reference>.<div eID="gen3412" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3413" type="x-p"/> This introduces the great tribulation <reference osisRef="ps 2:5">Psalms 2:5</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 7:14">Revelation 7:14</reference>")</hi> , which runs its awful course of three and a half years, culminating in the battle of See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 19:19">Revelation 19:19</reference>" at which time Christ becomes the smiting Stone of <reference osisRef="da 2:34">Daniel 2:34</reference>.<div eID="gen3413" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3414" type="x-p"/> The detail of this period (<reference osisRef="mt 24:15-28">Matthew 24:15-28</reference>) is:<div eID="gen3414" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The abomination in the holy place (<reference osisRef="mt 24:15">Matthew 24:15</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the warning (<reference osisRef="mt 24:16-20">Matthew 24:16-20</reference>) to believing Jews who will then be in Jerusalem;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the great tribulation, with renewed warning as to false Christs (<reference osisRef="mt 24:21-26">Matthew 24:21-26</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the sudden smiting of the Gentile world-power (<reference osisRef="mt 24:27 mt 24:28">Matthew 24:27,28</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the glorious appearing of the Lord, visible to all nations, and the regathering of Israel (<reference osisRef="mt 24:29-31">Matthew 24:29-31</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the sign of the fig-tree (<reference osisRef="mt 24:32 mt 24:33">Matthew 24:32,33</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) warnings, applicable to this present age over which these events are ever impending (<reference osisRef="mt 24:34-51">Matthew 24:34-51</reference>). <reference osisRef="phm 4:5">Philemon 4:5</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3415" type="x-p"/> Careful study of Da 2,7, 9, and Re 13 will make the interpretation clear. See, also, "Remnant" (<reference osisRef="Isa 1:19">Isa 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>). <div eID="gen3415" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv105"/><div sID="gen3416" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv105"/> <hi type="bold">iniquity</hi> <div eID="gen3416" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3417" type="x-p"/> i.e. lawlessness, sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3417" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3418" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">world</hi> <div eID="gen3418" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3419" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3419" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3420" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">world</hi> oikoumene = inhabited earth.<div eID="gen3420" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3421" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Lu 2:1">Luke 2:1</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Then let them which</hi> <div eID="gen3421" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3422" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference>. The passage in Luke refers in express terms to a destruction of Jerusalem which was fulfilled by Titus, A.D. 70; the passage in Matthew to a future crisis in Jerusalem after the manifestation of the abomination. See "Beast" ; <reference osisRef="da 7:8">Daniel 7:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:20">Revelation 19:20</reference> and "Armageddon" ; <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:17"> 19:17</reference>.<div eID="gen3422" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3423" type="x-p"/> As the circumstances in both cases will be similar, so are the warnings. In the former case Jerusalem was destroyed; in the latter it will be delivered by divine interposition.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen3423" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3424" type="x-p"/> Also <reference osisRef="mt 24:37 mt 24:39 mt 24:44">Matthew 24:37,39,44</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen3424" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3425" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">This generation</hi> <div eID="gen3425" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3426" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G35">ἀγενεαλόγητος</w>," the primary definition of which is, "race, kind, family, stock, breed)." (So all lexicons.) That the word is used in this sense because none of "these things," i.e. the world-wide preaching of the kingdom, the great tribulation, the return of the Lord in visible glory, and the regathering of the elect, occurred at the destruction of Jerusalem by Titus, A.D. 70. The promise is, therefore, that the generation--nation, or family of Israel-- will be preserved unto "these things"; a promise wonderfully fulfilled to this day.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen3426" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3427" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

Marg<div eID="gen3427" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3428" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <div eID="gen3428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3429" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <div eID="gen3429" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3430" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">faithful</hi> <div eID="gen3430" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3431" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="lu 12:42-46">Luke 12:42-46</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 4:2">1 Corinthians 4:2</reference>. It is faithfulness, not ability, in the Lord's service that is first approved by Him. <div eID="gen3431" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv106"/><div sID="gen3432" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.24"/>
<div eID="gen3432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3433" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="25" osisID="Matt.25" sID="Matt.25"/>

<hi type="bold">shall</hi> <div eID="gen3433" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3434" type="x-p"/> This part of the Olivet discourse goes beyond the "sign" questions of the disciples <reference osisRef="mt 24:3">Matthew 24:3</reference> and presents our Lord's return in three aspects:<div eID="gen3434" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) As testing profession, <reference osisRef="mt 25:1-13">Matthew 25:1-13</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) as testing service, <reference osisRef="mt 25:14-30">Matthew 25:14-30</reference>;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) as testing the Gentile nations, <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3435" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">virgins</hi> <div eID="gen3435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3436" type="x-p"/> The kingdom of heaven here is the sphere of profession, as in Mat 13. All alike have lamps, but two facts fix the real status of the foolish virgins: They "took no oil," and the Lord said, "I know you not." Oil is the symbol of the Holy Spirit, and "If any man have not the spirit of Christ, he is none of his" <reference osisRef="ro 8:9">Romans 8:9</reference><div eID="gen3436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3437" type="x-p"/> Nor could the Lord say to any believer, however unspiritual, "I know you not."<div eID="gen3437" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3438" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">heaven</hi> <div eID="gen3438" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3439" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <div eID="gen3439" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3440" type="x-p"/> Also <reference osisRef="mt 24:31">Matthew 24:31</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">the kingdom of heaven is</hi><div eID="gen3440" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3441" type="x-p"/> Omit the italicised words, "the kingdom of heaven is".
<hi type="bold">Well done</hi><div eID="gen3441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3442" type="x-p"/> The Lord's commendation may be earned by the weakest of His servants; it is given for faithful service.

<hi type="bold">Well done</hi><div eID="gen3442" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3443" type="x-p"/> The same commendation is gained by the servant with two talents as by him with five; he was equally faithful though his gift was less.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3443" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3444" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">angels</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">And before him</hi> <div eID="gen3444" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3445" type="x-p"/> This judgment is to be distinguished from the judgment of the great white throne. Here there is no resurrection; the persons judged are living nations; no books are opened; three classes are present, sheep, goats, and brethren; the time is at the return of Christ (<reference osisRef="mt 25:31">Matthew 25:31</reference>); and the scene is on the earth. All these particulars are in contrast with <reference osisRef="re 20:11-15">Revelation 20:11-15</reference>.<div eID="gen3445" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3446" type="x-p"/> The test in this judgment is the treatment accorded by the nations to those whom Christ here call "my brethren." These "brethren" are the Jewish Remnant who will have preached the Gospel of the kingdom to all nations during the tribulation. See "Remnant" <reference osisRef="isa 1:9">Isaiah 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>.<div eID="gen3446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3447" type="x-p"/> The test in <reference osisRef="re 20:11-15">Revelation 20:11-15</reference> is the possession of eternal life. See, for the other six judgments: <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 12:31">John 12:31</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="1co 11:31">1 Corinthians 11:31</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2co 5:10">2 Corinthians 5:10</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:eze 20:37">Ezekiel 20:37</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>" See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:re 20:12">Revelation 20:12</reference>"
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3447" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3448" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">righteous</hi><div eID="gen3448" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3449" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">angels</hi> <div eID="gen3449" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3450" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">into everlasting</hi> <div eID="gen3450" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3451" type="x-p"/> Judgments (the seven). <reference osisRef="lu 14:14">Luke 14:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:14">2 Samuel 7:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:12">Revelation 20:12</reference>. "Eternal" and "everlasting" are the same word. <div eID="gen3451" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv106"/><div sID="gen3452" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.25"/>
<div eID="gen3452" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3453" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="26" osisID="Matt.26" sID="Matt.26"/>

<hi type="bold">head</hi> <div eID="gen3453" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3454" type="x-p"/> No contradiction of <reference osisRef="joh 12:3">John 12:3</reference> is implied. The ordinary anointing of hospitality and honour was of the feet <reference osisRef="lu 7:38">Luke 7:38</reference> and head <reference osisRef="lu 7:46">Luke 7:46</reference> But Mary of Bethany, who alone of our Lord's disciples had comprehended His thrice repeated announcement of His coming death and resurrection, invested the anointing with the deeper meaning of the preparation of His body for burying. Mary of Bethany was not among the women who went to the sepulchre with intent to embalm the body of Jesus.<div eID="gen3454" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3455" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">woman</hi> i.e. Mary of Bethany.
<hi type="bold">for my</hi><div eID="gen3455" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3456" type="x-p"/> Supply to prepare me.

<hi type="bold">sat down with the twelve</hi><div eID="gen3456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3457" type="x-p"/> The order of events on the night of the Passover supper appears to have been:<div eID="gen3457" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The taking by our Lord and the disciples of their places at the table;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the contention who should be greatest;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the feet washing;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the identification Judas as the traitor;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the withdrawal of Judas;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the institution of the supper;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the words of Jesus while still in the room <reference osisRef="mt 26:26-29">Matthew 26:26-29</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:35-38">Luke 22:35-38</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 13:3-35">John 13:3-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 14:1-31">Matthew 14:1-31</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(8) the words of Jesus between the room and the garden <reference osisRef="mt 26:31-35">Matthew 26:31-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:26-31">Mark 14:26-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:16 joh 15:17">John 15:16,17</reference> it seems probable that the high-priestly prayer <reference osisRef="joh 17:1-26">John 17:1-26</reference> was uttered after they reached the garden;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(9) the agony in the garden;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(10) the betrayal and arrest;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(11) Jesus before Caiaphas; Peter's denial. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv106"/><div sID="gen3458" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv106"/> <hi type="bold">remission</hi> <div eID="gen3458" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3459" type="x-p"/> Forgiveness. Summary: The Greek word translated "remission" in <reference osisRef="mt 26:28">Matthew 26:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 10:43">Acts 10:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference> is elsewhere rendered "forgiveness." It means, to send off, or away. And this, throughout Scripture, is the one fundamental meaning of forgiveness--to separate the sin from the sinner. Distinction must be made between divine and human forgiveness:<div eID="gen3459" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Human forgiveness means the remission of penalty. In the Old Testament and the New, in type and fulfilment, the divine forgiveness follows the execution of the penalty. "The priest shall make an atonement for his sin that he had committed, and it shall be forgiven him" <reference osisRef="le 4:35">Leviticus 4:35</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3460" type="x-p"/> "This is my blood of the new covenant, which is shed for many for the remission sending away, forgiveness of sins" (<reference osisRef="mt 25:28">Matthew 25:28</reference>). "Without shedding of blood there is no remission" <reference osisRef="heb 9:22">Hebrews 9:22</reference>.<div eID="gen3460" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3461" type="x-p"/> See "Sacrifice" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 4:4">Genesis 4:4</reference>")</hi> ; <reference osisRef="ge 4:4">Genesis 4:4</reference> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:heb 10:18">Hebrews 10:18</reference>". The sin of the justified believer interrupts his fellowship, and is forgiven upon confession, but always on the ground of Christ's propitiating sacrifice ; <reference osisRef="1jo 1:6-9">1 John 1:6-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:2"> 2:2</reference>.<div eID="gen3461" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Human forgiveness rests upon and results from the divine forgiveness. In many passages this is assumed rather than stated, but the principle is declared in <reference osisRef="eph 4:32">Ephesians 4:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 18:32 mt 18:33">Matthew 18:32,33</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3462" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sins</hi> Sin.<div eID="gen3462" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3463" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">kingdom</hi><div eID="gen3463" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3464" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">cup</hi><div eID="gen3464" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3465" type="x-p"/> The "cup" must be interpreted by our Lord's own use of that symbol in speaking of His approaching sacrificial death <reference osisRef="mt 20:22">Matthew 20:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:11">John 18:11</reference>. In view of <reference osisRef="joh 10:17 joh 10:18">John 10:17,18,</reference> He could have been in no fear of an unwilling death. The value of the account of the agony in the Garden is in the evidence it affords that He knew fully what the agony of the cross would mean when His soul was made an offering for sin, <reference osisRef="isa 53:10">Isaiah 53:10,</reference> in the hiding of the Father's face. Knowing the cost to the utmost, he voluntarily paid it.
<hi type="bold">sinners</hi><div eID="gen3465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3466" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Friend</hi><div eID="gen3466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3467" type="x-p"/> Gr. "Hetaire," "comrade." Perhaps the most touching thing in the Bible. The Lord does not disown Judas.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen3467" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3468" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">led</hi><div eID="gen3468" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3469" type="x-p"/> A comparison of the narratives gives the following order of events in the crucifixion day:<div eID="gen3469" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Early in the morning Jesus is brought before Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin. He is condemned and mocked <reference osisRef="mt 26:57-68">Matthew 26:57-68</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:55-65">Mark 14:55-65</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:63-71">Luke 22:63-71</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:19-24">John 18:19-24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The Sanhedrin lead Jesus to Pilate, <reference osisRef="mt 27:1-2 mt 27:11-14">Matthew 27:1,2,11-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:1-5">Mark 15:1-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:1-5">Luke 23:1-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:28-38">John 18:28-38</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Pilate sends Jesus to Herod <reference osisRef="lu 23:6-12">Luke 23:6-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:4">John 19:4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Jesus is again brought before Pilate, who releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified <reference osisRef="mt 27:15-26">Matthew 27:15-26</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:6-15">Mark 15:6-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:13-25">Luke 23:13-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:39 joh 18:40">John 18:39,40</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:4-16"> 19:4-16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Jesus is crowned with thorns and mocked <reference osisRef="mt 27:26-30">Matthew 27:26-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:15-20">Mark 15:15-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:1-3">John 19:1-3</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Suicide of Judas <reference osisRef="mt 27:3-10">Matthew 27:3-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) Led forth to be crucified, the cross is laid upon Simon: Jesus discourses to the women <reference osisRef="mt 27:31 mt 27:32">Matthew 27:31,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:22">Mark 15:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:33">Luke 23:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:17">John 19:17</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the offer of the stupefying drink refused <reference osisRef="mt 27:34">Matthew 27:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:23">Mark 15:23</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Jesus is crucified between two thieves <reference osisRef="mt 27:35-38">Matthew 27:35-38</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:24-28">Mark 15:24-28</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:33-38">Luke 23:33-38</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:18-24">John 19:18-24</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) He utters the first cry from the cross, "Father, forgive," etc. <reference osisRef="lu 23:34">Luke 23:34</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The soldiers part His garments <reference osisRef="mt 27:35">Matthew 27:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 15:33">Mark 15:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:44">Luke 23:44</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(11) The fourth cry, "My God," etc. <reference osisRef="mt 27:46 mt 27:47">Matthew 27:46,47</reference>; <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv108"/><div sID="gen3478" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv108"/> <hi type="bold">This is</hi> <div eID="gen3478" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3479" type="x-p"/> Cf <reference osisRef="mr 15:26">Mark 15:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:38">Luke 23:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:19">John 19:19</reference> These accounts supplement, but do not contradict one another. No one of the Evangelists quotes the entire inscription. All have "The King of the Jews." Luke adds to this the further words, "This is"; Matthew quotes the name, "Jesus"; whilst John gives the additional words "of Nazareth." The narratives combined give the entire inscription: "This is Matthew, Luke Jesus Matthew,John of Nazareth John the King of the Jews" all.
<hi type="bold">why</hi><div eID="gen3479" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3480" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ps 22:3">Psalms 22:3</reference> gives the answer to this significant and terrible cry:

<hi type="bold">yielded up</hi><div eID="gen3480" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3481" type="x-p"/> Literally, "dismissed his spirit." The (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G111">ἀθέμιτος</w>). This expression, taken with <reference osisRef="mr 15:37">Mark 15:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:46">Luke 23:46</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:30">John 19:30</reference>. differentiates the death of Christ from all other physical death. He died by his own volition when He could say of His redemptive work, "It is finished." "No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself" <reference osisRef="joh 10:18">John 10:18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">veil</hi><div eID="gen3481" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3482" type="x-p"/> The veil which was rent was the veil which divided the holy place into which the priests entered from the holy of holies into which only the high priest might enter on the day of atonement, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 26:31">Exodus 26:31</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="le 16:1-30">Leviticus 16:1-30</reference> The rending of that veil, which was a type of the human body of Christ <reference osisRef="heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:20</reference> signified that a "new and living way" was opened for all believers into the very presence of God with no other sacrifice or priesthood save Christ's. (cf) ; <reference osisRef="heb 9:1-8">Hebrews 9:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:19-22"> 10:19-22</reference>.

<hi type="bold">graves</hi><div eID="gen3482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3483" type="x-p"/> That these bodies returned to their graves is not said and may not be inferred. The wave-sheaf <reference osisRef="le 23:10-12">Leviticus 23:10-12</reference> typifies the resurrection of Christ, but a sheaf implies plurality. It was a single "corn of wheat" that fell into the ground in the crucifixion and entombment of Christ <reference osisRef="joh 12:24">John 12:24,</reference> it was a sheaf which came forth in resurrection. The inference is that these saints, with the spirits of "just men made perfect" <reference osisRef="heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference> from Paradise, went with Jesus <reference osisRef="eph 4:8-10">Ephesians 4:8-10</reference> into heaven.

<hi type="bold">James</hi><div eID="gen3483" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3484" type="x-p"/> Son of Alphaeus. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:21">Matthew 4:21</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">other Mary</hi><div eID="gen3484" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3485" type="x-p"/> Supposed to be Mary the mother of James and Joses.

<hi type="bold">After three days</hi><div eID="gen3485" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3486" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="mt 16:21">Matthew 16:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 17:23"> 17:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 20:19"> 20:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:61"> 26:61</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 8:31">Mark 8:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 10:34"> 10:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 9:22">Luke 9:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:33"> 18:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 24:6 lu 24:7"> 24:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 2:19">John 2:19</reference> <div eID="gen3486" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv109"/><div sID="gen3487" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Matt.27"/>

<hi type="bold">In the end of the Sabbath</hi> <div eID="gen3488" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3489" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">In the end of the Sabbath</hi> <div eID="gen3489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3490" type="x-p"/> The order of events, combining the four narratives, is as follows: Three women, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and Salome, start for the sepulchre, followed by other women bearing spices. The three find the stone rolled away, and Mary Magdalene goes to tell the disciples. <reference osisRef="lu 23:55-lu 24:9">Luke 23:55-24:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:1 joh 20:2">John 20:1,2</reference>. Mary, the mother of James and Joses, draws nearer the tomb and sees the angel of the Lord <reference osisRef="mt 28:2">Matthew 28:2</reference>. She goes back to meet the other women following with the spices. Meanwhile Peter and John, warned by Mary Magdalene, arrive, look in, and go away <reference osisRef="joh 20:3-10">John 20:3-10</reference>. Mary Magdalene returns weeping, sees the two angels and then Jesus <reference osisRef="joh 20:11-18">John 20:11-18</reference> and goes as He bade her to tell the disciples. Mary (mother of James and Joses), meanwhile, has met the women with the spices and, returning with them, they see the two angels. ; <reference osisRef="lu 24:4 lu 24:5">Luke 24:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 16:5">Mark 16:5</reference>. They also receive the angelic message, and, going to seek the disciples, are met by Jesus. <reference osisRef="mt 28:8-10">Matthew 28:8-10</reference>.<div eID="gen3490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3491" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">end of</hi> Lit. end of the sabbaths. The sabbaths end, the first day comes. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 12:1">Matthew 12:1</reference>")</hi>. Also see, <reference osisRef="joh 20:19">John 20:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 20:7">Acts 20:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 16:2">1 Corinthians 16:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:10">Revelation 1:10</reference>.<div eID="gen3491" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3492" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">other Mary</hi> <div eID="gen3492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3493" type="x-p"/> Supposed to be Mary the mother of James and Joses.

<hi type="bold">the angel</hi><div eID="gen3493" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3494" type="x-p"/> an angel etc. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen3494" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3495" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Jesus</hi> <div eID="gen3495" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3496" type="x-p"/> The order of our Lord's appearances would seem to be: On the day of his resurrection:<div eID="gen3496" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) To Mary Magdalene <reference osisRef="joh 10:14-18">John 10:14-18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) To the women returning from the tomb with angelic message <reference osisRef="mt 28:8-10">Matthew 28:8-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) To Peter, probably in the afternoon <reference osisRef="lu 24:34">Luke 24:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:5">1 Corinthians 15:5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) To the Emmaus disciples toward evening <reference osisRef="lu 24:13-31">Luke 24:13-31</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) To the apostles, except Thomas <reference osisRef="lu 24:36-43">Luke 24:36-43</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:19-24">John 20:19-24</reference>. Eight days afterward:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) to the apostles, Thomas being present <reference osisRef="joh 20:24-29">John 20:24-29</reference>. In Galilee: (1a) To the seven by the Lake of Tiberias <reference osisRef="joh 21:1-23">John 21:1-23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) On a mountain, to the apostles and five hundred brethren <reference osisRef="1co 15:6">1 Corinthians 15:6</reference>. At Jerusalem and Bethany again:</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) To James <reference osisRef="1co 15:7">1 Corinthians 15:7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) To the eleven <reference osisRef="mt 28:16-20">Matthew 28:16-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 16:14-20">Mark 16:14-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 24:33-53">Luke 24:33-53</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:3-12">Acts 1:3-12</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3497" type="x-p"/> To Paul:<div eID="gen3497" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Near Damascus <reference osisRef="ac 9:3-6">Acts 9:3-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:8">1 Corinthians 15:8</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) In the temple <reference osisRef="ac 22:17-21">Acts 22:17-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 23:11"> 23:11</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3498" type="x-p"/> To Stephen outside Jerusalem <reference osisRef="ac 7:55">Acts 7:55</reference>.<div eID="gen3498" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3499" type="x-p"/> To John on Patmos <reference osisRef="re 1:10-19">Revelation 1:10-19</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Go</hi><div eID="gen3499" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3500" type="x-p"/> With the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ begins the "dispensation of the grace of God" <reference osisRef="eph 3:2">Ephesians 3:2,</reference> which is defined as "his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus"; and, "the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast." <reference osisRef="eph 2:7-9">Ephesians 2:7-9,</reference> under grace God freely gives to the believing sinner eternal life <reference osisRef="ro 6:23">Romans 6:23</reference> accounts to him a perfect righteousness ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:21 ro 3:22">Romans 3:21,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 4:4 ro 4:5"> 4:4,5</reference> and accords to him a perfect position <reference osisRef="eph 1:6">Ephesians 1:6</reference><div eID="gen3500" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3501" type="x-p"/> The predicted results of this sixth testing of man are<div eID="gen3501" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) the salvation of all who believe <reference osisRef="ac 16:31">Acts 16:31</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) judgment upon an unbelieving world and an apostate church. <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference>; <reference osisRef="2th 1:7-10">2 Thessalonians 1:7-10</reference> ; <reference osisRef="1pe 4:17 1pe 4:18">1 Peter 4:17,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:15 re 3:16">Revelation 3:15,16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Man's state at the beginning of the dispensation of Grace <reference osisRef="ro 3:19">Romans 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:22">Galatians 3:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:11 eph 2:12">Ephesians 2:11,12</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Man's responsibility under grace <reference osisRef="joh 1:11 joh 1:12">John 1:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:36"> 3:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:28 joh 6:29"> 6:28,29</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) His predicted failure <reference osisRef="mt 24:37-39">Matthew 24:37-39</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:8">Luke 18:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 19:12-14"> 19:12-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The judgment <reference osisRef="2th 2:7-12">2 Thessalonians 2:7-12</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3502" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Name</hi> <div eID="gen3502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3503" type="x-p"/> The word is in the singular, the "name," not names. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv109"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Mark</title> <div sID="gen3513" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="mr 1">Read first chapter of Mark</reference><div eID="gen3513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3514" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The writer of the second Gospel, Mark, called also John, was the son of one the New Testament "Marys", and nephew of Barnabas. He was an associate of the apostles, and is mentioned in the writings of Paul and of Luke <reference osisRef="ac 12:12 ac 12:25">Acts 12:12,25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:37 ac 15:39"> 15:37,39</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 4:10">Colossians 4:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:11">2 Timothy 4:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="phm 1:24">Philemon 1:24</reference>.<div eID="gen3514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3515" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of Mark has been variously placed between A.D. 57 and 63.<div eID="gen3515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3516" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The scope and purpose of the book are evident from its contents. In it Jesus is seen as the mighty Worker, rather than as the unique Teacher. It is the Gospel of Jehovah's "Servant the Branch" <reference osisRef="zec 3:8">Zechariah 3:8</reference> as Matthew is the Gospel of the "Branch...unto David" <reference osisRef="jer 33:15">Jeremiah 33:15</reference>.<div eID="gen3516" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3517" type="x-p"/> Everywhere the servant character of the incarnate Son is manifest. The key verse is <reference osisRef="mr 10:45">Mark 10:45</reference>. "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister." The characteristic word is "straightway," a servant's word. There is no genealogy, for who gives the genealogy of a servant? The distinctive character of Christ in Mark is that set forth in <reference osisRef="php 2:6-8">Philippians 2:6-8</reference>.<div eID="gen3517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3518" type="x-p"/> But this lowly Servant, who emptied Himself of the "form of God," "and was found in fashion as a man," was, nevertheless, "the mighty God" <reference osisRef="isa 9:6">Isaiah 9:6</reference> as Mark distinctly declares (<reference osisRef="mr 1:1">Mark 1:1</reference>) and therefore mighty works accompanied and authenticated His ministry. As befits a Servant-Gospel, Mark is characteristically a Gospel of deeds, rather than on words.<div eID="gen3518" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3519" type="x-p"/> The best preparation of the heart for the study of Mark is the prayerful reading of <reference osisRef="isa 42:1-21">Isaiah 42:1-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 50:4-11 isa 52:13-isa 53:12"> 50:4-11, 52:13-53:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 3:8">Zechariah 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:5-8">Philippians 2:5-8</reference>.<div eID="gen3519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3520" type="x-p"/> Mark is in five principal divisions:<div eID="gen3520" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The manifestation of the Servant-Son, 1:1-11.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Servant-Son tested as to His fidelity, 1:12,13.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Servant-Son at work, 1:14-13:37.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Servant-Son "obedient unto death," 14:1-15:47.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The ministry of the risen Servant-Son, now exalted to all authority, 16:1-20.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3521" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in this book cover a period of 7 years. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv109"/><hi type="bold">end of the world</hi><div eID="gen3521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3522" type="x-p"/> consummation of the age.
<hi type="bold">Lord</hi><div eID="gen3522" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3523" type="x-p"/> Jehovah. <reference osisRef="isa 40:3">Isaiah 40:3</reference>.

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv111"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Luke</title> <div sID="gen3662" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="lu 1">Read first chapter of Luke</reference><div eID="gen3662" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3663" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The writer of the third Gospel is called by Paul "the beloved physician" <reference osisRef="col 4:14">Colossians 4:14</reference> and, as we learn from the Acts, was Paul's frequent companion. He was of Jewish ancestry, but his correct Greek marks him as a Jew of the dispersion. Tradition says that he was a Jew of Antioch, as Paul was of Tarsus.<div eID="gen3663" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3664" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of Luke falls between A.D. 63 and 68.<div eID="gen3664" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3665" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Luke is the Gospel of the human-divine One, as John is of the divine-human One. The key-phrase is "Son of man," and the key-verse <reference osisRef="lu 19:10">Luke 19:10</reference>. "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost." In harmony with this intent, Luke relates those things concerning Jesus which demonstrate how entirely human He was. His genealogy is traced to Adam, and the most detailed account is given of His mother, and of His infancy and boyhood. The parables peculiar to Luke have distinctively the human and the seeking note. But Luke is careful to guard the Deity and Kingship of Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="lu 1:32-35">Luke 1:32-35</reference>. Luke, then, is the Gospel of "the man whose name is The BRANCH" <reference osisRef="zec 6:12">Zechariah 6:12</reference>.<div eID="gen3665" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3666" type="x-p"/> Luke has seven chief divisions:<div eID="gen3666" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The Evangelist's Introduction, 1:1-4.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The human relationships of Jesus, 1:5-2:52.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The baptism, ancestry, and testing of Jesus, 3:1-4:13.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The ministry of the Son of man as Prophet-King in Galilee, 4:14-9:50.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The final offer of the Son of man as King to israel, His rejection and sacrifice, 19:45-23:56.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The resurrection, resurrection ministry, and ascension of the Son of man, 24:1-53.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3667" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in this book cover a period of 39 years. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv111"/><hi type="bold">from</hi><div eID="gen3667" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3668" type="x-p"/> "From the very first": (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G509">ἄνωθεν</w>," "from above)." So translated in <reference osisRef="joh 3:31">John 3:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:11"> 19:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 1:17">James 1:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 3:15 jas 3:17"> 3:15,17</reference>. In no other place is ANOTHEN translated "from the very first." The use by Luke of anothen is an affirmation that his knowledge of these things, derived from those who had been eye-witnesses from the beginning <reference osisRef="lu 1:2">Luke 1:2</reference> was confirmed by revelation. In like manner Paul had doubtless heard from the eleven the story of the institution of the Lord's Supper, but he also had it by revelation from the Lord (cf) <reference osisRef="1co 11:23">1 Corinthians 11:23</reference> and his writing, like Luke's anothen knowledge, thus became first-hand, not traditional, merely.<div eID="gen3668" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3669" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">understanding</hi> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G509">ἄνωθεν</w>," lit). followed alongside of; or, closely traced.<div eID="gen3669" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3670" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in order</hi> The words "in order" are emphatic, indicating Luke's purpose to reduce to order the Gospel story.

<hi type="bold">just and devout</hi> <div eID="gen3689" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3690" type="x-p"/> righteousness<div eID="gen3690" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3691" type="x-p"/> The O.T. righteousness. Summary: In the O.T. "righteous" and "just" are English words used to translate the Hebrew words yasher, "upright"; tsadiq, "just"; tsidkah, "righteous." In all of these words but one idea inheres: the righteous, or just, man is so called, because he is right with God; and he is right with God because he has walked "in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless" <reference osisRef="lu 1:6">Luke 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:5">Romans 10:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="phm 3:6">Philemon 3:6</reference>. The O.T. righteous man was not sinless <reference osisRef="ec 7:20">Ecclesiastes 7:20,</reference> but one who, for all his sins, resorted to the ordinances, and offered in faith the required sacrifice (e.g.) <reference osisRef="le 4:27-35">Leviticus 4:27-35</reference> CF. "Righteousness (N.T.), <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi> and Paul's contrast, <reference osisRef="php 3:4-9">Philippians 3:4-9</reference>.

Cf. <reference osisRef="joh 1:1 joh 1:2">John 1:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:29"> 8:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 17:5">Matthew 17:5</reference>.

<hi type="bold">son of Heli</hi><div eID="gen3699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3700" type="x-p"/> In Matthew, where unquestionably we have the genealogy of Joseph, we are told <reference osisRef="mt 1:16">Matthew 1:16,</reference> that Joseph was the son of Jacob. In what sense, then, could he be called in Luke "the son of Heli"? He could not be by natural generation the son both of Jacob and of Heli. But in Luke it is not said that Heli begat Joseph, so that the natural explanation is that Joseph was the son-in-law of Heli, who was, like himself, a descendant of David. That he should in that case be called "son of Heli" ("son" is not in the Greek, but rightly supplied by the translators) would be in accord with Jewish usage.<div eID="gen3700" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3701" type="x-p"/> (CF) <reference osisRef="1sa 24:16">1 Samuel 24:16</reference> The conclusion is therefore inevitable that in Luke we have Mary's genealogy; and Joseph was "son of Heli" because espoused to Heli's daughter. The genealogy in Luke is Mary's, whose father, Heli, was descended from David.

<hi type="bold">teach us to pray</hi> <div eID="gen3744" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3745" type="x-p"/> This is the central N.T. passage on prayer. In the Sermon on the Mount Christ had announced the new basis of prayer, viz.: relationship <reference osisRef="mt 6:9 mt 6:28-32">Matthew 6:9,28-32</reference>. The believer is a child of God through the new birth. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 3:3">John 3:3</reference>")</hi>. The clear revelation of this fact at once establishes the reasonableness of prayer; a reasonableness against which the argument from the apparent uniformity of natural law shatters itself. God is more than a Creator, bringing a universe into being, and establishing laws for it; more than a decree- maker determining future events by an eternal fiat. Above all this is the divine family for whom the universe with its laws exists ; <reference osisRef="col 1:16-20">Colossians 1:16-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:2">Hebrews 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:10 heb 2:11"> 2:10,11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:17">Romans 8:17</reference>".<div eID="gen3745" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3746" type="x-p"/> When ye pray, say, Our Father." What God habitually does in the material universe concerns the reverent investigator of that universe. What He may do in His own family concerns Him, and them, and is matter for divine promise and revelation. Science, which deals only with natural phenomena, cannot intrude there <reference osisRef="1co 2:9">1 Corinthians 2:9</reference>.<div eID="gen3746" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3747" type="x-p"/> Christ's law of prayer may be thus summarized:<div eID="gen3747" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) He grounds prayer upon relationship, and reveals God as freely charging himself with all the responsibilities, as His heart glows with all the affections of a Father toward all who believe on Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="mt 6:25 mt 6:32">Matthew 6:25,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 7:9-11"> 7:9-11</reference>. Prayer, therefore, is a child's petition to an all-wise, all-loving, and all-powerful, Father-God.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) In the so-called Lord's prayer Christ gives an incomparable model for all prayer. It teaches that right prayer begins with worship; puts the interest of the kingdom before merely personal interest; accepts beforehand the Father's will, whether to grant or withhold; and petitions for present need, leaving the future to the Father's care and love. Used as a form, the Lord's prayer is, dispensationally, upon legal, not church ground; it is not a prayer in the name of Christ (cf) <reference osisRef="joh 14:13 joh 14:14">John 14:13,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 16:24"> 16:24</reference> and it makes human forgiveness, as under the law it must, the condition of divine forgiveness; an order which grace exactly reverses (cf) <reference osisRef="eph 4:32">Ephesians 4:32</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Prayer is to be definite <reference osisRef="lu 11:5 lu 11:6">Luke 11:5,6</reference> and,</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) importunate, that is undiscouraged by delayed answers. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">give</hi><div eID="gen3753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3754" type="x-p"/> It is evident that none of the disciples, with the possible exception of Mary of Bethany, asked for the Spirit in the faith of this promise. It was a new and staggering thing to a Jew that, in advance of the fulfilment of <reference osisRef="joe 2:28 joe 2:29">Joel 2:28,29</reference> all might receive the Spirit. Mary alone of the disciples understood Christ's repeated declaration concerning His own death and resurrection <reference osisRef="joh 12:3-7">John 12:3-7</reference>. Save Mary, not one of the disciples but Peter, and he only in the great confession <reference osisRef="mt 16:16">Matthew 16:16</reference> manifested a spark of spiritual intelligence till after the resurrection of Christ and the impartation of the Spirit ; <reference osisRef="joh 20:22">John 20:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:1-4">Acts 2:1-4</reference>. To go back to the promise of <reference osisRef="lu 11:13">Luke 11:13,</reference> is to forget Pentecost, and to ignore the truth that now every believer has the indwelling Spirit ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:9 ro 8:15">Romans 8:9,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 6:19">1 Corinthians 6:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:6">Galatians 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:20 1jo 2:27">1 John 2:20,27</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 2:4">Acts 2:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">hell</hi> <div eID="gen3782" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3783" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G86">ᾅδης</w>, "the unseen world," is revealed as the place of departed human spirits between death and resurrection). The word occurs, <reference osisRef="mt 11:23">Matthew 11:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 16:18"> 16:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 10:15">Luke 10:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:27 ac 2:31">Acts 2:27,31</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:18">Revelation 1:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 6:8"> 6:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:13 re 20:14"> 20:13,14</reference> and is the equivalent of the O.T. "sheol." <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5">Habakkuk 2:5</reference>")</hi>. The Septuagint invariably renders sheol by hades.<div eID="gen3783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3784" type="x-p"/> Summary:<div eID="gen3784" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Hades before the ascension of Christ. The passages in which the word occurs make it clear that hades was formerly in two divisions, the abodes respectively of the saved and of the lost. The former was called "paradise" and "Abraham's bosom." Both designations were Talmudic, but adopted by Christ in <reference osisRef="lu 16:22">Luke 16:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:43"> 23:43</reference>. The blessed dead were with Abraham, they were conscious and were "comforted" <reference osisRef="lu 16:25">Luke 16:25</reference>. The believing malefactor was to be, that day, with Christ in "paradise." The lost were separated from the saved by a "great gulf fixed" <reference osisRef="lu 16:26">Luke 16:26</reference>. The representative man of the lost who are now in hades is the rich man of <reference osisRef="lu 16:19-31">Luke 16:19-31</reference>. He was alive, conscious, in the full exercise of his faculties, memory, etc., and in torment.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Hades since the ascension of Christ. So far as the unsaved dead are concerned, no change of their place or condition is revealed in Scripture. At the judgment of the great white throne, hades will give them up, they will be judged, and will pass into the lake of fire <reference osisRef="re 20:13 re 20:14">Revelation 20:13,14</reference>. But a change has taken place which affects paradise. Paul was "caught up to the third heaven...into paradise" <reference osisRef="2co 12:1-4">2 Corinthians 12:1-4</reference>. Paradise, therefore, is now in the immediate presence of God. It is believed that <reference osisRef="eph 4:8-10">Ephesians 4:8-10</reference> indicates the time of the change. "When he ascended up on high he led a multitude of captives." It is immediately added that He had previously "descended first into the lower parts of the earth," i.e. the paradise division of Hades. During the present church-age the saved who died are "absent from the body, at home with the Lord." The wicked dead in hades, and the righteous dead "at home with the Lord," alike await the resurrection ; <reference osisRef="job 19:25">Job 19:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:52</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:22">Matthew 5:22</reference>")</hi>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv113"/><div sID="gen3785" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Luke.16"/>

<div eID="gen3788" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3789" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G1787">ἐντός</w> in the midst)." It could not be said of a self-righteous, Christ rejecting pharisee, that the kingdom of God, as to its spiritual content, was within him. The kingdom in its outward form, as covenanted to David <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference> and described by the prophets <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi> had been rejected by the Jews; so that, during this present age, it would not "come with observation" (lit. "outward show") but in the hearts of men (cf) ; <reference osisRef="lu 19:11 lu 19:12">Luke 19:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:6-8">Acts 1:6-8</reference>.<div eID="gen3789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3790" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 1:6">Acts 1:6</reference>")</hi>. <hi type="bold">when</hi><div eID="gen3825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3826" type="x-p"/> Verses 20,24 are not included in the report of the Olivet discourse as given by Matthew and Mark. Two sieges of Jerusalem are in view in that discourse. <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference> refers to the siege by Titus, A.D. 70, when the city was taken, and verse 24 literally fulfilled. But that siege and its horrors but adumbrate the final siege at the end of this age, in which the "great tribulation" culminates. At that time the city will be taken, but delivered by the glorious appearing of the Lord <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference>. The references in ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:15-28">Matthew 24:15-28,</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 13:14-26">Mark 13:14-26</reference> are to the final tribulation siege; <reference osisRef="lu 21:20-24">Luke 21:20-24</reference> to the destruction of Jerusalem by Titus. In Luke the sign is the compassing of Jerusalem by armies <reference osisRef="lu 21:20">Luke 21:20</reference> in ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:15">Matthew 24:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 13:14">Mark 13:14</reference> the sign is the abomination in the holy place. <reference osisRef="2th 2:4">2 Thessalonians 2:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">trodden down of the Gentiles</hi><div eID="gen3826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3827" type="x-p"/> The "times of the Gentiles" began with the captivity of Judah under Nebuchadnezzar <reference osisRef="2ch 36:1-21">2 Chronicles 36:1-21,</reference> since which time Jerusalem has been under Gentile overlordship.

The Jewish age was marked by temporal blessings as the reward of an obedient people. <reference osisRef="de 28:1-15">Deuteronomy 28:1-15</reference>.<div eID="gen3861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3862" type="x-p"/> In the kingdom-age spiritual and temporal blessings unite.<div eID="gen3862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3863" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">heaven</hi> <div eID="gen3863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3864" type="x-p"/> The Scriptures distinguish three heavens: first, the lower heavens, or the region of the clouds; secondly, the second or planetary heavens; and, thirdly, the heaven of heavens, the abode of God. <chapter eID="Luke.24"/><div eID="gen3864" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen3661" osisID="Luke" type="book"/>
