<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv113"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - John</title> <div sID="gen3866" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="joh 1">Read first chapter of John</reference><div eID="gen3866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3867" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The fourth Gospel was written by the Apostle John <reference osisRef="joh 21:24">John 21:24</reference>. This has been questioned on critical grounds, but on the same grounds and with equal scholarship, the early date and Johanean authorship have been maintained.<div eID="gen3867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3868" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of John's Gospel falls between A.D. 85 and 90. Probably the latter.<div eID="gen3868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3869" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: This is indicated both in the Prologue (<reference osisRef="joh 1:1-14"> 1:1-14</reference>), and in the last verse of the Gospel proper (<reference osisRef="joh 20:31"> 20:31</reference>), and is: The incarnation of the eternal Word, and Son of life; (2) that as many as believe on Him as "the Christ, the Son of God" (<reference osisRef="joh 20:31"> 20:31</reference>) may have eternal life. The prominent words are, "believed" and "life."<div eID="gen3869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3870" type="x-p"/> The book is in seven natural divisions:<div eID="gen3870" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Prologue: The eternal Word incarnate in Jesus the Christ, 1:1-14.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The witness of John the Baptist, 1:15-34.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The public ministry of Christ, 1:35-12:50.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The private ministry of Christ to His own, 13:1-17:26.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The sacrifice of Christ, 18:1-19:42.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The manifestation of Christ in resurrection, 20:1-31.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Epilogue: Christ the Master of life and service, 21:1-25.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3871" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in this book cover a period of 7 years. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv113"/><hi type="bold">Word</hi><div eID="gen3871" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3872" type="x-p"/> Gr. "Logos" (arm. "Memra," used in the Targums, or Heb. paraphrases, for God). The Greek term means,<div eID="gen3872" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) a thought or concept;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the expression or utterance of that thought. As a designation of Christ, therefore, Logos is peculiarly felicitous because,</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) in Him are embodied all the treasures of the divine wisdom, the collective "thought" of God <reference osisRef="1co 1:24">1 Corinthians 1:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:11">Ephesians 3:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 2:2 col 2:3">Colossians 2:2,3</reference> and,</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He is from eternity, but especially in His incarnation, the utterance or expression of the Person, and "thought" of Deity <reference osisRef="joh 1:3-5 joh 1:9 joh 1:14-18">John 1:3-5,9,14-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 14:9-11"> 14:9-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 2:9">Colossians 2:9</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3873" type="x-p"/> In the Being, Person, and work of Christ, Deity is told out.
<hi type="bold">comprehended</hi><div eID="gen3873" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3874" type="x-p"/> Or, apprehended; lit. "laid not hold of it."

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen3874" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3875" type="x-p"/> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">He came</hi><div eID="gen3875" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3876" type="x-p"/> i.e. He came unto his own things, and his own people received him not.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen3876" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3877" type="x-p"/> Grace. Summary:<div eID="gen3877" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Grace is "the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man... not by works of righteousness which we have done" <reference osisRef="tit 3:4 tit 3:5">Titus 3:4,5</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3878" type="x-p"/> It is, therefore, constantly set in contrast to law, under which God demands righteousness from man, as, under grace, he gives righteousness to man <reference osisRef="ro 3:21 ro 3:22">Romans 3:21,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:4"> 8:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="phm 3:9">Philemon 3:9</reference>. Law is connected with Moses and works; grace with Christ and faith ; <reference osisRef="joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:4-10">Romans 10:4-10</reference>. Law blesses the good; grace saves the bad ; <reference osisRef="ex 19:5">Exodus 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:1-9">Ephesians 2:1-9</reference>. Law demands that blessings be earned; grace is a free gift ; <reference osisRef="de 28:1-6">Deuteronomy 28:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:8">Ephesians 2:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 4:4 ro 4:5">Romans 4:4,5</reference>.<div eID="gen3878" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) As a dispensation, grace begins with the death and resurrection of Christ <reference osisRef="ro 3:24-26">Romans 3:24-26</reference> <reference osisRef="ro 4:24 ro 4:25"> 4:24,25</reference>. The point of testing is no longer legal obedience as the condition of salvation, but acceptance or rejection of Christ, with good works as a fruit of salvation, ; <reference osisRef="joh 1:12 joh 1:13">John 1:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:36"> 3:36</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 21:37">Matthew 21:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 22:24"> 22:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:22 joh 15:25">John 15:22,25</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:2">Hebrews 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:10-12">1 John 5:10-12</reference>. The immediate result of this testing was the rejection of Christ by the Jews, and His crucifixion by Jew and Gentile <reference osisRef="ac 4:27">Acts 4:27</reference>. The predicted end of the testing of man under grace is the apostasy of the professing church: See "Apostasy" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Ti 3:1">2 Timothy 3:1</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-8">2 Timothy 3:1-8</reference> and the resultant apocalyptic judgments.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Grace has a twofold manifestation: in salvation <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference> and in the walk and service of the saved <reference osisRef="ro 6:15">Romans 6:15</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen3879" type="x-p"/> See, for the other six dispensations:<div eID="gen3879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3880" type="x-p"/> Innocence, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:28">Genesis 1:28</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3881" type="x-p"/> Conscience, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:23">Genesis 3:23</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3881" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3882" type="x-p"/> Human Government, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 8:21">Genesis 8:21</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3883" type="x-p"/> Promise, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 12:1">Genesis 12:1</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3884" type="x-p"/> Law, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:8">Exodus 19:8</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen3884" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3885" type="x-p"/> Kingdom, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">hath seen God</hi><div eID="gen3885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3886" type="x-p"/> CF <reference osisRef="ge 32:20">Genesis 32:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 24:10">Exodus 24:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 33:18"> 33:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 6:22">Judges 6:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 13:22"> 13:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 22:4">Revelation 22:4</reference>. The divine essence, God, veiled in angelic form, and especially as incarnate in Jesus Christ, has been seen of men. ; <reference osisRef="ge 18:2 ge 18:22">Genesis 18:2,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 14:8 joh 14:9">John 14:8,9</reference>.<div eID="gen3886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3887" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">declared</hi> Lit. led him forth, i.e. into full revelation. <reference osisRef="joh 14:9">John 14:9</reference>.
<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen3887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3888" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Come</hi> The call to discipleship. Cf. <reference osisRef="mt 4:18-22">Matthew 4:18-22</reference> the call to service.<div eID="gen3888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tenth hour</hi> That was two hours before night.

<hi type="bold">born again</hi> <div eID="gen3891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3892" type="x-p"/> Regeneration:<div eID="gen3892" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The necessity of the new birth grows out of the incapacity of the natural man to "see" or "enter into" the kingdom of God. However gifted, moral, or refined, the natural man is absolutely blind to spiritual truth, and impotent to enter the kingdom; for he can neither obey, understand, nor please God <reference osisRef="joh 3:3 joh 3:5 joh 3:6">John 3:3,5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 51:5">Psalms 51:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 17:9">Jeremiah 17:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 7:21-23">Mark 7:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 2:14">1 Corinthians 2:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:7 ro 8:8">Romans 8:7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:3">Ephesians 2:3</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The new birth is not a reformation of the old nature <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 6:6">Romans 6:6</reference>")</hi> but a creative act of the holy Spirit <reference osisRef="joh 3:5">John 3:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:12 joh 1:13"> 1:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 5:17">2 Corinthians 5:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:10">Ephesians 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:24"> 4:24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The condition of the new birth is faith in Christ crucified <reference osisRef="joh 3:14 joh 3:15">John 3:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:12 joh 1:13"> 1:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:24">Galatians 3:24</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Through the new birth the believer becomes a partaker of the divine nature and of the life of Christ Himself <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:10">Ephesians 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:24"> 4:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:27">Colossians 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:23-25">1 Peter 1:23-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 1:4">2 Peter 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:10-12">1 John 5:10-12</reference> </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">I am the door of the sheep</hi> <div eID="gen3960" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3961" type="x-p"/> The shepherd work of our Lord has three aspects:<div eID="gen3961" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) As the "Good" Shepherd He gives His life for the sheep <reference osisRef="joh 10:11">John 10:11</reference> and is, therefore, "the door" by which "if any man enter in he shall be saved." <reference osisRef="joh 10:9">John 10:9</reference>. This answers to Ps 22.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He is the "Great" Shepherd, "brought again from the dead" <reference osisRef="heb 13:20">Hebrews 13:20</reference> to care for and make perfect the sheep. This answers to Ps 23.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) He is the "Chief" Shepherd, who is coming in glory to give crowns of reward to the faithful shepherds <reference osisRef="1pe 5:4">1 Peter 5:4</reference>. This answers to Ps 24. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">Mary</hi> As Martha stands for service, and Lazarus for communion, so Mary shows us the worship of a grateful heart. Others before her had come to his feet to have their need met; she came to give Him His due. Though two of the evangelists record her act, John alone gives her name.<div eID="gen3972" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3973" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">feet of</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 26:7">Matthew 26:7</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">when they</hi><div eID="gen3973" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3974" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 21:4">Matthew 21:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen3974" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3975" type="x-p"/> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">answered</hi><div eID="gen3975" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3976" type="x-p"/> He does not receive these Gentiles. A Christ in the flesh, King of the Jews, could be no proper object of faith to the Gentiles, though the Jews should have believed on Him as such. For Gentiles the corn of wheat must fall into the ground and die; Christ must be lifted up on the cross and believed in as a sacrifice for sin, as seed of Abraham, not David <reference osisRef="joh 12:24 joh 12:32">John 12:24,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:7-14">Galatians 3:7-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:11-13">Ephesians 2:11-13</reference>.<div eID="gen3976" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3977" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Except</hi><div eID="gen3977" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3978" type="x-p"/> Chapters 12-17 are a progression according to the order of approach to God in the tabernacle types: chapter 12., in which Christ speaks of His death, answers to the brazen altar of burnt-offering, type of the cross. Passing from the altar toward the holy of holies, the laver is next reached <reference osisRef="ex 30:17-21">Exodus 30:17-21,</reference> answering to Chapter 13. With His associate priests, now purified, the High Priest approaches and enters the holy place, in the high communion of Chapters 14-16. Entering alone the holy of holies <reference osisRef="joh 17:1">John 17:1,</reference> the High Priest intercedes. (Cf) <reference osisRef="heb 7:24-28">Hebrews 7:24-28</reference>. That intercession is not for the salvation, but the keeping and blessing of those for whom He prays. His death (assumed as accomplished), <reference osisRef="joh 17:4">John 17:4</reference> has saved them.

<hi type="bold">needeth</hi><div eID="gen3990" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3991" type="x-p"/> The underlying imagery is of an oriental returning from the public baths to his house. His feet would contract defilement and require cleansing, but not his body. So the believer is cleansed as before the law from all sin "once for all" <reference osisRef="heb 10:1-12">Hebrews 10:1-12</reference> but needs ever to bring his daily sins to the Father in confession, that he may abide in unbroken fellowship with the Father and with the Son <reference osisRef="1jo 1:1-10">1 John 1:1-10</reference>. The blood of Christ answers forever to all the law could say as to the believer's guilt, but he needs constant cleansing from the defilement of sin, ; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25-27">Ephesians 5:25-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:6">1 John 5:6</reference>. Typically, the order of approach to the presence of God was, first, the brazen altar of sacrifice, and then the laver of cleansing <reference osisRef="ex 40:6 ex 40:7">Exodus 40:6,7</reference>. See, also, the order in <reference osisRef="ex 30:17-21">Exodus 30:17-21</reference>. Christ cannot have communion with a defiled saint, but He can and will cleanse him.<div eID="gen3991" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3992" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">washed</hi> Lit. bathed. The Greek word signifies a complete ablution. "Wash" is another word.

<hi type="bold">Son of man</hi><div eID="gen3992" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3993" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 8:20">Matthew 8:20</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="John.13"/><div eID="gen3993" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">receive you unto myself</hi> <div eID="gen3994" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3995" type="x-p"/> This promise of a second advent of Christ is to be distinguished from His return in glory to the earth; it is the first intimation in Scripture of "the day of Christ". <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 1:8">1 Corinthians 1:8</reference>")</hi>. Here He comes for His saints <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference> there <reference osisRef="mt 24:29 mt 24:30">Matthew 24:29,30</reference>. He come to judge the nations, etc.

Translated "advocate," <reference osisRef="1jo 2:1">1 John 2:1</reference>. Christ is the believer's Paraclete with the Father when he sins; the Holy Spirit the believer's indwelling Paraclete to help his ignorance and infirmity and to make intercession <reference osisRef="ro 8:26 ro 8:27">Romans 8:26,27</reference>.<div eID="gen3996" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3997" type="x-p"/> (See "Holy Spirit," N.T. doctrine,) <reference osisRef="mt 1:18">Matthew 1:18</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 2:4">Acts 2:4</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen3997" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen3998" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">And I will</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Lu 11:13">Luke 11:13</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">purgeth</hi><div eID="gen4006" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4007" type="x-p"/> Three conditions of the fruitful life: Cleansing, <reference osisRef="joh 15:2 joh 15:3">John 15:2,3</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 13:10">John 13:10</reference>")</hi> , abiding , See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:joh 15:4">John 15:4</reference>", obedience, <reference osisRef="joh 15:4 joh 15:10 joh 15:12">John 15:4,10,12,</reference> (See "Law of Christ,") <reference osisRef="ga 6:2">Galatians 6:2</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2jo 1:5">2 John 1:5</reference>".

<hi type="bold">abide</hi><div eID="gen4007" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4008" type="x-p"/> To abide in Christ is, on the one hand, to have no known sin unjudged and unconfessed, no interest into which He is not brought, no life which He cannot share. On the other hand, the abiding one takes all burdens to Him, and draws all wisdom, life and strength from Him. It is not unceasing consciousness of these things, and of Him, but that nothing is allowed in the life which separates from Him.<div eID="gen4008" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4009" type="x-p"/> See "Fellowship," <reference osisRef="1jo 1:3">1 John 1:3</reference>. See "Communion," <reference osisRef="1co 10:16">1 Corinthians 10:16</reference>.

<hi type="bold">much fruit</hi><div eID="gen4009" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4010" type="x-p"/> Three degrees in fruit-bearing: "Fruit," <reference osisRef="joh 15:2">John 15:2,</reference> "more fruit," <reference osisRef="joh 15:2">John 15:2,</reference> "much fruit," <reference osisRef="joh 15:5 joh 15:8">John 15:5,8</reference>. As we bear "much fruit" the Father is glorified in us. The minor moralities and graces of Christianity are often imitated, but never the ninefold "fruit" of <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23">Galatians 5:22,23</reference>. Where such fruit is the Father glorified. The Pharisees were moral and intensely "religious," but not one of them could say with Christ, "I have glorified thee on the earth" <reference osisRef="joh 17:4">John 17:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">I have yet</hi><div eID="gen4018" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4019" type="x-p"/> Christ's pre-authentication of the New Testament:<div eID="gen4019" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) he expressly declared that He would leave "many things" unrevealed (<reference osisRef="joh 16:12">John 16:12</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He promised that this revelation should be completed ("all things") after the Spirit should come, and that such additional revelation should include new prophecies (Joh 16:)).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) He chose certain persons to receive such additional revelations, and to be His witnesses to them <reference osisRef="mt 28:19">Matthew 28:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:27">John 15:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 16:13"> 16:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:15-17">Acts 9:15-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) he gave to their words when speaking for Him in the Spirit precisely the same authority as His own <reference osisRef="mt 10:14 mt 10:15">Matthew 10:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 10:16">Luke 10:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 13:20">John 13:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 17:20"> 17:20</reference> see e.g. <reference osisRef="1co 14:37">1 Corinthians 14:37</reference> and "Inspiration," ; <reference osisRef="ex 4:15">Exodus 4:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 22:19">Revelation 22:19</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">glorify</hi> <div eID="gen4026" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4027" type="x-p"/> Seven petitions:<div eID="gen4027" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) That Jesus may be glorified as the Son who has glorified the Father (<reference osisRef="joh 17:1">John 17:1</reference>), <reference osisRef="php 2:9-11">Philippians 2:9-11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) for restoration to the eternal glory (<reference osisRef="joh 17:5">John 17:5</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) for the safety of believers from</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) the world (<reference osisRef="joh 17:11">John 17:11</reference>) (b) the evil one (<reference osisRef="joh 17:15">John 17:15</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) for the sanctification of believers (<reference osisRef="joh 17:17">John 17:17</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) for the spiritual unity of believers (<reference osisRef="joh 17:21">John 17:21</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) that the world may believe (<reference osisRef="joh 17:21">John 17:21</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) that believers may be with Him in heaven to behold and share His glory (<reference osisRef="joh 17:24">John 17:24</reference>). </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv117"/><div sID="gen4028" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv117"/> <hi type="bold">give eternal life</hi> <div eID="gen4028" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4029" type="x-p"/> Christ's gifts to those whom the Father gave Him: Eternal life <reference osisRef="joh 17:2">John 17:2</reference>; the Father's name (<reference osisRef="joh 17:6 joh 17:26">John 17:6,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:17"> 20:17</reference>), the Father's words (<reference osisRef="joh 17:8 joh 17:14">John 17:8,14</reference>)); His own joy (<reference osisRef="joh 17:13">John 17:13</reference>); His own glory (<reference osisRef="joh 17:22">John 17:22</reference>).<div eID="gen4029" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4030" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">given him</hi> <div eID="gen4030" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4031" type="x-p"/> Seven times Jesus speaks of believers as given to Him by the Father (<reference osisRef="joh 17:2 joh 17:6 joh 17:9 joh 17:11-12 joh 17:24">John 17:2,6,9,11,12,24</reference>). Jesus Christ is God's love-gift to the world (<reference osisRef="joh 3:16">John 3:16</reference>), and believers are the Father's love-gift to Jesus Christ. It is Christ who commits the believer to the Father for safe keeping, so that the believer's security rests upon the Father's faithfulness to His Son Jesus Christ.

A contradiction has been supposed. Three views are held:<div eID="gen4055" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) That Jesus speaks to Mary as the High Priest fulfilling the day of atonement (Le 16). Having accomplished the sacrifice, He was on His way to present the sacred blood in heaven, and that, between the meeting with Mary in the garden and the meeting of <reference osisRef="mt 28:9">Matthew 28:9</reference>. He had so ascended and returned: a view in harmony with types.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) That Mary Magdalene, knowing as yet only Christ after the flesh <reference osisRef="2co 5:15-17">2 Corinthians 5:15-17</reference> and having found her Beloved, sought only to hold Him so; while He, about to assume a new relation to His disciples in ascension, gently teaches Mary that now she must not seek to hold Him to the earth, but rather become His messenger of the new joy.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) That He merely meant: "Do not detain me now; I am not yet ascended; you will see me again; run rather to my brethren," etc.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4056" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Touch me not</hi> Or, do not detain me.

<hi type="bold">My Lord and My God</hi><div eID="gen4056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4057" type="x-p"/> The deity of Jesus Christ is declared in Scripture:<div eID="gen4057" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) In the intimations and explicit predictions of the O.T.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) The theophanies intimate the appearance of God in human form, and His ministry thus to man <reference osisRef="ge 16:7-13">Genesis 16:7-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 18:2-23"> 18:2-23</reference> especially ; <reference osisRef="ge 18:17">Genesis 18:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 32:28"> 32:28</reference> with ; <reference osisRef="ho 12:3-5">Hosea 12:3-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2-14">Exodus 3:2-14</reference>. (b) The Messiah is expressly declared to be the Son of God <reference osisRef="ps 2:2-9">Psalms 2:2-9</reference> and God ; <reference osisRef="ps 45:6 ps 45:7">Psalms 45:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:8 heb 1:9">Hebrews 1:8,9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 110:1">Psalms 110:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 22:44">Matthew 22:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:34">Acts 2:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:13">Hebrews 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 110:4">Psalms 110:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 5:6">Hebrews 5:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 6:20"> 6:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:17-21"> 7:17-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 6:13">Zechariah 6:13</reference>. (c) His virgin birth was foretold as the means through which God could be "Immanuel," God with us ; <reference osisRef="isa 7:13 isa 7:14">Isaiah 7:13,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 1:22 mt 1:23">Matthew 1:22,23</reference> (d) The Messiah is expressly invested with the divine names <reference osisRef="isa 9:6 isa 9:7">Isaiah 9:6,7</reference> (e) In a prophecy of His death He is called Jehovah's "fellow" ; <reference osisRef="zec 13:7">Zechariah 13:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 26:31">Matthew 26:31</reference>. (f) His eternal being is declared ; <reference osisRef="mic 5:2">Micah 5:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 2:6">Matthew 2:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 7:42">John 7:42</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Christ Himself affirmed His deity.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) He applied to Himself the Jehovistic I AM. (The pronoun "he" is not in the Greek; cf <reference osisRef="joh 8:24">John 8:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 8:56-58"> 8:56-58</reference>. The Jews correctly understood this to be our Lord's claim to full deity. <reference osisRef="joh 8:59">John 8:59</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4058" type="x-p"/> See also, <reference osisRef="joh 10:33">John 10:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 18:4-6"> 18:4-6</reference> where, also, "he" is not in the original.) (b) He claimed to be the Adonai of the O.T. <reference osisRef="mt 22:42-45">Matthew 22:42-45</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:2">Genesis 15:2</reference>")</hi>. (c) He asserted His identity with the Father ; <reference osisRef="mt 28:19">Matthew 28:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:62">Mark 14:62</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 10:30">John 10:30,</reference> that the Jews so understood Him is shown by ; <reference osisRef="joh 10:31 joh 10:32">John 10:31,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 14:8 joh 14:9"> 14:8,9</reference> <reference osisRef="joh 17:5"> 17:5</reference>. (d) He exercised the chief prerogative of God ; <reference osisRef="mr 2:5-7">Mark 2:5-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 7:48-50">Luke 7:48-50</reference>. (e) He asserted omnipresence ; <reference osisRef="mt 18:20">Matthew 18:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:13">John 3:13</reference> omniscience, <reference osisRef="joh 11:11-14">John 11:11-14,</reference> when Jesus was fifty miles away; <reference osisRef="mr 11:6-8">Mark 11:6-8,</reference> omnipotence ; <reference osisRef="mt 28:18">Matthew 28:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 7:14">Luke 7:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:21-23">John 5:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 6:19"> 6:19,</reference> mastery over nature, and creative power ; <reference osisRef="lu 9:16 lu 9:17">Luke 9:16,17</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 2:9">John 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 10:28"> 10:28</reference>. <div canonical="true" osisID="Acts" sID="gen4071" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Acts.1" sID="Acts.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv118"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Acts</title> <div sID="gen4072" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ac 1">Read first chapter of Acts</reference><div eID="gen4072" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4073" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: In the Acts of the Apostles Luke continues the account of Christianity begun in the Gospel which bears his name. In the "former treatise" he tells what Jesus "began both to do and teach"; in the Acts, what Jesus continued to do and teach through His Holy Spirit sent down.<div eID="gen4073" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4074" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The Acts concludes with the account of Paul's earliest ministry in Rome, A.D. 65, and appears to have been written at or near that time.<div eID="gen4074" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4075" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: This book records the ascension and promised return of the Lord Jesus, the descent of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost, Peter's use of the keys, opening the kingdom (considered as the sphere of profession, as in Mat. 13) to the Jews at Pentecost, and to the Gentiles in the house of Cornelius; the beginning of the Christian church and the conversion and ministry of Paul.<div eID="gen4075" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4076" type="x-p"/> The Holy Spirit fills the scene. As the presence of the Son, exalting and revealing the Father, is the great fact of the Gospels, so the presence of the Spirit, exalting and revealing the Son, is the great fact of the Acts.<div eID="gen4076" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4077" type="x-p"/> Acts is in two chief parts: In the first section (1-<reference osisRef="ac 9:43"> 9:43</reference>) Peter is the prominent personage, Jerusalem is the center, and the ministry is to Jews. Already in covenant relations with Jehovah, they had sinned in rejecting Jesus as the Christ. The preaching, therefore, was directed to that point, and repentance (i.e. "a changed mind") was demanded. The apparent failure of the Old Testament promises concerning the Davidic kingdom was explained by the promise that the kingdom would be set up at the return of Christ (<reference osisRef="ac 2:25-31">Acts 2:25-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-16">Acts 15:14-16</reference>). This ministry to Israel fulfilled <reference osisRef="lu 19:12-14">Luke 19:12-14</reference>. In the persecutions of the apostles and finally in the martyrdom of Stephen, the Jews sent after the king the message, "We will not have this man to reign over us." In the second division (<reference osisRef="lu 10:1"> 10:1</reference>-<reference osisRef="lu 28:31"> 28:31</reference>) Paul is prominent, a new center is established at Antioch, and the ministry is chiefly to Gentiles who, as "strangers from the covenants of promise" (<reference osisRef="Eph 2:12">Eph 2:12</reference>), had but to "believe on the Lord Jesus Christ" to be saved. Chapters 11,12, and 15 of this section are transitional, establishing finally the distinction, doctrinally, between law and grace. Galatians should be read in this connection.<div eID="gen4077" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4078" type="x-p"/> The events recorded in The Acts cover a period of 32 years. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv118"/><hi type="bold">being assembled</hi> Or, eating with them.<div eID="gen4078" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4079" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ye have heard</hi> Or, heard from me.

<hi type="bold">again the kingdom to Israel</hi><div eID="gen4079" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4080" type="x-p"/> Forty days the risen Lord had been instructing the apostles "of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God," doubtless, according to His custom <reference osisRef="lu 24:27 lu 24:32 lu 24:44 lu 24:45">Luke 24:27,32,44,45</reference> teaching them out of the Scriptures. One point was left untouched, viz., the time when He would restore the kingdom to Israel; hence the apostles' question. The answer was according to His repeated teaching; the time was God's secret. ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:36 mt 24:42 mt 24:44">Matthew 24:36,42,44</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:13"> 25:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 5:1">1 Thessalonians 5:1</reference>.<div eID="gen4080" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4081" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">restore</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">come</hi><div eID="gen4081" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4082" type="x-p"/> The two Advents--Summary:<div eID="gen4082" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The O.T. foreview of the coming Messiah is in two aspects--that of rejection and suffering (as e.g. in Is 53), and that of earthly glory and power (as e.g. In Is 11 Jer 23 Eze 37). Often these two aspects blend in one passage (e.g. Ps 2). The prophets themselves were perplexed by this seeming contradiction <reference osisRef="1pe 1:10 1pe 1:11">1 Peter 1:10,11</reference>. It was solved by partial fulfilment. In due time the Messiah, born of a virgin according to Isaiah, appeared among men and began His ministry by announcing the predicted kingdom as "at hand."</item> </list> <div sID="gen4083" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:17">Matthew 4:17</reference>")</hi>. The rejection of King and kingdom followed.<div eID="gen4083" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Thereupon the rejected King announced His approaching crucifixion, resurrection, departure, and return (Mat. 24., 25). <reference osisRef="mt 12:38-40">Matthew 12:38-40</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 16:1-4 mt 16:21 mt 16:27"> 16:1-4,21,27</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 12:35-46">Luke 12:35-46</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 17:20-36"> 17:20-36</reference> ; <reference osisRef="lu 18:31-34"> 18:31-34</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 19:12-27"> 19:12-27</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) He uttered predictions concerning the course of events between His departure and return <reference osisRef="mt 13:1-50">Matthew 13:1-50</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 16:18"> 16:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:4-26"> 24:4-26</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) This promised return of Christ becomes a prominent theme in the Acts, Epistles, and Revelation.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4084" type="x-p"/> Taken together, the N.T. teachings concerning the return of Jesus Christ may be summarized as follows:<div eID="gen4084" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) That return is an event, not a process, and is personal and corporeal <reference osisRef="mt 23:39">Matthew 23:39</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:30"> 24:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:31"> 25:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 14:62">Mark 14:62</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 17:24">Luke 17:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 14:3">John 14:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:11">Acts 1:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21">Philippians 3:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) His coming has a threefold relation: to the church, to Israel, to the nations.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) To the church the descent of the Lord into the air to raise the sleeping and change the living saints is set forth as a constant expectation and hope <reference osisRef="mt 24:36 mt 24:44 mt 24:48-51">Matthew 24:36,44,48-51</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:13"> 25:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:51 1co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:51,52</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:20">Philippians 3:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 1:10">1 Thessalonians 1:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17"> 4:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 6:14">1 Timothy 6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 2:13">Titus 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 22:20">Revelation 22:20</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) To Israel, the return of the Lord is predicted to accomplish the yet unfulfilled prophecies of her national regathering, conversion, and establishment in peace and power under the Davidic Covenant <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference> with <reference osisRef="zec 14:1-9">Zechariah 14:1-9</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4085" type="x-p"/> See "Kingdom (O.T.)" <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference>.<div eID="gen4085" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4086" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 13:8">Zechariah 13:8</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen4086" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4087" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference><div eID="gen4087" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4088" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen4088" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-2">(c) To the Gentile nations the return of Christ is predicted to bring the destruction of the present political world-system <reference osisRef="da 2:34 da 2:35">Daniel 2:34,35</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 19:11">Revelation 19:11</reference>")</hi> , the judgment of <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference> followed by world-wide Gentile conversion and participation in the blessings of the kingdom ; <hi type="bold">Holy Ghost</hi><div eID="gen4094" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4095" type="x-p"/> The Holy Spirit, N.T. Summary (see <reference osisRef="mal 2:15">Malachi 2:15,</reference> note): <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mal 2:15">Malachi 2:15</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4095" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The Holy Spirit is revealed as a divine Person. This is expressly declared (e.g.) <reference osisRef="joh 14:16 joh 14:17 joh 14:26">John 14:16,17,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:26"> 15:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 16:7-15"> 16:7-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 28:19">Matthew 28:19</reference> and everywhere implied.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The revelation concerning Him is progressive</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) In the O.T. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mal 2:15">Malachi 2:15</reference>")</hi>. He comes upon whom He will, apparently without reference to conditions in them</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(b) During His earth-life, Christ taught His disciples <reference osisRef="lu 11:13">Luke 11:13</reference> that they might receive the Spirit through prayer to the Father.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(c) At the close of His ministry He promised that He would Himself pray the Father, and that in answer to prayer the Comforter would come to abide <reference osisRef="joh 14:16 joh 14:17">John 14:16,17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(d) On the evening of His resurrection He came to the disciples in the upper room, and breathed on them saying, "Receive ye the Holy Ghost" <reference osisRef="joh 20:22">John 20:22</reference> but instructed them to wait before beginning their ministry till the Spirit should come upon them ; <reference osisRef="lu 24:49">Luke 24:49</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(e) On the day of Pentecost the Spirit came upon the whole body of believers <reference osisRef="ac 2:1-4">Acts 2:1-4</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-2">(f) After Pentecost, so long as the Gospel was preached to Jews only, the Spirit was imparted to such as believed by the laying on of hands <reference osisRef="ac 8:17">Acts 8:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 9:17"> 9:17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(g) When Peter opened the door of the kingdom to the Gentiles (Ac 10.), the Holy Spirit, without delay, or other condition than faith, was given to those who believed. <reference osisRef="ac 10:44">Acts 10:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 11:15-18"> 11:15-18</reference>. This is the permanent fact for the entire church age. Every believer is born of the Spirit ; <reference osisRef="joh 3:3 joh 3:6">John 3:3,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:1">1 John 5:1</reference> indwelt by the Spirit, whose presence makes the believer's body a temple ; <reference osisRef="1co 6:19">1 Corinthians 6:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:9-15">Romans 8:9-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:27">1 John 2:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:6">Galatians 4:6</reference> and baptized by the Spirit ; <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:20 1jo 2:27">1 John 2:20,27</reference> thus sealing him for God ; <reference osisRef="eph 1:13">Ephesians 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:30"> 4:30</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The N.T. distinguishes between having the Spirit, which is true of all believers, and being filled with the Spirit, which is the believer's privilege and duty (cf) <reference osisRef="ac 2:4">Acts 2:4</reference> with ; <reference osisRef="ac 4:29-31">Acts 4:29-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:13 eph 1:14">Ephesians 1:13,14</reference> with <reference osisRef="eph 5:18">Ephesians 5:18</reference>. --"One baptism, many fillings."</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The Holy Spirit is related to Christ in His Conception <reference osisRef="mt 1:18-20">Matthew 1:18-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:35">Luke 1:35</reference> baptism ; <reference osisRef="mt 3:16">Matthew 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 1:10">Mark 1:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 3:22">Luke 3:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:32 joh 1:33">John 1:32,33</reference> walk and service <reference osisRef="lu 4:1 lu 4:14">Luke 4:1,14</reference> resurrection <reference osisRef="ro 8:11">Romans 8:11,</reference> and as His witness throughout this age ; <reference osisRef="joh 15:26">John 15:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 16:8-11 joh 16:13-14"> 16:8-11,13,14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The Spirit forms the church <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>")</hi> by baptizing all believers into the body of Christ <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13,</reference> imparts gifts for service to every member of that body <reference osisRef="1co 12:7-11 1co 12:27 1co 12:30">1 Corinthians 12:7-11,27,30,</reference> guide the members in their service ; <reference osisRef="lu 2:27">Luke 2:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 4:1"> 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 16:6 ac 16:7">Acts 16:6,7</reference> and is Himself the power of that service ; <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:4"> 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 2:4">1 Corinthians 2:4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The Spirit abides in the company of believers who constitute a local church, making of them, corporately, a temple <reference osisRef="1co 3:16 1co 3:17">1 Corinthians 3:16,17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) Christ indicates a threefold personal relationship of the Spirit to the believer: "With", "In", "upon" <reference osisRef="joh 14:17">John 14:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 24:49">Luke 24:49</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:8">Acts 1:8</reference>. "With" indicates the approach of God to the soul, convicting of sin <reference osisRef="joh 16:9">John 16:9</reference> presenting Christ as the object of faith <reference osisRef="joh 16:14">John 16:14</reference> imparting faith <reference osisRef="eph 2:8">Ephesians 2:8</reference> and regenerating <reference osisRef="joh 3:3-16">John 3:3-16</reference>. "In" describes the abiding presence of the Spirit in the believer's body <reference osisRef="1co 6:19">1 Corinthians 6:19</reference> to give victory over the flesh ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:2-4">Romans 8:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 5:16 ga 5:17">Galatians 5:16,17</reference> to create the Christian character <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23">Galatians 5:22,23</reference> to help infirmities <reference osisRef="ro 8:26">Romans 8:26</reference> to inspire prayer <reference osisRef="eph 6:18">Ephesians 6:18</reference> to give conscious access to God <reference osisRef="eph 2:18">Ephesians 2:18</reference> to actualize to the believer his sonship <reference osisRef="ga 4:6">Galatians 4:6</reference> to apply the Scripture in cleansing and sanctification ; <reference osisRef="eph 5:26">Ephesians 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="2th 2:13">2 Thessalonians 2:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:2">1 Peter 1:2</reference> to comfort and intercede ; <reference osisRef="ac 9:31">Acts 9:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:26">Romans 8:26</reference> and to reveal Christ <reference osisRef="joh 16:14">John 16:14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(8) Sins against the Spirit committed by unbelievers are: To blaspheme <reference osisRef="mt 12:31">Matthew 12:31,</reference> resist <reference osisRef="ac 7:51">Acts 7:51,</reference> insult <reference osisRef="heb 10:29">Hebrews 10:29,</reference> "despite," lit. insult). Believers' sins against the Spirit are: To grieve Him by allowing evil in heart or life <reference osisRef="eph 4:30 eph 4:31">Ephesians 4:30,31</reference> and to quench Him by disobedience <reference osisRef="1th 5:19">1 Thessalonians 5:19</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4096" type="x-p"/> The right attitude toward the Spirit is yieldedness to His sway in walk and service, and in constant willingness that He shall "put away" whatever grieves Him or hinders His power <reference osisRef="eph 4:31">Ephesians 4:31</reference>.<div eID="gen4096" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(9) The symbols of the Spirit are: (a) oil <reference osisRef="joh 3:34">John 3:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:9">Hebrews 1:9</reference> (b) water, <reference osisRef="joh 7:38 joh 7:39">John 7:38,39,</reference> (c) wind ; <reference osisRef="ac 2:2">Acts 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 3:8">John 3:8,</reference> (d) fire <reference osisRef="ac 2:3">Acts 2:3,</reference> (e) a dove <reference osisRef="mt 3:16">Matthew 3:16,</reference> (f) a seal ; <reference osisRef="eph 1:13">Ephesians 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:30"> 4:30,</reference> (g) an earnest or pledge <reference osisRef="eph 1:14">Ephesians 1:14</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">said unto them</hi><div eID="gen4099" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4100" type="x-p"/> The theme of Peter's sermon at Pentecost is stated in <reference osisRef="ac 2:36">Acts 2:36</reference>. It is, that Jesus is the Messiah. No message could have been more unwelcome to the Jews who had rejected His Messianic claims, and crucified Him. Peter, therefore, does not announce his theme until he has covered every possible Jewish objection. The point of difficulty with the Jews was the apparent failure of the clear and repeated prophetic promise of a regathered Israel established in their own land under their covenanted King (e.g). ; <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-12">Isaiah 11:10-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="jer 23:5-8">Jeremiah 23:5-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 37:21-18">Ezekiel 37:21-18</reference>. Instead of explaining, as Rome first taught, followed by some Protestant commentators, that the covenant and promises were to be fulfilled in the church in a so-called "spiritual" sense, Peter shows <reference osisRef="ac 2:25-32">Acts 2:25-32</reference> from Ps 16. that David himself understood that the dead and risen Christ would fulfil the covenant and sit on his throne <reference osisRef="lu 1:32 lu 1:33">Luke 1:32,33</reference>. In precisely the same way James <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference> met the same difficulty. See "Kingdom (O.T.)," <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference> (N.T.), ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:33">Luke 1:33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>.

<hi type="bold">last days</hi><div eID="gen4100" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4101" type="x-p"/> A distinction must be observed between "the last days" when the prediction relates to Israel, and the "last days" when the prediction relates to the church <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1-3">1 Timothy 4:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-8">2 Timothy 3:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:1 heb 1:2">Hebrews 1:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 1:4 1pe 1:5">1 Peter 1:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:1-9">2 Peter 3:1-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:18 1jo 2:19">1 John 2:18,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:17-19">Jude 1:17-19</reference>. Also distinguish the expression the "last days" (plural) from "the last day" (singular); the latter expression referring to the resurrections and last judgment ; <reference osisRef="joh 6:39 joh 6:40 joh 6:44 joh 6:54">John 6:39,40,44,54</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 11:24"> 11:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:48"> 12:48</reference>. The "last days" as related to the church began with the advent of Christ <reference osisRef="heb 1:2">Hebrews 1:2</reference> but have especial reference to the time of declension and apostasy at the end of this age ; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1">2 Timothy 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:4"> 4:4</reference>. The "last days" as related to Israel are the days of Israel's exaltation and blessing, and are synonymous with the kingdom-age ; <reference osisRef="isa 2:2-4">Isaiah 2:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 4:1-7">Micah 4:1-7</reference>. They are "last" not with reference to this dispensation, but with reference to the whole of Israel's history.

<hi type="bold">And he shall</hi><div eID="gen4110" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4111" type="x-p"/> The appeal here is national to the Jewish people as such, not individuals as in Peter's first sermon <reference osisRef="ac 2:38 ac 2:39">Acts 2:38,39</reference>. There those who were pricked in heart were exhorted to save themselves from (among) the untoward nation; here the whole people is addressed, and the promise to national repentance is national deliverance: "and he shall send Jesus Christ" to bring in the times which the prophets had foretold<div eID="gen4111" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4112" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 2:14">Acts 2:14</reference>")</hi>. The official answer was the imprisonment of the apostles, and the inhibition to preach, so fulfilling <reference osisRef="lu 19:14">Luke 19:14</reference>.

<hi type="bold">restitution</hi><div eID="gen4112" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4113" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G3485">ναός</w> = restoration, occurring here and <reference osisRef="ac 1:6">Acts 1:6</reference> only. The meaning is limited by the words: "Which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets." The prophets speak of the restoration of Israel to the land (see "Israel," ; <reference osisRef="ge 12:2 ge 12:3">Genesis 12:2,3</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:26">Romans 11:26</reference> also "Palestinian Covenant," <reference osisRef="de 30:1-9">Deuteronomy 30:1-9</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi> and of the restoration the theocracy under David's Son. (See "Davidic Covenant," <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference>).<div eID="gen4113" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4114" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>")</hi> , "Kingdom," <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>". No prediction of the conversion and restoration of the wicked dead is found in the prophets, or elsewhere. In the wilderness Israel was a true church (G. ecclesia = called-out assembly), but in striking contrast with the N.T. ecclesia<div eID="gen4145" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4146" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4146" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4147" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angel</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Jesus</hi><div eID="gen4147" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4148" type="x-p"/> i.e. Joshua.
<hi type="bold">Lord</hi><div eID="gen4148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4149" type="x-p"/> Jehovah. <reference osisRef="isa 66:1 isa 66:2">Isaiah 66:1,2</reference>.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen4149" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4150" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">When they heard</hi><div eID="gen4150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4151" type="x-p"/> They had brought false witnesses against Stephen; he bears true witness against them, quoting the testimony of writers they owned to be inspired. He speaks of the persistent rejection of God and His servants by the nation til at last it is brought home to themselves, and arouses the maddened enmity of their hearts. It was the final trial of the nation.
<hi type="bold">God</hi><div eID="gen4151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4152" type="x-p"/> Omit God. Lit. And were stoning Stephen as he was invoking and saying, Lord Jesus, give welcome unto my spirit.

<hi type="bold">city of</hi> <div eID="gen4155" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4156" type="x-p"/> The Jews having rejected Stephen's witness to, and of, them, the Gospel now begins to go out to "all nations." Cf. <reference osisRef="lu 24:47">Luke 24:47</reference>.

<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4156" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4157" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">desert</hi> Contra, <reference osisRef="ac 8:6-8">Acts 8:6-8</reference>.
<hi type="bold">And</hi><div eID="gen4157" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4158" type="x-p"/> The best authorities omit v. 37. <chapter eID="Acts.8"/><div eID="gen4158" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">of this way</hi> <div eID="gen4159" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4160" type="x-p"/> that were of The Way, i.e. Christ. <reference osisRef="joh 14:6">John 14:6</reference>.
<hi type="bold">me?</hi><div eID="gen4160" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4161" type="x-p"/> The Lord identifies Himself with His people.

<hi type="bold">voice</hi><div eID="gen4161" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4162" type="x-p"/> Cf <reference osisRef="ac 22:9">Acts 22:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 26:14"> 26:14</reference>.<div eID="gen4162" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4163" type="x-p"/> A contradiction has been imagined. The three statements should be taken together. The men heard the "voice" as a sound ( (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G400">ἀναφωνέω</w>), but did not hear the "voice" as articulating the words, "Saul, Saul," etc).

<hi type="bold">that he is the Son of God</hi><div eID="gen4163" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4164" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ac 2:36">Acts 2:36</reference>. Peter, while maintaining the deity of Jesus--"God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ"--gives especial prominence to His Messiahship. Paul, fresh from the vision of the glory, puts the emphasis on His Deity. Peter's charge was that the Jews had crucified the Son of David <reference osisRef="ac 2:25-30">Acts 2:25-30</reference> Paul's that they had crucified the Lord of glory <reference osisRef="1co 2:8">1 Corinthians 2:8</reference>. In the A.V. the sense is largely lost. The point was, not that the Christ was God, a truth plainly taught by Isaiah. ; <reference osisRef="isa 7:14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 9:6 isa 9:7"> 9:6,7</reference> but that Jesus, the crucified Nazarene, was the Christ and therefore God the Son.

<hi type="bold">But Saul</hi><div eID="gen4164" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4165" type="x-p"/> It seems probable that <reference osisRef="ac 9:22-25">Acts 9:22-25</reference> refer to Paul's labours in Damascus after his return from Arabia <reference osisRef="ga 1:17">Galatians 1:17</reference>.<div eID="gen4165" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4166" type="x-p"/> The "many days" of verse <reference osisRef="ac 9:23">Acts 9:23</reference> may represent the "three years" of <reference osisRef="ga 1:18">Galatians 1:18,</reference> which intervened between Paul's return to Damascus and his visit to Peter.

<hi type="bold">gone to Jerusalem</hi><div eID="gen4166" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4167" type="x-p"/> The Acts records four visits of Paul to Jerusalem after conversion:<div eID="gen4167" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) <reference osisRef="ac 9:23-30">Acts 9:23-30</reference>. This seems identical with the visit of <reference osisRef="ga 1:18 ga 1:19">Galatians 1:18,19</reference>. The "apostles" of verse <reference osisRef="ac 9:27">Acts 9:27</reference> were Peter, and James, the Lord's brother.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) <reference osisRef="ac 11:30">Acts 11:30</reference>. Paul may have been in Jerusalem during the events of <reference osisRef="ac 12:1-25">Acts 12:1-25</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) <reference osisRef="ac 15:1-30">Acts 15:1-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:2-10">Galatians 2:2-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) <reference osisRef="ac 21:17-ac 23:35">Acts 21:17-23:35</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">While Peter yet spake</hi><div eID="gen4176" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4177" type="x-p"/> Verse 44 is one of the pivotal points of Scripture. Heretofore the Gospel has been offered to Jews only, and the Holy Spirit bestowed upon believing Jews through apostolic mediation. But now the normal order for this age is reached: the Holy Spirit is given without delay, mediation, or other condition than simple faith in Jesus Christ.
