<hi type="bold">spiritual gifts</hi> <div eID="gen4616" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4617" type="x-p"/> The word pneumatika, lit. "spirituals," i.e. matters of or from the Holy Spirit, gives the key to Chapters 12., 13., 14. Chapter 12. concerns the Spirit in relation to the body of Christ. This relation is twofold:<div eID="gen4617" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The baptism with the Spirit forms the body by uniting believers to Christ the risen and glorified Head, and to each other (<reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference>). The symbol of the body thus formed is the natural, human body (<reference osisRef="1co 12:12">1 Corinthians 12:12</reference>), and all the analogies are freely used (<reference osisRef="1co 12:14-26">1 Corinthians 12:14-26</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) To each believer is given a spiritual enablement and capacity for specific service. No believer is destitute of such gift (<reference osisRef="1co 12:7 1co 12:11 1co 12:27">1 Corinthians 12:7,11,27</reference>), but in their distribution the Spirit acts in free sovereignty (<reference osisRef="1co 12:11">1 Corinthians 12:11</reference>). There is no room for self-choosing, and Christian service is simply the ministry of such gift as the individual may have received (cf) <reference osisRef="ro 12:4-8">Romans 12:4-8</reference>. The gifts are diverse (<reference osisRef="1co 12:6 1co 12:8-10 1co 12:28-30">1 Corinthians 12:6,8-10,28-30</reference>), but all are equally honourable because bestowed by the same Spirit, administered under the same Lord, and energized by the same God. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv131"/><div sID="gen4618" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv131"/> <hi type="bold">gifts</hi> <div eID="gen4618" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4619" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="eph 4:8 eph 4:11 eph 4:12">Ephesians 4:8,11,12</reference>. The Spirit gives gifts for service to men, Christ gives the gifted men to the churches.

<hi type="bold">prophecy</hi><div eID="gen4619" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4620" type="x-p"/> The N.T. prophet is not ordinarily a foreteller, but rather a forth-teller, one whose gift enabled him to speak "to edification, and exhortation, and comfort" <reference osisRef="1co 14:3">1 Corinthians 14:3</reference>.

<hi type="bold">more excellent</hi><div eID="gen4620" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4621" type="x-p"/> Chapter 13. continues the pneumatika begun in Chapter 12. Gifts are good, but only if ministered in love. <reference osisRef="1co 13:1 1co 13:2">1 Corinthians 13:1,2</reference>. Benevolence is good, but not apart from love.<div eID="gen4621" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4622" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1co 13:3">1 Corinthians 13:3</reference> Love is described.<div eID="gen4622" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4623" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1co 13:4-7">1 Corinthians 13:4-7</reference> Love is better than our present incomplete knowledge, <reference osisRef="1co 13:8-12">1 Corinthians 13:8-12</reference> and greater than even faith and hope <reference osisRef="1co 13:13">1 Corinthians 13:13</reference>. <div eID="gen4623" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv132"/><div sID="gen4624" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="1Cor.12"/>
<div eID="gen4624" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4625" type="x-p"/><chapter n="13" osisID="1Cor.13" sID="1Cor.13"/>

<hi type="bold">angels</hi> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4626" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">charity</hi> i.e. love; and so in <reference osisRef="1co 13:2-4 1co 13:8 1co 13:13">1 Corinthians 13:2-4,8,13</reference>.

<hi type="bold">charity</hi><div eID="gen4626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4627" type="x-p"/> i.e. love; and so in <reference osisRef="1co 13:2-4 1co 13:8 1co 13:13">1 Corinthians 13:2-4,8,13</reference>.

<hi type="bold">charity</hi><div eID="gen4627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4628" type="x-p"/> i.e. love; and so in <reference osisRef="1co 13:2-4 1co 13:8 1co 13:13">1 Corinthians 13:2-4,8,13</reference>.

<hi type="bold">charity</hi><div eID="gen4628" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4629" type="x-p"/> i.e. love; and so in <reference osisRef="1co 13:2-4 1co 13:8 1co 13:13">1 Corinthians 13:2-4,8,13</reference>. <div eID="gen4629" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv132"/><div sID="gen4630" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="1Cor.13"/>
<div eID="gen4630" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4631" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="14" osisID="1Cor.14" sID="1Cor.14"/>

<hi type="bold">rather</hi> <div eID="gen4631" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4632" type="x-p"/> The subject is still the pneumatika. Chapter 12, described the gifts and the Body; Chapter 13. the love which alone gives ministry of gift any value; Chapter 14. regulates the ministry of gift in the primitive, apostolic assembly of saints.<div eID="gen4632" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The important gift is that of prophecy (<reference osisRef="1co 1:1">1 Corinthians 1:1</reference>)). The N.T. prophet was not merely a preacher, but an inspired preacher, through whom, until the N.T. was written, new revelations suited to the new dispensation were given <reference osisRef="1co 14:29 1co 14:30">1 Corinthians 14:29,30</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Tongues and the sign gifts are to cease, and meantime must be used with restraint, and only if an interpreter be present <reference osisRef="1co 14:1-19 1co 14:27-28">1 Corinthians 14:1-19,27-28</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) In the primitive church there was liberty for the ministry of all the gifts which might be present, but for prophecy more especially <reference osisRef="1co 14:23-26 1co 14:31 1co 14:39">1 Corinthians 14:23-26,31,39</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) In such meetings, when "the whole church" came together "in one place," women were required to keep silence <reference osisRef="1co 14:34 1co 14:35">1 Corinthians 14:34,35</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:3-16"> 11:3-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 2:11-14">1 Timothy 2:11-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) These injunctions are declared to be "the commandments of the Lord" <reference osisRef="1co 14:36 1co 14:37">1 Corinthians 14:36,37</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv132"/><div sID="gen4633" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv132"/> <hi type="bold">an unknown</hi> <div eID="gen4633" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4634" type="x-p"/> Or, a tongue; and so in 1Co 14: 4,13,14,19,27.
<hi type="bold">be not children</hi> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G96">Ἀδμίν</w>, youths).<div eID="gen4634" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4635" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">be ye children</hi> babies.

<hi type="bold">obedience</hi><div eID="gen4635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4636" type="x-p"/> Cf. <reference osisRef="ge 3:16">Genesis 3:16</reference>. <chapter eID="1Cor.14"/><div eID="gen4636" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">born out of due time</hi><div eID="gen4640" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4641" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G27">ἀγαπητός</w>, "before the due time)." Paul thinks of himself here as an Israelite whose time to be born again had not come, nationally (cf) <reference osisRef="mt 23:39">Matthew 23:39</reference> so that his conversion by the appearing of the Lord in glory <reference osisRef="ac 9:3-6">Acts 9:3-6</reference> was an illustration, or instance before the time, of the future national conversion of Israel. See ; <reference osisRef="eze 20:34-38">Ezekiel 20:34-38</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 2:14-17">Hosea 2:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:10-zec 13:6">Zechariah 12:10-13:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:25-27">Romans 11:25-27</reference>.
<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen4641" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4642" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">Adam</hi><div eID="gen4642" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4643" type="x-p"/> Adam was a contrasting type of Christ, <reference osisRef="1co 15:45-47">1 Corinthians 15:45-47</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 5:14-19">Romans 5:14-19</reference>.<div eID="gen4643" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) "The first man Adam was made a living soul" <reference osisRef="ge 2:7">Genesis 2:7,</reference> i.e. he derived life from another, that is, God. "The last Adam was a life-giving spirit." So far from deriving life, He was Himself the fountain of life, and He gave that life to others ; <reference osisRef="joh 1:4">John 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:21"> 5:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 10:10"> 10:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:24"> 12:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:12">1 John 5:12</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) In origin the first man was of the earth, earthy; the Second Man is the Lord from heaven.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Each is the head of a creation, and these also are in contrast: in Adam all die; in Christ all will be made alive; the Adamic creation is "flesh"; the new creation, "spirit." <reference osisRef="joh 3:6">John 3:6</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv133"/><div sID="gen4644" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv133"/> <hi type="bold">kingdom</hi> <div eID="gen4644" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4645" type="x-p"/> Kingdom (N.T.), Summary: See "Kingdom (O.T.)" <reference osisRef="ge 1:26-28">Genesis 1:26-28</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>")</hi>. Kingdom truth is developed in the N.T. in the following order:<div eID="gen4645" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The promise of the kingdom to David and his seed, and described in the prophets <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17,</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference> enters the N.T. absolutely unchanged. <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>. The King was born in Bethlehem ; <reference osisRef="mt 2:1">Matthew 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="mic 5:2">Micah 5:2</reference> of a virgin. ; <reference osisRef="mt 1:18-25">Matthew 1:18-25</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 7:14">Isaiah 7:14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The kingdom announced as "at hand" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:17">Matthew 4:17</reference>")</hi> , by John the Baptist, by the King, and by the Twelve, was rejected by the Jews, first morally, See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 11:20">Matthew 11:20</reference>", and afterward officially <reference osisRef="mt 21:42 mt 21:43">Matthew 21:42,43</reference> and the King, crowned with thorns, was crucified.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) In anticipation of His official rejection and crucifixion, the King revealed the "mysteries" of the kingdom of heaven, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi> to be fulfilled in the interval between His rejection and His return in glory <reference osisRef="mt 13:1-50">Matthew 13:1-50</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Afterward He announced His purpose to "build" His church <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference> another "mystery" revealed through Paul which is being fulfilled contemporaneously with the mysteries of the kingdom. The "mysteries of the kingdom of heaven" and the "mystery" of the church <reference osisRef="eph 3:9-11">Ephesians 3:9-11</reference> occupy, historically, the same period, i.e, this present age.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The mysteries of the kingdom will be brought to an end by "the harvest" <reference osisRef="mt 13:39-43 mt 13:49-50">Matthew 13:39-43,49-50</reference> at the return of the King in glory, the church having previously been caught up to meet Him in the air <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Upon His return the King will restore the Davidic monarchy in His own person, re- gather dispersed Israel, establish His power over all the earth, and reign one thousand years <reference osisRef="mt 24:27-30">Matthew 24:27-30</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:1-10">Revelation 20:1-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) The kingdom of heaven <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference>")</hi> thus established under David's divine Son, has for its object the restoration of the divine authority in the earth, which may be regarded as a revolted province of the great kingdom of God See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 6:33">Matthew 6:33</reference>". When this is done (<reference osisRef="1co 14:24 1co 14:25">1 Corinthians 14:24,25</reference>) the Son will deliver up the kingdom (of heaven), <reference osisRef="mt 3:2">Matthew 3:2</reference> to "God, even the Father," that "God" (i.e. the triune God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit) "may be all in all" (<reference osisRef="1co 14:28">1 Corinthians 14:28</reference>). The eternal throne is that "of God, and of the Lamb" <reference osisRef="re 22:1">Revelation 22:1</reference>. The kingdom-age constitutes the seventh Dispensation, See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:eph 1:10">Ephesians 1:10</reference>".</item> </list> <div sID="gen4646" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Then cometh</hi> Then, finally, when he delivers up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he has done away with every rule, and every authority and power (for he must reign till he has put all enemies under his feet), the last enemy, death, is destroyed.

<hi type="bold">dead</hi><div eID="gen4646" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4647" type="x-p"/> i.e. who, through the introductory rite of baptism, are taking the places in the ranks left vacant by Christians who have died.
<hi type="bold">sin</hi><div eID="gen4647" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4648" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">was made</hi><div eID="gen4648" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4649" type="x-p"/> Omit italicized words "was made."
<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><div eID="gen4649" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4650" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">raised</hi><div eID="gen4650" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4651" type="x-p"/> Resurrection, Summary:<div eID="gen4651" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The resurrection of the dead was believed by the patriarchs <reference osisRef="ge 22:5">Genesis 22:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 11:19">Hebrews 11:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="job 19:25-27">Job 19:25-27</reference> and revealed through the prophets ; <reference osisRef="isa 26:19">Isaiah 26:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 12:2 da 12:13">Daniel 12:2,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 13:14">Hosea 13:14</reference> and miracles of the dead restored to life are recorded in the O.T. ; <reference osisRef="2ki 4:32-35">2 Kings 4:32-35</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ki 13:21"> 13:21</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Jesus Christ restored life to the dead <reference osisRef="mt 9:25">Matthew 9:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 7:12-15">Luke 7:12-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 11:43 joh 11:44">John 11:43,44</reference> and predicted His own resurrection ; <reference osisRef="joh 10:18">John 10:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 24:1-8">Luke 24:1-8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) A resurrection of bodies followed the resurrection of Christ <reference osisRef="mt 27:52 mt 27:53">Matthew 27:52,53</reference> and the apostles raised the dead ; <reference osisRef="ac 9:36-41">Acts 9:36-41</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 20:9 ac 20:10"> 20:9,10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Two resurrections are yet future, which are inclusive of "all that are in the graves" <reference osisRef="joh 5:28">John 5:28</reference>. These are distinguished as "of life" ; <reference osisRef="1co 15:22 1co 15:23">1 Corinthians 15:22,23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:4">Revelation 20:4</reference> and "of judgment" ; <reference osisRef="joh 5:28 joh 5:29">John 5:28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:11-13">Revelation 20:11-13</reference>. They are separated by a period of one thousand years <reference osisRef="re 20:5">Revelation 20:5</reference>. The "first resurrection," that "unto life," will occur at the second coming of Christ <reference osisRef="1co 15:23">1 Corinthians 15:23</reference> the saints of the O.T. and church ages meeting Him in the air <reference osisRef="1th 4:16 1th 4:17">1 Thessalonians 4:16,17</reference> while the martyrs of the tribulation, who also have part in the resurrection <reference osisRef="re 20:4">Revelation 20:4</reference> are raised at the end of the great tribulation.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The mortal body will be related to the resurrection body as grain sown is related to the harvest <reference osisRef="1co 15:37 1co 15:38">1 Corinthians 15:37,38</reference> that body will be incorruptible, glorious, powerful, and spiritual <reference osisRef="1co 15:42-44 1co 15:49">1 Corinthians 15:42-44,49</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The bodies of living believers will, at the same time, be instantaneously changed <reference osisRef="1co 15:50-53">1 Corinthians 15:50-53</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21">Philippians 3:20,21</reference>. This "change" of the living, and resurrection of the dead in Christ, is called the "redemption of the body" ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:23">Romans 8:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:13 eph 1:14">Ephesians 1:13,14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) After the thousand years the "resurrection unto judgment" <reference osisRef="joh 5:29">John 5:29</reference> occurs. The resurrection-body of the wicked dead is not described. They are judged according to their works, and cast into the lake of fire. <reference osisRef="re 20:7-15">Revelation 20:7-15</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv135"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 2 Corinthians</title> <div sID="gen4659" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2co 1">Read first chapter of 2 Corinthians</reference><div eID="gen4659" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4660" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul<div eID="gen4660" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4661" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: A.D. 60; probably from Philippi, after the events of <reference osisRef="ac 19:23-ac 20:1-3">Acts 19:23-20:1-3</reference>.<div eID="gen4661" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4662" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The Epistle discloses the touching state of the great apostle at this time. It was one of physical weakness, weariness, and pain. But his spiritual burdens were greater. These were two kinds--solicitude for the maintenance of the churches in grace as against the law-teachers, and anguish of heart over the distrust felt toward him by Jews and Jewish Christians. The chilling doctrines of the legalizers were accompanied by detraction, and by denial of his apostleship.<div eID="gen4662" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4663" type="x-p"/> It is evident that the really dangerous sect in Corinth was that which said, "and I of Christ" (<reference osisRef="1co 1:12">1 Corinthians 1:12</reference>). They rejected the new revelation through Paul of the doctrines of grace; grounding themselves, probably, on the kingdom teachings of our Lord as "a minister of circumcision" (<reference osisRef="ro 15:8">Romans 15:8</reference>); seemingly oblivious that a new dispensation had been introduced by Christ's death. This made necessary a defence of the origin and extent of Paul's apostolic authority.<div eID="gen4663" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4664" type="x-p"/> The Epistle is in three parts:<div eID="gen4664" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Paul's principles of action, 1:1-7-16.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The collection for the poor saints at Jerusalem, 8:1-9:15.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Paul's defence of his apostolic authority, 10:1-13:14.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4665" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv135"/> <hi type="bold">comforteth</hi> <div eID="gen4665" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4666" type="x-p"/> encourages; and so also where "comfort," etc., occurs in following verses.
<hi type="bold">salvation</hi><div eID="gen4666" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4667" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen4667" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4668" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). vs. <reference osisRef="2co 4:15">2 Corinthians 4:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">come out from among them</hi><div eID="gen4699" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4700" type="x-p"/> Separation, Summary:<div eID="gen4700" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Separation in Scripture is twofold: "from" whatever is contrary to the mind of God; and "unto" God Himself. The underlying principle is that in a moral universe it is impossible for God to fully bless and use His children who are in compromise or complicity with evil. The unequal yoke is anything which unites a child of God and an unbeliever in a common purpose <reference osisRef="de 22:10">Deuteronomy 22:10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Separation from evil implies (a) separation in desire, motive, and act, from the world, in the ethically bad sense of this present world-system. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi> and (b) separation from believers, especially false teachers, who are "vessels unto dishonour" <reference osisRef="2ti 2:20 2ti 2:21">2 Timothy 2:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="2jo 1:9-11">2 John 1:9-11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Separation is not from contact with evil in the world or the church, but from complicity with and conformity to <reference osisRef="joh 17:15">John 17:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 6:14-18">2 Corinthians 6:14-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:1">Galatians 6:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The reward of separation is the full manifestation of the divine fatherhood <reference osisRef="2co 6:17 2co 6:18">2 Corinthians 6:17,18</reference> unhindered communion and worship <reference osisRef="heb 13:13-15">Hebrews 13:13-15</reference> and fruitful service <reference osisRef="2ti 2:21">2 Timothy 2:21</reference> as world-conformity involves the loss of these, though not of salvation. Here, as in all else, Christ is the model. He was "holy, harmless, undefiled, and separate from sinners" <reference osisRef="heb 7:26">Hebrews 7:26</reference> and yet in such contact with them for their salvation that the Pharisees, who illustrate the mechanical and ascetic conception of separation <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 3:7">Matthew 3:7</reference>")</hi> , judged Him as having lost His Nazarite character. <reference osisRef="lu 7:39">Luke 7:39</reference> Cf ; <reference osisRef="1co 9:19-23">1 Corinthians 9:19-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 10:27"> 10:27</reference>. </item> </list> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv136"/><div sID="gen4701" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="2Cor.6"/>

<hi type="bold">Moreover</hi> <div eID="gen4707" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4708" type="x-p"/> In 2Cor. 8., 9., the apostle sums up the Christian doctrine of giving. It may be thus summarized:<div eID="gen4708" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) It is a "grace," i.e. a disposition created by the Spirit <reference osisRef="2co 8:7">2 Corinthians 8:7</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) In contrast with the law, which imposed giving as a divine requirement, Christian giving is voluntary, and a test of sincerity and love <reference osisRef="2co 8:8-12">2 Corinthians 8:8-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 9:1 2co 9:2 2co 9:5 2co 9:7"> 9:1,2,5,7</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The privilege is universal, belonging, according to ability, to rich and poor <reference osisRef="2co 8:1-3 2co 8:12-15">2 Corinthians 8:1-3,12-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 16:1 1co 16:2">1 Corinthians 16:1,2</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Giving is to be proportioned to income <reference osisRef="2co 8:12-14">2 Corinthians 8:12-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 16:2">1 Corinthians 16:2</reference>. The O.T. proportion was the tithe, a proportion which antedates the law <reference osisRef="ge 14:20">Genesis 14:20</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The rewards of Christian giving are (a) joy <reference osisRef="2co 8:2">2 Corinthians 8:2</reference> (b) increased ability to give in proportion to that which has been already given <reference osisRef="2co 9:7-11">2 Corinthians 9:7-11</reference> (c) increased thankfulness to God <reference osisRef="2co 9:12">2 Corinthians 9:12</reference> (d) God and the Gospel glorified <reference osisRef="2co 9:13 2co 9:14">2 Corinthians 9:13,14</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">thorn</hi><div eID="gen4720" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4721" type="x-p"/> It has been conjectured that Paul's "thorn in the flesh" was chronic ophthalmia, inducing bodily weakness, and a repulsive appearance <reference osisRef="ga 4:15">Galatians 4:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 2:3 1co 2:4">1 Corinthians 2:3,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 10:10">2 Corinthians 10:10</reference>. This cannot be positively known, and the reserve of Scripture is as sure a mark of inspiration as its revelations. Paul's particular "thorn" is not described that his consolations may avail for all to who any thorn is given.

<div canonical="true" osisID="Gal" sID="gen4728" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>

<chapter n="1" osisID="Gal.1" sID="Gal.1"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv137"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Galatians</title> <div sID="gen4729" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="ga 1">Read first chapter of Galatians</reference><div eID="gen4729" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4730" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="ga 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4730" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4731" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Galatians was probably written A.D. 60, during Paul's third visit to Corinth, The occasion of the Epistle is evident. It had come to Paul's knowledge that the fickle Galatians, who were not Greeks, but Gauls, "a stream from the torrent of barbarians which poured into Greece in the third century before Christ," had become the prey of the legalizers, the Judaizing missionaries from Palestine.<div eID="gen4731" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4732" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The theme of Galatians is the vindication of the Gospel of the grace of God from any admixture of law-conditions, which qualify or destroy its character of pure grace.<div eID="gen4732" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4733" type="x-p"/> The Galatian error had two forms, both of which are refuted. The first is the teaching that obedience to the law is mingled with faith as the ground of the sinner's justification; the second, that the justified believer is made perfect by keeping the law. Paul meets the first form of the error by a demonstration that justification is through the Abrahamic Covenant (<reference osisRef="ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>), and that the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after the confirmation of that covenant, and the true purpose of which was condemnation, not justification, cannot disannul a salvation which rests upon the earlier covenant. Paul meets the second and more subtle form by vindicating the office of the Holy Spirit as Sanctifier.<div eID="gen4733" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4734" type="x-p"/> The book is in seven parts:<div eID="gen4734" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Salutation1:1-5</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Theme, 1:6-9.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Paul's Gospel is a revelation, 1:10-2:14.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Justification is by faith without law, 2:15-3:24.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rule of the believer's life is gracious, not legal, 3:25-5:15.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Sanctification is through the Spirit, not the law, 5:16-24.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Exhortations and conclusion, 5:25-6:18.</item> </list> <chapter eID="Gal.1"/>
<div sID="gen4735" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Gal.2" sID="Gal.2"/>

<hi type="bold">Grace</hi> <div eID="gen4735" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4736" type="x-p"/> Grace (in salvation). <reference osisRef="ga 1:6 ga 1:15">Galatians 1:6,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:21"> 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen4736" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4737" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen4737" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4738" type="x-p"/> The test of the Gospel is grace. If the message excludes grace, or mingles law with grace as the means of either of justification or sanctification <reference osisRef="ga 2:21">Galatians 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:1-3"> 3:1-3</reference> or denies the fact or guilt of sin which alone gives grace its occasion and opportunity, it is "another" gospel, and the preacher of it is under the anathema of God <reference osisRef="ga 1:8 ga 1:9">Galatians 1:8,9</reference>.

<hi type="bold">For now do</hi><div eID="gen4738" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4739" type="x-p"/> The demonstration is as follows:<div eID="gen4739" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The Galatians know Paul, that he is no seeker after popularity <reference osisRef="ga 1:10">Galatians 1:10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He puts his known character back of the assertion that his Gospel of grace was a revelation from God (<reference osisRef="ga 1:11 ga 1:12">Galatians 1:11,12</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) As for the Judaizers, Paul had been a foremost Jew, and had forsaken Judaism for something better (<reference osisRef="Ga 1:13-14">Galatians 1:13-14</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) He had preached grace years before he saw any of the other apostles (<reference osisRef="ga 1:15-24">Galatians 1:15-24</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) When he did meet the other apostles they had nothing to add to his revelations <reference osisRef="ga 2:1-6">Galatians 2:1-6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The other apostles fully recognized Paul's apostleship. <reference osisRef="ga 2:7-10">Galatians 2:7-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) If the legalizers pleaded Peter's authority, the answer was that he himself had claimed none when rebuked (<reference osisRef="ga 2:11-14">Galatians 2:11-14</reference>). </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv137"/><div sID="gen4740" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv137"/> <hi type="bold">Jews' religion</hi> <div eID="gen4740" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4741" type="x-p"/> The new dispensation of grace having come in, the Mosaic system, if still persisted in, becomes a mere "Jews' religion."

<hi type="bold">religion</hi><div eID="gen4741" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4742" type="x-p"/> In verses 13 and 14 the Greek word for "the Jews' religion" is Ioudaismos (Judaism). In <reference osisRef="ac 26:5">Acts 26:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 1:26 jas 1:27">James 1:26,27</reference> threskeia--religious service--is translated "religion," and in <reference osisRef="col 2:18">Colossians 2:18,</reference> "worshipping." Excepting <reference osisRef="jas 1:27">James 1:27,</reference> "religion" has always a bad sense, and nowhere is it synonymous with salvation or spirituality.

<hi type="bold">We who are</hi><div eID="gen4742" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4743" type="x-p"/> Paul here quotes from his words to Peter when he withstood him at Antioch to show the Galatians that, whatever the legalists may have pretended, Peter and he were in perfect accord doctrinally. Paul appealed to the common belief of Peter and himself as a rebuke of Peter's inconsistent practice.<div eID="gen4743" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4744" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sinners</hi> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">we seek</hi><div eID="gen4744" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4745" type="x-p"/> That is, "we" Jews. <reference osisRef="ro 3:19-23">Romans 3:19-23</reference>. The passage might be thus paraphrased: If we Jews, in seeking to be justified by faith in Christ, take our places as mere sinners, like the Gentiles, is it therefore Christ who makes us sinners? By no means. It is by putting ourselves again under law after seeking justification through Christ, that we act as if we were still unjustified sinners, seeking to become righteous through law-works. <reference osisRef="ga 5:1-4">Galatians 5:1-4</reference>.<div eID="gen4745" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4746" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sinners</hi> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">transgressor</hi><div eID="gen4746" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4747" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">not I</hi><div eID="gen4747" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4748" type="x-p"/> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 4:24">Ephesians 4:24</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). vs. <reference osisRef="ga 5:4">Galatians 5:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4748" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4749" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen4749" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv138"/><div sID="gen4750" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gal.2"/>
<div eID="gen4750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4751" type="x-p"/><chapter n="3" osisID="Gal.3" sID="Gal.3"/>

<hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). vs. <reference osisRef="ga 5:4">Galatians 5:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4751" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4752" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><div eID="gen4752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4753" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">God</hi><div eID="gen4753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4754" type="x-p"/> Jehovah. <reference osisRef="ge 15:6">Genesis 15:6</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Wherefore then</hi><div eID="gen4754" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4755" type="x-p"/> The answer is sixfold:<div eID="gen4755" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The law was added because of transgressions, i.e. to give to sin the character of transgression.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(a) Men had been sinning before Moses, but in the absence of law their sins were not put to their account. <reference osisRef="ro 5:13">Romans 5:13</reference>. The law gave to sin the character of "transgression," i.e. of personal guilt. (b) Also, since men not only continued to transgress after the law was given, but were provoked to transgress by the very law that forbade it <reference osisRef="ro 7:8">Romans 7:8,</reference> the law conclusively proved the inveterate sinfulness of man's nature <reference osisRef="ro 7:11-13">Romans 7:11-13</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The law, therefore, "concluded all under sin" <reference osisRef="ro 3:19 ro 3:20 ro 3:23">Romans 3:19,20,23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The law was an ad interim dealing, "till the seed should come". <reference osisRef="ga 3:19">Galatians 3:19</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The law shut sinful man up to faith as the only avenue of escape. <reference osisRef="ga 3:23">Galatians 3:23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The law was to the Jews what the pedagogue was in a Greek household, a ruler of children in their minority, and it had this character "unto" i.e. until Christ <reference osisRef="ga 3:24">Galatians 3:24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) Christ having come, the believer is no longer under the pedagogue. <reference osisRef="ga 3:25">Galatians 3:25</reference></item> </list> <div sID="gen4756" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">because of</hi> for the sake, i.e. in order that sin might be made manifest as transgression. See, <reference osisRef="ro 4:15">Romans 4:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 5:20"> 5:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 7:7 ro 7:13"> 7:7,13</reference>. <div eID="gen4756" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv138"/><div sID="gen4757" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv138"/> <hi type="bold">righteousness</hi> <div eID="gen4757" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4758" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">law</hi><div eID="gen4758" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4759" type="x-p"/> I. The law of Moses, Summary:<div eID="gen4759" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The Mosaic Covenant was given to Israel in three parts: the commandments, expressing the righteous will of God <reference osisRef="ex 20:1-26">Exodus 20:1-26,</reference> the "judgments," governing the social life of Israel <reference osisRef="ex 21:1-ex 24:11">Exodus 21:1-24:11</reference>, and the "ordinances," governing the religious life of Israel ; <reference osisRef="ex 24:12">Exodus 24:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 31:18"> 31:18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The commandments and ordinances were one complete and inseparable whole. When an Israelite sinned, he was held "blameless" if he brought the required offering <reference osisRef="lu 1:6">Luke 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:6">Philippians 3:6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Law, as a method of the divine dealing with man, characterized the dispensation extending from the giving of the law to the death of Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="ga 3:13 ga 3:14 ga 3:23 ga 3:24">Galatians 3:13,14,23,24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The attempt of legalistic teachers (e.g.) <reference osisRef="ac 15:1-31">Acts 15:1-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:1-5">Galatians 2:1-5,</reference> to mingle law with grace as the divine method for this present dispensation of grace, brought out the true relation of the law to the Christian, viz.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4760" type="x-p"/> II. The Christian doctrine of the law:<div eID="gen4760" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Law is in contrast with grace. Under the latter God bestows the righteousness which, under law, He demanded <reference osisRef="ex 19:5">Exodus 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:21">Romans 3:21</reference>")</hi>. ; <reference osisRef="ro 10:3-10">Romans 10:3-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:30">1 Corinthians 1:30</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The law is, in itself, holy, just, good, and spiritual <reference osisRef="ro 7:12-14">Romans 7:12-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Before the law the whole world is guilty, and the law is therefore of necessity a ministry of condemnation, death, and the divine curse <reference osisRef="ro 3:19">Romans 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 3:7-9">2 Corinthians 3:7-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:10">Galatians 3:10</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4761" type="x-p"/> For Another Point of View: See Topic 301242<div eID="gen4761" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4762" type="x-p"/> Other Factors to Consider: See Topic 301187<div eID="gen4762" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Christ bore the curse of the law, and redeemed the believer both from the curse and from the dominion of the law <reference osisRef="ga 3:13">Galatians 3:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:5-7"> 4:5-7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Law neither justifies a sinner nor sanctifies a believer <reference osisRef="ga 2:16">Galatians 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:2 ga 3:3 ga 3:11 ga 3:12"> 3:2,3,11,12</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The believer is both dead to the law and redeemed from it, so that he is "not under the law, but under grace" <reference osisRef="ro 6:14">Romans 6:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 7:4"> 7:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:19">Galatians 2:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:4-7"> 4:4-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 1:8 1ti 1:9">1 Timothy 1:8,9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) Under the new covenant of grace the principle of obedience to the divine will is inwrought <reference osisRef="heb 10:6">Hebrews 10:6</reference>. So far is the life of the believer from the anarchy of self-will that he is "inlawed to Christ" <reference osisRef="1co 9:21">1 Corinthians 9:21</reference> and the new "law of Christ" ; <reference osisRef="ga 6:2">Galatians 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="2jo 1:5">2 John 1:5</reference> is his delight; while, through the indwelling Spirit, the righteousness of the law is fulfilled in him ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:2-4">Romans 8:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 5:16-18">Galatians 5:16-18</reference>. The commandments are used in the distinctively Christian Scriptures as an instruction in righteousness ; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:16">2 Timothy 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 13:8-10">Romans 13:8-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 6:1-3">Ephesians 6:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 9:8 1co 9:9">1 Corinthians 9:8,9</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4763" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to bring us</hi> Omit "to bring us."<div eID="gen4763" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4764" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto</hi> up to, or until.

<hi type="bold">schoolmaster</hi><div eID="gen4764" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4765" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G3807">παιδαγωγός</w>, "child-conductor)." "among the Greeks and Romans, persons, for the most part slaves, who had it in charge to educate and give constant attendance upon boys till they came of age."--H.A.W. Meyer. The argument does not turn upon the extent or nature of the pedagogue's authority, but upon the fact that it wholly ceased when the "child" <reference osisRef="ga 4:1">Galatians 4:1</reference> became a ; <reference osisRef="so 1:1">Song 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-6">Galatians 4:1-6</reference> when the minor became an adult. The adult "son" does voluntarily that which formerly he did in fear of the pedagogue. But even if he does not, it is no longer a question between the son and the pedagogue (the law), but between the son and his Father--God. (Cf) ; <reference osisRef="heb 12:5-10">Hebrews 12:5-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:1 1jo 2:2">1 John 2:1,2</reference>.

<hi type="bold">the children</hi><div eID="gen4765" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(Greek - <w lemma="strong:G3807">παιδαγωγός</w> = sons). <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:5">Ephesians 1:5</reference>")</hi>. </item> </list> <chapter eID="Gal.3"/>
<chapter n="4" osisID="Gal.4" sID="Gal.4"/> <div sID="gen4766" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">world</hi> <div eID="gen4766" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4767" type="x-p"/> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">little children</hi><div eID="gen4767" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4768" type="x-p"/> The allegory <reference osisRef="ga 4:22-31">Galatians 4:22-31</reference> is addressed to justified but immature believers (cf) <reference osisRef="1co 3:1 1co 3:2">1 Corinthians 3:1,2</reference> who, under the influence of legalistic teachers, "desire to be under the law," and has, therefore, no application to a sinner seeking justification. It raises and answers, for the fifth time in this Epistle, the question, Is the believer under the law? ; <reference osisRef="ga 2:19-21">Galatians 2:19-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:1-3 ga 3:25-26"> 3:1-3 3:25,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:4-6"> 4:4-6</reference> <reference osisRef="ga 4:9-31"> 4:9-31</reference>.
<hi type="bold">Agar</hi><div eID="gen4768" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4769" type="x-p"/> Hagar.
<hi type="bold">Agar</hi><div eID="gen4769" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4770" type="x-p"/> Hagar. <chapter eID="Gal.4"/><div eID="gen4770" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4771" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Gal.5" sID="Gal.5"/>

<hi type="bold">no effect</hi> <div eID="gen4771" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4772" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">grace</hi> <div eID="gen4772" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4773" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">no effect</hi> i.e. of no experimental effect: the sense of liberty is lost. <reference osisRef="ga 2:21">Galatians 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:23">Colossians 1:23</reference>.<div eID="gen4773" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4774" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). <reference osisRef="eph 1:6 eph 1:7">Ephesians 1:6,7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ga 1:6">Galatians 1:6</reference>")</hi> , See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>".

<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen4774" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4775" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">under the law</hi><div eID="gen4775" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4776" type="x-p"/> i.e. not under bondage of effort to please God by law-works. <reference osisRef="2co 3:17">2 Corinthians 3:17</reference>.

<hi type="bold">But the fruit</hi><div eID="gen4776" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4777" type="x-p"/> Christian character is not mere moral or legal correctness, but the possession and manifestation of nine graces: love, joy, peace--character as an inward state; longsuffering, gentleness, goodness--character in expression toward man; faith, meekness, temperance-- character in expression toward God. Taken together they present a moral portrait of Christ, and may be taken as the apostle's explanation of <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference> "Not I, but Christ," and as a definition of "fruit" in <reference osisRef="joh 15:1-8">John 15:1-8</reference> This character is possible because of the believer's vital union to Christ ; <reference osisRef="joh 15:5">John 15:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference> and is wholly the fruit of the Spirit in those believers who are yielded to Him. <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23">Galatians 5:22,23</reference>. <div eID="gen4777" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv139"/><div sID="gen4778" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Gal.5"/>
<div eID="gen4778" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4779" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="6" osisID="Gal.6" sID="Gal.6"/>

<hi type="bold">fault</hi> <div eID="gen4779" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4780" type="x-p"/> i.e. sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">communicate</hi><div eID="gen4780" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4781" type="x-p"/> Or, share with him. <reference osisRef="1co 9:7-15">1 Corinthians 9:7-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 5:18">1 Timothy 5:18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">large</hi><div eID="gen4781" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4782" type="x-p"/> (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G848">αὑτου̑</w> )...mine own hand." The apostle was, it appears from many considerations, afflicted with ophthalmia, a common disease in the East, to the point almost of total blindness (e.g.) <reference osisRef="ga 4:13-15">Galatians 4:13-15</reference>. Ordinarily, therefore, he dictated his letters. But now, having no amanuensis at hand, but urged by the spiritual danger of his dear Galatians, he writes, we cannot know with what pain and difficulty, with his own hand, in the "large letters" his darkened vision compelled him to use.

<hi type="bold">constrain you to be circumcised</hi><div eID="gen4782" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4783" type="x-p"/> "Circumcision" stands here for externality in religion -- form rather than spirit. <reference osisRef="col 2:16-23">Colossians 2:16-23</reference>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen4783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4784" type="x-p"/> kosmos = world-system. <reference osisRef="eph 2:2">Ephesians 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 7:7">John 7:7</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Gal.6"/><div eID="gen4784" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen4728" osisID="Gal" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Eph" sID="gen4785" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Eph.1" sID="Eph.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv139"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Ephesians</title> <div sID="gen4786" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="eph 1">Read first chapter of Ephesians</reference><div eID="gen4786" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4787" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="eph 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4787" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4788" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Ephesians was written from Rome in A.D. 64. It is the first in order of the Prison Epistles. <reference osisRef="ac 20:1-ac 27:44">Acts 20:1-27:44</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 28:30">Acts 28:30</reference>")</hi> and was sent by Tychicus, concurrently with Colossians and Philemon. It is probable that the two greater letters had their occasion in the return of Onesimus to Philemon. Ephesians is the most impersonal of Paul's letters. Indeed the words, "to the Ephesians," are not in the best manuscripts. <reference osisRef="col 4:16">Colossians 4:16</reference> mentions an epistle to the Laodiceans. It has been conjectured that the letter known to us as Ephesians is really the Laodicean letter. Probably it was sent to Ephesus and Laodicea without being addressed to any church. The letter would then be "to the saints and the faithful in Christ Jesus" anywhere.<div eID="gen4788" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4789" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The doctrine of the Epistle confirms this view. It contains the highest church truth, but has nothing about church order. The church here is the true church, "His body," not the local church, as in Philippians, Corinthians, etc. Essentially, three lines of truth make up this Epistle: the believer's exalted position through grace; the truth concerning the body of Christ; and a walk in accordance with that position.<div eID="gen4789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4790" type="x-p"/> There is a close spiritual affinity between Ephesians and Joshua, the "heavenlies" answering in Christian position to Canaan in Israel's experience. In both there is conflict, often failure, but also victory, rest, and possession <reference osisRef="jos 21:43-45">Joshua 21:43-45</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 1:3">Ephesians 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:14-19"> 3:14-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 6:16 eph 6:23"> 6:16,23</reference>. As befits a complete revelation, the number seven is conspicuous in the structure of Ephesians.<div eID="gen4790" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4791" type="x-p"/> The divisions are, broadly, four:<div eID="gen4791" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The apostolic greeting1:1,2</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Positional; the believer's standing "Christ" and "in the heavenlies" through pure grace, 1:3-3:21.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Walk and service, 4:1-5:17</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The walk and warfare of the Spirit-filled believer, 5:18-6:24.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4792" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv139"/> <hi type="bold">in Christ</hi> <div eID="gen4792" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4793" type="x-p"/> The believer's place as a member of the body of Christ, vitally united to Him by the baptism with the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference>.

<hi type="bold">in heavenly places</hi><div eID="gen4793" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4794" type="x-p"/> Literally, the heavenlies. The same Greek word is used in <reference osisRef="joh 3:12">John 3:12</reference> where "things" is added. In both places the word signifies that which is heavenly in contradistinction to that which is earthy. In Ephesians "places" is especially misleading. "The heavenlies" may be defined as the sphere of the believer's spiritual experience as identified with Christ in nature. <reference osisRef="2pe 1:4">2 Peter 1:4,</reference> life, ; <reference osisRef="col 3:4">Colossians 3:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:12">1 John 5:12,</reference> relationships ; <reference osisRef="joh 20:17">John 20:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:11">Hebrews 2:11</reference> service, ; <reference osisRef="joh 17:18">John 17:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 28:20">Matthew 28:20,</reference> suffering ; <reference osisRef="php 1:29">Philippians 1:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:10"> 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:24">Colossians 1:24</reference> inheritance <reference osisRef="ro 8:16 ro 8:17">Romans 8:16,17</reference> and future glory in the kingdom ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:18-21">Romans 8:18-21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:6">Revelation 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 5:10"> 5:10</reference>. The believer is a heavenly man, and a stranger and pilgrim on the earth. ; <reference osisRef="heb 3:1">Hebrews 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 2:11">1 Peter 2:11</reference>.

<hi type="bold">predestinated</hi><div eID="gen4794" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4795" type="x-p"/> Predestination is that effective exercise of the will of God by which things before determined by Him are brought to pass. See Election,<div eID="gen4795" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4796" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Pe 1:2">1 Peter 1:2</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen4796" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4797" type="x-p"/> Foreknowledge, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Pe 1:20">1 Peter 1:20</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen4797" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4798" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">adoption</hi> <div eID="gen4798" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4799" type="x-p"/> Adoption (huiothesia, "placing as a son") is not so much a word of relationship as of position. The believer's relation to God as a child results from the new birth <reference osisRef="joh 1:12 joh 1:13">John 1:12,13</reference> whereas adoption is the act of God whereby one already a child is, through redemption from the law, placed in the position of an adult son. <reference osisRef="ga 4:1-5">Galatians 4:1-5</reference>.<div eID="gen4799" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4800" type="x-p"/> The indwelling Spirit gives the realization of this in the believer's present experience <reference osisRef="ga 4:6">Galatians 4:6</reference> but the full manifestation of the believer's sonship awaits the resurrection, change, and translation of saints, which is called "the redemption of the body" ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:23">Romans 8:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference> ; <reference osisRef="eph 1:14">Ephesians 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:2">1 John 3:2</reference>.

<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen4800" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4801" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4801" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4802" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). <reference osisRef="Eph 1:6-7">Eph 1:6-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph 2:5 Eph 2:7-8"> 2:5,7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><div eID="gen4802" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4803" type="x-p"/> See, <reference osisRef="ro 16:25 ro 16:26">Romans 16:25,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:3">Ephesians 3:3</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">dispensation of the fullness of times</hi><div eID="gen4803" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4804" type="x-p"/> The Dispensation of the Fulness of Times. This, the seventh and last of the ordered ages which condition human life on the earth, is identical with the kingdom covenanted to David. <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference><div eID="gen4804" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4805" type="x-p"/> Summary;<div eID="gen4805" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4806" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24,</reference> and gathers into itself under Christ all past "times":<div eID="gen4806" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The time of oppression and misrule ends by Christ taking His kingdom. <reference osisRef="isa 11:3 isa 11:4">Isaiah 11:3,4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The time of testimony and divine forbearance ends in judgment. <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 17:30 ac 17:31">Acts 17:30,31</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:7-15">Revelation 20:7-15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The time of toil ends in rest and reward. <reference osisRef="2th 1:6 2th 1:7">2 Thessalonians 1:6,7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The time of suffering ends in glory. <reference osisRef="ro 8:17 ro 8:18">Romans 8:17,18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The time of Israel's blindness and chastisement ends in restoration and conversion. <reference osisRef="ro 11:25-27">Romans 11:25-27</reference>; <reference osisRef="eze 39:25-29">Ezekiel 39:25-29</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The times of the Gentiles end in the smiting of the image and the setting up of the kingdom of the heavens. <reference osisRef="da 2:34 da 2:35">Daniel 2:34,35</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:15-21">Revelation 19:15-21</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) The time of creation's thraldom ends in deliverance at the manifestation of the sons of God. <reference osisRef="ge 3:17">Genesis 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 11:6-8">Isaiah 11:6-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:19-21">Romans 8:19-21</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv140"/><div sID="gen4807" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv140"/> <hi type="bold">sealed</hi> <div eID="gen4807" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4808" type="x-p"/> The Holy Spirit is Himself the seal. In the symbolism of Scripture a seal signifies:<div eID="gen4808" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) A finished transaction <reference osisRef="jer 32:9 jer 32:10">Jeremiah 32:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 17:4">John 17:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 19:30"> 19:30</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Ownership <reference osisRef="jer 32:11 jer 32:12">Jeremiah 32:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 2:19">2 Timothy 2:19</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Security <reference osisRef="es 8:8">Esther 8:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 6:17">Daniel 6:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:30">Ephesians 4:30</reference> </item> </list> <chapter eID="Eph.1"/>
<div sID="gen4809" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Eph.2" sID="Eph.2"/>

<hi type="bold">world</hi> <div eID="gen4809" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4810" type="x-p"/> kosmos = world-system. <reference osisRef="col 2:20">Colossians 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 7:7">John 7:7</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">dead</hi><div eID="gen4810" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4811" type="x-p"/> Death (spiritual), Summary: Spiritual death is the state of the natural or unregenerate man as still in his sins. <reference osisRef="eph 2:1">Ephesians 2:1</reference> alienated from the life of God <reference osisRef="eph 4:18 eph 4:19">Ephesians 4:18,19</reference> and destitute of the Spirit. Prolonged beyond the death of the body, spiritual death is a state of eternal separation from God in conscious suffering. This is called "the second death." ; <reference osisRef="re 2:11">Revelation 2:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:6 re 20:14"> 20:6,14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 21:8"> 21:8</reference>.<div eID="gen4811" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4812" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saved</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). Ep 5,7,8 <reference osisRef="col 1:6">Colossians 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen4812" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4813" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">saved</hi> <div eID="gen4813" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4814" type="x-p"/> See note, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>
<hi type="bold">created</hi><div eID="gen4814" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4815" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 4:24">Ephesians 4:24</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen4815" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4816" type="x-p"/> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">new man</hi><div eID="gen4816" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4817" type="x-p"/> Here the "new man" is not the individual believer but the church, considered as the body of Christ in the sense of <reference osisRef="eph 1:22 eph 1:23">Ephesians 1:22,23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:10 col 3:11">Colossians 3:10,11</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Eph.2"/><div eID="gen4817" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">grace</hi> <div eID="gen4818" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4819" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). <reference osisRef="eph 3:2-8">Ephesians 3:2-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:7 eph 4:29">Ephesians 4:7,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>.
<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><div eID="gen4819" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4820" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">That the Gentiles</hi><div eID="gen4820" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4821" type="x-p"/> That the Gentiles were to be saved was no mystery <reference osisRef="ro 9:24-33">Romans 9:24-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 10:19-21">Romans 10:19-21</reference>. The mystery "hid in God" was the divine purpose to make of Jew and Gentile a wholly new thing--"the church, which is his Christ's body," formed by the baptism with the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="1co 12:12 1co 12:13">1 Corinthians 12:12,13</reference> and in which the earthly distinction of Jew and Gentile disappears ; <reference osisRef="eph 2:14 eph 2:15">Ephesians 2:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:10 col 3:11">Colossians 3:10,11</reference>. The revelation of this mystery, which was foretold, but not explained by Christ <reference osisRef="mt 16:18">Matthew 16:18</reference> was committed to Paul. In his writings alone we find the doctrine, position, walk, and destiny of the church.

<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><div eID="gen4821" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4822" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Eph.3"/><div eID="gen4822" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4823" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Eph.4" sID="Eph.4"/>

<hi type="bold">gave</hi> <div eID="gen4823" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4824" type="x-p"/> In <reference osisRef="1co 12:8-28">1 Corinthians 12:8-28</reference> the Spirit is seen as enduing the members of the body of Christ with spiritual gifts, or enablements for a varied service; here certain Spirit-endued men, viz. apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers, are themselves the gifts whom the glorified Christ bestows upon His body the church. In Corinthians the gifts are spiritual enablements for specific service; in Ephesians the gifts are men who have such enablements.<div eID="gen4824" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4825" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">some</hi> <div eID="gen4825" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4826" type="x-p"/> The Lord, in bestowing the gifted men, determines, providentially (e.g.) <reference osisRef="ac 11:22-26">Acts 11:22-26</reference> or directly through the Spirit (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="ac 13:1 ac 13:2">Acts 13:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 16:6 ac 16:7"> 16:6,7</reference> the places of their service. "Some" (churches or places) need one gift, as, (e.g.) evangelist; "some" (churches or places) need rather a pastor or teacher. Absolutely nothing in Christ's service is left to mere human judgment or self-choosing. Even an apostle was not permitted to choose his place of service <reference osisRef="ac 16:7 ac 16:8">Acts 16:7,8</reference>.
<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><div eID="gen4826" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4827" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">old man</hi><div eID="gen4827" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4828" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 6:6">Romans 6:6</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">new man</hi><div eID="gen4828" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4829" type="x-p"/> The new man is the regenerate man as distinguished from the old man <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 6:6">Romans 6:6</reference>")</hi> and is a new man as having become a partaker of the divine nature and life <reference osisRef="2pe 1:4">2 Peter 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:3 col 3:4">Colossians 3:3,4</reference> and in no sense the old man made over, or improved ; <reference osisRef="2co 5:17">2 Corinthians 5:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:15">Galatians 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 2:10">Ephesians 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:10">Colossians 3:10</reference>. The new man is Christ, "formed" in the believer ; <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:19"> 4:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:27">Colossians 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 4:12">1 John 4:12</reference>.<div eID="gen4829" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4830" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">sin</hi><div eID="gen4830" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4831" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen4831" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4832" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). vs. <reference osisRef="php 1:7">Philippians 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>. <chapter eID="Eph.4"/><div eID="gen4832" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4833" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="Eph.5" sID="Eph.5"/>
<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi> <div eID="gen4833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4834" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">saviour</hi><div eID="gen4834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4835" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">even as Christ</hi><div eID="gen4835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4836" type="x-p"/> Christ's love-work for the church is threefold: past, present, future:<div eID="gen4836" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) For love He gave Himself to redeem the church (<reference osisRef="eph 5:25">Ephesians 5:25</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) in love He is sanctifying the church (<reference osisRef="eph 5:26">Ephesians 5:26</reference>);</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) for the reward of His sacrifice and labour of love He will present the church to Himself in flawless perfection, "one pearl of great price" (<reference osisRef="eph 5:27">Ephesians 5:27</reference>) <reference osisRef="mt 13:46">Matthew 13:46</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv141"/><div sID="gen4837" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv141"/> <hi type="bold">bride</hi> <div eID="gen4837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4838" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="eph 5:30 eph 5:31">Ephesians 5:30,31</reference> are quoted from <reference osisRef="ge 2:23 ge 2:24">Genesis 2:23,24</reference> and exclude the interpretation that the reference is to the church merely as the body of Christ. Eve, taken from Adam's body, was truly "bone of his bones, and flesh of his flesh," but she was also his wife, united to him in a relation which makes of "twain... one flesh" <reference osisRef="mt 19:5 mt 19:6">Matthew 19:5,6</reference> and so a clear type of the church as bride of Christ. <reference osisRef="2co 11:2 2co 11:3">2 Corinthians 11:2,3</reference>. The bride type are Eve <reference osisRef="ge 2:23 ge 2:24">Genesis 2:23,24</reference> Rebecca<div eID="gen4838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4839" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 24:1">Genesis 24:1</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4840" type="x-p"/> Asenath <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 41:45">Genesis 41:45</reference>")</hi><div eID="gen4840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4841" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 37:2">Genesis 37:2</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen4841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4842" type="x-p"/> Zipporah <reference osisRef="ex 2:21">Exodus 2:21</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ho 2:2">Hosea 2:2</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4843" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">mystery</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Eph.5"/><div eID="gen4843" type="x-p"/>

<hi type="bold">salvation</hi> <div eID="gen4844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4845" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<div canonical="true" osisID="Phil" sID="gen4847" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv142"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Philippians</title> <div sID="gen4848" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="php 1">Read first chapter of Philippians</reference><div eID="gen4848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4849" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="php 1:1">Philippians 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4849" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4850" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of Philippians cannot be positively fixed. It is one of the prison letters. Whether Paul was twice imprisoned, and if so, whether Philippians was written during the first or second imprisonment, affects in no way the message of the Epistle. A.D. 64 is the commonly received date. The immediate occasion of the Epistle is disclosed in <reference osisRef="php 4:10-18">Philippians 4:10-18</reference>.<div eID="gen4850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4851" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The theme of Philippians is Christian experience. Soundness of doctrine is assumed. There is nothing in church order to set right. Philippi is a normal New Testament assembly--"saints in Christ Jesus, with the bishops (elders) and deacons." The circumstances of the apostle are in striking contrast with his Christian experience. As to the former, he was Nero's prisoner. As to the latter, there was the shout of victory, the paean of joy. Christian experience, he would teach us, is not something which is going on around the believer, but something which is going on within him.<div eID="gen4851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4852" type="x-p"/> The key-verse is, "For me to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (<reference osisRef="php 1:21">Philippians 1:21</reference>). Right Christian experience, then, is the outworking, whatever one's circumstances may be, of the life, nature, and mind of Christ living in us (<reference osisRef="php 1:6 php 1:11">Philippians 1:6,11</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:5 php 2:13"> 2:5,13</reference>).<div eID="gen4852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4853" type="x-p"/> The divisions are indicated by the chapters:<div eID="gen4853" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Christ, the believer's life, rejoicing in suffering, 1:1-30.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christ, the believer's pattern, rejoicing in lowly service, 2:1-30</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christ, the believer's object, rejoicing despite imperfections, 3:1-21.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christ, the believer's strength, rejoicing over anxiety, 4:1-23.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4854" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv142"/> <hi type="bold">which are at</hi> <div eID="gen4854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4855" type="x-p"/> Churches (local), Summary: A local church is an assembly of professed believers on the Lord Jesus Christ, living for the most part in one locality, who assemble themselves together in His name for the breaking of bread, worship, praise, prayer, testimony, the ministry of the word, discipline, and the furtherance of the Gospel, <reference osisRef="heb 10:25">Hebrews 10:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 20:7">Acts 20:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 14:26">1 Corinthians 14:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 5:4 1co 5:5"> 5:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 4:14-18">Philippians 4:14-18</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 1:8">1 Thessalonians 1:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 13:1-4">Acts 13:1-4</reference>. Such a church exists where two or three are thus gathered <reference osisRef="mt 18:20">Matthew 18:20</reference>. Every such local church has Christ in the midst, is a temple of God, and indwelt by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="1co 3:16 1co 3:17">1 Corinthians 3:16,17</reference>. When perfected in organization a local church consists of "saints, with the bishops elders and deacons."
<hi type="bold">day of</hi><div eID="gen4855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4856" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 1:8">1 Corinthians 1:8</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen4856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4857" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">the palace</hi><div eID="gen4857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4858" type="x-p"/> Or, Caesar's court. <reference osisRef="php 4:22">Philippians 4:22</reference>.

<hi type="bold">form of God</hi> <div eID="gen4861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4862" type="x-p"/> "Form," etc. (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G3444">μορφή</w>, the form by which a person or thing strikes the vision, the external appearance)."--Thayer. CF <reference osisRef="joh 17:15">John 17:15</reference>. "The glory which I had with Thee before the world was." Nothing in this passage teaches that the Eternal Word <reference osisRef="joh 1:1">John 1:1</reference> emptied Himself of either His divine nature, or His attributes, but only of the outward and visible manifestation of the Godhead. "He emptied, stripped Himself of the insignia of Majesty."--Lightfoot. "When occasion demanded He exercised His divine attributes."-- Moorehead. CF <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:1">John 1:1</reference>")</hi>.
