<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv143"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Colossians</title> <div sID="gen4877" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="col 1">Read first chapter of Colossians</reference><div eID="gen4877" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4878" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="col 1:1">Colossians 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4878" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4879" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Colossians was sent by the same messenger who bore Ephesians and Philemon, and was probably written at the same time.<div eID="gen4879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4880" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Epaphras, who laboured in the Word in the assembly at Colosse, was Paul's fellow-prisoner at Rome. Doubtless from him Paul learned the state of that church. As to fundamentals that state was excellent (<reference osisRef="col 1:3-8"> 1:3-8</reference>), but in a subtle way two forms of error were at work: The first was legality in its Alexandrian form of asceticism, "touch not, taste not," with a trace of the Judaic observance of "days"; the object of which was the mortification of the body (cf <reference osisRef="ro 8:13">Romans 8:13</reference>). The second form of error was false mysticism, "intruding into those things which he hath not seen"--the result of philosophic speculation. Because these are ever present perils, Colossians was written, not for that day only, but for the warning of the church in all days.<div eID="gen4880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4881" type="x-p"/> The Epistle is in seven divisions:<div eID="gen4881" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Introduction1:1-8</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The apostolic prayer1:9-14</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The exaltation of Christ, Creator, Redeemer, Indweller1:15-29</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Godhead incarnate in Christ, in whom the believer is complete. 2:1-23.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The believer's union with Christ in resurrection life and glory3:1-4</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christian living, the fruit of union with Christ, 3:5-4:6</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christian fellowship, 4:7-18</item> </list> <div sID="gen4882" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv143"/> <hi type="bold">grace</hi> <div eID="gen4882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4883" type="x-p"/> Grace (in salvation). vs. <reference osisRef="2th 2:16">2 Thessalonians 2:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">redemption</hi><div eID="gen4883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4884" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">reconciled</hi><div eID="gen4884" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4885" type="x-p"/> Reconciliation. The Greek word signifies "to change thoroughly from," and occurs, <reference osisRef="ro 5:10">Romans 5:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 11:15"> 11:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 7:11">1 Corinthians 7:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 5:18 2co 5:19 2co 5:20">2 Corinthians 5:18,19,20</reference>. Reconciliation looks toward the effect of the death of christ upon man, as propitiation <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:25">Romans 3:25</reference>")</hi> , is the Godward aspect, and is that effect of the death of Christ upon the believing sinner which, through divine power, works in him a "thorough change" toward God from enmity and aversion to love and trust. It is never said that God is reconciled. God is propitiated, the sinner reconciled (cf) <reference osisRef="2co 5:18-21">2 Corinthians 5:18-21</reference>.
<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><div eID="gen4885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4886" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">mystery</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4887" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Christ</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 4:24">Ephesians 4:24</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Col.1"/><div eID="gen4887" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4888" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Col.2" sID="Col.2"/>

<hi type="bold">mystery of God</hi> <div eID="gen4888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4889" type="x-p"/> The "mystery of God" is Christ, as incarnating the fulness of the Godhead, and all the divine wisdom and knowledge for the redemption and reconciliation of man.<div eID="gen4889" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4890" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">mystery</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4890" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4891" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and of</hi> The best authorities omit "and of the Father, and of Christ."

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen4891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4892" type="x-p"/> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">the sins of</hi><div eID="gen4892" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4893" type="x-p"/> Omit "the sins of."

<hi type="bold">intruding into those things</hi><div eID="gen4893" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4894" type="x-p"/> The errorists against whom Paul warns the Colossians, and against whom, in principle, the warning has perpetual significance, were called "Gnostics," from gnosis, "knowledge." These Gnostics "came most keenly into conflict with the exalted rank and redeeming rank of Christ, to whom they did not leave His full divine dignity, but assigned to Him merely the highest rank in the order of spirits, while they exalted angels as concerned in bringing the Messianic salvation."--H.A.W. Meyer. Paul's characteristic word in Colossians for the divine revelation is epignosis, i.e. "full knowledge." <reference osisRef="col 1:9 col 1:10">Colossians 1:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:10"> 3:10</reference> as against the pretended "knowledge" of the errorists. The warnings apply to all extra-biblical forms, doctrines, and customs, and to all ascetic practices.<div eID="gen4894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4895" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angels</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">world</hi><div eID="gen4895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4896" type="x-p"/> kosmos = world-system. <reference osisRef="jas 1:27">James 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 7:7">John 7:7</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">not in any</hi><div eID="gen4896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4897" type="x-p"/> Or, "which do not really honour God, but only satisfy the flesh" (i.e. by creating a reputation for superior sanctity). <div eID="gen4897" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv144"/><div sID="gen4898" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="Col.2"/>
<div eID="gen4898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4899" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Col.3" sID="Col.3"/>

<hi type="bold">not in any</hi> <div eID="gen4899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4900" type="x-p"/> Or, "which do not really honour God, but only satisfy the flesh" (i.e. by creating a reputation for superior sanctity).
<hi type="bold">old man</hi><div eID="gen4900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4901" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 6:6">Romans 6:6</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">created</hi><div eID="gen4901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4902" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 4:24">Ephesians 4:24</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">perfectness</hi><div eID="gen4902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4903" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">God</hi><div eID="gen4903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4904" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">God</hi> Christ.<div eID="gen4904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4905" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rule</hi> See <reference osisRef="joh 14:27">John 14:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 14:17">Romans 14:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 4:7">Philippians 4:7</reference>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen4905" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4906" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). vs. <reference osisRef="col 4:6">Colossians 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>. <chapter eID="Col.3"/><div eID="gen4906" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4907" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="Col.4" sID="Col.4"/>
<hi type="bold">mystery</hi> <div eID="gen4907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4908" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">grace</hi><div eID="gen4908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4909" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). <reference osisRef="2th 1:12">2 Thessalonians 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Epaphras</hi><div eID="gen4909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4910" type="x-p"/> A touching illustration of priestly service, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>")</hi> as distinguished from ministry of gift. Shut up in prison, no longer able to preach, Epaphras was still, equally with all believers, a priest. No prison could keep him from the throne of grace, so he gave himself wholly to the priestly work of intercession.<div eID="gen4910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4911" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">perfect</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Col.4"/><div eID="gen4911" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen4876" osisID="Col" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="1Thess" sID="gen4912" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="1Thess.1" sID="1Thess.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv144"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 1 Thessalonians</title> <div sID="gen4913" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1th 1">Read first chapter of 1 Thessalonians</reference><div eID="gen4913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4914" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="1th 1:1">1 Thessalonians 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4915" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The Epistle was written from Corinth, A.D. 54, shortly after Paul's departure from Thessalonica (Ac16:, 17.), and is the earliest of his letters.<div eID="gen4915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4916" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The theme of the Epistle is threefold:<div eID="gen4916" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">To confirm young disciples in the foundational truths already taught them;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">To exhort them to go on to holiness;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">To comfort them concerning those who had fallen asleep. The second coming of Christ is prominent throughout. The Epistle is incidentally most interesting as showing the richness in doctrine of the primitive evangelism. During a mission of about one month the apostle had taught all the great doctrines of the Christian faith.</item> </list> <div sID="gen4917" type="x-p"/> The divisions of the Epistle are sufficiently indicated by the Chapters.<div eID="gen4917" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The model church, and the three tenses of the Christian life1:1-10</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The model servant and his reward2:1-20</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The model brother, and the believer's sanctification3:1-13</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The model walk, and the believer's hope, 4:1-18</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The model walk, and the day of Jehovah, 5:1-28</item> </list> <div sID="gen4918" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv144"/> <hi type="bold">work of faith</hi> <div eID="gen4918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4919" type="x-p"/> Lit. operative faith, and laborious love, and hope-filled patience.

<hi type="bold">how ye turned</hi><div eID="gen4919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4920" type="x-p"/> The tenses of the believer's life here indicated are logical and give the true order. They occur also in <reference osisRef="1th 1:3">1 Thessalonians 1:3</reference>. The "work of faith" is to "turn to God from idols" (cf) <reference osisRef="joh 6:28 joh 6:29">John 6:28,29</reference> the "labour of love" is to "serve the living and true God"; and the "patience of hope" is to "wait for his Son from heaven" (cf) ; <reference osisRef="mt 24:42">Matthew 24:42</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:13"> 25:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 12:36-48">Luke 12:36-48</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:11">Acts 1:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21">Philippians 3:20,21</reference>. Paul repeats this threefold sequence in <reference osisRef="tit 2:11-13">Titus 2:11-13</reference>. <chapter eID="1Thess.1"/><div eID="gen4920" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4921" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="1Thess.2" sID="1Thess.2"/>

<hi type="bold">saved</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen4921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4922" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sins</hi> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="1Thess.2"/><div eID="gen4922" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4923" type="x-p"/><chapter n="3" osisID="1Thess.3" sID="1Thess.3"/>
<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="1Thess.3"/><div eID="gen4923" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4924" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="4" osisID="1Thess.4" sID="1Thess.4"/>

<hi type="bold">caught up</hi> <div eID="gen4924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4925" type="x-p"/> Not church saints only, but all bodies of the saved, of whatever dispensation, are included in the first resurrection. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:52</reference>")</hi> as here described, but it is peculiarly the "blessed hope" of the Church (cf) <reference osisRef="mt 24:42">Matthew 24:42</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:13"> 25:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 12:36-48">Luke 12:36-48</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 1:11">Acts 1:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21">Philippians 3:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 2:11-13">Titus 2:11-13</reference>. <chapter eID="1Thess.4"/><div eID="gen4925" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4926" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="5" osisID="1Thess.5" sID="1Thess.5"/>
<hi type="bold">salvation</hi> <div eID="gen4926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4927" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">whole spirit and soul and body</hi><div eID="gen4927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4928" type="x-p"/> Man a trinity. That the human soul and spirit are not identical is proved by the facts that they are divisible. <reference osisRef="heb 4:12">Hebrews 4:12</reference> and that soul and spirit are sharply distinguished in the burial and resurrection of the body. It is sown a natural body (soma psuchikon= "soul- body"), it is raised a spiritual body (soma pneumatikon). <reference osisRef="1co 15:44">1 Corinthians 15:44</reference>. To assert, therefore, that there is no difference between soul and spirit is to assert that there is no difference between the mortal body and the resurrection body. In Scripture use, the distinction between spirit and soul may be traced. Briefly, that distinction is that the spirit is that part of man which "knows" <reference osisRef="1co 2:11">1 Corinthians 2:11</reference> his mind; the soul is the seat of the affections, desires, and so of the emotions, and of the active will, the self. "My soul is exceeding sorrowful" <reference osisRef="mt 26:38">Matthew 26:38</reference> see also ; <reference osisRef="mt 11:29">Matthew 11:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:27">John 12:27</reference>. The word transliterated "soul" in the O.T. (nephesh) is the exact equivalent of the N.T. word for soul ( (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G2174">εὐψυχέω</w>), and the use of "soul" in the O).T. is identical with the use of that word in the N.T. (see, e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="de 6:5">Deuteronomy 6:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 14:26"> 14:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 18:1">1 Samuel 18:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1sa 20:4 1sa 20:17"> 20:4,17</reference>; <reference osisRef="job 7:11 job 7:15">Job 7:11,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="job 14:22"> 14:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 42:6">Psalms 42:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 84:2"> 84:2</reference>. The N.T. word for spirit (pneuma) like the O.T. (ruach), is trans. "air", "breath", "wind," but predominantly "spirit," whether of God (e.g.) ; <reference osisRef="ge 1:2">Genesis 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 3:16">Matthew 3:16</reference> or of man ; <reference osisRef="ge 41:8">Genesis 41:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 5:5">1 Corinthians 5:5</reference>. Because man is "spirit" he is capable of God-consciousness, and of communication with God ; <reference osisRef="job 32:8">Job 32:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 18:28">Psalms 18:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="pr 20:27">Proverbs 20:27</reference> because he is "soul" he has self- consciousness ; <reference osisRef="ps 13:2">Psalms 13:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 42:5 ps 42:6 ps 42:11"> 42:5,6,11</reference> because he is "body" he has, through his senses, world consciousness.<div eID="gen4928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4929" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="1Thess.5"/><div eID="gen4929" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen4912" osisID="1Thess" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="2Thess" sID="gen4930" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="2Thess.1" sID="2Thess.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv145"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 2 Thessalonians</title> <div sID="gen4931" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2th 1">Read first chapter of 2 Thessalonians</reference><div eID="gen4931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4932" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="2th 1:1">2 Thessalonians 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4932" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4933" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Second Thessalonians was evidently written very soon after Paul's first letter to that church. The occasion may well have been the return of the bearer of the former Epistle and his report.<div eID="gen4933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4934" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The theme of Second Thessalonians is, unfortunately, obscured by a mistranslation in the A.V. of <reference osisRef="2th 2:2">2 Thessalonians 2:2</reference> where "day of Christ is at hand" <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 1:8">1 Corinthians 1:8</reference>")</hi> should be, "day of the Lord is now present" (See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Is 2:12">Is 2:12</reference>"). The Thessalonian converts were "shaken in mind" and "troubled," supposing, perhaps on the authority of a forged letter as from Paul, that the persecutions from which they were suffering were those of the "great and terrible day of the Lord," from which they had been taught to expect deliverance by "the day of Christ, and out gathering together unto him" (<reference osisRef="2th 2:1">2 Thessalonians 2:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4935" type="x-p"/> The present letter, then, was written to instruct the Thessalonians concerning the day of Christ, "and our gathering together unto him" <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference> and the relation of the "day of Christ" to the "day of the Lord." First Thessalonians had more in view the "day of Christ"; the present Epistle the "day of the Lord."<div eID="gen4935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4936" type="x-p"/> The Epistle is in five divisions:<div eID="gen4936" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Salutation, 1:1-4</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Comfort, 1:5-12</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Instruction concerning the day of the Lord and the man of sin, 2:1-12</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Exhortations and apostolic commands, 2:13-3:15</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Benediction and authentication, 3:16-18</item> </list> <div sID="gen4937" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv145"/> <hi type="bold">angels</hi> <div eID="gen4937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4938" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="2Thess.1"/><div eID="gen4938" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen4939" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="2Thess.2" sID="2Thess.2"/>
<hi type="bold">day of</hi> <div eID="gen4939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4940" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Isa 2:12">Isaiah 2:12</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">for that day</hi><div eID="gen4940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4941" type="x-p"/> The order of events is:<div eID="gen4941" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The working of the mystery of lawlessness under divine restraint which had already begun in the apostle's time <reference osisRef="2th 2:7">2 Thessalonians 2:7</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the apostasy of the professing church <reference osisRef="2th 1:3">2 Thessalonians 1:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 18:8">Luke 18:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-8">2 Timothy 3:1-8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the removal of that which restrains the mystery of lawlessness <reference osisRef="2th 2:6 2th 2:7">2 Thessalonians 2:6,7</reference>. The restrainer is a person--"he," and since a "mystery" always implies a supernatural element <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi> this Person can be none other than the Holy Spirit in the church, to be "taken out of the way" ; <reference osisRef="2th 2:7">2 Thessalonians 2:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the manifestation of the lawless one <reference osisRef="2th 2:8-10">2 Thessalonians 2:8-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 7:8">Daniel 7:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:27"> 9:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:15">Matthew 24:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 13:2-10">Revelation 13:2-10</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the coming of Christ in glory and the destruction of the lawless one <reference osisRef="2th 2:8">2 Thessalonians 2:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the day of Jehovah <reference osisRef="2th 2:9-12">2 Thessalonians 2:9-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 2:12">Isaiah 2:12</reference> </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">salvation</hi><div eID="gen4944" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4945" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv147"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 1 Timothy</title> <div sID="gen4948" type="x-p"/> SCOFIELD REFERENCE NOTES (Old Scofield 1917 Edition)<div eID="gen4948" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4949" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1ti 1">Read first chapter of 1 Timothy</reference><div eID="gen4949" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4950" type="x-p"/> The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to Timothy<div eID="gen4950" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4951" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul<div eID="gen4951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4952" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The date of this Epistle turns upon the question of the two imprisonments of Paul. If there were two (see: <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ac 28:30">Acts 28:30</reference>")</hi> then it is clear that First Timothy was written during the interval. If Paul endured but one Roman imprisonment, the Epistle was written shortly before Paul's last journey to Jerusalem.<div eID="gen4952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4953" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: As the churches of Christ increased in number, the questions of church order, of soundness in the faith, and of discipline became important. At first the apostles regulated these things directly, but the approaching end of the apostolic period made it necessary that a clear revelation should be made for the guidance of the churches. Such a revelation is in First Timothy, and in Titus. The key-phrase of the Epistle is, "That thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God." Well had it been with the churches if they had neither added to nor taken from the divine order.<div eID="gen4953" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4954" type="x-p"/> The divisions are five:<div eID="gen4954" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4955" type="x-p"/> I. Legality and unsound doctrine rebuked, <reference osisRef="1ti 1:1-20"> 1:1-20</reference> II. Prayer and the divine order of the sexes enjoined, <reference osisRef="1ti 2:1-15"> 2:1-15</reference> III. The qualifications of elders and deacons, <reference osisRef="1ti 3:1-16"> 3:1-16</reference> IV. The walk of the "good minister," <reference osisRef="1ti 4:1-16"> 4:1-16</reference> V. The work of the "good minister," <reference osisRef="1ti 5:1-1ti 6:21"> 5:1-6:21</reference>; <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv147"/><hi type="bold">world</hi> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4955" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4956" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">save</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4956" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4957" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sinners</hi> Grace (in salvation). <reference osisRef="2ti 1:14 2ti 1:15">2 Timothy 1:14,15</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 1:9"> 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">immortal</hi> incorruptible.<div eID="gen4957" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4958" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">invisible</hi> Cf. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:18">John 1:18</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Hymenaeus and Alexander</hi><div eID="gen4958" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4959" type="x-p"/> It is significant as bearing upon the seriousness of all false teaching, and particularly as related to resurrection, that Paul calls it blasphemy to teach that "the resurrection is past already" <reference osisRef="2ti 2:17 2ti 2:18">2 Timothy 2:17,18</reference>. <div eID="gen4959" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv148"/><div sID="gen4960" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.1"/>

<hi type="bold">church</hi><div eID="gen4967" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4968" type="x-p"/> Church (visible), Summary: The passages under this head <reference osisRef="1co 10:32">1 Corinthians 10:32</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 3:15">1 Timothy 3:15</reference> refer to that visible body of professed believers called, collectively, "the Church," of which history takes account as such, though it exists under many names and divisions based upon differences in doctrine or in government. Within, for the most part, this historical "Church" has existed the true Church, "which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all <reference osisRef="eph 1:22 eph 1:23">Ephesians 1:22,23</reference>.<div eID="gen4968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4969" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:23</reference>")</hi> like the believing Remnant within Israel<div eID="gen4969" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4970" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 11:5">Romans 11:5</reference>")</hi> The predicted future of the visible Church is apostasy <reference osisRef="lu 18:8">Luke 18:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-8">2 Timothy 3:1-8</reference> of the true Church, glory ; <reference osisRef="mt 13:36-43">Matthew 13:36-43</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:18-23">Romans 8:18-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-17">1 Thessalonians 4:14-17</reference>.

<hi type="bold">mystery</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 13:11">Matthew 13:11</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4970" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4971" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angels</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4971" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4972" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">world</hi> kosmos = mankind. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:8">Matthew 4:8</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen4972" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv148"/><div sID="gen4973" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="1Tim.3"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv148"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 2 Timothy</title> <div sID="gen4986" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2ti 1">Read first chapter of 2 Timothy</reference><div eID="gen4986" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4987" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="2ti 1:1">2 Timothy 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen4987" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4988" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: The touching letter was written by Paul to his "dearly beloved son" shortly before his martyrdom (<reference osisRef="2ti 4:6-8">2 Timothy 4:6-8</reference>), and contains the last words of the great apostle which inspiration has preserved.<div eID="gen4988" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4989" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Second Timothy (in common with Second Peter, Jude, and Second and Third John) has to do with the personal walk and testimony of a true servant of Christ in a day of apostasy and declension. The key-phrases are, "All they which are in Asia be turned away from me" (<reference osisRef="2ti 1:15">2 Timothy 1:15</reference>); and, "A good soldier of Jesus Christ" (<reference osisRef="2ti 2:3">2 Timothy 2:3</reference>). The Asian churches had not disbanded, nor ceased to call themselves Christian, but they had turned away from the doctrines of grace distinctively revealed through the Apostle Paul (see Introduction, p. 1189). This was the proof that already the apostasy had set in its first form, legalism.<div eID="gen4989" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4990" type="x-p"/> The natural divisions are four:<div eID="gen4990" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The Apostle's greeting, 1:1-18</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The pathway of an approved servant in a day of apostasy2:1-26</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Apostasy and the Word, 3:1-17</item> <item type="x-indent-1">A faithful servant and his faithful Lord, 4:1-22</item> </list> <div sID="gen4991" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv148"/><hi type="bold">saved</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen4991" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4992" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (in salvation). vs. <reference osisRef="tit 2:11">Titus 2:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Saviour</hi><div eID="gen4992" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4993" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">suffer</hi><div eID="gen4993" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4994" type="x-p"/> The believer's resources in a day of general declension and apostasy are:<div eID="gen4994" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Faith <reference osisRef="2ti 1:5">2 Timothy 1:5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the Spirit <reference osisRef="2ti 1:6 2ti 1:7">2 Timothy 1:6,7</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the word of God <reference osisRef="2ti 1:13">2 Timothy 1:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-17"> 3:1-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3 2ti 4:4"> 4:3,4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the grace of Christ <reference osisRef="2ti 2:1">2 Timothy 2:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) separation from vessels unto dishonour <reference osisRef="2ti 2:4 2ti 2:20 2ti 2:21">2 Timothy 2:4,20,21</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the Lord's sure reward <reference osisRef="2ti 4:7 2ti 4:8">2 Timothy 4:7,8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the Lord's faithfulness and power <reference osisRef="2ti 2:13 2ti 2:19">2 Timothy 2:13,19</reference>. </item> </list> <chapter eID="2Tim.1"/>
<div sID="gen4995" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="2Tim.2" sID="2Tim.2"/>

<hi type="bold">salvation</hi><div eID="gen4996" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4997" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Lord</hi><div eID="gen4997" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4998" type="x-p"/> Jehovah. <reference osisRef="nu 16:5">Numbers 16:5</reference>.

<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen4998" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4999" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen4999" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv149"/><div sID="gen5000" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.2"/>
<div eID="gen5000" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5001" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="2Tim.3" sID="2Tim.3"/>

<hi type="bold">know</hi> <div eID="gen5001" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5002" type="x-p"/> Apostasy, Summary: Apostasy, "falling away," is the act of professed Christians who deliberately reject revealed truth<div eID="gen5002" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) as to the deity of Jesus Christ, and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) redemption through His atoning and redeeming sacrifice <reference osisRef="1jo 4:1-3">1 John 4:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:18">Philippians 3:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:1">2 Peter 2:1</reference>. Apostasy differs from error concerning truth, which may be the result of ignorance <reference osisRef="ac 19:1-6">Acts 19:1-6</reference> or heresy, which may be due to the sphere of Satan <reference osisRef="2ti 2:25 2ti 2:26">2 Timothy 2:25,26</reference> both of which may consist with true faith. The apostate is perfectly described in <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3 2ti 4:4">2 Timothy 4:3,4</reference>. Apostates depart from the faith, but not from the outward profession of Christianity <reference osisRef="2ti 3:5">2 Timothy 3:5</reference>. Apostate teachers are described in ; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3">2 Timothy 4:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:1-19">2 Peter 2:1-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:4 jude 1:8 jude 1:11-13 jude 1:16">Jude 1:4,8,11-13,16</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5003" type="x-p"/> Apostasy in the church, as in Israel <reference osisRef="isa 1:5 isa 1:6">Isaiah 1:5,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 5:5-7"> 5:5-7</reference> is irremediable, and awaits judgment ; <reference osisRef="2th 2:10-12">2 Thessalonians 2:10-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:17 2pe 2:21">2 Peter 2:17,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:11-15">Jude 1:11-15</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:14-16">Revelation 3:14-16</reference>.
<hi type="bold">sins</hi><div eID="gen5003" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5004" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">salvation</hi><div eID="gen5004" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5005" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen5005" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5006" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">perfect</hi><div eID="gen5006" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5007" type="x-p"/> complete. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>. <div eID="gen5007" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv149"/><div sID="gen5008" type="x-p"/> <chapter eID="2Tim.3"/>

<chapter n="1" osisID="Titus.1" sID="Titus.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv149"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Titus</title> <div sID="gen5013" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="tit 1">Read first chapter of Titus</reference><div eID="gen5013" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5014" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="tit 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5014" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5015" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Practically the same with First Timothy<div eID="gen5015" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5016" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Titus has much in common with First Timothy. Both Epistles are concerned with the due order of the churches. The distinction is that in First Timothy sound doctrine is more prominent <reference osisRef="1ti 1:3-10">1 Timothy 1:3-10</reference> in Titus the divine order for the local churches <reference osisRef="tit 1:5">Titus 1:5</reference>. The permanent use of these Epistles lies in this twofold application, on the one hand to churches grown careless as to the truth of God, on the other, to churches careless as to the order of God's house. The importance of this order is made solemnly emphatic in that the tests by which true elders and deacons may be known are repeated ; <reference osisRef="1ti 3:1-7">1 Timothy 3:1-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 1:6-9">Titus 1:6-9</reference>.<div eID="gen5016" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5017" type="x-p"/> There are two divisions:<div eID="gen5017" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The qualifications and functions of elders, 1:1-16.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The pastoral work of the true elder, 2:1-3,15.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5018" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv149"/> <hi type="bold">Saviour</hi> <div eID="gen5018" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5019" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">wanting</hi><div eID="gen5019" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5020" type="x-p"/> It is not at all a question of the presence in the assembly of persons having the qualifications of elders, made overseers by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="ac 20:28">Acts 20:28</reference> that such persons were in the churches of Crete is assumed; the question is altogether one of the appointment of such persons. These assemblies were not destitute of elders; but were "wanting," in that they were not duly appointed. There is a progress of doctrine in respect of the appointing of elders. Cf. v. 5, note.<div eID="gen5020" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5021" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">elders</hi> <div eID="gen5021" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5022" type="x-p"/> Elder (presbuteros) and bishop (episcopos = "overseer") designate the same office (cf <reference osisRef="tit 1:7">Titus 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 20:17">Acts 20:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 20:28"> 20:28</reference> the former referring to the man, the latter to a function of the office. The eldership in the apostolic local churches was always plural. There is no instance of one elder in a local church. The functions of the elders are: to rule ; <reference osisRef="1ti 3:4 1ti 3:5">1 Timothy 3:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 5:17"> 5:17</reference> to guard the body of revealed truth from perversion and error <reference osisRef="tit 1:9">Titus 1:9</reference> to "oversee" the church as a shepherd his flock ; <reference osisRef="ac 20:28">Acts 20:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 21:16">John 21:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 13:17">Hebrews 13:17</reference>. <reference osisRef="1pe 5:2">1 Peter 5:2</reference>. Elders are made or "set" in the churches by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="ac 20:28">Acts 20:28</reference> but great stress is laid upon their due appointment ; <reference osisRef="ac 14:23">Acts 14:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 1:5">Titus 1:5</reference>. At first they were ordained ( (Greek - <w lemma="strong:G4401">προχειροτονέω</w>," "to elect," "to designate with the hand,") by an apostle; e).g. <reference osisRef="ac 14:23">Acts 14:23</reference> but in Titus and First Timothy the qualifications of an elder become part of the Scriptures for the guidance of the churches in such appointment. <reference osisRef="1ti 3:1-7">1 Timothy 3:1-7</reference>. <chapter eID="Titus.1"/><div eID="gen5022" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5023" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="Titus.2" sID="Titus.2"/>

<hi type="bold">grace</hi> <div eID="gen5023" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5024" type="x-p"/> Grace (in salvation). vs. <reference osisRef="tit 3:7">Titus 3:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Saviour</hi><div eID="gen5024" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5025" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">redeem</hi><div eID="gen5025" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5026" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Titus.2"/><div eID="gen5026" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5027" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Titus.3" sID="Titus.3"/>

<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 10:3">Romans 10:3</reference>")</hi> <div eID="gen5027" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5028" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">saved</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Saviour</hi><div eID="gen5028" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5029" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">by his grace</hi><div eID="gen5029" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5030" type="x-p"/> Grace (in salvation). <reference osisRef="heb 2:9">Hebrews 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24">Romans 3:24</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">sinneth</hi><div eID="gen5030" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5031" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Titus.3"/><div eID="gen5031" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen5012" osisID="Titus" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Phlm" sID="gen5032" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv150"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Philemon</title> <div sID="gen5033" type="x-p"/> SCOFIELD REFERENCE NOTES (Old Scofield 1917 Edition)<div eID="gen5033" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5034" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="phm 1">Read first chapter of Philemon</reference><div eID="gen5034" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5035" type="x-p"/> The Epistle of Paul the Apostle to Philemon<div eID="gen5035" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5036" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="phm 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5036" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5037" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 64. It is one of the Prison Epistles. See Introductions to Ephesians and Colossians.<div eID="gen5037" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5038" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Onesimus ("profitable"), a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colosse, had robbed his master and fled to Rome. There he became a convert through Paul, who sent him back to Philemon with this letter. It is of priceless value as a teaching<div eID="gen5038" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) in practical righteousness;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) in Christian brotherhood;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) in Christian courtesy;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) in the law of love.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5039" type="x-p"/> The divisions are four<div eID="gen5039" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5040" type="x-p"/> I. Greeting 1-3.<div eID="gen5040" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5041" type="x-p"/> II. The character of Philemon, 4-7.<div eID="gen5041" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5042" type="x-p"/> III. Intercession for Onesimus, 8-21.<div eID="gen5042" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5043" type="x-p"/> IV. Salutations and conclusion, 22-25. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv150"/><hi type="bold">account</hi><div eID="gen5043" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5044" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="phm 1:17 phm 1:18">Philemon 1:17,18</reference> perfectly illustrate imputation: "Receive him as myself"--reckon to him my merit; "If he hath wronged thee or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account"-- reckon to me his demerit.<div eID="gen5044" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5045" type="x-p"/> See "Imputation," <reference osisRef="le 25:50">Leviticus 25:50</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jas 2:23">James 2:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Phlm.1"/><div eID="gen5045" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen5032" osisID="Phlm" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Heb" sID="gen5046" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Heb.1" sID="Heb.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv151"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Hebrews</title> <div sID="gen5047" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="heb 1">Read first chapter of Hebrews</reference><div eID="gen5047" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5048" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The authorship of Hebrews has been in controversy from the earliest times. The book is anonymous, but the reference in <reference osisRef="2pe 3:15">2 Peter 3:15</reference> seems conclusive that Paul was the writer. See also <reference osisRef="heb 13:23">Hebrews 13:23</reference>. All agree that, whether by Paul or another, the point of view is Pauline. We undoubtedly have here the method of Paul's synagogue addresses. No book of Scripture more fully authenticates itself as inspired.<div eID="gen5048" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5049" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: From internal evidence it is clear that Hebrews was written before the destruction of the Temple, A.D. 70 (cf <reference osisRef="heb 10:11">Hebrews 10:11</reference>).<div eID="gen5049" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5050" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The doctrinal passages reveal the purpose of the book. It was written with a twofold intent:<div eID="gen5050" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">To confirm Jewish Christians by showing that Judaism had come to an end through the fulfilment by Christ of the whole purpose of the law; and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The hortatory passages show that the writer had in view the danger ever present to Jewish professed believers of either lapsing back into Judaism, or of pausing short of true faith in Jesus Christ. It is clear from the Acts that even the strongest of the believers in Palestine were held to a strange mingling of Judaism and Christianity (e.g. Acts21:18-24 and that snare would be especially apt to entangle professed Christians amongst the Jews of the dispersion.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5051" type="x-p"/> The key-word is "better." Hebrews is a series of contrasts between the good things of Judaism and the better things of Christ. Christ is "better" than angels, than Moses, than Joshua, than Aaron; and the New Covenant than the Mosaic Covenant. Church truth does not appear, the ground of gathering only being stated (<reference osisRef="heb 13:13">Hebrews 13:13</reference>). The whole sphere of Christian profession is before the writer; hence exhortations necessary to warn and alarm a mere professor.<div eID="gen5051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5052" type="x-p"/> Hebrews is in six divisions, but these include five parenthetic passages of exhortation.<div eID="gen5052" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The great salvation1:1-2:18 (2:1-4, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rest of God, 3:1-4:16 (all parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Our great High Priest, 5:1-8,6 (5:11-6:12, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The new covenant and the heavenly sanctuary, 8:7-10:39 (10:26-39, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The superiority of the faith way, 11:1-40.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The worship and walk of the believer-priest, 12:1-13:25 (12:3-17, parenthetic).</item> </list> <div sID="gen5053" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv151"/> <hi type="bold">angels</hi> <div eID="gen5053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5054" type="x-p"/> Angel, Summary: Angel, "messenger," is used of God, of men, and of an order of created spiritual beings whose chief attributes are strength and wisdom. <reference osisRef="2sa 14:20">2 Samuel 14:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 103:20">Psalms 103:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 104:4"> 104:4</reference>. In the O.T. the expression "the angel of the Lord" (sometimes "of God") usually implies the presence of Deity in angelic form. ; <reference osisRef="ge 16:1-13">Genesis 16:1-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 21:17-19"> 21:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 22:11-16">Genesis 22:11-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 31:11-13"> 31:11-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2-4">Exodus 3:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 2:1">Judges 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 6:12-16"> 6:12-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 13:3-22"> 13:3-22</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mal 3:1">Malachi 3:1</reference>")</hi>. The word "angel" is used of men in ; <reference osisRef="lu 7:24">Luke 7:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:25">James 2:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:20">Revelation 1:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 2:1 re 2:8 re 2:12 re 2:18"> 2:1,8,12,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:1 re 3:7 re 3:14"> 3:1,7,14</reference> In <reference osisRef="re 8:3-5">Revelation 8:3-5</reference>. Christ is evidently meant. Sometimes angel is used of the spirit of man. ; <reference osisRef="mt 18:10">Matthew 18:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:15">Acts 12:15</reference>. Though angels are spirits ; <reference osisRef="ps 104:4">Psalms 104:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:14">Hebrews 1:14</reference> power is given them to become visible in the semblance of human form. <reference osisRef="ge 19:1">Genesis 19:1</reference> cf ; <reference osisRef="ge 19:5">Genesis 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2">Exodus 3:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 22:22-31">Numbers 22:22-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 2:1">Judges 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 6:11 jud 6:22"> 6:11,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 13:3 jud 13:6"> 13:3,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 21:16 1ch 21:20">1 Chronicles 21:16,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 1:20">Matthew 1:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:26">Luke 1:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:12">John 20:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 7:30">Acts 7:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:7 ac 12:8"> 12:7,8,</reference> etc.). The word is always used in the masculine gender, though sex, in the human sense, is never ascribed to angels. ; <reference osisRef="mt 22:30">Matthew 22:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 12:25">Mark 12:25</reference>. They are exceedingly numerous. ; <reference osisRef="mt 26:53">Matthew 26:53</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:22">Hebrews 12:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 5:11">Revelation 5:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 68:17">Psalms 68:17</reference>. The power is inconceivable. <reference osisRef="2ki 19:35">2 Kings 19:35</reference>. Their place is about the throne of God. ; <reference osisRef="re 5:11">Revelation 5:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 7:11"> 7:11</reference>. Their relation to the believer is that of "ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation," and this ministry has reference largely to the physical safety and well-being of believers. ; <reference osisRef="1ki 19:5">1 Kings 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 34:7">Psalms 34:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 91:11"> 91:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 6:22">Daniel 6:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 2:13 mt 2:19">Matthew 2:13,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 4:11"> 4:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:43">Luke 22:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:19">Acts 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:7-10">Acts 12:7-10</reference>. From ; <reference osisRef="heb 1:14">Hebrews 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 18:10">Matthew 18:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 91:11">Psalms 91:11</reference> it would seem that this care for the heirs of salvation begins in infancy and continues through life. The angels observe us ; <reference osisRef="1co 4:9">1 Corinthians 4:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:10">Ephesians 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ec 5:6">Ecclesiastes 5:6</reference> a fact which should influence conduct. They receive departing saints. <reference osisRef="lu 16:22">Luke 16:22</reference>. Man is made "a little lower than the angels," and in incarnation Christ took "for a little "time" this lower place. ; <reference osisRef="ps 8:4 ps 8:5">Psalms 8:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:6 heb 2:9">Hebrews 2:6,9</reference> that He might lift the believer into His own sphere above angels. <reference osisRef="heb 2:9 heb 2:10">Hebrews 2:9,10</reference>. The angels are to accompany Christ in His second advent. <reference osisRef="mt 25:31">Matthew 25:31</reference>. To them will be committed the preparation of the judgment of the nations. <reference osisRef="mt 13:30 mt 13:39 mt 13:41 mt 13:42">Matthew 13:30,39,41,42</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 25:32">Matthew 25:32</reference>". The kingdom-age is not to be subject to angels, but to Christ and those for whom He was made a little lower than the angels. <reference osisRef="heb 2:5">Hebrews 2:5</reference> An archangel, Michael, is mentioned as having a particular relation to Israel and to the resurrections. ; <reference osisRef="da 10:13 da 10:21">Daniel 10:13,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 12:1 da 12:2"> 12:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:9">Jude 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:16">1 Thessalonians 4:16</reference>. The only other angel whose name is revealed Gabriel, was employed in the most distinguished services. ; <reference osisRef="da 8:16">Daniel 8:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:21"> 9:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:19 lu 1:26">Luke 1:19,26</reference>.<div eID="gen5054" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5055" type="x-p"/> Fallen angels. Two classes of these are mentioned:<div eID="gen5055" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) "The angels which kept not their first estate place, but left their own habitation," are "chained under darkness," awaiting judgment. <reference osisRef="2pe 2:4">2 Peter 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 6:3">1 Corinthians 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:22">John 5:22</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 6:4">Genesis 6:4</reference>")</hi></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The angels who have Satan <reference osisRef="ge 3:1">Genesis 3:1</reference> as leader.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5056" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen5056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5057" type="x-p"/> The origin of these is nowhere explicitly revealed. They may be identical with the demons.<div eID="gen5057" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5058" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>. <hi type="bold">Melchisedec</hi><div eID="gen5085" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5086" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen5086" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5087" type="x-p"/> Melchisedec was a suitable type of Christ as High Priest, because:<div eID="gen5087" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) he was a king-priest <reference osisRef="ge 14:18">Genesis 14:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 6:12 zec 6:13">Zechariah 6:12,13</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) his name means, "my king is righteous" (cf) <reference osisRef="isa 11:5">Isaiah 11:5</reference> and he was king of Salem (i.e. "peace," cf <reference osisRef="isa 11:6-9">Isaiah 11:6-9</reference>.)</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) he had no (recorded) "beginning of days" (cf) <reference osisRef="joh 1:1">John 1:1</reference> nor "end of life" (cf) ; <reference osisRef="ro 6:9">Romans 6:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 7:23-25">Hebrews 7:23-25,</reference> nor</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) was he made a high priest by human appointment <reference osisRef="ps 110:4">Psalms 110:4</reference>. But the contrast between the high priesthood of Melchisedec and Aaron is only as to person, "order" (or appointment), and duration. In His work Christ follows the Aaronic pattern, the "shadow" of which Christ was the substance. ; <reference osisRef="heb 8:1-6">Hebrews 8:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:1-28"> 9:1-28</reference>. </item> </list>

The New Covenant, Summary:<div eID="gen5104" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) "Better" than the Mosaic covenant not morally, but efficaciously <reference osisRef="heb 7:19">Hebrews 7:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 8:3 ro 8:4">Romans 8:3,4</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Established on "better" (i.e. unconditional) promises. In the Mosaic Covenant God said, "If ye will" <reference osisRef="ex 19:5">Exodus 19:5,</reference> in the New Covenant He says, "I will" <reference osisRef="heb 8:10 heb 8:12">Hebrews 8:10,12</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Under the Mosaic Covenant obedience sprang from fear <reference osisRef="heb 2:2">Hebrews 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:25-27"> 12:25-27</reference> under the New from a willing heart and mind <reference osisRef="heb 8:10">Hebrews 8:10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The New Covenant secures the personal revelation of the Lord to every believer <reference osisRef="heb 8:11">Hebrews 8:11</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the complete oblivion of sins <reference osisRef="heb 8:12">Hebrews 8:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:17"> 10:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:3"> 10:3</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) rests upon an accomplished redemption <reference osisRef="mt 26:27 mt 26:28">Matthew 26:27,28</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:25">1 Corinthians 11:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:11-12 heb 9:18-23">Hebrews 9:11-12,18-23</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) and secures the perpetuity, future conversion, and blessing of Israel. <reference osisRef="jer 31:31-40">Jeremiah 31:31-40</reference>. See also "Kingdom (O.T.)," and <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5105" type="x-p"/> The New Covenant is the eighth, thus speaking of resurrection and of eternal completeness.<div eID="gen5105" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5106" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Covenant</hi> <div eID="gen5106" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5107" type="x-p"/> I. The Eight Covenants, Summary:<div eID="gen5107" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The Edenic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:26">Genesis 1:26</reference>")</hi> conditioned the life of man in innocency.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The Adamic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:14">Genesis 3:14</reference>")</hi> conditions the life of fallen man and gives promise of a Redeemer.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The Noahic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>")</hi>. establishes the principle of human government.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The Abrahamic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18">Genesis 15:18</reference>")</hi> founds the nation of Israel, and confirms, with specific additions, the Adamic promise of redemption.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The Mosaic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:25">Exodus 19:25</reference>")</hi>. condemns all men, "for that all have sinned."</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The Palestinian Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3">Deuteronomy 30:3</reference>")</hi> secures the final restoration and conversion of Israel.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) The Davidic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Sa 7:16">2 Samuel 7:16</reference>")</hi> establishes the perpetuity of the Davidic family (fulfilled in Christ), <reference osisRef="mt 1:1">Matthew 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33,</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 1:3">Romans 1:3</reference> and of the Davidic kingdom, over Israel, and over the whole earth; to be fulfilled in and by Christ ; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17">2 Samuel 7:8-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8">Zechariah 12:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17">Acts 15:14-17</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(8) The New covenant rests upon the sacrifice of Christ, and secures the eternal blessedness, under the Abrahamic Covenant <reference osisRef="ga 3:13-29">Galatians 3:13-29</reference> of all who believe. It is absolutely unconditional, and, since no responsibility is by it committed to man, it is final and irreversible.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5108" type="x-p"/> II. The relation of Christ to the eight covenants is as follows:<div eID="gen5108" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) To the Edenic Covenant, Christ, as the "second Man," the "last Adam" <reference osisRef="1co 15:45-47">1 Corinthians 15:45-47</reference> takes the place over all things which the first Adam lost ; <reference osisRef="col 2:10">Colossians 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:7-8">Hebrews 2:7-8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) He is the "Seed of the woman" of the Adamic Covenant <reference osisRef="ge 3:15">Genesis 3:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 12:31">John 12:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:8">1 John 3:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 4:4">Galatians 4:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference> and fulfilled its conditions of toil <reference osisRef="mr 6:3">Mark 6:3</reference> and obedience.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) As the greatest son of Shem, in Him was fulfilled supremely the promise to Shem in the Noahic Covenant. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1">Genesis 9:1</reference>")</hi> <reference osisRef="col 2:9">Colossians 2:9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) He is the "Seed to whom the promises were made" in the Abrahamic Covenant; the son of Abraham obedient unto death <reference osisRef="ge 22:18">Genesis 22:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 3:16">Galatians 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:8">Philippians 2:8</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) He lived sinlessly under the Mosaic covenant and bore for us its curse. <reference osisRef="ga 3:10-13">Galatians 3:10-13</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) He lived obediently as a Jew in the land under the Palestinian Covenant, and will yet perform it gracious promises <reference osisRef="de 28:1-de 30:9">Deuteronomy 28:1-30:9</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) He is the "Seed," "Heir," and "King" under the Davidic Covenant <reference osisRef="mt 1:1">Matthew 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33">Luke 1:31-33</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(8) His sacrifice is the foundation of the New Covenant <reference osisRef="mt 26:28">Matthew 26:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:25">1 Corinthians 11:25</reference>. </item> </list>

<hi type="bold">die</hi><div eID="gen5119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5120" type="x-p"/> Death, physical, Summary:<div eID="gen5120" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Physical death is a consequence of sin <reference osisRef="ge 3:19">Genesis 3:19</reference> and the universality of death proves the universality of sin <reference osisRef="ro 5:12-14">Romans 5:12-14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Physical death affects the body only, and is neither cessation of life nor of consciousness <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5">Habakkuk 2:5</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:lu 16:23">Luke 16:23</reference>". <reference osisRef="re 6:9 re 6:10">Revelation 6:9,10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) All physical death ends in the resurrection of the body. See "Resurrection" <reference osisRef="job 19:25">Job 19:25</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:52</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Because physical death is a consequence of sin, it is not inevitable to the redeemed <reference osisRef="ge 5:24">Genesis 5:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:51 1co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:51,52</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:15-17">1 Thessalonians 4:15-17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) Physical death has for the believer a peculiar qualification. It is called "sleep," because his body may be "awakened" at any moment <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21">Philippians 3:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-18">1 Thessalonians 4:14-18</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) The soul and spirit live, independently of the death of the body, which is described as a "tabernacle" (tent), in which the "I" dwells, and which may be put off <reference osisRef="2co 5:1-8">2 Corinthians 5:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:42-44">1 Corinthians 15:42-44</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 1:13-15">2 Peter 1:13-15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) At the believer's death he is "clothed upon" with a "house from heaven" pending the resurrection of the "earthly house," and is at once "with the Lord." <reference osisRef="2co 5:1-8">2 Corinthians 5:1-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 1:23">Philippians 1:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 23:43">Luke 23:43</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5121" type="x-p"/> As to the death of Christ, <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 27:50">Matthew 27:50</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">faith</hi><div eID="gen5152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5153" type="x-p"/> The essence of faith consists in receiving what God has revealed, and may be defined as that trust in the God of the Scriptures and in Jesus Christ whom He hath sent, which receives Him as Saviour and Lord, and impels to loving obedience and good works <reference osisRef="joh 1:12">John 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:14-26">James 2:14-26</reference>. The particular uses of faith give rise to its secondary definitions:<div eID="gen5153" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) For salvation, faith is personal trust, apart from meritorious works, in the Lord Jesus Christ, as delivered for our offences, and raised again for our justification <reference osisRef="ro 4:5 ro 4:23-25">Romans 4:5,23-25</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) As used in prayer, faith is the "confidence that we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he heareth us" <reference osisRef="1jo 5:14 1jo 5:15">1 John 5:14,15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) As used in reference to unseen things of which Scripture speaks, faith "gives substance" to them, so that we act upon the conviction of their reality. <reference osisRef="heb 11:1-3">Hebrews 11:1-3</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) As a working principle in life, the uses of faith are illustrated in <reference osisRef="heb 11:1-39">Hebrews 11:1-39</reference>. </item> </list>

<chapter n="1" osisID="Jas.1" sID="Jas.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv155"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - James</title> <div sID="gen5178" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jas 1">Read first chapter of James</reference><div eID="gen5178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5179" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: James <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:21">Matthew 4:21</reference>")</hi> , called "the Just" mentioned by Paul with Cephas and John as "pillars" in the church at Jerusalem <reference osisRef="ga 2:9">Galatians 2:9</reference>. He seems to have been, as a religious man, austere, legal, ceremonial <reference osisRef="ac 21:18-24">Acts 21:18-24</reference>.<div eID="gen5179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5180" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Tradition fixes the martyrdom of James in the year 62, but his Epistle shows no trace of the larger revelations concerning the church and the distinctive doctrines of grace made through the Apostle Paul, nor even of the discussion concerning the relation of Gentile converts to the law of Moses, which culminated in the first council (Ac 15.), over which James presided. This presumes the very early date of James, which may confidently be set down as "the first Epistle to Christians."--Weston.<div eID="gen5180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5181" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: By "the twelve tribes scattered abroad" we are to understand, not Jews, but Christian Jews of the Dispersion. The church began with such <reference osisRef="ac 2:5-11">Acts 2:5-11</reference> and James, who seems not to have left Jerusalem, would feel a particular pastoral responsibility for these scattered sheep. They still resorted to the synagogues, or called their own assemblies by that name <reference osisRef="jas 2:2">James 2:2,</reference> where "assembly" is "synagogue" in the Gr.). It appears from <reference osisRef="jas 2:1-8">James 2:1-8</reference> that they still held the synagogue courts for the trial of causes arising amongst themselves. The Epistle, then, is elementary in the extreme. To suppose that <reference osisRef="jas 2:14-26">James 2:14-26</reference> is a polemic against Paul's doctrine of justification is absurd. Neither Galatians nor Romans was yet written.<div eID="gen5181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5182" type="x-p"/> James' theme, then, is "religion" (Gr., threskeia, "outward religious service") as the expression and proof of faith. He does not exalt works as against faith, but faith as producing works. His style is that of the Wisdom-books of the O.T.<div eID="gen5182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5183" type="x-p"/> The divisions are five:<div eID="gen5183" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The testing of faith1:1-2:26</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The reality of faith tested by the tongue, 3:1-18</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rebuke of worldliness, 4:1-17</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rich warned5</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Hortatory</item> </list> <div sID="gen5184" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv155"/> <hi type="bold">perfect</hi> <div eID="gen5184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5185" type="x-p"/> mature and complete. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">tempted</hi><div eID="gen5185" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5186" type="x-p"/> "Temptation" is used in two senses:<div eID="gen5186" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Solicitation to evil (e.g. <reference osisRef="ge 3:1-6">Genesis 3:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 4:1">Matthew 4:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 10:13">1 Corinthians 10:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 11:3 2co 11:4">2 Corinthians 11:3,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 1:14">James 1:14</reference>).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) Testing under trial (eg) <reference osisRef="ge 22:1">Genesis 22:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:28">Luke 22:28</reference> Cf <reference osisRef="lu 4:2">Luke 4:2,</reference> Cf <reference osisRef="mt 6:13">Matthew 6:13</reference> (solicitation to evil) and <reference osisRef="1pe 1:6">1 Peter 1:6</reference> (testing under trial). </item> </list>
