<hi type="bold">wife</hi><div eID="gen5564" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5565" type="x-p"/> The "Lamb's wife" here is the "bride" <reference osisRef="re 21:9">Revelation 21:9</reference> the Church, identified with the "heavenly Jerusalem" <reference osisRef="heb 12:22 heb 12:23">Hebrews 12:22,23</reference> and to be distinguished from Israel, the adulterous and repudiated "wife" of Jehovah, yet to be restored ; <reference osisRef="isa 54:1-10">Isaiah 54:1-10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ho 2:1-17">Hosea 2:1-17</reference> who is identified with the earth <reference osisRef="ho 2:23">Hosea 2:23</reference>. A forgiven and restored wife could not be called either a virgin <reference osisRef="2co 11:2 2co 11:3">2 Corinthians 11:2,3</reference> or a bride.

<hi type="bold">righteousness</hi><div eID="gen5565" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5566" type="x-p"/> The garment is Scripture is a symbol of righteousness. In the bad ethical sense it symbolizes self-righteousness (e.g) <reference osisRef="isa 64:6">Isaiah 64:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 3:6-8">Philippians 3:6-8</reference> the best that a moral and religious man under law could do). In the good ethical sense the garment symbolizes "the righteousness of God...upon all them that believe."<div eID="gen5566" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5567" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:21">Romans 3:21</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">saw heaven opened</hi><div eID="gen5567" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5568" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">saw heaven opened</hi> <div eID="gen5568" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5569" type="x-p"/> The vision is of the departure from heaven of Christ and the saints and angels preparatory to the catastrophe in which Gentile world-power, headed up in the Beast, is smitten by the "stone cut out without hands," <reference osisRef="da 2:34 da 2:35">Daniel 2:34,35</reference>.<div eID="gen5569" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5570" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">white horse</hi> Contra, <reference osisRef="re 6:2">Revelation 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 45:4">Psalms 45:4,</reference> contra, <reference osisRef="mt 21:2-5">Matthew 21:2-5</reference><div eID="gen5570" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5571" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Day of the Lord</hi> (Day of Jehovah) vs. <reference osisRef="isa 2:10-22">Isaiah 2:10-22</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 4:1-6"> 4:1-6</reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 11:10-13"> 11:10-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 13:9-16"> 13:9-16</reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 24:21-23"> 24:21-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 26:20 isa 26:21"> 26:20,21</reference> <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-6"> 63:1-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 66:15-24"> 66:15-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference>.

<hi type="bold">Come</hi><div eID="gen5571" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5572" type="x-p"/> Armageddon (the ancient hill and valley of Megiddo, west of Jordan in the plain of Jezreel) is the appointed place for the beginning of the great battle in which the Lord, at His coming in glory, will deliver the Jewish remnant besieged by the Gentile world- powers under the Beast and False Prophet <reference osisRef="re 16:13-16">Revelation 16:13-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="zec 12:1-9">Zechariah 12:1-9</reference>. Apparently the besieging hosts, whose approach to Jerusalem is described in <reference osisRef="isa 10:28-32">Isaiah 10:28-32</reference> alarmed by the signs which precede the Lord's coming <reference osisRef="mt 24:29 mt 24:30">Matthew 24:29,30</reference> have fallen back to Megiddo, after the events of <reference osisRef="zec 14:2">Zechariah 14:2</reference> where their destruction begins; a destruction consummated in Moab and the plains of Idumea <reference osisRef="isa 63:1-6">Isaiah 63:1-6</reference>. This battle is the first event in "the day of Jehovah" <reference osisRef="isa 2:12">Isaiah 2:12</reference> and is the fulfilment of the smiting-stone prophecy of <reference osisRef="da 2:35">Daniel 2:35</reference>.

<hi type="bold">make war</hi><div eID="gen5572" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5573" type="x-p"/> The day of Jehovah (called, also, "that day," and "the great day") is that lengthened period of time beginning with the return of the Lord in glory, and ending with the purgation of the heavens and the earth by fire preparatory to the new heavens and the new earth <reference osisRef="isa 65:17-19">Isaiah 65:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="isa 66:22">Isaiah 66:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:13">2 Peter 3:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 21:1">Revelation 21:1</reference>. The order of events appears to be:<div eID="gen5573" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The return of the Lord in glory <reference osisRef="mt 24:29 mt 24:30">Matthew 24:29,30</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the destruction of the Beast and his host, "the kings of the earth and their armies," and the false prophet, which is the "great and terrible" aspect of the day <reference osisRef="re 19:11-21">Revelation 19:11-21</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the judgment of the nations <reference osisRef="zec 14:1-9">Zechariah 14:1-9</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 25:31-46">Matthew 25:31-46</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the thousand years, i.e, the kingdom-age <reference osisRef="re 20:4-6">Revelation 20:4-6</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the Satanic revolt and its end <reference osisRef="re 20:7-10">Revelation 20:7-10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the second resurrection and final judgment <reference osisRef="re 20:11-15">Revelation 20:11-15</reference> and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the "day of God," earth purged by fire <reference osisRef="2pe 3:10-13">2 Peter 3:10-13</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5574" type="x-p"/> The day of the Lord is preceded by seven signs:<div eID="gen5574" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The sending of Elijah <reference osisRef="mal 4:5">Malachi 4:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 11:3-6">Revelation 11:3-6</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) cosmical disturbances <reference osisRef="joe 2:1-12">Joel 2:1-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 24:29">Matthew 24:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 2:19 ac 2:20">Acts 2:19,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 6:12-17">Revelation 6:12-17</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the insensibility of the professing church <reference osisRef="1th 5:1-3">1 Thessalonians 5:1-3</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the apostasy of the professing church, then become "Laodicea" <reference osisRef="2th 2:3">2 Thessalonians 2:3</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the rapture of the true church <reference osisRef="1th 4:17">1 Thessalonians 4:17</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the manifestation of the "man of sin," the Beast <reference osisRef="2th 2:1-8">2 Thessalonians 2:1-8</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the apocalyptic judgments (Rev. 11.-18).</item> </list> <div sID="gen5575" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make war</hi> Armageddon (battle of). See note, <reference osisRef="re 16:14">Revelation 16:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 19:17"> 19:17</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 19:17">Revelation 19:17</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">Beast</hi><div eID="gen5575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5576" type="x-p"/> The Beast, Summary: This "Beast" is the "little horn" of <reference osisRef="da 7:24-26">Daniel 7:24-26</reference> and "desolator" of <reference osisRef="da 9:27">Daniel 9:27</reference> the "abomination of desolation" of <reference osisRef="mt 24:15">Matthew 24:15</reference> the "man of sin" of <reference osisRef="2th 2:4-8">2 Thessalonians 2:4-8</reference> earth's last and most awful tyrant, Satan's fell instrument of wrath and hatred against God and the Jewish saints. He is, perhaps, identical with the rider on the white horse of <reference osisRef="re 6:2">Revelation 6:2</reference> who begins by the peaceful conquest of three of the ten kingdoms into which the former Roman empire will then be divided, but who soon establishes the ecclesiastical and governmental tyranny described in Dan. 7., 9., 11.; Re 13. To him Satan gives the power which he offered to Christ. ; <reference osisRef="mt 4:8 mt 4:9">Matthew 4:8,9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 13:4">Revelation 13:4</reference>. See "The great tribulation," <reference osisRef="ps 2:5">Psalms 2:5</reference>.<div eID="gen5576" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5577" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 7:14">Revelation 7:14</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Rev.19"/><div eID="gen5577" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5578" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="20" osisID="Rev.20" sID="Rev.20"/>

<hi type="bold">thousand years</hi> <div eID="gen5578" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5579" type="x-p"/> The duration of the kingdom of heaven in its mediatorial form <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:24">1 Corinthians 15:24</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">first resurrection</hi><div eID="gen5579" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5580" type="x-p"/> The "resurrection of the just" is mentioned in <reference osisRef="lu 14:13 lu 14:14">Luke 14:13,14</reference> and the resurrection of "life" distinguished from the "resurrection unto damnation" in <reference osisRef="joh 5:29">John 5:29</reference>. We here learn for the first time what interval of time separates these two resurrections.<div eID="gen5580" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5581" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:52">1 Corinthians 15:52</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">Gog</hi><div eID="gen5581" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5582" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 38:2">Ezekiel 38:2</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">devil</hi><div eID="gen5582" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5583" type="x-p"/> Satan, Summary: This fearful being, apparently created one of the cherubim <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 1:5">Ezekiel 1:5</reference>")</hi> See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:eze 28:12">Ezekiel 28:12</reference>" and anointed for a position of great authority, perhaps over the primitive creation, (note 3); See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 1:2">Genesis 1:2</reference>" <reference osisRef="eze 28:11-15">Ezekiel 28:11-15</reference> fell through pride <reference osisRef="isa 14:12-14">Isaiah 14:12-14</reference> His "I will" <reference osisRef="isa 14:13">Isaiah 14:13</reference> marks the introduction of sin into the universe. Cast out of heaven <reference osisRef="lu 10:18">Luke 10:18</reference> he makes earth and air the scene of his tireless activity ; <reference osisRef="eph 2:2">Ephesians 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 5:8">1 Peter 5:8</reference>. After the creation of man he entered into the serpent. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:ge 3:1">Genesis 3:1</reference>", and, beguiling Eve by his subtilty, secured the downfall of Adam and through him of the race, and the entrance of sin into the world of men <reference osisRef="ro 5:12-14">Romans 5:12-14</reference>.<div eID="gen5583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5584" type="x-p"/> The Adamic Covenant <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:14">Genesis 3:14</reference>")</hi> promised the ultimate destruction of Satan through the "Seed of the woman." Then began his long warfare against the work of God in behalf of humanity, which still continues. The present world-system <reference osisRef="re 13:8">Revelation 13:8</reference> organized upon the principle of force, greed, selfishness, ambition, and sinful pleasure, is his work and was the bribe which he offered to Christ <reference osisRef="mt 4:8 mt 4:9">Matthew 4:8,9</reference>. Of that world-system he is prince ; <reference osisRef="joh 14:30">John 14:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 16:11"> 16:11</reference> and god <reference osisRef="2co 4:4">2 Corinthians 4:4</reference>. As "prince of the power of the air" <reference osisRef="eph 2:2">Ephesians 2:2</reference> he is at the head of vast host of demons. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>". To him, under God, was committed upon earth the power of death <reference osisRef="heb 2:14">Hebrews 2:14</reference>. Cast out of heaven as his proper sphere and "first estate," he still has access to God as the "accuser of the brethren" <reference osisRef="re 12:10">Revelation 12:10</reference> and is permitted a certain power of sifting or testing the self-confident and carnal among believers ; <reference osisRef="job 1:6-11">Job 1:6-11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:31 lu 22:32">Luke 22:31,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 5:5">1 Corinthians 5:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ti 1:20">1 Timothy 1:20</reference> but this is strictly permissive and limited power, and believers so sifted are kept in faith through the advocacy of Christ <reference osisRef="lu 22:31 lu 22:32">Luke 22:31,32</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1jo 2:1">1 John 2:1</reference>". At the beginning of the great tribulation Satan's privilege of access to God as accuser will be withdrawn <reference osisRef="re 12:7-12">Revelation 12:7-12</reference>. At the return of Christ in glory Satan will be bound for one thousand years <reference osisRef="re 20:2">Revelation 20:2</reference> after which he will be "loosed for a little season" <reference osisRef="re 20:3 re 20:7 re 20:8">Revelation 20:3,7,8</reference> and will become the head of final effort to overthrow the kingdom. Defeated in this, he will be finally cast into the lake of fire, his final doom. The notion that he reigns in hell is Miltonic, not biblical. He is prince of this present world-system, but will be tormented in the lake of fire.

<hi type="bold">And I saw</hi><div eID="gen5584" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5585" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">great white throne</hi> <div eID="gen5585" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5586" type="x-p"/> The expressions, "the judgment," or, "day of judgment," as the passages and their context show, refer to the final judgment of <reference osisRef="re 20:11-15">Revelation 20:11-15</reference>.<div eID="gen5586" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5587" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">there was found no place for him</hi> <div eID="gen5587" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5588" type="x-p"/> The "day of destruction" is that aspect of the day of Jehovah <reference osisRef="isa 2:12">Isaiah 2:12</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 19:19">Revelation 19:19</reference>")</hi> (Summary) which visits final and eternal judgment upon the wicked. Three such "days" are included in the "day" of Jehovah, and are described in the references beginning with <reference osisRef="isa 34:1-9">Isaiah 34:1-9</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 25:32">Matthew 25:32</reference>".<div eID="gen5588" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5589" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">And I saw</hi><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 20:12">Revelation 20:12</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">judged</hi><div eID="gen5589" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5590" type="x-p"/> The final judgment. The subjects are the "dead." As the redeemed were raised from among the dead one thousand years before <reference osisRef="re 20:5">Revelation 20:5</reference> and have been in glory with Christ during that period, the "dead" can only be the wicked dead, from the beginning to the setting up of the great white throne in space. As there are degrees of punishment <reference osisRef="lu 12:27 lu 12:48">Luke 12:27,48</reference> the dead are judged according to their works. The book of life is there to answer such as plead their works for justification, e.g. <reference osisRef="mt 7:22 mt 7:23">Matthew 7:22,23</reference> an awful blank where the name might have been.<div eID="gen5590" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5591" type="x-p"/> The Judgments, Summary: Among the many judgments mentioned in Scripture, seven are invested with especial significance. These are:<div eID="gen5591" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The judgment of the Believer's sins in the cross of Christ <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 12:31">John 12:31</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the believer's self-judgment <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 11:31">1 Corinthians 11:31</reference>")</hi>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) the judgment of the believers' works <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Co 5:10">2 Corinthians 5:10</reference>")</hi></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the judgment of the nations at the return of Christ <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 25:32">Matthew 25:32</reference>")</hi></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the judgment of Israel at the return of Christ <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Eze 20:37">Ezekiel 20:37</reference>")</hi></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) the judgment of angels after the one thousand years <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>")</hi> , and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) the judgment of the wicked dead with which the history of the present earth ends. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv169"/><div sID="gen5592" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv169"/> <hi type="bold">hell</hi> <div eID="gen5592" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5593" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Lu 16:23">Luke 16:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold">second death</hi><div eID="gen5593" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5594" type="x-p"/> Second death, Summary: "The second death" and the "lake of fire" are identical terms <reference osisRef="re 20:14">Revelation 20:14</reference> and are used of the eternal state of the wicked. It is "second" relative to the preceding physical death of the wicked in unbelief and rejection of God; their eternal state is one of eternal "death" (i.e. separation from God) in sins <reference osisRef="joh 8:21 joh 8:24">John 8:21,24</reference>. That the second death is not annihilation is shown by a comparison of ; <reference osisRef="re 19:20">Revelation 19:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10"> 20:10</reference>. After one thousand years in the lake of fire the Beast and False Prophet are still there, undestroyed. The words "forever and forever" ("to the ages of the ages") are used in <reference osisRef="heb 1:8">Hebrews 1:8</reference> for the duration of the throne of God, eternal in the sense of unending. <chapter eID="Rev.20"/><div eID="gen5594" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5595" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="21" osisID="Rev.21" sID="Rev.21"/>

<hi type="bold">second death</hi> <div eID="gen5595" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5596" type="x-p"/> Second death, Summary: "The second death" and the "lake of fire" are identical terms <reference osisRef="re 20:14">Revelation 20:14</reference> and are used of the eternal state of the wicked. It is "second" relative to the preceding physical death of the wicked in unbelief and rejection of God; their eternal state is one of eternal "death" (i.e. separation from God) in sins <reference osisRef="joh 8:21 joh 8:24">John 8:21,24</reference>. That the second death is not annihilation is shown by a comparison of ; <reference osisRef="re 19:20">Revelation 19:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10"> 20:10</reference>. After one thousand years in the lake of fire the Beast and False Prophet are still there, undestroyed. The words "forever and forever" ("to the ages of the ages") are used in <reference osisRef="heb 1:8">Hebrews 1:8</reference> for the duration of the throne of God, eternal in the sense of unending.
<hi type="bold">angels</hi><div eID="gen5596" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5597" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.
<hi type="bold">angel</hi><div eID="gen5597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5598" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>

<hi type="bold">street</hi> <div eID="gen5598" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5599" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="re 22:2">Revelation 22:2,</reference> cf: <reference osisRef="re 3:4">Revelation 3:4</reference>.

<hi type="bold">saved</hi><div eID="gen5599" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5600" type="x-p"/> Scofield "<reference osisRef="ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>". <chapter eID="Rev.21"/><div eID="gen5600" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5601" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="22" osisID="Rev.22" sID="Rev.22"/>
<hi type="bold">angel</hi> <div eID="gen5601" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5602" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 1:4">Hebrews 1:4</reference>")</hi>.

See definitions O.T. righteousness <reference osisRef="lu 2:25">Luke 2:25</reference> N.T. righteousness <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:21">Romans 3:21</reference>")</hi> , <reference osisRef="ro 10:10">Romans 10:10</reference> righteous living <reference osisRef="1jo 3:7">1 John 3:7</reference> self-righteousness <reference osisRef="ro 10:3">Romans 10:3</reference>.<div eID="gen5602" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5603" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">holy</hi> <div eID="gen5603" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5604" type="x-p"/> Sanctification, holiness, Summary:<div eID="gen5604" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) In both Testaments the same Hebrew and Greek words are rendered by the English works "sanctify" and "holy," in their various grammatical forms. The one uniform meaning is, "to set apart for God."</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) In both Testaments the words are used of "things" and "persons".</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) When used of things no moral quality is implied; they are sanctified or made holy because set apart for God.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) Sanctification when used of persons has a threefold meaning.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(a) In position, believers are eternally set apart for God by redemption, "through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once" <reference osisRef="heb 10:9 heb 10:10">Hebrews 10:9,10</reference>. Positionally, therefore, believers are "saints" and "holy" from the moment of believing ; <reference osisRef="php 1:1">Philippians 1:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 3:1">Hebrews 3:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(b) In experience, the believer is being sanctified by the work of the Holy Spirit through the Scriptures <reference osisRef="joh 17:17">John 17:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 3:18">2 Corinthians 3:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 5:25 eph 5:26">Ephesians 5:25,26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 5:23 1th 5:24">1 Thessalonians 5:23,24</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(c) In consummation, the believer's complete sanctification awaits the appearing of the Lord <reference osisRef="eph 5:27">Ephesians 5:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:2">1 John 3:2</reference> See "Salvation," <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv170"/><div sID="gen5605" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv170"/>Inspiration: Summary. The testimony of the Bible to itself.<div eID="gen5605" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The writers affirm, where they speak of the subject at all, they speak by direct divine authority.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) They invariably testify that the words, and not the ideas merely, are inspired. The most important passage is <reference osisRef="1co 2:7-15">1 Corinthians 2:7-15</reference> which see.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The whole attitude of Jesus Christ toward the Old Testament, as disclosed in His words, both before His death and after His resurrection, confirms its truth and divine origin, and He explicitly ascribes the Pentateuch to Moses.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) In promising subsequent revelations after the predicted advent of the Spirit <reference osisRef="joh 16:12-15">John 16:12-15</reference> our Lord prepared the way for the New Testament.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) The writers of the New Testament invariably treat the Old Testament as authoritative and inspired. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:2Pe 1:19">2 Peter 1:19</reference>")</hi>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1co 2:13">1 Corinthians 2:13</reference>".</item> </list> <div sID="gen5606" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">life</hi> Eternal life, Summary of the teaching:<div eID="gen5606" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) The life is called "eternal" because it was from the eternity which is past unto the eternity which is to come--it is the life of God revealed in Jesus Christ, who is God <reference osisRef="joh 1:4">John 1:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:26"> 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 1:1 1jo 1:2">1 John 1:1,2</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) This life of God, which was revealed in Christ, is imparted in a new birth by the Holy Spirit, acting upon the word of God, to every believer on the Lord Jesus Christ <reference osisRef="joh 3:3-15">John 3:3-15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) The life thus imparted was from the beginning." But the recipient is a "new creation" <reference osisRef="2co 5:17">2 Corinthians 5:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:15">Galatians 6:15</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The life of God which is the believer is an unsevered part of the life which eternally was, and eternally is, in Christ Jesus--one life, in Him and in the believer--Vine and branches; Head and members <reference osisRef="1co 6:17">1 Corinthians 6:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:20">Galatians 2:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 1:27">Colossians 1:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:3 col 3:4"> 3:3,4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 5:11 1jo 5:12">1 John 5:11,12</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 15:1-5">John 15:1-5</reference> <reference osisRef="1co 12:12-14">1 Corinthians 12:12-14</reference>. </item> </list> <chapter eID="Rev.22"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen5387" osisID="Rev" type="book"/>
